EX-21 states no ownership percentages, so the ownership column above is inferred from listing rather than disclosed. China is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, not a VIE, so there is no contractual-control gap, but Shanghai is fully consolidated and exposed to export controls. No entity is designated holder of Full Self-Driving or Optimus intellectual property: robotaxi operations sit in Tesla Robotaxi, LLC while software, data and chip designs stay in the parent, so no separately capitalised autonomy asset exists.

### Customers, buyers and how growth arrives

Tesla sells direct in two segments: automotive at $69,526m of 2025 revenue and energy at $12,771m [S71]. The vehicle buyer is a household or fleet paying cash or Tesla financing; the energy buyer is a utility or developer signing multi-year procurement, with 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026 against 18.5% for automotive. Growth now comes from storage, software (1.74 million FSD subscriptions) and paying Cybercab rides in Austin since 2026-09-03.

### Ownership is concentrated without a dual class

| Holder | Class | Shares | % ownership | % votes | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Elon Musk | Common, incl. 286,428,773 restricted | 699,580,882 | 19.8% | 19.8% | S5 |
| Elon Musk, pledged as collateral | Common | 207,498,721 | 5.2% of outstanding | 5.2% | S5 |
| Vanguard Capital Management | Common | 210,796,512 | 5.3% | 5.3% | S5 |
| Unearned 2025 award shares | Restricted, unearned | 423,743,904 | 10.7% of outstanding | proportional to other shares | S5 |
| Other public holders | Common | balance | 74.9% | 74.9% | S5 |

Percentages follow the proxy, whose denominator excludes unearned award shares; free float is capped by the Musk and Vanguard stakes shown, and a margin call on the pledged block would add supply at the worst moment. With one class and no super-voting stock, control runs through the CEO office, the board seat and stake size rather than a charter provision, unlike Ford's dual-class family control or Alphabet's founder shares.

### Control is priced through a contingent award

The 2025 CEO Performance Award is the control instrument: 423,743,904 shares in 12 tranches of 35,311,992, each tied to a market-capitalisation milestone from $2.0 trillion to $8.5 trillion and to 1 of 12 operational milestones (20 million vehicles, 10 million FSD subscriptions, 1 million bots, 1 million robotaxis, Adjusted EBITDA of $50bn to $400bn); none was earned at 2026-10-19 [S5]. At $2.0 trillion the first tranche implies $506 per share on 3.95 billion shares, and because the operational test falls away in a change of control, a deal at $3.0 trillion would earn three tranches, 105.9 million shares, with no robotaxi or Optimus milestone met. Expense is already running: $802m in the first nine months of 2026, $9.74bn unrecognised on the one milestone management judges probable, and $105.82bn-$120.37bn on the rest [S4]. Dilution of 10.7% is designed, not tail, and sits above the current valuation rather than beside it.

### The board can refuse less than it appears

Nine directors sit in three classes, six labelled independent under Nasdaq rules, with Robyn Denholm as chair since November 2018. Ira Ehrenpreis, who chairs both the compensation and the nominating and governance committees, joined SpaceX's board in February 2026; Kimbal Musk is the CEO's brother; JB Straubel, a director, runs Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier. Related-party flows are small in dollars but pointed: Tesla agreed on 2026-01-16 to invest $2.00bn in xAI, converted into SpaceX Class A stock when SpaceX bought xAI on 2026-02-02 and funded on 2026-03-12, while xAI bought $430.1m of Megapacks and SpaceX bought $143.3m of vehicles in 2025. A board setting a Tesla-SpaceX exchange ratio would do so with three of nine directors tied to SpaceX, and the retail auto-voting programme in the 2026 proxy offers standing instructions to vote with the board outside a defined special matter [S78]. The counterweight is narrow: the Special Committee used only Denholm and Wilson-Thompson, and 78.2% of votes cast backed 2025 pay.

### Capital allocation has no return floor

Tesla has never paid a dividend, repurchased no shares in 2025, and holds no authorisation to offset dilution. It ended 2026-09-30 with $45.45bn of cash and short-term investments, generated $14.90bn of operating cash flow in nine months against $13.01bn of capex, guided 2026 capex above $20bn, and signed three credit agreements with $30bn of commitments in September 2026 [S6]. Against Ford and GM, which return cash, Tesla offers neither dividend nor buyback, so the capital returned to holders is zero while insiders realise value through equity sales. Litigation moved rather than vanished: the Delaware Supreme Court reinstated the 2018 award on 2025-12-19, the 96,000,000-share interim award was forfeited on 2026-04-21, and a securities class action filed on 2025-08-04 in the Western District of Texas covers purchasers from 2023-04-19 to 2025-06-22 over Autopilot, FSD and Robotaxi statements.

A multi-year holder is paid for four things: a contingent award that accelerates on a deal price rather than operating proof; conflict committees that include SpaceX-affiliated directors; new debt against a thin free-cash-flow buffer; and key-person concentration in a CEO who also runs SpaceX. Three conditions would change this judgement — an independent special committee for any SpaceX transaction, no change-of-control acceleration without operating milestones, and a buyback sized to offset stock compensation. None appears in the 2026 proxy, so the governance discount stays. Confidence is high on structure, medium on how a Texas court would treat a challenge to the award; diligence should ask for the pledge's loan-to-value.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 技术与产品 Technology & Product (technology_product, revision 4 by Product Analyst, 8,820 characters)
Tesla's technology is proven where it is a manufacturing problem — dry-electrode cells, Megapack integration — and unproven where the valuation sits. Its 2.0 million cumulative autonomous miles compare with Waymo's 500,000 paid rides a week, its 486,532 quarterly deliveries trail BYD's 762,478 electric cars, and its paid driverless permit exists in one state. The technology justifies a premium to a capital-intensive manufacturer in energy and process engineering; it does not yet justify the multiple of a software platform [S6, S59, S76].

### How FSD works, and where it stops

FSD (Supervised) is vision-only. Eight cameras feed an end-to-end neural network that outputs steering, acceleration and braking; it learns from video from a fleet of 10.2 million delivered vehicles and runs on Tesla's in-house inference silicon. There is no lidar, no radar and no pre-mapped corridors as Waymo has. Training runs on the Cortex clusters in Texas, with 400 MW of compute targeted by 2026-12-31. Two problems stay unsolved. The first is degradation detection when cameras are blinded by rain, fog or low sun: NHTSA's Engineering Analysis EA26002, opened 2026-03-19 over 13 crashes and 2.88 million vehicles, asks whether the system notices and warns the driver. The second is the reliability increment that permits removing the supervisor, which is why customer-owned unsupervised driving moved to Q2 2027 [S58, S80].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |

### Robotaxi: a real service, on one state's terms

Paid Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03, and Tesla claimed 300-plus Cybercabs serving the city on 2026-10-10; Texas records showed 319 authorised Cybercab VINs. It has not disclosed fares, revenue or how many run without a monitor. Permits are the constraint: Texas allows self-certified commercial driverless operation under its 2026 law, while California lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC only for testing with a driver and omits it from the driverless-testing and deployment lists (2026-10-22). NHTSA's defect petition DP26010, opened 2026-10-09 on school-zone speeding, puts the monitored fleet at 1,000 vehicles. Set against Waymo's 500,000 paid rides a week, Tesla's robotaxi is a pilot; set against BYD's 762,478 quarterly BEVs, its car business is the higher-cost producer [S73, S74, S59, S76].

### Cells: a cost moat, not a performance one

Giga Texas runs above one million 4680 cells a week at more than 40 GWh of installed capacity, and since January 2026 both electrodes use the dry process in production — a step CATL, Panasonic, LG and Samsung SDI have not taken to commercial scale. The economics are real: electrode cost 50% lower at full scale, 41% less line capex and more than 30% less factory energy. The product is not: energy density trails by 10-15%, charging is slower than Panasonic 2170 packs, yields above 90% sit below the 98% of mature producers, and Tesla still buys CATL LFP and Panasonic or LG 2170 cells for Shanghai and Fremont Model Y. Battery availability, not demand, remained the stated limit on 2026 volume [S56].

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fleet data and training set | 7 | 10.2 million vehicles and billions of FSD miles, if compute and labelling keep pace | 3-4 years | S6 |
| Dry-electrode process | 7 | Both electrodes dry at more than 90% yield; no competitor at commercial scale | 3 years | S56 |

| Driverless permits | 4 | Texas self-certification is easy; California and the EU are not | 1-2 years Texas, 3+ California | S73 |
| **Composite** | **6/10** | A funded 50-person team would need 3 years for the cell line and 2 for Megapack integration; patents disclose little of either | **3 years of lead time** | S56, S73 |

### Patents: thin disclosure, deliberately

| US20260310299A1 | Flexible touch sensors for robotic hands | US | Not disclosed | — | Published 2025-10-08 | Tactile sensing for manipulation | S75 |
| Maxwell portfolio (acquired 2019, $235m) | Dry electrode manufacturing IP | US | Pre-2019 | Granted, owned | In force | Underpins the 4680 dry process | S56 |

The 10-K does not present patents as a competitive advantage; it rests the case on data, manufacturing cost and vertical integration. The Optimus filings show the limit: Musk said in April 2026 that the V3 hand would not use the patented design because it "ultimately didn't work", so the public record trails the programme.

### Product inventory

| Optimus | Early production | 2026-10 | None | None | 20,000 units a week by end-2027, company claim | S57 |

### Energy is the proven technology

Megapack is the one line where Tesla holds a genuine integration advantage and prices it: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026, a 33.1% gross margin and record order rate and backlog, with 50 GWh of Texas capacity starting. Wood Mackenzie ranks Tesla second among storage integrators behind Sungrow. The counterweight is pricing: revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881bn even as volume rose [S4, S72].

::: evidence
**The headline safety statistic is a company measurement, not an audited record.**

Tesla's October 2026 report puts FSD (Supervised) at 6,006,200 miles per major collision against 660,164 for US driving overall, but the ratio is not fault-based, comes from Tesla telemetry and has not been verified by the regulator, which is running an engineering analysis over 13 low-visibility crashes instead [S58, S80].
:::

### What would change the judgement

The strongest case against my caution is that FSD is already monetised: attach, subscriptions and deferred revenue all rose in Q3 2026, and services gross profit reached a record. Against it, repeated NHTSA recall campaigns on the 2026 Model Y show launch quality slipping on the highest-volume car, and the attach rate is North American only while China sales fell in Q3 2026 with FSD approval still pending.

Diligence questions: what did Austin earn per robotaxi per week, and how many Cybercabs ran without a monitor? What is blended pack cost per kWh? Does EA26002 end in a recall, and what would that do to the unsupervised release date? Until the first two are answered, Tesla owns the best-proven manufacturing technology in the sector and has not yet proven the one the share price pays for."}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 市场与行业分析 Market & Industry Analysis (market, revision 4 by Market Analyst, 8,747 characters)
Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. That split constrains the investment case: no plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from a regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable for a different reason and on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism and the size: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, 2.8% lower year on year, with incentives at 12% of price, $6,594 per vehicle, and the EV premium over comparable petrol vehicles down to $4,847, or 9.7%. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a run-rate near 0.95 million units a year at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank at a high-single-digit rate in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, with France up 74.2% and Germany up 53.1%; hybrids took 36.6% and plug-in hybrids 10%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September alone, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6% a year earlier; the Model Y was the best-selling battery-electric model in September with 17,413 units against 8,227. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced in 2026 by the energy-price shock that lifted European electric-car sales close to 30% in the first quarter. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, in line with the market, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved in Tesla's favour for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2% and lithium costs rose 160%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base whose utilisation depends on demand outside China, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 商业模式 Business Model (business_model, revision 6 by Fundamentals Analyst, 8,999 characters)
Tesla still makes most of its gross profit selling cars, but after regulatory credits the car business earns little at the operating line. Credits supplied 45.8% of FY2025 operating income and 15.7% in Q3 2026; incremental profit now comes from a 33.1%-margin energy-storage business and a 15.9%-margin services business while AI spending absorbs 86.9% of gross profit. Nine-month 2026 revenue of $78,669 million split into automotive $57,310 million (including $639 million of credits), energy $8,428 million and services $12,931 million, against an automotive share of 85.1% in FY2023. Q3 2026 gross profit divided $3,806 million automotive (69%), $954 million energy (17%) and $734 million services (13%), versus 91%/6%/3% in FY2023. Cash arrives when a vehicle changes hands, on storage milestones and prepayments ($3.30 billion of customer prepayments in deferred revenue at 2026-09-30, from $2.04 billion), and monthly for Supercharging, insurance and FSD [S3, S4, S6].

| Segment | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M 2026 | Q3 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue excluding credits ($M) | 80,629 | 74,307 | 67,533 | 56,671 | 20,447 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Automotive regulatory credits ($M) | 1,790 | 2,763 | 1,993 | 639 | 113 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Energy generation and storage revenue ($M) | 6,035 | 10,086 | 12,771 | 8,428 | 2,881 | S3, S4 |
| Services and other revenue ($M) | 8,319 | 10,534 | 12,530 | 12,931 | 4,605 | S3, S4 |
| Automotive gross margin excluding credits | 17.7% | 15.4% | 15.4% | 17.7% | 18.1% | S1, S3, S4, S63 |
| Energy gross margin | 18.9% | 26.2% | 29.8% | 30.2% | 33.1% | S3, S4 |

The credit franchise is ending. Tesla booked $2,763 million of automotive regulatory credits in FY2024, $1,993 million in FY2025 and $639 million in 9M 2026; Q3 2026 alone was $113 million, down 73% from $417 million. Credits carry no cost of revenue, so a credit dollar is nearly a dollar of operating profit: 20.1% of operating income in FY2023, 39.0% in FY2024, 45.8% in FY2025, 31.1% in 9M 2026 and 15.7% in Q3 2026. An implied Q4 2025 figure of $542 million shows the collapse came with the removal of the compliance obligation in 2026, not the lapse of the consumer credit: the Department of Transportation finalised its CAFE rollback on 2026-10-01, ending the requirement that made legacy automakers buy zero-emission credits. Without credits, FY2025's 4.6% operating margin is 2.5% and Q3 2026's 2.6% is 2.2% [S4, S64, S66].

Per vehicle the business improved even as credits disappeared. Q3 2026 automotive revenue per delivery excluding credits was $42,026, up 0.5%, while cost of revenue per delivery fell 2.7% to $34,436, so gross profit per vehicle rose 18.0% to $7,591 (18.1% margin) from $6,433 (15.4%). The gain is cost and regional mix, not price: management attributes the 270 basis points to a higher Asia-Pacific delivery mix, where Shanghai is the lowest-cost plant. Tesla does not disclose customer acquisition cost; SG&A per delivery of $4,142 is an upper bound carrying corporate and non-vehicle cost, and the first vehicle's gross profit covers 1.8 times it. A three-year LTV estimate of $8,455 adds three years of services gross profit per vehicle in the fleet ($288 a year on 10.2 million cumulative deliveries), giving LTV:CAC of 2.0:1 and payback inside the delivery quarter. Tesla is the only one of the three with positive per-vehicle gross profit after credits: BYD's automotive gross margin was 20.49% in FY2025, from 22.31%, and Rivian's automotive gross profit was a $(36) million loss in Q2 2026 [S63, S65, S68].

Energy is the highest-margin dollar of growth. Storage revenue per GWh fell 23% to $210 million from $273 million, but gross profit per GWh fell only 19% to $69.6 million because cost per GWh fell 25% to $141 million, lifting segment margin to 33.1% from 31.4%. The mechanism is cell integration: the first Megapacks built with Tesla's own Nevada LFP cells shipped in Q3 2026, Megafactory Texas began production with 50 GWh of capacity, and the Megapack backlog is nearly sold out through 2027. Fluence earned 13.1% in FY2025; Tesla's advantage is owning the cell, not pricing. Part of the 33.1% is not repeatable: management attributed it partly to tariff refunds and cell-related warranty reimbursements. Services is the quieter engine: revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million on 2% fewer deliveries and gross margin reached 15.9% from 10.5%. Each extra $1 billion of energy revenue at 30% adds $300 million of gross profit; the same dollar of automotive revenue at 18% adds $180 million. FSD and software grow but remain too small to see in the income statement: active subscriptions rose to 1.74 million from 1.04 million, deferred revenue for FSD, connectivity and software was $4.08 billion against $3.87 billion at 2025-12-31, and obligations beyond one year were $10.73 billion, of which $4.80 billion falls due within twelve months. Management's claim that FSD is attached to more than 75% of North American deliveries is company-reported and cannot be tied to a revenue line, because Tesla does not disclose FSD revenue; the observable is $2,345 of deferred balance per active subscription, a stock rather than a price [S67, S4].

The newest change in money flows is who owns the asset. Selling a car converts inventory into revenue once; a robotaxi fleet keeps the vehicle on Tesla's balance sheet and earns per mile, shifting the model from a hardware sale to a utilisation business paid on hours operated, fares and uptime rather than deliveries. The Cybercab entered Tesla's own Austin fleet on 2026-09-03, but no fare revenue, fleet size or per-mile economics are disclosed, so the model cannot yet be tested. Until then the investable model remains the one in the tables: cars, storage and services.

Counter-case: gross margin improves while the company gets less profitable. Operating expenses of $4,776 million rose 39% against $5,494 million of gross profit, R&D alone rose 69% to $2,761 million, and depreciation rose 17% to $1,580 million and will accelerate as more than $20 billion of 2026 capital expenditure is commissioned. The warranty reserve rose 26% to $10,138 million on 2% fewer deliveries, with claims incurred up 29% to $1,614 million while the provision per delivery fell to $1,227 from $1,463. Inventory rose 13.7% to $14,092 million, with 11 days of vehicle supply. The vehicle line covers its own costs, so break-even is about the cost base: operating expenses of $4,776 million need $27.0 billion of revenue at a 17.7% blended margin, and Q3 2026 delivered $28.0 billion for $718 million of operating profit. Normalise energy to a 30% margin and take credits to zero and the quarter earns $515 million, a 1.8% operating margin. For a position, that argues for sizing on the energy and services annuity, with rising margins and a 2027 backlog, and treating autonomy as an option rather than earnings, because at a 1.8% margin the vehicle franchise cannot carry the cost base alone. Confidence is high on the segment arithmetic and medium on how much of the 2026 cost relief is structural rather than tariff and mix. Four diligence questions remain: what is the North American automotive margin excluding credits? What is the energy margin excluding tariff refunds, and at what price is the 2027 backlog contracted? Will Tesla disclose FSD revenue and robotaxi recognition? When do R&D and capital expenditure stop rising as a share of revenue? [S4, S6]

::: evidence
**Tesla's profit now rests on energy and services gross profit, not on credits or on the car**

Energy storage and services supplied $1,688 million of Q3 2026 gross profit at 33.1% and 15.9% margins, while regulatory credits fell to $113 million, 15.7% of operating income, from 45.8% of FY2025 operating income, and operating expenses absorbed 86.9% of gross profit [S4, S6].
:::"}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 退出策略分析 Exit Strategy Analysis (exit, revision 3 by Valuation Analyst, 8,315 characters)
Tesla offers no cash exit at $1.59 trillion. It has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation, and its entire $45.4B of cash and short-term investments would retire 2.85% of the 3.953B shares outstanding. The largest buyout ever completed — Electronic Arts at $55B in August 2026 — is 3.4% of Tesla's market capitalisation, so no financial sponsor can write this cheque, and no automaker can either: GM and Ford together are $118.4B, 7.4% of Tesla. What remains is a sale into a market that trades $14.0B of Tesla a day, or a share exchange into SpaceX, and both leave the return hostage to a re-rating that five years have not delivered. [S3, S130]

### The company returns nothing, and cannot return much

Tesla's 10-K states that it has never declared or paid a cash dividend, does not anticipate doing so, and purchased no equity securities in fiscal 2025. Trailing free cash flow of $3,303M is a 0.2% yield on the capitalisation, and nine-month capital expenditure of $13,014M runs at 2.1x depreciation: the cash is going into factories, cells and training compute, not to holders. Against GM's 12.4% total shareholder yield and Ford's 5.9%, Tesla's is zero. What Musk Said and What He Left Out

With the new filings, Tesla has 36 ADS crash reports in the data NHTSA has published since the current version of the order took effect on June 16, 2025, days before Tesla's Austin Robotaxi launch. August's nine is the most for any single incident month in that data; the next highest is five, in January 2026.
The first Cybercab report
In Austin, a Cybercab was "proceeding straight in a parking lot going as fast as 5MPH and drove into a large pothole filled with water," Tesla's narrative says. The car had "a safety monitor present in the vehicle with no passengers." The crash happened in August, before public Cybercab rides opened in Austin on Sept. 4. It is the only Cybercab entry in Tesla's ADS reports so far; the other 35 involve Model Y robotaxis.
What the other August reports describe

Remote operators driving: In two crashes a remote support operator was in control. In an Austin alley the car touched a dumpster at about 1 mph, and on a Dallas residential street it hit a parked SUV at 0.40 mph after the operator took over remotely. Neither car had passengers.
Chains across driveways: In Tampa and Dallas, robotaxis following their navigation route drove into low-hanging metal chains blocking a parking lot exit (4 mph) and entrance (3 mph). The same release includes an updated report on a similar chain crash in Austin in July.
Tight alleys: Two Dallas robotaxis made low-speed contact while turning, one with a utility meter at 0.45 mph and one with a guardrail at 0.25 mph.
Other drivers: In Dallas, a pickup truck pulled out from a stop sign into a robotaxi's path. Tesla says its car, which had been going as fast as 27 mph, slowed to 3 mph and steered right before the truck hit its left side. In Austin, an SUV rear-ended a robotaxi that was stopped at a yield sign with three passengers inside.

What the numbers don't tell you
NHTSA cautions that the reports are not adjusted for fleet size or miles driven, and Tesla doesn't publish robotaxi mileage with them. Its fleet has grown fast: Texas records listed 769 Tesla Robotaxi vehicles as of Oct. 14, including 349 Cybercabs (see our Robotaxi tracker). Seven of the nine August reports list a pre-crash speed of 3 mph or less.
The data lands while NHTSA is already looking at the Robotaxi program. The agency is auditing how Tesla self-certified the steering-wheel-free Cybercab, with a response due Oct. 30, and is weighing a petition alleging robotaxis speed in active school zones. For more on what the fleet numbers do and don't show, see our look at Tesla's Austin Cybercab count.

arguments.title: 247 Wall St: Tesla and SpaceX just formed special committees to weigh a merger (2026-10-21)
arguments.claims: On the SpaceX Q3 call of 2026-10-20 Musk said both companies formed special committees of independent directors and that he is conflicted and has no role; that no terms have been agreed and there is no guarantee of a deal. He said a Tesla vote would need 50% of all shares outstanding, not of votes cast, which makes every non-vote a no. Tesla's 2026-10-19 proxy sets the annual meeting for 2026-12-03 with three company proposals and no merger vote, so any deal goes to a later meeting. Tesla closed $373.71 on 2026-10-20 and was worth $1.48 trillion; SpaceX closed $147.79 and was worth $2.01 trillion, so Tesla holders would own less than half of a combined group. No exchange ratio has been disclosed. Ira Ehrenpreis joined SpaceX's board after 2026-02-02.
arguments.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that a negotiated SpaceX combination would carry a premium to the undisturbed Tesla price: no ratio exists, the vote needs 50% of all shares, and SpaceX is the larger side. It also confirms the roughly 3.95 billion share count implied by a $1.48 trillion value at $373.71, which contradicts the 3,541 million share count used for the $1,428 billion capitalisation in the financial section.

arguments.title: USA TODAY: Musk's SpaceX, Tesla to build $16.8B Terafab chip factory in Texas (2026-08-07)
arguments.claims: SpaceX announced on 2026-08-06 that Terafab, a vertically integrated chip plant of more than 100 million square feet in Grimes County, Texas, will be built jointly by SpaceX and Tesla, with an initial phase of about $16.8 billion of capital investment from the two companies and potential later phases. Chips are for Optimus robots, Cybercabs and SpaceX space-based data centres. At least 3,000 jobs are promised and Texas granted $30 million from the Enterprise Fund to SpaceX.
arguments.claims_weakened: Undercuts the scenario assumption that 2027 capital expenditure stays at or below $25 billion and that free cash flow is positive without a draw on the September 2026 facilities: Tesla's share of a $16.8 billion joint commitment is not disclosed and sits outside the $20 billion 2026 capital budget. It also adds a related-party capital allocation channel with the controlling shareholder's other company ahead of any exchange ratio.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 竞争格局 Competitive Landscape (competition, revision 3 by Market Analyst, 8,868 characters)
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it trails Waymo by more than an order of magnitude. The proof is in the three numbers together: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5%, so share improves while the absolute business outside Europe shrinks [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% year on year to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were real but small: Toyota 4,964 units (+34.9% month on month), Chevrolet +30.3% and Cadillac +13.1%. Weaker EV programmes retreated after the credit expired and the survivor with the widest line and lowest cost took the share without cutting price. Rivian is the exception that could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in the second quarter of 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only it led 30,317 to 7,498 in every one of those countries, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse for Tesla: its Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Cost of automotive sales was $16,570 million in Q3 2026 for 486,532 deliveries, $34,060 per vehicle, against automotive sales revenue of $41,300 per unit (up from $40,955) and automotive gross margin of 18.5%, up from 17.0%. That is a healthy margin at a premium price point, and it sits 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the cleanest measure of how far Tesla's cost base is from the low end. The margin is protected by mix and software rather than price: FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. A price war in the $25,000-35,000 band would be fought on a cost base Tesla cannot currently match [S4, S6, S101].

| Competitor | Product | Technology | Regulatory status | 2026 scale and price | Share | Strengths vs Tesla | Weaknesses vs Tesla | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BYD | Seal, Sealion, Qin, Yuan | BEV plus PHEV, in-house LFP cells | China MIIT; EU countervailing duty | 39,583 European registrations in September 2026, all powertrains | 2.7% of EU registrations in June 2026 | Two powertrains meet CO2 limits at lower cost; cell integration | Only 7,498 BEVs in the September panel against Tesla's 30,317 | S104, S101 |
| Geely | Xingyuan, Galaxy | BEV and PHEV | China MIIT; EU tariff on China-built units | Nearly 197,500 Xingyuan units February-July 2026 at just under RMB 100,000 | Best-selling model in China | Price point a third of Model Y; mass-segment volume | Thin autonomy and software stack | S101 |
| Xiaomi | SU7, YU7 | BEV, consumer-electronics software | China MIIT | Model Y outsold SU7 and Li Auto's i6 in the February-July 2026 top ten | Not disclosed | Brand pull with Chinese tech buyers; phone-channel distribution | Capacity ramp unproven; China-only | S101 |
| GM | Chevrolet, Cadillac EVs | Ultium BEV | US FMVSS; no federal credit since 2025-09-30 | Chevrolet +30.3% and Cadillac +13.1% month on month in August 2026 | Below Tesla's 51.7% | Dealer network; truck and SUV franchises | Smaller EV volume; margin dilution | S103 |
| Hyundai-Kia | Ioniq, EV6, EV9 | 800V BEV | US FMVSS; EU type approval | Hyundai fourth in US EV sales in August 2026; Kia +12% month on month | Below Tesla's 51.7% | 800V charging speed; warranty; cost control | Weaker software and charging network | S103 |
| Rivian | Mid-size SUV and pickup | BEV, zonal architecture | US FMVSS; deliveries from Q2 2026 | 215,000 units of Normal capacity; Autonomy+ charging since April 2026 | Below Tesla's 51.7% | Purpose-built brand; entry price below Model X | Unprofitable at current utilisation; no energy business | S96 |

### Storage and autonomy are where the advantage is thinnest

In grid storage the pricing power sits with the cell makers: CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of energy-storage batteries in the first half of 2026, up 81%, for 27.1% of the global ESS battery market, while Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months and its energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Tesla's differentiation is integration, grid-forming software and delivery speed rather than cell cost. In autonomy the gap is scale: Waymo runs 3,000 vehicles and 500,000 paid rides a week across 10 US cities, Baidu's Apollo Go operates in more than 10 Chinese cities, and Tesla had 44 active robotaxi vehicles across seven metros in the first half of 2026 before Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03 [S81, S4, S107, S6].

| Product | Position | Leader | Challenger | Niche | Emerging threat | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compact and mid-size BEV | Tesla leads | Tesla: 51.7% of US EV sales | BYD: 39,583 European registrations | Geely Xingyuan at under RMB 100,000 | Xiaomi SU7 and YU7 | S103, S104, S101 |
| Grid battery storage | Tesla challenges | CATL: 27.1% of ESS cells | Tesla: 36.0 GWh in 9M 2026 | Fluence and Sungrow | Chinese LFP integrators | S81, S4 |
| Robotaxi | Tesla emerges | Waymo: 500,000 paid rides a week | Baidu Apollo Go: more than 10 cities | Zoox and Pony.ai | Tesla Cybercab | S107, S6 |

The counter-case is that Tesla is converting rather than losing advantage: its US and European share gains came while rivals retreated, automotive gross margin rose year on year, and the Chinese price war ended with more than a dozen automakers raising prices, removing the deflation that hurt it most. That reading is partly right and does not change the conclusion, because the share gains are in shrinking pools and the margin gain is mix-driven rather than price-driven. Confidence is high on the US and European share data, medium on the China comparison because retail and wholesale definitions differ, and low on the autonomy comparison because no operator discloses audited paid rides. Two diligence questions follow: what is Tesla's share of US EV sales in the fourth quarter of 2026 once Toyota's bZ and Chevrolet's Bolt ramp, and how much of BYD's European volume is plug-in hybrid under the 2027 CO2 review?

::: evidence
**Tesla's competitive position is strongest where the market is shrinking and weakest where it is growing**

Tesla held 51.7% of US EV sales in August 2026 in a market down 46.9% year on year, registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country European panel in January-September 2026 (+51%), and sold 381,088 cars in China (-11.9%) at RMB 263,500-313,500 against a Geely bestseller at under RMB 100,000. Its cost per vehicle of $34,060 is 2.3 times that Chinese retail price, and CATL holds 27.1% of ESS cells while Tesla's energy revenue fell 16% year on year [S103, S104, S102, S4, S81].
:::

| Weaknesses | Cost per vehicle $34,060 against a Chinese bestseller at under RMB 100,000; no product below Model 3; China retail -11.9%; energy revenue -16%; 44 active robotaxi vehicles in H1 2026 | S4, S101, S102, S107 |
| Opportunities | EU battery-electric registrations +40.5% in H1 2026; storage market at 353.4 GWh in 2026 with Megafactory Texas at 50 GWh; Cybercab from 2026-09-03; China price war reversing | S99, S108, S105, S6 |
| Threats | BYD's two-powertrain range at lower cost; Xiaomi and Geely pricing below Model Y; CATL's 27.1% cell share; Waymo's 500,000 weekly paid rides; cell tariffs under OBBBA | S104, S101, S81, S107 |

The competition section is dense and strong, but it uses S107 (low confidence robotaxi tracker) for "44 active robotaxi vehicles across seven metros in H1 2026" — that's a weak-sourced statistic used twice (market and competition). Also the competition section states "Tesla had 44 active robotaxi vehicles across seven metros in H1 2026" which is contradicted by the Texas record of 769 vehicles at 2026-10-14 (different date, so not contradiction). And it says Waymo "across 10 US cities" while my source says 15 metros — minor.

Now for weakest sections. Candidates:
1. strategy — unread. 
2. risk/thesis/scoring — unwritten.
3. esg — has a factual conflict (seven vs six of nine) plus a confusing claim about "the 2025 10-K discloses no material environmental proceeding".
4. market — open advisory + relies on S107 low-confidence for 44 vehicles and the $0.4-0.7B robotaxi bookings.
5. technology_product — open advisory; heavy company-reported KPIs (2.0M miles, 6,006,200 miles/collision, 300+ Cybercabs, 20,000/week Optimus) which are labelled as company measurements in an evidence block, so actually handled reasonably.

Hmm, the Lead said two have open formatting advisories (tech_product, market). I should name three weakest and say whether the advisories matter. I'd say: the two advisories are formatting, not substance — technology_product already has a named-rival table (Waymo, BYD, CATL), and market has the TAM figures in its pool table; the check wants the figure in prose, and a one-sentence fix closes each without new evidence.

My three weakest (substantive):
1. financials — the $1,428bn capitalisation on 3,541m shares conflicts with $1,594.1bn elsewhere and understates EV by $166bn; every multiple in it is ~10% low and the reverse DCF inherits it. That's a real error.
2. market — the robotaxi pool ($0.4-0.7bn bookings, 44 active vehicles across seven metros) rests on S107, the only source the register flags as low confidence, and the same number is reused in competition; also the TAM figure advisory.
3. esg or company_overview — the board independence count conflicts (six vs seven), and the esg section's risk-matrix uses a non-standard column set ("Factor | Exposure | Probability | Impact on company | Mitigant | Source") which isn't the required risk-matrix format but will render as a data table; more importantly its policy claims are well-sourced. Hmm.

Alternatively name technology_product as third because its central facts are company-provided and unverifiable (miles per collision, 6M figure), though labelled.

I think for the red-team review's "weakest_section" field I'll name financials (a wrong share count that propagates into the reverse DCF and every multiple). And in the reply name three: financials, market, technology_product — with company_overview/esg counted as the inconsistency (not a section weakness but a cross-section fix).

Hmm, but wait: is financials' $1,428B really wrong? Let me test with the 247wallst number: Tesla $1.48T at $373.71 → 3,960M shares. But 247wallst may itself just use a data-provider market cap. Two independent-ish sources: funding_valuation says $1,594.1B on 3,952.6M (from S15 Yahoo). $1,594.1B/$403.30 = 3,952.6M — internally consistent, and Yahoo's market cap convention uses shares outstanding. Meanwhile $1,428B/3,541M = $403.30 exactly, so financials used 3,541M — which is the diluted EPS denominator for 9M 2026 (since diluted EPS 0.67 on net income 2,378 → 2,378/0.67 = 3,549M ≈ 3,541M). Yes! So financials computed market cap on the diluted EPS share count. That's a methodological error for market cap (diluted EPS count is a weighted average including dilutive securities, excluding unvested performance awards perhaps). So: financials' market cap and EV are understated by 10.4%, and the correct figure for the price the market pays is $1,594.1B on 3,952.6M issued shares. Confirmed by 247wallst's $1.48T at $373.71 (3,960M).

Also: 3,952.6M includes 423.7M unearned restricted shares — those are legally outstanding and vote, so including them in market cap is right; but for intrinsic value per share you'd use the same 3.95B + future grants (4.00B), which funding_valuation does. Consistent. Good.

Impact on the thesis: none in direction. But it changes (a) the reverse DCF requirement: at EV $1,558B vs $1,392B, the required 2031 FCF rises ~12% from $141B to ~$158B... wait, financials' $141B comes from funding_valuation which used EV $1,558B. Good. The financials' multiples (13.4x revenue) understate. If someone used financials' EV, the reverse DCF would need only $126B. So the error makes the stock look 10% cheaper than it is — direction of the error favours the bull case; correcting it strengthens the reduce case marginally. Good phrasing: "the mislabelled count makes the shares look 10% cheaper than they are, so correcting it strengthens rather than weakens the conclusion."

Now the numbers I need for section 10. Let me assemble the key figures:

Valuation:
- Price $403.30 (2026-10-29); market cap $1,594.1B; EV $1,558.0B [S15, S6].
- SOTP core $170B = $42.50/share on 4.00B [S6, S131].
- Autonomy residual $1,424B = $356/share = 89% of price = 11.3x Waymo's $126B [S120].
- Vehicle segment TTM revenue $75.0B; 1.0x = $75B; GM implied 0.39x → at GM's multiple, vehicles = $29B, not $75B. That's a $46B difference = $11.5/share. So a control buyer using GM's multiple pays $29B for vehicles, $18B for services (1.0x of... hmm services revenue $16.3B), energy at Fluence 0.5x = $6B. Total core at pure peer multiples: $29+$6+$16+$36 = $87B = $21.75/share. That's the honest "peer-multiple" control value — versus the $42.50 in the SOTP, which already applies a 2.5x premium to GM for vehicles. So the answer to the Lead's Q1: the $42.50 core is generous, not harsh, by ~$20/share on a strict peer basis. That is a powerful, specific attack: the core is worth $21.75 on strict peers and $42.50 on the section's premium, so the "89% autonomy" is if anything understated (92-95%).
- But also the counter: energy at 3.5x vs CATL-scale upside. FY2025 energy revenue $12.8B; if energy hit CATL-like scale... CATL revenue is ~RMB 400B (~$56B) — not in register. Can't cite. Instead: if energy revenue doubles to $25B at a 30% margin and 5x sales = $125B, that's $31/share vs $43B in base ($10.75/share) — adds ~$20/share. So even a doubling of energy at a richer multiple adds $20, not $300. That's the answer on "energy at CATL scale": no.
- FSD licensing: 1.74M subscriptions. If FSD revenue were $100/month × 1.74M × 12 = $2.1B/year at 80% margin = $1.7B; at 25x = $42B = $10.5/share. Even a 5x bigger FSD business adds $50/share. So FSD licensing cannot support $600B. Good arithmetic. Need a source for the subscription count [S6] and a clear "arithmetic" label (N2: every material figure needs a source ID; arithmetic on sourced inputs is fine).

Scenarios:
- 25/50/25 → $115. Base $107 is -73%. 
- Bear $35 = core at 0.5x/2.0x + $40B autonomy. Strongest below $35: autonomy $0, vehicles at GM's 0.39x ($29B), energy 1.5x ($18B), net cash $29B after Terafab ($16.8B × Tesla's undisclosed share) and capex overrun → $76B = $19/share. Plus litigation/warranty tail → $15. So the floor is ~$15-20, i.e., the bear is 40-55% too high. Impact on the weighted value: if bear were $20 instead of $35, weighted value = $115 - 0.25×15 = $111.25. Immaterial to the rating. So: bear too shallow, but doesn't change the call. Good.
- Strongest path above $437: (a) a merger where the combined group re-rates (needs SpaceX holders to accept a ratio above market; not evidenced); (b) FSD unsupervised ships Q2 2027 and a second state permits → the tree's "scale" branch $600B (20%) → $212; to get $437 you need the 5% dominance branch. The missed path: a licensing deal with a major OEM (e.g., FSD licensed to a legacy maker at $500-1,000/vehicle on 10M vehicles = $5-10B revenue at 80% margin → $100-200B of value = $25-50/share). Hmm, that doesn't reach $437. Another missed path: Tesla Energy becoming the default supplier for AI data centres (xAI/SpaceX space data centres) — Terafab + Megapack + grid; if energy revenue went to $60B at 25% margin and 8x sales = $480B → $120/share. Combined with base autonomy $259B → $739B+core → $190/share. Still below $403. So the strongest path above $437 is really the narrative re-rating/merger, not operations. That's an important finding: no operational path to $437 within five years; only a multiple event. That supports the reduce call strongly.
Actually the blue-sky $437 = $1,747B equity = core $170B + $1,500B autonomy. To get there you need autonomy at $1.5T = 12x Waymo, i.e., global robotaxi + humanoids. Fine.
- Is 25/50/25 right? Attack: the three branches are not mutually exclusive in timing; the base case (50%) already includes $259B of autonomy (60% of base equity value) at 1.0x Waymo — which is itself generous for a 769-vehicle pilot. So the base case gives autonomy $259B while the bull gives $600B and the blue sky $1,500B. If autonomy were valued at the "regional" $40B in the base (i.e., 35% weight), base value = $170B + $40B = $210B = $52.50/share. plan.visual: 8-10行风险矩阵（概率、每股影响、等级、时点、预警信号、缓解措施、来源）加5行压力测试表，再加一张“换股溢价是唯一不需要交付即可证明现价”的danger卡。
plan.prohibited: 不写“风险可控”“竞争激烈”“护城河稳固”等空话；不用“近期”“大幅”等模糊词；不引用内部审核或修订编号；不把公司自报的里程、车队数与Optimis目标当作已核实事实；不重复其他各节的段落。

rows.finding: 分部之和把汽车、服务、能源与净现金定在$170B（$42.50/股），而同业严格倍数（通用隐含0.39倍市销率、Fluence 0.5倍）只给$87B（$21.75/股）；退出分析里的控制权买家区间是$200-250B，即$50-62.50/股。
rows.mechanism: 核心资产的价值取决于用谁的倍数：1.0倍市销率对2.2-2.5%剥离信用后的营业利润率是40倍上下的营业利润倍数，本身已含溢价；严格的同业倍数把核心压到$22，控制权溢价把它抬到$50-62.50。任何一种口径下自主性都占股价84-95%。
rows.benchmark: 通用汽车隐含0.39倍市销率、Fluence 0.5倍、同业中位16.5倍市盈率；控制权区间$200-250B。
rows.weakens: 若能源按宁德时代式规模重估（收入翻倍至$25B、5倍市销率），核心增加$82B即每股$20，仍不足以改变84%以上的自主性依赖。
rows.implication: 核心资产不是过严而是偏宽，减持结论不依赖苛刻假设；反过来说，任何“核心被低估”的辩护最多值每股$20。
rows.confidence: high：分部收入与毛利率来自10-Q，倍数来自公开可比；控制权区间来自本报告退出分析。
rows.follow_up: 若把能源按2027年订单价格重估到5倍市销率，核心能否到$70/股？

rows.finding: 25/50/25的情景树给$115/股，但基准情形$107里自主性已占$259B（60%），相当于给一支2026-10-14登记769辆车（含349辆Cybercab）、8月上报9起事故、无每英里收入披露的车队1.0倍Waymo（$126B）；按情景树自己的“区域化”分支$40B计，基准为$52.50，加权值约$78。
rows.mechanism: 概率加权值对基准分支的自主性赋值最敏感：把$259B换成$40B，加权值下降$37/股，方向不变但安全边际扩大。
rows.benchmark: Waymo 2026-02-02的$16B融资、$126B估值；情景树区域化分支$40B。
rows.weakens: 若769辆车在2027年跑到每车每周$1,000收入，年化$40M，仍只支持两位数亿美元的估值，而非$259B。
rows.implication: 情景权重对公司偏宽，不是偏紧；修正后仍是减持，但基准不应再当作“中性”读。

在$403.30（2026-10-29收盘）、$1,594.1B市值的位置上，89%的股价买的是自主性与机器人业务，而支撑这笔估值的三个前提同时在恶化：行政许可悬在一份2026-10-30到期的无方向盘Cybercab自认证问询上，合并对价需要一个“全体股份50%”的表决，九个月自由现金流的正数由供应商账期提供。我把市场缩小一半、客户获取成本翻倍、收入下降30%、融资推迟六个月、倍数压缩到同业中位、自由现金流再降30%逐项跑过：没有一项能推翻减持的结论，被推翻的是“这些风险已反映在价格里”的说法。真正能改变判断的是相反方向——若换股比例给特斯拉10-15%溢价，股东无需任何运营交付即可拿到$443-487/股，而这条路径的议价权在评级更高、增长更快的SpaceX一侧。风险不是清单，是排序：能一次关闭自主性期权的是行政与合约事件，不是需求或竞争。[S15, S6]

### 核心资产不是过严，是过宽

分部之和给汽车、服务、能源与净现金$170B（每股$42.50），汽车与服务按1.0倍市销率计$91B。放在同业旁边这个倍数是溢价而不是折价：通用汽车隐含0.39倍市销率，按此汽车与服务只值$29B；Fluence市销率0.5倍、毛利率13.1%，特斯拉能源3.5倍、毛利率29.7%，溢价有依据。按严格的同业倍数，核心是$87B，每股$21.75，自主性占股价95%。向上的辩护也做过：能源收入翻倍到$25B、给5倍市销率，核心多$82B，每股$20；FSD订阅174万，按每人每年$1,200、80%毛利、25倍计，$42B，每股$10.5。把两项都加上，核心仍是每股$70上下，自主性仍占83%。铁路另一边是控制权买家：本报告的退出分析给这些资产$200-250B，即每股$50-62.50，取上限时自主性仍占84%。所以核心的三种口径分别给出$21.75、$42.50、$62.50，结论只有一个：$356的自主性溢价不是市场对核心的低估，是对一个尚未产生收入披露的业务的高估，$600B以上的“FSD授权+Optimus+宁德时代规模储能”叙事在算术上都只能提供每股$20-30。[S6, S131, S120]

### 情景权重对公司偏宽

25/50/25的分配不是太苛刻，是太宽容。基准情形$107里自主性已占$259B，等于给一支2026-10-14在德州登记769辆车（其中349辆Cybercab）、8月向NHTSA上报9起事故、从不披露每英里收入的联合体1.0倍Waymo（2026年2月$126B）。按情景树自己的“区域化”分支$40B计，基准是$52.50，加权值降到约$78，仍然是减持。熊市的$35反而太浅：自主性归零、汽车按通用的0.39倍（$29B）、能源1.5倍（$18B）、净现金因Terafab首期$16.8B中特斯拉未披露的份额扣到$29B，得$76B，每股$19；叠加上市公司诉讼与保修尾部，$15-20才是底。把熊市改成$19，加权值只从$115降到$111，所以情景的正确修正是“基准更保守、熊市更深”，不是改评级。$437以上我原先漏掉的最强路径不是经营，是换股：按$3.60T合并市值，10-15%的比例溢价即$443-487/股；而$35以下最强的路径是合并破裂叠加2027年非监督发布再推迟一年——两条极端路径都由同一件事决定，即特别委员会。[S120, S137, S135]

### 现金能扛滑期，扛不住滑期加收入下降

arguments.markdown:
在$403.30（2026-10-29收盘）、$1,594.1B市值的位置上，89%的股价买的是自主性与机器人业务，而支撑这笔估值的三个前提同时在恶化：行政许可悬在一份2026-10-30到期的无方向盘Cybercab自认证问询上，合并对价需要一个“全体股份50%”的表决，九个月自由现金流的正数由供应商账期提供。我把市场缩小一半、客户获取成本翻倍、收入下降30%、融资推迟六个月、倍数压缩到同业中位、自由现金流再降30%逐项跑过：没有一项能推翻减持的结论，被推翻的是“这些风险已经反映在价格里”的说法。这个区别是实质性的，因为清单式风险让人以为时间站在持有者一边，而三件最可能发生的事都在未来十二个月内到期，自主性的收入证据却最早要到2027年下半年才可能出现。真正能改变判断的是相反方向——若换股比例给特斯拉10-15%溢价，股东无需任何运营交付即可拿到$443-487/股，而这条路径的议价权在评级更高、增长更快的SpaceX一侧。风险要排序，不要罗列：能一次关闭自主性期权的是行政与合约事件，不是需求，也不是竞争。[S15, S6]

### 核心资产不是过严，是过宽

分部之和给汽车、服务、能源与净现金$170B（每股$42.50），其中汽车与服务按1.0倍市销率计$91B。放在同业旁边这个倍数是溢价而不是折价：通用汽车隐含0.39倍市销率，按此口径汽车与服务只值$29B；Fluence市销率0.5倍、毛利率13.1%，特斯拉能源3.5倍、毛利率29.7%，能源的溢价有依据。按严格的同业倍数，核心是$87B，每股$21.75，自主性占股价95%。向上的辩护也做过：能源收入翻倍到$25B、给5倍市销率，核心多$82B，每股$20；FSD订阅174万，按每人每年$1,200、80%毛利、25倍计，$42B，每股$10.5。两项都加上，核心仍是每股$70上下，自主性占83%。另一边是控制权买家：这些资产在并购市场值$200-250B，即每股$50-62.50，取上限时自主性仍占84%。战略买家的名单是空的——通用与福特合计市值$118.4B，是特斯拉的7.4%，能开支票的只有Alphabet，而它恰是无人驾驶领域最直接的竞争者，反垄断而非价格才是障碍。三种口径分别给出$21.75、$42.50、$62.50，结论只有一个：$356的自主性溢价不是市场对核心的低估，是对一项没有收入披露的业务的高估，它等于Waymo 2026年2月$126B融资的11.3倍；“FSD授权＋Optimus＋宁德时代规模储能”的叙事在算术上只能再提供每股$20-30，撑不起$600B。[S6, S131, S120]

### 情景权重对公司偏宽，熊市却不够深

25/50/25的分配不是太苛刻，是太宽容。基准情形$107里自主性已占$259B，等于给一支2026-10-14在德州登记769辆车（其中349辆Cybercab）、8月向NHTSA上报9起事故、从不披露每英里收入的联合体1.0倍Waymo。按情景树自己的“区域化”分支$40B计，基准是$52.50，加权值降到$78，仍然是减持。我把非监督客户FSD在2027年内按期落地的概率定在40%，把合并一年内成交的概率也定在40%，这两个数已经高于记录支持的水平：前者面对一份未结案的工程分析与一份10-12开立的校区超速缺陷请愿，后者面对一条从未跑通的跨公司表决路径。熊市的$35反而太浅：自主性归零、汽车按通用的0.39倍（$29B）、能源1.5倍（$18B）、净现金因Terafab首期$16.8B中特斯拉未披露的份额扣到$29B，得$76B，每股$19；叠加上市公司诉讼与保修尾部，$15-20才是底。把熊市改成$19，加权值只从$115降到$111，所以情景的正确修正是“基准更保守、熊市更深”，不是改评级。$437以上我原先漏掉的最强路径不是经营，是换股；$35以下最强的路径则是合并破裂叠加非监督发布再推迟一年。两条极端路径由同一件事决定，即特别委员会，而它们都不在25/50/25的树里。[S120, S137, S135]

### 现金能扛滑期，扛不住滑期加收入下降

$36.18B净现金、$45.45B现金与短期投资、2026年9月签下的$30B承诺额度，足以承受两年的自主性滑期而不增发：即使自由现金流两年为零，净现金仍在$30B以上，额度未动。压力出现在叠加情形。按19%毛利率，收入下降30%使毛利减少$6.0B，年化运营费用$19.1B，经营现金流降到0至-$2B，再减$20-25B资本开支，年消耗$20-27B，现金加额度在2029年前用尽，之后才是股权，而那时股价已按核心资产定价。更近的问题是现金质量：九个月自由现金流$1,883M中的$7,332M来自应付账款与应计，账期从62.8天拉到75.3天，在九个月成本基础上相当于$2.9B一次性现金，剔除后自由现金流为-$1.0B。存货上升13.7%而交付下降2%、保修准备上升26%、已发生索赔上升29%，三项都是计提不足的先行指标；储能客户预付增加$1,746M是订单证据，也是客户集中度。融资这一侧的缓冲比现金更薄：穆迪给特斯拉Baa3、展望稳定，SpaceX是Baa1，而2026年9月的三份信贷协议未披露定价与期限，一旦提款，利息成本会落在2.2-2.5%的剥离信用后营业利润率之上。Terafab的$16.8B首期由SpaceX与特斯拉共同出资、特斯拉份额未披露，且不在“2026年资本开支>$20B”的预算口径内，所以“2027年资本开支≤$250亿且自由现金流为正”在公司材料里找不到支撑。[S4, S134, S138]

### 合并是期权，不是底价

2026-10-20马斯克本人说两家公司已成立独立董事特别委员会，但“尚未就任何交易条款达成一致，也不保证会达成”，并称特斯拉表决需要“全体股份的50%，而非出席股份”——未投票等于反对，散户基础使这条门槛比表面更高；2026-10-19的委托书把年会定在2026-12-03，三项议案中并没有合并表决，任何交易都要另开股东大会。按市价换股在数学上是价值中性的：$1,594.1B加$2.01T等于$3.60T，特斯拉股东拿44%，正是今天的市值。溢价只能来自SpaceX委员会让渡，而SpaceX是更大、增长更快、穆迪Baa1的一方，特斯拉是Baa3——合并后特斯拉股东用一股一票换到44%的经济权益和马斯克84%的投票权，这是治理降级而非价值创造。价值转移的机制写在2025年CEO奖励里：控制权变更时经营里程碑失效，市值达标即归属，$3.0T对应3批105.9M股，headline价值越高，稀释越大；同一份奖励已有$9.74B在“很可能达成”的那一档确认，未达可能的区间是$105.82-120.37B。207.5M股（5.2%）已质押，股价下行会在最差时点增加供给；九名董事中三名与SpaceX有关联，特别委员会只用了Denholm与Wilson-Thompson两人，而xAI投资在2026-02-02被换成SpaceX股份的先例说明关联资产互换在这个董事会里无需股东事先批准。[S5, S135, S138]

### 政策是小期权，竞争是终值风险

CAFE回滚可逆，但幅度小。25位州检察长与12个城市县于2026-03-19在哥伦比亚特区巡回法院起诉EPA撤销2009年危害认定（2026-02-12终局），2026-05-20并入同一案并争议行政记录是否被修改；若撤销被推翻，合规信用池回归，但信用收入即使恢复到$1.5B、给15倍也只值$22.5B，每股$5.6，而下降已经入账：Q3信用收入$113M、同比-73%，FY2025信用占营业利润45.8%。它是$5.6/股的期权，不是估值摆动项，也不该被写成“政策风险”了事。竞争压缩的是每英里价格而非2027年销量：比亚迪在欧洲与特斯拉同为2.4%份额、单车便宜€5,500，小米在首个量产年就接近盈亏平衡，Waymo每周50万次付费行程、3,000辆车，对特斯拉769辆；若每英里收入从$0.60被压到$0.45，反向DCF所需车队从1,570万辆升到2,090万辆，超过全球汽车年产能。这条风险落在牛市的终值上，-$40至-$60/股，不在明年的损益上；它也不会以价格战的形式出现，而是以“特斯拉定不了价”的形式出现。[S136, S138, S59]

### 信息最薄的三处与改口条件

三处信息在任何公开披露里都找不到：机器人出租车损益（收入、每车每周、无安全员比例）、每英里成本、特斯拉在Terafab的出资份额。它们不是背景空白：第一项决定基准情形的自主性赋值是否成立，第二项决定反向DCF的收入假设，第三项决定明后两年是否需要股权融资。要问管理层两个问题：奥斯汀每车每周收入与无安全员车辆占比是多少？特斯拉在Terafab的出资比例与时间表是什么？可以推翻我的只有四件事：季度更新首次披露机器人出租车收入行且单位经济优于反向DCF的假设；加州发出无安全员部署许可；特别委员会公布含溢价而非按市价的换股比例；或剥离信用后的营业利润率回到两位数。四件都不会在2026-12-03股东大会前发生，所以未来六周的合理动作是等待，而不是加仓。

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 风险评估 Risk Assessment (risk, revision 2 by Red Team Analyst, 5,847 characters)
在$403.30（2026-10-29收盘）、$1,594.1B市值的位置上，89%的股价买的是自主性与机器人业务，而支撑这笔估值的三个前提同时在恶化：行政许可悬在一份2026-10-30到期的无方向盘Cybercab自认证问询上，合并对价需要一个“全体股份50%”的表决，九个月自由现金流的正数由供应商账期提供。我把市场缩小一半、客户获取成本翻倍、收入下降30%、融资推迟六个月、倍数压缩到同业中位、自由现金流再降30%逐项跑过：没有一项能推翻减持的结论，被推翻的是“这些风险已经反映在价格里”的说法。这个区别是实质性的，因为清单式风险让人以为时间站在持有者一边，而三件最可能发生的事都在未来十二个月内到期，自主性的收入证据却最早要到2027年下半年才可能出现。真正能改变判断的是相反方向——若换股比例给特斯拉10-15%溢价，股东无需任何运营交付即可拿到$443-487/股，而这条路径的议价权在评级更高、增长更快的SpaceX一侧。风险要排序，不要罗列：能一次关闭自主性期权的是行政与合约事件，不是需求，也不是竞争。[S15, S6]

### 核心资产不是过严，是过宽

分部之和给汽车、服务、能源与净现金$170B（每股$42.50），其中汽车与服务按1.0倍市销率计$91B。放在同业旁边这个倍数是溢价而不是折价：通用汽车隐含0.39倍市销率，按此口径汽车与服务只值$29B；Fluence市销率0.5倍、毛利率13.1%，特斯拉能源3.5倍、毛利率29.7%，能源的溢价有依据。按严格的同业倍数，核心是$87B，每股$21.75，自主性占股价95%。向上的辩护也做过：能源收入翻倍到$25B、给5倍市销率，核心多$82B，每股$20；FSD订阅174万，按每人每年$1,200、80%毛利、25倍计，$42B，每股$10.5。两项都加上，核心仍是每股$70上下，自主性占83%。另一边是控制权买家：这些资产在并购市场值$200-250B，即每股$50-62.50，取上限时自主性仍占84%。战略买家的名单是空的——通用与福特合计市值$118.4B，是特斯拉的7.4%，能开支票的只有Alphabet，而它恰是无人驾驶领域最直接的竞争者，反垄断而非价格才是障碍。三种口径分别给出$21.75、$42.50、$62.50，结论只有一个：$356的自主性溢价不是市场对核心的低估，是对一项没有收入披露的业务的高估，它等于Waymo 2026年2月$126B融资的11.3倍；“FSD授权＋Optimus＋宁德时代规模储能”的叙事在算术上只能再提供每股$20-30，撑不起$600B。[S6, S131, S120]

### 情景权重对公司偏宽，熊市却不够深

25/50/25的分配不是太苛刻，是太宽容。基准情形$107里自主性已占$259B，等于给一支2026-10-14在德州登记769辆车（其中349辆Cybercab）、8月向NHTSA上报9起事故、从不披露每英里收入的联合体1.0倍Waymo。按情景树自己的“区域化”分支$40B计，基准是$52.50，加权值降到$78，仍然是减持。我把非监督客户FSD在2027年内按期落地的概率定在40%，把合并一年内成交的概率也定在40%，这两个数已经高于记录支持的水平：前者面对一份未结案的工程分析与一份10-12开立的校区超速缺陷请愿，后者面对一条从未跑通的跨公司表决路径。熊市的$35反而太浅：自主性归零、汽车按通用的0.39倍（$29B）、能源1.5倍（$18B）、净现金因Terafab首期$16.8B中特斯拉未披露的份额扣到$29B，得$76B，每股$19；叠加上市公司诉讼与保修尾部，$15-20才是底。把熊市改成$19，加权值只从$115降到$111，所以情景的正确修正是“基准更保守、熊市更深”，不是改评级。$437以上我原先漏掉的最强路径不是经营，是换股；$35以下最强的路径则是合并破裂叠加非监督发布再推迟一年。两条极端路径由同一件事决定，即特别委员会，而它们都不在25/50/25的树里。[S120, S137, S135]

### 现金能扛滑期，扛不住滑期加收入下降

$36.18B净现金、$45.45B现金与短期投资、2026年9月签下的$30B承诺额度，足以承受两年的自主性滑期而不增发：即使自由现金流两年为零，净现金仍在$30B以上，额度未动。压力出现在叠加情形。按19%毛利率，收入下降30%使毛利减少$6.0B，年化运营费用$19.1B，经营现金流降到0至-$2B，再减$20-25B资本开支，年消耗$20-27B，现金加额度在2029年前用尽，之后才是股权，而那时股价已按核心资产定价。更近的问题是现金质量：九个月自由现金流$1,883M中的$7,332M来自应付账款与应计，账期从62.8天拉到75.3天，在九个月成本基础上相当于$2.9B一次性现金，剔除后自由现金流为-$1.0B。存货上升13.7%而交付下降2%、保修准备上升26%、已发生索赔上升29%，三项都是计提不足的先行指标；储能客户预付增加$1,746M是订单证据，也是客户集中度。融资这一侧的缓冲比现金更薄：穆迪给特斯拉Baa3、展望稳定，SpaceX是Baa1，而2026年9月的三份信贷协议未披露定价与期限，一旦提款，利息成本会落在2.2-2.5%的剥离信用后营业利润率之上。Terafab的$16.8B首期由SpaceX与特斯拉共同出资、特斯拉份额未披露，且不在“2026年资本开支>$20B”的预算口径内，所以“2027年资本开支≤$250亿且自由现金流为正”在公司材料里找不到支撑。[S4, S134, S138]

### 合并是期权，不是底价

2026-10-20马斯克本人说两家公司已成立独立董事特别委员会，但“尚未就任何交易条款达成一致，也不保证会达成”，并称特斯拉表决需要“全体股份的50%，而非出席股份”——未投票等于反对，散户基础使这条门槛比表面更高；2026-10-19的委托书把年会定在2026-12-03，三项议案中并没有合并表决，任何交易都要另开股东大会。按市价换股在数学上是价值中性的：$1,594.1B加$2.01T等于$3.60T，特斯拉股东拿44%，正是今天的市值。溢价只能来自SpaceX委员会让渡，而SpaceX是更大、增长更快、穆迪Baa1的一方，特斯拉是Baa3——合并后特斯拉股东用一股一票换到44%的经济权益和马斯克84%的投票权，这是治理降级而非价值创造。价值转移的机制写在2025年CEO奖励里：控制权变更时经营里程碑失效，市值达标即归属，$3.0T对应3批105.9M股，headline价值越高，稀释越大；同一份奖励已有$9.74B在“很可能达成”的那一档确认，未达可能的区间是$105.82-120.37B。207.5M股（5.2%）已质押，股价下行会在最差时点增加供给；九名董事中三名与SpaceX有关联，特别委员会只用了Denholm与Wilson-Thompson两人，而xAI投资在2026-02-02被换成SpaceX股份的先例说明关联资产互换在这个董事会里无需股东事先批准。[S5, S135, S138]

### 政策是小期权，竞争是终值风险

CAFE回滚可逆，但幅度小。25位州检察长与12个城市县于2026-03-19在哥伦比亚特区巡回法院起诉EPA撤销2009年危害认定（2026-02-12终局），2026-05-20并入同一案并争议行政记录是否被修改；若撤销被推翻，合规信用池回归，但信用收入即使恢复到$1.5B、给15倍也只值$22.5B，每股$5.6，而下降已经入账：Q3信用收入$113M、同比-73%，FY2025信用占营业利润45.8%。它是$5.6/股的期权，不是估值摆动项，也不该被写成“政策风险”了事。竞争压缩的是每英里价格而非2027年销量：比亚迪在欧洲与特斯拉同为2.4%份额、单车便宜€5,500，小米在首个量产年就接近盈亏平衡，Waymo每周50万次付费行程、3,000辆车，对特斯拉769辆；若每英里收入从$0.60被压到$0.45，反向DCF所需车队从1,570万辆升到2,090万辆，超过全球汽车年产能。这条风险落在牛市的终值上，-$40至-$60/股，不在明年的损益上；它也不会以价格战的形式出现，而是以“特斯拉定不了价”的形式出现。[S136, S138, S59]

### 信息最薄的三处与改口条件

三处信息在任何公开披露里都找不到：机器人出租车损益（收入、每车每周、无安全员比例）、每英里成本、特斯拉在Terafab的出资份额。它们不是背景空白：第一项决定基准情形的自主性赋值是否成立，第二项决定反向DCF的收入假设，第三项决定明后两年是否需要股权融资。要问管理层两个问题：奥斯汀每车每周收入与无安全员车辆占比是多少？特斯拉在Terafab的出资比例与时间表是什么？可以推翻我的只有四件事：季度更新首次披露机器人出租车收入行且单位经济优于反向DCF的假设；加州发出无安全员部署许可；特别委员会公布含溢价而非按市价的换股比例；或剥离信用后的营业利润率回到两位数。四件都不会在2026-12-03股东大会前发生，所以未来六周的合理动作是等待，而不是加仓。

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 融资历程与估值 Funding History & Valuation (funding_valuation, revision 7 by Valuation Analyst, 8,492 characters)
At $403.30 (NasdaqGS, 2026-10-29 20:00 UTC) Tesla's equity is worth $1,594.1B and its enterprise value $1,558.0B. On a sum of the parts, 89% of that price — $1,424B, or $356 a share — buys autonomy and robotics, while the automotive, energy and services businesses plus $36.2B of net cash are worth a computed $42.50 a share at peer multiples. That residual is 11.3 times the $126B at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026, and Waymo is the only operator running a scaled driverless service. My probability-weighted value is $115 a share, 71% below the close, and the disagreement is not about cars: my $42.50 for the core sits within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 a share for the same business. It is about whether 2.0M cumulative unsupervised miles, a robotaxi service confined to one city and zero disclosed Optimus revenue can carry $1.4 trillion. [S15, S120, S6]

### A five-year flat line and a violent quarter

The price has gone nowhere over the period shown below and has lagged the index; the last quarter reversed part of that lag, a window that contains the third-quarter results and the merger remarks Musk made on the same earnings call.

### 443 times trailing earnings, 183 times 2027 consensus

On trailing figures Tesla trades at 443.2x earnings, 15.0x sales and 170.5x EBITDA — or 104x on the company's own $15.0B adjusted EBITDA, which excludes $4.3B of stock compensation. The six-company peer median is 16.5x earnings and 5.0x sales. Consensus that already assumes a robotaxi ramp barely normalises the multiple: 2026 revenue of $108.5B and EPS of $1.67 give 241x, and 2027 revenue of $123.9B and EPS of $2.20 give 183x. [S115] Tesla's own history does not support the level either: the P/E at the last five fiscal year ends was 72.8x (2021), 34.0x (2022), 57.8x (2023), 204.6x (2024) and 420.8x (2025), so today sits above every year-end mark in the series.

Solvency is not the risk; the return on the capital being deployed is [S4].

That return has collapsed. Invested capital of $53,109 million (equity $89,289 million plus debt less cash and securities) earned a trailing ROIC of 5.5% and an ROE of 3.8%, against 28.3% and 27.9% in FY2023, when the equity base was $62,634 million. Against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a beta of 1.5 to 2.0, our estimate of the cost of capital is 11% to 14%, so the company is destroying economic value at current margins. Read strategically, this converts a cost advantage in vehicles and cells into a capital-intensive compute and robotics business before that business has customers, so the shares trade on optionality rather than earnings. Capital allocation offers no offset: no dividend, no buyback, capital expenditure guided above $20 billion for 2026, and $1.95 billion of stock paid for an AI hardware company in Q2 2026. Equity compensation is the other claim on shareholders: $3,557 million in nine months is 4.5% of revenue, the 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423.7 million shares, or 12% of the 3,541 million diluted count, with $9.74 billion of unrecognised expense on the one milestone judged probable, and the 2018 award was exercised for 304.0 million options in Q2 2026, leaving restricted shares that vest on 2028-01-19 [S4, S15, S24].

The price is an option, not a multiple. At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 the equity is worth $1,428 billion and the enterprise $1,392 billion after net cash: 13.4x trailing revenue, 401x operating income, 92x trailing adjusted EBITDA of $14,995 million and 431x free cash flow. Confidence is high on the statements and the cash bridge, medium on the cost of capital, and low on any estimate that requires autonomous revenue to be sized. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 退出策略分析 Exit Strategy Analysis (exit, revision 3 by Valuation Analyst, 8,315 characters)
Tesla offers no cash exit at $1.59 trillion. It has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation, and its entire $45.4B of cash and short-term investments would retire 2.85% of the 3.953B shares outstanding. The largest buyout ever completed — Electronic Arts at $55B in August 2026 — is 3.4% of Tesla's market capitalisation, so no financial sponsor can write this cheque, and no automaker can either: GM and Ford together are $118.4B, 7.4% of Tesla. What remains is a sale into a market that trades $14.0B of Tesla a day, or a share exchange into SpaceX, and both leave the return hostage to a re-rating that five years have not delivered. [S3, S130]

### The company returns nothing, and cannot return much

Tesla's 10-K states that it has never declared or paid a cash dividend, does not anticipate doing so, and purchased no equity securities in fiscal 2025. Trailing free cash flow of $3,303M is a 0.2% yield on the capitalisation, and nine-month capital expenditure of $13,014M runs at 2.1x depreciation: the cash is going into factories, cells and training compute, not to holders. Against GM's 12.4% total shareholder yield and Ford's 5.9%, Tesla's is zero. Even a maximal buyback using the whole cash pile would move the share count by less than three points, and it would leave a company spending $17B a year on capital projects with no liquidity buffer. Capital return is a governance choice, and the controlling shareholder has consistently chosen reinvestment. [S6]

### The exit that always works is the tape

The secondary market is the only channel that is always open. Tesla trades 36.96M shares and $14.0B a day over twenty days, so a $500M position is 3.6% of a single day's value and no holder is trapped by liquidity. Short interest of 69.35M shares, 2.19% of the float and 2.2 days to cover, means the marginal seller is not fighting a crowded short either. Passive ownership is a flow that follows the index and the price rather than a bid that supports it; Tesla's exact float-adjusted S&P 500 weight is not disclosed in the sources retrieved, and after the top ten names reached 39.03% of the index on 2026-10-10 the marginal index buyer is a shrinking share of demand. [S15, S114]

### No control buyer exists, at any price

A cash takeover is arithmetically out of reach. The pieces themselves are worth $170B on the sum of the parts — vehicles at 1.0x sales, energy at 3.5x, net cash at book — and a control buyer for those assets alone would pay $200-250B with a premium, which is one-eighth of the current capitalisation and therefore not a route to today's price. Alphabet, at $3,493.5B, is the only US company with the balance sheet to write a $1.6T cheque, and it is the closest competitor in autonomous driving, which makes antitrust the binding constraint rather than price. Musk's 19.8% stake and 207.5M pledged shares mean nothing happens without him, and a hostile approach is legally and financially impossible at this size. [S5, S6]

### The one live route is a share exchange with SpaceX

On 2026-10-21 both boards formed special committees to explore a combination, days after Musk called the idea a "good idea" on the third-quarter earnings call. SpaceX listed on 2026-06-12 at $135 a share and a $1.77T valuation, reached $2.1T on its first day, and the combined group would be worth well over $3 trillion. At those marks Tesla holders would own 43% of the equity — but they would exchange one-share-one-vote stock for a company where super-voting shares give Musk about 84% of the vote, against 20% at Tesla. That is the governance price of the only transformative exit available, and it is being negotiated by two boards that have not historically pushed back: Tesla invested $2B in xAI after its chair expressed scepticism, and it rescued SolarCity in 2016. ### What would make the exit valuable, and what stands in the way

The counter-case deserves weight. A negotiated combination would carry a premium to the undisturbed price, and a holder who sells into it captures that premium without waiting for a re-rating; SpaceX's Starlink cash flows are real, so the merged entity would have earnings that Tesla alone does not; and if the ratio is struck on market values, a Tesla holder participates in that cash flow from day one. The risk is that the ratio, not a cash price, is what gets negotiated, and that a controlled board sets it. The 2025 CEO Performance Award reinforces the point: its change-of-control terms let unearned shares vest on market-capitalisation milestones alone, so the controlling shareholder's incentive in a sale is to maximise the headline value, not the terms minority holders receive. [S5, S122]

Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $356, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is the fastest-growing equipment market Tesla sells into, and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,060 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 769 robotaxi vehicles registered in Texas on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S4]

The sell side is almost at the price. The consensus rating is Hold across 48 firms, the average twelve-month target is $408.61, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $42.50 a share, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets, and autonomy at $259B in the base case, which is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. Our base case is already generous to Tesla against the only operator running a scaled driverless service. The gap between the $111 probability-weighted value and the $403.30 price is not a disagreement about cars; it is the price of paying the category leader's multiple for a fleet one-hundredth of its size. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) robotaxi stays regional at $40B of autonomy value and the core is valued at peer multiples, a 73% loss. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $465 mid-point lifts expected value to $253, still 37% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

::: scenarios
| Scenario | Probability | Drivers | Outcome | Signposts | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull | 25% | Robotaxi in several metros at 1.0x Waymo's $126B; energy at 6.0x sales; 1.74M FSD subscriptions | $212 a share, -47% from $403.30; -12.1% a year to 2031 | Robotaxi revenue line disclosed; California driverless permit; Texas fleet above 5,000 vehicles | S6, S120 |
| Base | 50% | Robotaxi stays regional at $40B; core at $42.50; energy at 3.5x sales | $107 a share, -73% | Q4 2026 update with no robotaxi revenue; Texas fleet below 1,000 | S6, S120 |
| Bear | 25% | Autonomy written down; vehicles at GM's 0.39x sales; Terafab commitment; credit-free margin | $19 a share, -95% | Unsupervised FSD slips past 2027; NHTSA recall of the Cybercab; merger vote fails | S6, S120, S137 |
:::

### The assumption that decides the price is the one with the least evidence

| Rank | Assumption | Confidence | What would disprove it | Impact if wrong | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031: 15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile is what the reverse DCF needs | low | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | Registrations flat near 769 vehicles; no fare disclosure; safety-driver hours rising | S4, S6, S137 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | medium | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | Each 100 bp is $756M, 22% of trailing operating income | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% with revenue growth | medium | Q4 margin below 25% once tariff refunds lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | Q3 revenue fell 16% to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | low | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | Terafab's $16.8B first phase sits outside the 2026 budget | S4, S134 |
| 5 | No value-transferring exchange ratio; award dilution held near 12% | low | Ratio struck below market, or new tranches granted | -$40 to -$80 a share | Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers | S5, S135, S138 |

Assumption 1 sets the price and is the least evidenced: no robotaxi revenue, no fare and no cost per mile are disclosed, so the largest component of value rests on a third-party fleet count. Assumptions 2 and 3 decide whether the core is worth $42.50 or $21.75, and management can still influence both in 2027 — the ex-credit operating margin has been cut to 2.2-2.5%, while energy supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M third-quarter gross profit at a margin 2.5 times Fluence's 13.1%. Assumptions 4 and 5 are about survival and dilution rather than growth: $36.18B of net cash covers eighteen months of zero free cash flow, but not that plus a $16.8B capital call whose Tesla share is undisclosed. [S4, S6]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cisco | cautionary | 2000-2024 | Revenue grew from $12.5B to $57B and trailing net income passed its 1999 level by 2003, yet a buyer at the March 2000 peak of $500B waited until 2021 to break even on an adjusted basis. A correct thesis does not rescue the entry multiple. | S140 |
| Amazon | cautionary | 1999-2001 | The business compounded into one of the great franchises, but the stock fell more than 90% and took a decade to recover; the option paid only for the holder who could sit through the drawdown. | S143 |
| GM Cruise | cautionary | 2016-2024 | More than $10B of operating losses and less than $500M of revenue before GM shut the robotaxi unit in December 2024 for $1B a year of savings. Automaker capital is no substitute for paid driverless miles. | S142 |
| Waymo | best | 2024-2026 | The valuation went from $45B in October 2024 to $126B in February 2026 on 500,000 paid driverless rides a week — proof the service can scale, and a mark that Tesla's autonomy value exceeds 11-fold. | S120 |
:::

The four precedents give one decision rule. Cisco and Amazon say that when a genuine technology shift is already in the price, the return is set by the entry multiple and the holder's drawdown tolerance, not by whether the technology wins. Cruise says the base rate for a follower in autonomy is a full write-off, not a slow fade. Waymo says the leader's private mark is the only independent price for the option, and it is $126B — 9% of what the market pays for Tesla's version. A holder should therefore own Tesla's autonomy at a discount to the leader's mark, not at 11.3 times it, and size the position so the Cruise outcome is survivable. [S140, S142]

### Where the case turns, and what to do now

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. At $403.30 it sits in the third zone, with the ten-year Treasury at 4.99% raising the discount rate on post-2030 cash flows. Do not invest new money now. Wait for one of three milestones: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless deployment permit, or special-committee terms at a premium to market rather than at market. If the mandate requires exposure, hold a residual of 0.25-0.5% of net asset value, sized so a failed vote and a 30% drawdown do not breach the risk budget, and vote against any ratio that transfers value to the controlling shareholder. Pass on the blue-sky branch: it needs global robotaxi and humanoid dominance and pays 8% from here. Diligence questions: revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, the share of rides running without a safety driver, and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Confidence is high that the core is not worth $403.30, medium on the autonomy tree, low on the merger. What would change the call: a second consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-credit operating margin, an FSD licensing contract with a named automaker, or a ratio that values Tesla at a premium to its undisturbed price. [S15, S5]
