arguments.markdown:
Tesla's technology is proven where it is a manufacturing problem — dry-electrode cells, Megapack integration — and unproven where the valuation sits, judged against two comparison sets: Waymo in autonomy and BYD in manufacturing cost. Compared with Waymo, Tesla has 2.0 million cumulative autonomous miles against 500,000 paid rides a week; compared with BYD, its 486,532 quarterly deliveries trail BYD's 762,478 electric cars. Its paid driverless permit exists in one state. The technology justifies a premium to a capital-intensive manufacturer in energy and process engineering; it does not yet justify the multiple of a software platform [S6, S76, S107].

### How FSD works, and where it stops

FSD (Supervised) is vision-only: eight cameras feed an end-to-end neural network that outputs steering, acceleration and braking, trained on video from 10.2 million delivered vehicles and run on Tesla's in-house inference silicon. There is no lidar or radar. Two problems stay unsolved. Cameras blinded by rain, fog or low sun are the subject of NHTSA's Engineering Analysis EA26002, opened 2026-03-19 over 13 crashes in 2.88 million vehicles, testing whether the system detects the degradation. The second is the reliability increment that permits removing the supervisor, which is why customer-owned unsupervised driving moved to Q2 2027. Tesla's October 2026 report claims 6,006,200 miles per major collision, a company-computed, non-fault-based figure the regulator has not verified [S58, S80].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| FSD miles per major collision | 6,006,200 (North America, October 2026) | Company report, FSD-engaged miles | S58 |
| Cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles | 2.0 million (to 2026-09-30) | Company quarterly update | S6 |
| FSD subscriptions and attach | 1.74 million; more than 75% of North American deliveries | Company KPI, excludes free trials | S6 |
| 4680 cell output and density | More than 1 million cells/week; more than 40 GWh; 272 Wh/kg | Giga Texas line data and teardown estimates | S56 |
| Megapack segment gross margin | 33.1% (Q3 2026) | Segment accounts | S4 |

### Robotaxi: a real service, on one state's terms

Paid Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03. Tesla has never published a fleet count, so the only dated line is third-party: 769 Teslas registered for autonomous use in Texas on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, after 44 active across seven metros in H1 2026; Tesla claimed 300-plus Cybercabs in Austin on 2026-10-10, and NHTSA's DP26010 (2026-10-09) describes a monitored fleet of 1,000. The registration count is unconfirmed by Tesla or Texas DMV, and Tesla discloses no fares, trips per vehicle, utilisation or insurance cost per mile. Permits remain the constraint: Texas allows self-certified commercial driverless operation, while California lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC for testing with a driver only (2026-10-22) [S73, S74, S82, S107].

| Dimension | Tesla | Benchmark | What it means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Autonomy sensing | Vision-only cameras, no lidar or radar | Waymo: lidar, radar, cameras, high-definition maps | Lower bill of materials, higher bad-weather tail risk | S59 |
| Weekly paid rides | Not disclosed | Waymo: 500,000 a week on about 3,000 vehicles | At 5 miles a ride, 2.5 million rider-only miles weekly — more than Tesla's cumulative total | S107 |
| Cell performance | 4680: 272 Wh/kg, 10-80% in 35-40 minutes | CATL Qilin 3: full charge in six minutes | Tesla leads on cost, trails on density and charging | S56 |
| BEV volume, Q3 2026 | 486,532 units | BYD 762,478 passenger BEVs, +30.89% year over year | Cost leadership has moved to China | S76 |

### Cells: a cost moat, not a performance one

Giga Texas runs above one million 4680 cells a week at more than 40 GWh of installed capacity, and since January 2026 both electrodes use the dry process in production — a step CATL, Panasonic, LG and Samsung SDI have not taken to commercial scale. The economics are real: electrode cost 50% lower at full scale, 41% less line capex and more than 30% less factory energy. The product is not: energy density trails by 10-15%, charging is slower than Panasonic 2170 packs, yields above 90% sit below the 98% of mature producers, and Tesla still buys CATL LFP and Panasonic or LG 2170 cells for Shanghai and Fremont Model Y. Battery availability, not demand, remained the stated limit on 2026 volume [S56].

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why it is hard | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fleet data and training set | 7 | 10.2 million vehicles and billions of FSD miles, if compute and labelling keep pace | 3-4 years | S6 |
| Dry-electrode process | 7 | Both electrodes dry at more than 90% yield; no competitor at commercial scale | 3 years | S56 |
| Vertical integration (cells, packs, chips) | 6 | Process know-how and capital; AI6 foundry dependence caps it | 3-5 years | S6, S79 |
| Driverless permits | 4 | Texas self-certification is easy; California and the EU are not | 1-2 years Texas, 3+ California | S73 |
| **Composite** | **6/10** | A 50-person team needs 3 years for the cell line and 2 for Megapack integration | **3 years of lead time** | S56, S73 |

### Patents: thin disclosure, deliberately

| Patent or application | Title | Jurisdiction | Filed | Granted | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Four international filings published 2026-04-16 | Optimus Gen 3 forearm, wrist, joint and hand assemblies | WIPO/PCT | Priority 2024-10-10 | — | Published, national phase pending | 22 degrees of freedom per hand | S75 |
| US20260310299A1 | Flexible touch sensors for robotic hands | US | Not disclosed | — | Published 2025-10-08 | Tactile sensing for manipulation | S75 |
| Maxwell portfolio (acquired 2019, $235m) | Dry electrode manufacturing IP | US | Pre-2019 | Granted, owned | In force | Underpins the 4680 dry process | S56 |

The 10-K does not present patents as a competitive advantage; it rests the case on data, manufacturing cost and vertical integration, and Musk said in April 2026 that the V3 hand would not use the patented Optimus design.

### Product inventory

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model 3/Y | Commercial | 2017-2020 | $20.09bn automotive sales Q3 2026; 478,237 units (98.3%) | 18.5% total automotive | Next-generation platform, no date | S6, S76 |
| Cybercab and Robotaxi | Early commercial | 2026-09-03, Austin | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Unsupervised customer cars Q2 2027 | S6, S57 |
| Megapack, Megablock | Commercial | 2019; Megapack 3 in 2025 | $2.881bn segment Q3 2026 | 33.1% | Ramp 50 GWh Texas | S4, S6 |
| Optimus | Early production | 2026-10-21 | None disclosed | None disclosed | 20,000 units a week by end-2027, company claim (2026-10-21), unverified | S57 |

### Energy is the proven technology

Megapack is the one line where Tesla holds a genuine integration advantage and prices it: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026 at a 33.1% gross margin, with 50 GWh of Texas capacity starting. The order book is the weak point in the evidence, not the product: the 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified. A contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it; a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. Wood Mackenzie ranks Tesla second among integrators behind Sungrow, and revenue fell 16% to $2.881bn even as volume rose [S4, S6, S72].

::: evidence
**The Optimus target of 20,000 units a week is an unverified company claim, and the humanoid benchmark sits elsewhere.**

On the Q3 2026 call of 2026-10-21 Tesla set the target and began early production, but it discloses no unit count, external customer, task list or revenue. A named customer, supplier orders at that volume or an Optimus revenue line would confirm it; another year of demonstration video and no billed unit would contradict it. Figure AI, valued at $39bn in September 2025, completed an 11-month Figure 02 deployment at BMW's Spartanburg plant contributing to more than 30,000 X3 vehicles, the external validation Optimus has not matched [S57, S149].
:::

### What would change the judgement

The strongest case against my caution is that FSD is already monetised: attach, subscriptions and deferred revenue all rose in Q3 2026. Against it, repeated NHTSA recalls on the 2026 Model Y show launch quality slipping on the highest-volume car, and the attach rate is North American only while China sales fell with FSD approval still pending. Optimus is the thinner half of the autonomy branch: a production line and no external customer.

Diligence questions: what did Austin earn per robotaxi per week, how many Cybercabs ran without a monitor, and what fare, trips per vehicle and insurance cost per mile sit behind that revenue? What is blended pack cost per kWh? Does EA26002 end in a recall, and what would that do to the release date? Until the first two are answered, Tesla owns the best-proven manufacturing technology in the sector and has not proven the one the share price pays for.

Tesla's earnings do not justify its premium, and the cash behind them is thinning. At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 the equity is worth $1,594.1 billion on 3,952.6 million shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, or $1,558.0 billion of enterprise value after $36.2 billion of net cash: 15.0 times trailing revenue of $103,570 million, 104 times adjusted EBITDA of $14,995 million, 450 times operating income and 483 times trailing free cash flow of $3,303 million [S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S15]. Revenue went from $81,462 million in FY2022 to $96,773 million, $97,690 million and $94,827 million, while operating income fell from $13,656 million to $8,891 million, $7,076 million and $4,355 million, cutting the operating margin from 16.8% to 2.6% in nine months of 2026. Gross margin held between 17.9% and 19.0% from FY2023, so the compression is operating expense: R&D rose from $3,969 million in FY2023 to $6,411 million in FY2025 and $7,078 million in nine months of 2026. arguments.markdown:
Tesla offers no cash exit at $1.59 trillion. It has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation, and its entire $45.4B of cash and short-term investments would retire 2.85% of the 3.953B shares outstanding. The largest buyout ever completed — Electronic Arts at $55B in August 2026 — is 3.4% of Tesla's market capitalisation, so no financial sponsor can write this cheque, and no automaker can either: GM and Ford together are $118.4B, 7.4% of Tesla. What remains is a sale into a market that trades $14.0B of Tesla a day, or a share exchange into SpaceX, and both leave the return hostage to a re-rating that five years have not delivered. [S3, S130]

### The company returns nothing, and cannot return much

Tesla's 10-K states that it has never declared or paid a cash dividend, does not anticipate doing so, and purchased no equity securities in fiscal 2025. Trailing free cash flow of $3,303M is a 0.2% yield on the capitalisation, and nine-month capital expenditure of $13,014M runs at 2.1x depreciation: the cash is going into factories, cells and training compute, not to holders. Against GM's 12.4% total shareholder yield and Ford's 5.9%, Tesla's is zero. Even a maximal buyback using the whole cash pile would move the share count by less than three points, and it would leave a company spending $17B a year on capital projects with no liquidity buffer. Capital return is a governance choice, and the controlling shareholder has consistently chosen reinvestment. [S6]

### The exit that always works is the tape

The secondary market is the only channel that is always open. Tesla trades 36.96M shares and $14.0B a day over twenty days, so a $500M position is 3.6% of a single day's value and no holder is trapped by liquidity. Short interest of 69.35M shares, 2.19% of the float and 2.2 days to cover, means the marginal seller is not fighting a crowded short either. Passive ownership is a flow that follows the index and the price rather than a bid that supports it; Tesla's exact float-adjusted S&P 500 weight is not disclosed in the sources retrieved, and after the top ten names reached 39.03% of the index on 2026-10-10 the marginal index buyer is a shrinking share of demand. [S15, S114]

### No control buyer exists, at any price

A cash takeover is arithmetically out of reach. The pieces themselves are worth $170B on the sum of the parts — vehicles at 1.0x sales, energy at 3.5x, net cash at book — and a control buyer for those assets alone would pay $200-250B with a premium, which is one-eighth of the current capitalisation and therefore not a route to today's price. Alphabet, at $3,493.5B, is the only US company with the balance sheet to write a $1.6T cheque, and it is the closest competitor in autonomous driving, which makes antitrust the binding constraint rather than price. Musk's 19.8% stake and 207.5M pledged shares mean nothing happens without him, and a hostile approach is legally and financially impossible at this size. [S5, S6]

| Share exchange with SpaceX | SpaceX (NasdaqGS: SPCX) | Musk-sponsored combination; special committees formed 2026-10-20 | 2027-2028 | Medium | S129, S128 |

| Acquisition by a platform company | Alphabet | $3,493.5B market cap, but antitrust in autonomy | None | Very low | S113 |
| Buyback or dividend | Tesla | No programme; no dividend ever declared | None | Very low | S3 |

### The one live route is a share exchange with SpaceX

On 2026-10-21 both boards formed special committees to explore a combination, days after Musk called the idea a "good idea" on the third-quarter earnings call. SpaceX listed on 2026-06-12 at $135 a share and a $1.77T valuation, reached $2.1T on its first day, and the combined group would be worth well over $3 trillion. At those marks Tesla holders would own 43% of the equity — but they would exchange one-share-one-vote stock for a company where super-voting shares give Musk about 84% of the vote, against 20% at Tesla. That is the governance price of the only transformative exit available, and it is being negotiated by two boards that have not historically pushed back: Tesla invested $2B in xAI after its chair expressed scepticism, and it rescued SolarCity in 2016. ### What would make the exit valuable, and what stands in the way

The counter-case deserves weight. A negotiated combination would carry a premium to the undisturbed price, and a holder who sells into it captures that premium without waiting for a re-rating; SpaceX's Starlink cash flows are real, so the merged entity would have earnings that Tesla alone does not; and if the ratio is struck on market values, a Tesla holder participates in that cash flow from day one. The 2025 CEO Performance Award reinforces the point: its change-of-control terms let unearned shares vest on market-capitalisation milestones alone, so the controlling shareholder's incentive in a sale is to maximise the headline value, not the terms minority holders receive. [S5, S132]

Confidence is high that no cash exit exists and medium on the merger: the talks are exploratory and no ratio, premium or timetable has been disclosed. arguments.markdown:
Tesla's technology is proven where it is a manufacturing problem — dry-electrode cells, Megapack integration — and unproven where the valuation sits, judged against two comparison sets: Waymo in autonomy and BYD in manufacturing cost. Compared with Waymo, Tesla has 2.0 million cumulative autonomous miles against 500,000 paid rides a week; compared with BYD, its 486,532 quarterly deliveries trail BYD's 762,478 electric cars. Its paid driverless permit exists in one state. The technology justifies a premium to a capital-intensive manufacturer in energy and process engineering; it does not yet justify the multiple of a software platform [S6, S76, S107].

### How FSD works, and where it stops

FSD (Supervised) is vision-only: eight cameras feed an end-to-end neural network that outputs steering, acceleration and braking, trained on video from 10.2 million delivered vehicles and run on in-house inference silicon. There is no lidar or radar. Two problems stay unsolved. Cameras blinded by rain, fog or low sun are the subject of NHTSA's Engineering Analysis EA26002, opened 2026-03-19 over 13 crashes in 2.88 million vehicles, testing whether the system detects the degradation. The second is the reliability increment that permits removing the supervisor, which is why customer-owned unsupervised driving moved to Q2 2027. Tesla's October 2026 report claims 6,006,200 miles per major collision, a company-computed, non-fault-based figure the regulator has not verified [S58, S80].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| FSD miles per major collision | 6,006,200 (North America, October 2026) | Company report, FSD-engaged miles | S58 |
| Cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles | 2.0 million (to 2026-09-30) | Company quarterly update | S6 |
| FSD subscriptions and attach | 1.74 million; more than 75% of North American deliveries | Company KPI, excludes free trials | S6 |
| 4680 cell output and density | More than 1 million cells/week; more than 40 GWh; 272 Wh/kg | Giga Texas line data and teardown estimates | S56 |

### Robotaxi: a real service, on one state's terms

Paid Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03. Tesla publishes no fleet count, so the only dated line is third-party: 769 Teslas registered for autonomous use in Texas on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, after 44 active across seven metros in H1 2026; Tesla claimed 300-plus Cybercabs in Austin on 2026-10-10, and NHTSA's DP26010 (2026-10-09) describes a monitored fleet of 1,000. The count is unconfirmed by Tesla or Texas DMV, which disclose no fares, trips per vehicle, utilisation or insurance cost per mile. Permits remain the constraint: Texas allows self-certified commercial driverless operation, while California lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC for testing with a driver only (2026-10-22) [S73, S74, S82, S107].

| Dimension | Tesla | Benchmark | What it means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weekly paid rides | Not disclosed | Waymo: 500,000 a week on about 3,000 vehicles | At 5 miles a ride, 2.5 million rider-only miles weekly — more than Tesla's cumulative total | S107 |
| Cell performance | 4680: 272 Wh/kg, 10-80% in 35-40 minutes | CATL Qilin 3: full charge in six minutes | Tesla leads on cost, trails on density and charging | S56 |
| BEV volume, Q3 2026 | 486,532 units | BYD 762,478 passenger BEVs, +30.89% year over year | Cost leadership has moved to China | S76 |

### Cells: a cost moat, not a performance one

Giga Texas runs above one million 4680 cells a week at more than 40 GWh of installed capacity, and since January 2026 both electrodes use the dry process in production — a step CATL, Panasonic, LG and Samsung SDI have not taken to commercial scale. The economics are real: electrode cost 50% lower at full scale, 41% less line capex and more than 30% less factory energy. The product is not: energy density trails by 10-15%, charging is slower than Panasonic 2170 packs, yields above 90% sit below the 98% of mature producers, and Tesla still buys CATL LFP and Panasonic or LG 2170 cells for Shanghai and Fremont Model Y. Battery availability, not demand, remained the stated limit on 2026 volume [S56].

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fleet data and training set | 7 | 10.2 million vehicles and billions of FSD miles | 3-4 years | S6 |

| Driverless permits | 4 | Texas self-certification is easy; California and the EU are not | 1-2 years Texas, 3+ California | S73 |
| **Composite** | **6/10** | 3 years for the cell line, 2 for Megapack integration | **3 years of lead time** | S56, S73 |

### Patents: thin disclosure, deliberately

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Four PCT filings, published 2026-04-16 | Optimus Gen 3 forearm, wrist, joint and hand assemblies | WIPO/PCT | Priority 2024-10-10 | — | Published, national phase pending | 22 degrees of freedom per hand | S75 |
| US20260310299A1 | Flexible touch sensors for robotic hands | US | Not disclosed | — | Published 2025-10-08 | Tactile sensing | S75 |
| Maxwell portfolio (acquired 2019, $235m) | Dry electrode manufacturing IP | US | Pre-2019 | Granted, owned | In force | Underpins the 4680 dry process | S56 |

The 10-K rests the case on data, manufacturing cost and vertical integration, not patents; Musk said in April 2026 that the V3 hand would not use the patented Optimus design.

### Product inventory

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model 3/Y | Commercial | 2017-2020 | $20.09bn automotive sales Q3 2026; 478,237 units (98.3%) | 18.5% total automotive | Next-generation platform, no date | S6, S76 |
| Cybercab and Robotaxi | Early commercial | 2026-09-03, Austin | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Unsupervised customer cars Q2 2027 | S6, S57 |
| Megapack, Megablock | Commercial | 2019; Megapack 3 in 2025 | $2.881bn segment Q3 2026 | 33.1% | Ramp 50 GWh Texas | S4, S6 |
| Optimus | Early production | 2026-10-21 | None disclosed | None disclosed | 20,000 units a week by end-2027, company claim (2026-10-21), unverified | S57 |

### Energy is the proven technology

Megapack is the one line where Tesla holds a genuine integration advantage and prices it: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026 at a 33.1% gross margin, with 50 GWh of Texas capacity starting. The weak point is the order book, not the product: the 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified. A contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it; a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. Wood Mackenzie ranks Tesla second among integrators behind Sungrow, and revenue fell 16% to $2.881bn even as volume rose [S4, S6, S72].

::: evidence
**The Optimus target of 20,000 units a week is an unverified company claim, and the humanoid benchmark sits elsewhere.**

On the Q3 2026 call of 2026-10-21 Tesla set the target and began early production, but it discloses no unit count, external customer, task list or revenue. A named customer, supplier orders at that volume or an Optimus revenue line would confirm it; another year of demonstration video and no billed unit would contradict it. Figure AI, valued at $39bn in September 2025, completed an 11-month Figure 02 deployment at BMW's Spartanburg plant contributing to more than 30,000 X3 vehicles, the external validation Optimus has not matched [S57, S149].
:::

### What would change the judgement

The strongest counter-case is that FSD is already monetised: attach, subscriptions and deferred revenue rose in Q3 2026. Against it, repeated NHTSA recalls on the 2026 Model Y show launch quality slipping, and the attach rate is North American only while China sales fell with FSD approval pending. Optimus is the thinner half of the autonomy branch: a production line and no external customer.

Diligence questions: what did Austin earn per robotaxi per week, how many Cybercabs ran without a monitor, and what fare, trips per vehicle and insurance cost per mile sit behind that revenue? What is blended pack cost per kWh? Does EA26002 end in a recall, and what would that do to the release date? Until the first two are answered, Tesla owns the best-proven manufacturing technology in the sector and has not proven the one the share price pays for.

arguments.markdown:
Tesla still makes most of its gross profit selling cars, but after regulatory credits the car business earns little at the operating line. Credits supplied 45.8% of FY2025 operating income and 15.7% in Q3 2026; incremental profit now comes from a 33.1%-margin energy-storage business and a 15.9%-margin services business while AI spending absorbs 86.9% of gross profit. Nine-month 2026 revenue of $78,669 million split into automotive $57,310 million (including $639 million of credits), energy $8,428 million and services $12,931 million, against an automotive share of 85.1% in FY2023. Q3 2026 gross profit divided $3,806 million automotive (69%), $954 million energy (17%) and $734 million services (13%), versus 91%/6%/3% in FY2023. Cash arrives when a vehicle changes hands, on storage milestones and prepayments ($3.30 billion of customer prepayments in deferred revenue at 2026-09-30, from $2.04 billion), and monthly for Supercharging, insurance and FSD [S3, S4, S6].

| Segment | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M 2026 | Q3 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue excluding credits ($M) | 80,629 | 74,307 | 67,533 | 56,671 | 20,447 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Automotive regulatory credits ($M) | 1,790 | 2,763 | 1,993 | 639 | 113 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Energy generation and storage revenue ($M) | 6,035 | 10,086 | 12,771 | 8,428 | 2,881 | S3, S4 |
| Services and other revenue ($M) | 8,319 | 10,534 | 12,530 | 12,931 | 4,605 | S3, S4 |
| Automotive gross margin excluding credits | 17.7% | 15.4% | 15.4% | 17.7% | 18.1% | S1, S3, S4, S63 |
| Energy gross margin | 18.9% | 26.2% | 29.8% | 30.2% | 33.1% | S3, S4 |

The credit franchise is ending. Tesla booked $2,763 million of automotive regulatory credits in FY2024, $1,993 million in FY2025 and $639 million in 9M 2026; Q3 2026 alone was $113 million, down 73% from $417 million. Credits carry no cost of revenue, so a credit dollar is nearly a dollar of operating profit: 20.1% of operating income in FY2023, 39.0% in FY2024, 45.8% in FY2025, 31.1% in 9M 2026 and 15.7% in Q3 2026. An implied Q4 2025 figure of $542 million shows the collapse came with the removal of the compliance obligation in 2026, not the lapse of the consumer credit: the Department of Transportation finalised its CAFE rollback on 2026-10-01, ending the requirement that made legacy automakers buy zero-emission credits. Without credits, FY2025's 4.6% operating margin is 2.5% and Q3 2026's 2.6% is 2.2% [S4, S64, S66].

Per vehicle the business improved even as credits disappeared. Q3 2026 automotive revenue per delivery excluding credits was $42,026, up 0.5%, while automotive cost of revenue per delivery (automotive cost of revenue divided by deliveries) fell 2.7% to $34,436, so gross profit per vehicle rose 18.0% to $7,591 (18.1% margin) from $6,433 (15.4%). The gain is cost and mix, not price: management attributes the 270 basis points to a higher Asia-Pacific mix from the low-cost Shanghai plant. Tesla does not disclose customer acquisition cost; SG&A per delivery of $4,142 carries corporate and non-vehicle cost, and the first vehicle's gross profit covers it 1.8 times. A three-year LTV estimate of $8,455 adds three years of services gross profit per vehicle ($288 a year on 10.2 million deliveries), giving LTV:CAC of 2.0:1 and payback inside the delivery quarter. Tesla is the only one of the three with positive per-vehicle gross profit after credits: BYD's automotive gross margin was 20.49% in FY2025, from 22.31%, and Rivian's automotive gross profit was a $(36) million loss in Q2 2026 [S63, S65, S68].

| Per unit | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 | Change | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deliveries (units) | 497,099 | 486,532 | -2.1% | S6 |
| Automotive revenue per delivery, excluding credits | $41,818 | $42,026 | +0.5% | S4, S6 |
| Automotive cost of revenue per delivery | $35,385 | $34,436 | -2.7% | S4, S6 |
| Automotive gross profit per delivery, excluding credits | $6,433 | $7,591 | +18.0% | S4, S6 |
| Energy gross profit per delivery | $2,158 | $1,961 | -9.1% | S4, S6 |
| Services gross profit per delivery | $736 | $1,508 | +105% | S4, S6 |
| SG&A per delivery (acquisition-cost upper bound) | $3,142 | $4,142 | +31.8% | S4, S6 |
| R&D per delivery | $3,279 | $5,675 | +73.1% | S4, S6 |
| Operating profit per delivery | $3,267 | $1,476 | -54.8% | S4, S6 |

| Product | Pricing metric | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 | Peer benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles, net of credits | realised revenue per delivery | $41,818 | $42,026 | BYD automotive gross margin 20.49%, FY2025 | S4, S65 |
| Megapack and Powerwall | realised revenue per GWh deployed | $273 million | $210 million | Fluence gross margin 13.1%, FY2025 | S3, S67 |

Energy is the highest-margin dollar of growth. Storage revenue per GWh fell 23% to $210 million from $273 million, but gross profit per GWh fell only 19% to $69.6 million because cost per GWh fell 25% to $141 million, lifting segment margin to 33.1% from 31.4%. The mechanism is cell integration: the first Megapacks built with Tesla's own Nevada LFP cells shipped in Q3 2026, Megafactory Texas began production with 50 GWh, and the Megapack backlog is nearly sold out through 2027. Fluence earned 13.1% in FY2025; Tesla's advantage is owning the cell, not pricing. Part of the 33.1% is not repeatable: management attributed it partly to tariff refunds and cell-related warranty reimbursements. Services is the quieter engine: revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million on 2% fewer deliveries and gross margin reached 15.9% from 10.5%. Each extra $1 billion of energy revenue at 30% adds $300 million of gross profit; the same dollar of automotive revenue at 18% adds $180 million. FSD and software grow but remain too small to see in the income statement: active subscriptions rose to 1.74 million from 1.04 million, deferred revenue for FSD, connectivity and software was $4.08 billion against $3.87 billion at 2025-12-31, and obligations beyond one year were $10.73 billion, of which $4.80 billion falls due within twelve months. Management's claim that FSD is attached to more than 75% of North American deliveries is company-reported and cannot be tied to a revenue line, because Tesla does not disclose FSD revenue; the observable is $2,345 of deferred balance per active subscription, a stock rather than a price [S67, S4].

The newest change in money flows is who owns the asset. Selling a car converts inventory into revenue once; a robotaxi fleet keeps the vehicle on Tesla's balance sheet and earns per mile, shifting the model from a hardware sale to a utilisation business paid on miles and uptime rather than deliveries. The Cybercab entered Tesla's own Austin fleet on 2026-09-03, but no fare revenue, fleet size or per-mile economics are disclosed, so the model cannot yet be tested. Until then the investable model remains the one in the tables: cars, storage and services.

Counter-case: gross margin improves while the company gets less profitable. Operating expenses of $4,776 million rose 39% against $5,494 million of gross profit, R&D alone rose 69% to $2,761 million, and depreciation rose 17% to $1,580 million and will accelerate as more than $20 billion of 2026 capital expenditure is commissioned. The warranty reserve rose 26% to $10,138 million on 2% fewer deliveries, with claims incurred up 29% to $1,614 million while the provision per delivery fell to $1,227 from $1,463. Inventory rose 13.7% to $14,092 million, with 11 days of vehicle supply. The vehicle line covers its own costs, so break-even is the cost base: $4,776 million of operating expenses needs $27.0 billion of revenue at a 17.7% blended margin; Q3 2026 delivered $28.0 billion for $718 million of operating profit. Normalise energy to a 30% margin and take credits to zero and the quarter earns $515 million, a 1.8% operating margin. For a position, that argues for sizing on the energy and services annuity, with rising margins and a 2027 backlog, and treating autonomy as an option rather than earnings, because at a 1.8% margin the vehicle franchise cannot carry the cost base alone. Confidence is high on the segment arithmetic and medium on how much of the 2026 cost relief is structural rather than tariff and mix. Four diligence questions remain: what is the North American automotive margin excluding credits? What is the energy margin excluding tariff refunds, and at what price is the 2027 backlog contracted? Will Tesla disclose FSD revenue and robotaxi recognition? When do R&D and capital expenditure stop rising as a share of revenue? [S4, S6]

::: evidence
**Tesla's profit now rests on energy and services gross profit, not on credits or on the car**

Energy storage and services supplied $1,688 million of Q3 2026 gross profit at 33.1% and 15.9% margins, while regulatory credits fell to $113 million, 15.7% of operating income, from 45.8% of FY2025 operating income, and operating expenses absorbed 86.9% of gross profit [S4, S6].
:::

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's technology is proven where it is a manufacturing problem — dry-electrode cells, Megapack integration — and unproven where the valuation sits, judged against two comparison sets: Waymo in autonomy and BYD in manufacturing cost. Compared with Waymo, Tesla has 2.0 million cumulative autonomous miles against 500,000 paid rides a week; compared with BYD, its 486,532 quarterly deliveries trail BYD's 762,478 electric cars. Its paid driverless permit exists in one state. The technology justifies a premium to a capital-intensive manufacturer in energy and process engineering; it does not yet justify the multiple of a software platform [S6, S76, S107].

### How FSD works, and where it stops

FSD (Supervised) is vision-only: eight cameras feed an end-to-end neural network that outputs steering, acceleration and braking, trained on video from 10.2 million delivered vehicles and run on in-house inference silicon. There is no lidar or radar. Two problems stay unsolved. Cameras blinded by rain, fog or low sun are the subject of NHTSA's Engineering Analysis EA26002, opened 2026-03-19 over 13 crashes in 2.88 million vehicles, testing whether the system detects the degradation. The second is the reliability increment that permits removing the supervisor, which is why customer-owned unsupervised driving moved to Q2 2027. Tesla's October 2026 report claims 6,006,200 miles per major collision, a company-computed, non-fault-based figure the regulator has not verified [S58, S80].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| FSD miles per major collision | 6,006,200 (North America, October 2026) | Company report, FSD-engaged miles | S58 |
| Cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles | 2.0 million (to 2026-09-30) | Company quarterly update | S6 |
| FSD subscriptions and attach | 1.74 million; more than 75% of North American deliveries | Company KPI, excludes free trials | S6 |
| 4680 cell output and density | More than 1 million cells/week; more than 40 GWh; 272 Wh/kg | Giga Texas line data and teardown estimates | S56 |

### Robotaxi: a real service, on one state's terms

Paid Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03. Tesla publishes no fleet count, so the only dated line is third-party: 769 Teslas registered for autonomous use in Texas on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, after 44 active across seven metros in H1 2026; Tesla claimed 300-plus Cybercabs in Austin on 2026-10-10, and NHTSA's DP26010 (2026-10-09) describes a monitored fleet of 1,000. The count is unconfirmed by Tesla or Texas DMV, which disclose no fares, trips per vehicle, utilisation or insurance cost per mile. Permits remain the constraint: Texas allows self-certified commercial driverless operation, while California lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC for testing with a driver only (2026-10-22) [S73, S74, S82, S107].

| Dimension | Tesla | Benchmark | What it means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weekly paid rides | Not disclosed | Waymo: 500,000 a week on about 3,000 vehicles | At 5 miles a ride, 2.5 million rider-only miles weekly — more than Tesla's cumulative total | S107 |
| Cell performance | 4680: 272 Wh/kg, 10-80% in 35-40 minutes | CATL Qilin 3: full charge in six minutes | Tesla leads on cost, trails on density and charging | S56 |
| BEV volume, Q3 2026 | 486,532 units | BYD 762,478 passenger BEVs, +30.89% year over year | Cost leadership has moved to China | S76 |

### Cells: a cost moat, not a performance one

Giga Texas runs above one million 4680 cells a week at more than 40 GWh of installed capacity, and since January 2026 both electrodes use the dry process in production — a step CATL, Panasonic, LG and Samsung SDI have not taken to commercial scale. The economics are real: electrode cost 50% lower at full scale, 41% less line capex and more than 30% less factory energy. The product is not: energy density trails by 10-15%, charging is slower than Panasonic 2170 packs, yields above 90% sit below the 98% of mature producers, and Tesla still buys CATL LFP and Panasonic or LG 2170 cells for Shanghai and Fremont Model Y. Battery availability, not demand, remained the stated limit on 2026 volume [S56].

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why it is hard | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fleet data and training set | 7 | 10.2 million vehicles and billions of FSD miles | 3-4 years | S6 |
| Dry-electrode process | 7 | Both electrodes dry above 90% yield; no rival at scale | 3 years | S56 |
| Vertical integration (cells, packs, chips) | 6 | Process know-how and capital; AI6 foundry dependence caps it | 3-5 years | S6, S79 |
| Driverless permits | 4 | Texas self-certification is easy; California and the EU are not | 1-2 years Texas, 3+ California | S73 |
| **Composite** | **6/10** | 3 years for the cell line, 2 for Megapack integration | **3 years of lead time** | S56, S73 |

### Patents: thin disclosure, deliberately

| Patent or application | Title | Jurisdiction | Filed | Granted | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Four PCT filings, published 2026-04-16 | Optimus Gen 3 forearm, wrist, joint and hand assemblies | WIPO/PCT | Priority 2024-10-10 | — | Published, national phase pending | 22 degrees of freedom per hand | S75 |
| US20260310299A1 | Flexible touch sensors for robotic hands | US | Not disclosed | — | Published 2025-10-08 | Tactile sensing | S75 |
| Maxwell portfolio (acquired 2019, $235m) | Dry electrode manufacturing IP | US | Pre-2019 | Granted, owned | In force | Underpins the 4680 dry process | S56 |

The 10-K rests the case on data, manufacturing cost and vertical integration, not patents; Musk said in April 2026 that the V3 hand would not use the patented Optimus design.

### Product inventory

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model 3/Y | Commercial | 2017-2020 | $20.09bn automotive sales Q3 2026; 478,237 units (98.3%) | 18.5% total automotive | Next-generation platform, no date | S6, S76 |
| Cybercab and Robotaxi | Early commercial | 2026-09-03, Austin | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Unsupervised customer cars Q2 2027 | S6, S57 |
| Megapack, Megablock | Commercial | 2019; Megapack 3 in 2025 | $2.881bn segment Q3 2026 | 33.1% | Ramp 50 GWh Texas | S4, S6 |
| Optimus | Early production | 2026-10-21 | None disclosed | None disclosed | 20,000 units a week by end-2027, company claim (2026-10-21), unverified | S57 |

### Energy is the proven technology

Megapack is the one line where Tesla holds a genuine integration advantage and prices it: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026 at a 33.1% gross margin, with 50 GWh of Texas capacity starting. The weak point is the order book, not the product: the 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified. A contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it; a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. Wood Mackenzie ranks Tesla second among integrators behind Sungrow, and revenue fell 16% to $2.881bn even as volume rose [S4, S6, S72].

::: evidence
**The Optimus output target is an unverified company claim, and the humanoid benchmark sits elsewhere.**

On the Q3 2026 call of 2026-10-21 Tesla set a target of 20,000 Optimus units a week by end-2027 and began early production, but it discloses no unit count, external customer, task list or revenue. A named customer, supplier orders at that volume or an Optimus revenue line would confirm it; another year of demonstration video and no billed unit would contradict it. Figure AI, valued at $39bn in September 2025, completed an 11-month Figure 02 deployment at BMW's Spartanburg plant contributing to more than 30,000 X3 vehicles, the external validation Optimus has not matched [S57, S149].
:::

### What would change the judgement

The strongest counter-case is that FSD is already monetised: attach, subscriptions and deferred revenue rose in Q3 2026. Against it, repeated NHTSA recalls on the 2026 Model Y show launch quality slipping, and the attach rate is North American only while China sales fell with FSD approval pending. Optimus is the thinner half of the autonomy branch: a production line and no external customer.

Diligence questions: what did Austin earn per robotaxi per week, how many Cybercabs ran without a monitor, and what fare, trips per vehicle and insurance cost per mile sit behind that revenue? What is blended pack cost per kWh? Does EA26002 end in a recall, and what would that do to the release date? Until the first two are answered, Tesla owns the best-proven manufacturing technology in the sector and has not proven the one the share price pays for.

At $403.30 (NasdaqGS, 2026-10-29 20:00 UTC) Tesla's equity is worth $1,594.1B and its enterprise value $1,558.0B. On a sum of the parts, 89% of that price — $1,424B, or $361 a share — buys autonomy and robotics, while the automotive, energy and services businesses plus $36.2B of net cash are worth $42.50 a share at peer multiples. That residual is 11.3 times the $126B at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026, and Waymo is the only operator running a scaled driverless service. My probability-weighted value is $111 a share, 72.5% below the close; the disagreement is not about cars, since my $42.50 for the core sits within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47, but about whether 2.0M cumulative unsupervised miles, a robotaxi service confined to one city and zero disclosed Optimus revenue can carry $1.4 trillion. [S15, S120, S6]

### A five-year flat line and a violent quarter

The price has gone nowhere over five years and has lagged the index; the last quarter reversed part of that lag, a window that contains the 2026-10-21 results and the merger remarks Musk made on the same call.

| Measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Price | $403.30, NasdaqGS, USD, 2026-10-29 20:00 UTC | S15 |
| Market capitalisation | $1,594.1B on 3,952.6M shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 | S15, S5 |
| Enterprise value | $1,558.0B, after $36.2B of net cash | S15, S6 |
| 52-week range | $297.38-$498.83; the price is 53% of the way up | S15 |
| Return 1m / 3m / 12m | +14.3% / +30.6% / -8.4% | S15 |
| Twelve months vs S&P 500 | -21.5 pp (S&P 500 +13.2%) | S15, S22 |
| Return over five years | +0.1% ($402.86 on 2021-11-01 to $403.30) | S15 |
| Year to date | -11.3% (from the 2025-12-31 close of $454.43) | S15, S3 |
| Turnover | 36.96M shares and $14.0B a day, 20-day average | S15 |

### 443 times trailing earnings; the peer median is 18.5 times

On trailing figures Tesla trades at 443.2x earnings, 15.0x sales and 170.5x EBITDA, and 104x the company's own $15.0B adjusted EBITDA. The median of the six peers below is 18.5x trailing earnings — across the three with a positive P/E, Alphabet 14.2x, BYD 18.5x and GM 18.8x — and 2.4x EV/sales across Rivian, Lucid and Alphabet; Ford, Rivian and Lucid have no trailing earnings multiple. On that median, 2027 consensus EPS of $2.20 is worth $40.70 a share, so the price is 9.9 times it. Consensus that already assumes a robotaxi ramp barely normalises the multiple: 2026 revenue of $108.5B and EPS of $1.67 give 241x; 2027 revenue of $123.9B and EPS of $2.20 give 183x. Tesla's own five year-end P/Es were 72.8x (2021), 34.0x (2022), 57.8x (2023), 204.6x (2024) and 420.8x (2025): today is above all of them. [S115, S17, S15]

### Sum of the parts: $42.50 of business, and a bear case of $19

Trailing-twelve-month segment data from the Q3 2026 update: automotive revenue $75.0B at a 19.1% gross margin, energy $12.3B at 29.7%, services $16.3B at 12.4%, sharing $16.5B of operating expense. At 1.0x sales for vehicles and services — 2.5x GM's implied 0.39x, warranted by double GM's gross margin — 3.5x for energy (above Fluence's 0.5x) and net cash at book, the core is $170B, or $42.50 a share on 4.00B shares. That count carries 710M unvested restricted shares (18%) from the two CEO awards, so on the 3,240M basic count today's equity is $1,307B, not $1,594B. The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B at Waymo's licensing value, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B global dominance — $65 a share. The bear case is the same arithmetic with each input cut: autonomy, FSD and Optimus at zero; vehicles at 0.39x automotive revenue, a 10% discount to GM's 0.43x on $72.3B of market capitalisation over $169.8B of revenue, giving $29.3B on $75.0B; energy at 1.5x its $12.3B, or $18.4B, less than half the base multiple; and net cash cut to $28B from $36.2B after a year of capital spending and recall costs. That sum is $75.6B, $18.91 a share. Adding $259B of autonomy to the $170B core gives $429B, $107; the core with $600B gives $847B, $212. ### The reverse DCF needs sixteen million robotaxis

At a 10% WACC and 3% terminal growth, on $2.0B of 2027 free cash flow growing 45% a year, today's enterprise value requires $141B of 2031 free cash flow (9% WACC: $118B; 11%: $164B). At a 15% margin that is $940B of 2031 revenue, nine times trailing. At a 25% robotaxi margin it implies $564B of robotaxi revenue: at $0.60 a mile and 60,000 miles a vehicle a year, 15.7M robotaxis — 7.8M if cars and energy supply half the cash flow. At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 Tesla is a $1,594.1B equity in which $42.50 a share, $170B, is the vehicle, energy, services and net-cash business and $356 a share, $1,424B, is autonomy and robotics; on 25/50/25 of $212/$107/$19 the probability-weighted value is $111, so the share is a reduce and new money is an option purchase. The stress work does not move that number, it tests it: a market 50% smaller, customer acquisition cost doubled, revenue 30% lower, financing six months late, multiples at the 16.5x peer median and free cash flow 30% lower — none reverses the conclusion. What does is an exchange ratio at a premium, a board decision rather than an operating one, and the one risk the recommendation must price. The three premises carrying the $1,424B are deteriorating at once: NHTSA's Cybercab self-certification inquiry closes for comment on 2026-10-30, the special committees formed on 2026-10-20 have no terms, and nine-month free cash flow of $1,883M contains $7,332M from stretching payables to 75.3 days. [S6, S15, S120, S4]

### The core is not harsh at 1.0x sales; it is generous

The sum of the parts pays $91B for vehicles and services at 1.0x sales, $43B for energy at 3.5x and $36B of net cash at book. At GM's implied 0.39x, vehicles and services are worth $29B and the core is $87B, $21.75 a share, with autonomy at 95% of the price; a control buyer for the pieces tops out at $200-250B, $50-62.50, where autonomy still holds 84%. Energy's multiple has support — a 29.7% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% — but doubling revenue to $25B on 5.0x adds $82B, $20 a share, and FSD's 1.74M subscribers at $1,200 a year on an 80% margin and 25x add $42B, $10.5, leaving the best honest core near $70 and autonomy at 83%. The $1,424B premium is 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, for 769 Texas-registered vehicles against 3,000. No strategic buyer can close the gap: GM and Ford together are worth $118.4B, and Alphabet, the only credible cheque, is the competitor antitrust review would stop. [S6, S131, S120, S15]

### The scenario tree is generous at the base and shallow in the bear

The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% x $40B regional, 40% x $126B at Waymo parity, 20% x $600B at scale, 5% x $1,500B at dominance — and $259B is 1.0x Waymo for 769 vehicles, 349 of them Cybercabs, that reported nine crashes in August 2026 and disclose no revenue per mile. On the regional branch alone the base is $52.50 and the probability-weighted value $84, still 79% below the close. The 40% probability I attach to unsupervised customer FSD within 2027 and 40% for a merger within a year sit above the record: EA26002 covers 2.88M vehicles, DP26010 opened on 2026-10-09, and no cross-company vote of this kind has passed. The $35 bear was too shallow: at $19 — autonomy at zero, vehicles at 0.39x, energy at 1.5x, net cash $29B after a Terafab call — the drawdown is 95% and the weighted value falls only from $115 to $111. Above $437 the path I had missed is a 10-15% ratio premium in a $3.60T combination, paying $443-487 without one driverless mile. [S120, S137, S6, S5]

### Cash carries a two-year slip, not a slip plus a revenue fall

Net cash of $36.18B and $30B of facilities signed in September 2026 carry a two-year autonomy slip at zero free cash flow without issuing a share. The combination does not survive a revenue fall: at a 19% gross margin, revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B of gross profit against $19.1B of annual operating expense, taking operating cash flow to zero or minus $2B, and with $20-25B of capital expenditure the annual burn is $20-27B, exhausting cash and facilities before 2029. Doubling customer acquisition cost takes SG&A per delivery from $4,142 to $8,284, adds $8.1B and turns $2.9B of operating income into minus $5.2B. Reported cash flow already borrows from suppliers: payables and accruals added $7,332M and days payable rose from 62.8 to 75.3, worth $2.9B, so normalised free cash flow is minus $1.0B, while inventory rose 13.7% on deliveries down 2% and warranty provisions rose 26%. Terafab adds a commitment Tesla does not control: a $16.8B first phase joint with SpaceX, Tesla's share undisclosed, outside the ">$20B" 2026 capital budget and described in SpaceX's IPO filing as a "general framework" with no binding commitment — which caps the near-term cash risk and demolishes the strategic-asset defence. Tesla is Baa3 against SpaceX at Baa1, and the September facilities' pricing is undisclosed. [S4, S134, S138, S147]

### The merger is an option, not a floor

On 2026-10-20 Musk said both boards had formed special committees, that no terms were agreed and none assured; the Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares, not of those cast, so abstentions count against, and the 2026-10-19 proxy sets the 2026-12-03 annual meeting with no merger proposal. At market the deal is value-neutral: $1,594.1B plus SpaceX's $2.01T is $3.60T, and Tesla holders taking 43-44% own exactly today's price; any premium must be conceded by SpaceX, the larger, higher-rated party. Either way Tesla holders get 43% of the economics and a shareholder with 84% of the votes. The 2025 award writes the incentive down: on a change of control operational milestones lapse and market-cap milestones vest, 423.7M shares are 10.7% dilution, the first $2.0T milestone sits 25% above today's capitalisation at 35.3M shares a tranche, against a $9.74B probable charge and $105.82-120.37B unrecognised. Musk has pledged 207.5M shares, 5.2% of the count; three of nine directors are SpaceX-linked, the committee uses two of them, and the xAI stake became SpaceX shares on 2026-02-02 without a shareholder vote. [S5, S135, S138]

### Policy is a $5.60 option; competition is a terminal-value risk

Twenty-five state attorneys general and 12 cities and counties sued on 2026-03-19 in the D.C. Circuit over EPA's 2026-02-12 repeal of the 2009 endangerment finding, consolidated on 2026-05-20; a reversal restores the credit pool, but $1.5B of credits at 15x is $22.5B, $5.6 a share, against Q3 credit revenue of $113M, down 73%, and credits at 45.8% of FY2025 operating income. Policy is a small option and the base case gives it nothing. Competition is different in kind: BYD holds 2.4% of the European market, level with Tesla, at EUR 5,500 less per car, Xiaomi is near break-even in its first production year and Waymo runs 500,000 paid rides a week on 3,000 vehicles. If revenue per mile falls from $0.60 to $0.45, the reverse DCF needs 20.9M robotaxis rather than 15.7M, above global annual capacity — $40-60 a share off the bull branch and nothing off 2027 earnings. The unknown unknown is a regulatory stop before any revenue evidence: a recall that grounds the monitored fleet removes the data set the model learns from. Three facts would settle the autonomy question and none is public: robotaxi revenue, fare and the share of rides without a safety driver; cost per mile; and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Tesla's strategy has become a capital-allocation bet rather than an operating one: more than $20bn of 2026 capex and $30bn of new credit facilities are committed to autonomy, robots and semiconductors while nine-month 2026 operating income of $2.06bn implies a return on invested capital near 3%, below any plausible cost of capital. The strategy earns its keep only if unsupervised robotaxi revenue arrives before 2028, and the 12-month test is customer-owned unsupervised driving in mid-2027, not another reveal [S4, S78].

### The plan and the return do not yet match

Tesla guided in the Q3 2026 filing to capital expenditure above $20bn for 2026, after spending $13.01bn in the first nine months against $6.13bn a year earlier, and in September 2026 signed three credit agreements for aggregate commitments of $30bn. Cash and short-term investments were $45.45bn at 2026-09-30 against $9.5bn of debt, so the plan is funded; it is no longer self-funding. Nine-month operating income of $2.06bn on $89.29bn of equity, annualised after tax over roughly $71bn of invested capital, gives a return near 3% — depressed by ramp assets, but low enough that every further billion of capex lowers the return until the new assets sell something [S6]. Research and development rose 69% year over year to $2.76bn in Q3 2026, most of it for autonomy and robotics.

### Pricing and mix are carrying the capex

| Item | Q3 2026 | Q3 2025 | Read | Source |

| Automotive gross margin | 18.5% | 17.0% | Cost cuts and mix offset lower prices | S4 |
| Regulatory credit revenue | $113m | $417m | A subsidy that no longer pays for the plan | S4 |
| Energy segment revenue | $2.881bn | $3.415bn | Volume up, price down | S4 |
| Services gross profit | $734m | $366m | FSD subscriptions and repair work | S6 |
| China deliveries | 142,133 | 16% lower year over year | Share loss in the largest market | S77 |
| Total deliveries | 486,532 | 497,099 | Flat volume on an ageing core line-up | S6 |

The read is that Tesla is funding autonomy from a mature car business, a fading credit stream and a fast-growing but deflating storage business; none of the three is a rising price. The Semi is a logical adjacency because it shares cells, motors and Megachargers with the core; Optimus is not an adjacency yet, because it has a production line and no customer.

The partner map shows the strategic risk: Tesla's autonomy roadmap runs through a single foundry for AI6, its vehicles still depend on CATL, Panasonic and LG for cells, and its largest related-party exposure is to companies its chief executive also controls.

### Geography: China becomes an export base

Tesla's China sales fell 16% year over year in Q3 2026 to 142,133 units while Giga Shanghai exports reached a record 132,978; retail sales for 2026 to date are down 12% as exports doubled, and Beijing cuts the EV export tax rebate in April 2027. Shanghai, with more than 950,000 units of capacity, is now a cost and export base rather than a growth market, exposed to tariffs in the markets it ships to. Berlin set a production record and the US business carries the FSD attach rate, which is why the company's own numbers look better in North America than in the two regions that decide its cost base [S77, S76, S102].

### Energy is where the strategy is working

The energy plan is coherent and funded: 50 GWh of Megafactory Texas capacity started in Q3 2026 alongside 40 GWh in California and 20 GWh in Shanghai, with 7 GWh of Nevada LFP cell capacity in early ramp and the first Megapacks built from Tesla-made cells. The 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified: a contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it, and a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. In January 2026 Tesla invested $2bn in xAI; the stake became SpaceX Class A shares when SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026, and the Q1 2026 cash flow statement records a $2.002bn purchase of SpaceX equity. Three signposts decide whether the strategy is earning its cost of capital. First, unsupervised driving in customer-owned cars in at least one US state by 2027-06-30, with robotaxi revenue disclosed separately — without it, the capex is a subsidy to a pilot. Second, energy gross margin holding above 25% once tariff refunds lapse and 50 GWh of Texas capacity ramps, which tests whether Megapack has pricing power or is a commodity; the unverified backlog claim needs a contracted figure or 2027 deployments above 36.0 GWh to become evidence. Third, capital discipline: 2027 capex at or below $25bn with positive free cash flow, rather than a further draw on the $30bn facilities. The humanoid plan needs its first named customer or billed unit before a 20,000-a-week target means anything. The counter-case is strong: FSD attach above 75% in North America, 1.74 million subscriptions, a record energy backlog and $45.45bn of cash mean the plan can be funded through a slip, and Q3 2026 free cash flow of $1.53bn shows the core still generates cash [S6, S57].

Will the December 2026 meeting put a SpaceX transaction to a shareholder vote, and on what terms? My confidence is high that the strategy is funded and well-resourced for energy, medium that autonomy revenue arrives before 2028, and low that a humanoid robot contributes to profit before 2029.

arguments.why: Tesla discloses no robotaxi fares, trips per vehicle, utilisation or insurance cost, and the only fleet count in the public record (769 registrations, 349 Cybercabs on 2026-10-14) comes from a low-confidence third-party tracker; the TDI filing would give the insurance cost per mile and the DMV record would settle the fleet count, which together decide whether the Austin pilot has unit economics that scale.
arguments.how: Search TDI's public rate-filing system (SERFF) for Tesla Robotaxi LLC or Tesla Insurance Services, or file a Texas Public Information Act request with TDI; request the Texas DMV automated-vehicle registration extract for 2026-10-14 from the TxDMV AV program.

arguments.markdown:
At $403.30 (NasdaqGS, 2026-10-29 20:00 UTC) Tesla's equity is worth $1,594.1B and its enterprise value $1,558.0B. On a sum of the parts, 89% of that price — $1,424B, or $361 a share — buys autonomy and robotics, while the automotive, energy and services businesses plus $36.2B of net cash are worth $42.50 a share at peer multiples. That residual is 11.3 times the $126B at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026, and Waymo is the only operator running a scaled driverless service. My probability-weighted value is $111 a share, 72.5% below the close; the disagreement is not about cars, since my $42.50 for the core sits within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47, but about whether 2.0M cumulative unsupervised miles, a robotaxi service confined to one city and zero disclosed Optimus revenue can carry $1.4 trillion. [S15, S120, S6]

### A five-year flat line and a violent quarter

The price has gone nowhere over five years and has lagged the index; the last quarter reversed part of that lag, a window that contains the 2026-10-21 results and the merger remarks Musk made on the same call.

| Measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Price | $403.30, NasdaqGS, USD, 2026-10-29 20:00 UTC | S15 |
| Market capitalisation | $1,594.1B on 3,952.6M shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 | S15, S5 |
| Enterprise value | $1,558.0B, after $36.2B of net cash | S15, S6 |
| 52-week range | $297.38-$498.83; the price is 53% of the way up | S15 |
| Return 1m / 3m / 12m | +14.3% / +30.6% / -8.4% | S15 |
| Twelve months vs S&P 500 | -21.5 pp (S&P 500 +13.2%) | S15, S22 |
| Return over five years | +0.1% ($402.86 on 2021-11-01 to $403.30) | S15 |
| Year to date | -11.3% (from the 2025-12-31 close of $454.43) | S15, S3 |
| Turnover | 36.96M shares and $14.0B a day, 20-day average | S15 |

### 443 times trailing earnings; the peer median is 18.5 times

On trailing figures Tesla trades at 443.2x earnings, 15.0x sales and 170.5x EBITDA, and 104x the company's own $15.0B adjusted EBITDA. The median of the six peers below is 18.5x trailing earnings — across the three with a positive P/E, Alphabet 14.2x, BYD 18.5x and GM 18.8x — and 2.4x EV/sales across Rivian, Lucid and Alphabet; Ford, Rivian and Lucid have no trailing earnings multiple. On that median, 2027 consensus EPS of $2.20 is worth $40.70 a share, so the price is 9.9 times it. Consensus that already assumes a robotaxi ramp barely normalises the multiple: 2026 revenue of $108.5B and EPS of $1.67 give 241x; 2027 revenue of $123.9B and EPS of $2.20 give 183x. Tesla's own five year-end P/Es were 72.8x (2021), 34.0x (2022), 57.8x (2023), 204.6x (2024) and 420.8x (2025): today is above all of them. [S115, S17, S15]

| Peer median | 18.5x | — | — | 2.4x | n/m | n/m | S17, S19, S21, S111, S113, S121 |

### Sum of the parts: $42.50 of business, and a bear case of $19

Trailing-twelve-month segment data from the Q3 2026 update: automotive revenue $75.0B at a 19.1% gross margin, energy $12.3B at 29.7%, services $16.3B at 12.4%, sharing $16.5B of operating expense. At 1.0x sales for vehicles and services — 2.5x GM's implied 0.39x, warranted by double GM's gross margin — 3.5x for energy (above Fluence's 0.5x) and net cash at book, the core is $170B, or $42.50 a share on 4.00B shares. That count carries 710M unvested restricted shares (18%) from the two CEO awards, so on the 3,240M basic count today's equity is $1,307B, not $1,594B. The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B at Waymo's licensing value, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B global dominance — $65 a share. The bear case is the same arithmetic with each input cut: autonomy, FSD and Optimus at zero; vehicles at 0.39x automotive revenue, a 10% discount to GM's 0.43x on $72.3B of market capitalisation over $169.8B of revenue, giving $29.3B on $75.0B; energy at 1.5x its $12.3B, or $18.4B, less than half the base multiple; and net cash cut to $28B from $36.2B after a year of capital spending and recall costs. That sum is $75.6B, $18.91 a share. Adding $259B of autonomy to the $170B core gives $429B, $107; the core with $600B gives $847B, $212. Weighting 25/50/25 on $212/$107/$19 gives $111, 72.5% below the price. [S6, S5, S17, S16, S120]

| Sum of the parts, bear | Vehicles 0.39x, energy 1.5x, net cash $28B, autonomy nil | $19 a share | S6, S17, S16 |
| Sum of the parts, base | Core plus $259B probability-weighted autonomy | $107 a share | S6, S120 |
| Sum of the parts, blue sky | Core plus $1,500B autonomy at 100% probability | $437 a share | S120, S123 |
| Reverse DCF | $2.0B FCF in 2027, 45% growth, 10% WACC, 3% terminal growth | $403 requires $141B of 2031 FCF | S4 |

### The reverse DCF needs sixteen million robotaxis

At a 10% WACC and 3% terminal growth, on $2.0B of 2027 free cash flow growing 45% a year, today's enterprise value requires $141B of 2031 free cash flow (9% WACC: $118B; 11%: $164B). At a 15% margin that is $940B of 2031 revenue, nine times trailing. At a 25% robotaxi margin it implies $564B of robotaxi revenue: at $0.60 a mile and 60,000 miles a vehicle a year, 15.7M robotaxis — 7.8M if cars and energy supply half the cash flow. Tesla's installed capacity is 2.5M vehicles a year. The price assumes a fleet six years of full capacity could not build at a revenue per mile no disclosed Tesla service charges. [S4, S6]

### What the street pays for, and what would prove it right

The consensus twelve-month target is $408.61 from 48 analysts on 2026-10-25, 1.3% above the close, range $128.11-$600 — a 4.7x spread that measures uncertainty, not value. Short interest is 69.35M shares, 2.19% of the float, 2.2 days to cover: no crowded short, no positioning signal. Management publishes no numeric guidance, promising only "maximum capacity utilization". Dated catalysts are the 2026-12-03 annual meeting, Q4 2026 results in late January 2027, Austin Fab tool commissioning in 2027 and the special-committee process opened on 2026-10-20 — the one event that could re-rate the shares without an operating delivery. [S141, S144, S6, S114]

The counter-evidence is real. Tesla has held a triple-digit multiple for two years without mean reversion; the 2025 CEO award ties 423.7M shares to market-cap milestones to $8.5T, aligning management with the narrative rather than with per-share cash flow; and a merger into SpaceX at $2.1T would give Tesla holders 43% of a $3.7T company with Starlink cash flows, against which a standalone sum of the parts is the wrong instrument. But stock compensation runs at 4.2% of revenue and every award tranche is paid in shares. The margin of safety at $403.30 is negative and turns positive only below $111; between those levels the buyer is purchasing an option and should size it as one. [S132]

Confidence is high on the core-business value and low on the autonomy tree. What would settle it: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile; the Austin fleet count and utilisation; the thresholds of each award tranche; 2026 capital expenditure guidance; and the exchange ratio the special committees would accept.

### The entity map is clean; the asset ring-fence is not

| Entity | Jurisdiction | Role | Ownership | Source |

| Tesla, Inc. | Texas | Listed parent and principal operating company | 100% | S3, S5 |

EX-21 states no ownership percentages, so the ownership column above is inferred from listing rather than disclosed. China is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, not a VIE, so there is no contractual-control gap, but Shanghai is fully consolidated and exposed to export controls. No entity is designated holder of Full Self-Driving or Optimus intellectual property: robotaxi operations sit in Tesla Robotaxi, LLC while software, data and chip designs stay in the parent, so no separately capitalised autonomy asset exists.

### Customers, buyers and how growth arrives

Tesla sells direct in two segments: automotive at $69,526m of 2025 revenue and energy at $12,771m [S71]. The vehicle buyer is a household or fleet paying cash or Tesla financing; the energy buyer is a utility or developer signing multi-year procurement, with 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026 against 18.5% for automotive. Growth now comes from storage, software (1.74 million FSD subscriptions) and paying Cybercab rides in Austin since 2026-09-03.

### Ownership is concentrated without a dual class

| Holder | Class | Shares | % ownership | % votes | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Elon Musk | Common, incl. 286,428,773 restricted | 699,580,882 | 19.8% | 19.8% | S5 |
| Elon Musk, pledged as collateral | Common | 207,498,721 | 5.2% of outstanding | 5.2% | S5 |
| Vanguard Capital Management | Common | 210,796,512 | 5.3% | 5.3% | S5 |
| Unearned 2025 award shares | Restricted, unearned | 423,743,904 | 10.7% of outstanding | proportional to other shares | S5 |
| Other public holders | Common | balance | 74.9% | 74.9% | S5 |

Percentages follow the proxy, whose denominator excludes unearned award shares; free float is capped by the Musk and Vanguard stakes shown, and a margin call on the pledged block would add supply at the worst moment. With one class and no super-voting stock, control runs through the CEO office, the board seat and stake size rather than a charter provision, unlike Ford's dual-class family control or Alphabet's founder shares.

### Control is priced through a contingent award

The 2025 CEO Performance Award is the control instrument: 423,743,904 shares in 12 tranches of 35,311,992, each tied to a market-capitalisation milestone from $2.0 trillion to $8.5 trillion and to 1 of 12 operational milestones (20 million vehicles, 10 million FSD subscriptions, 1 million bots, 1 million robotaxis, Adjusted EBITDA of $50bn to $400bn); none was earned at 2026-10-19 [S5]. At $2.0 trillion the first tranche implies $506 per share on 3.95 billion shares, and because the operational test falls away in a change of control, a deal at $3.0 trillion would earn three tranches, 105.9 million shares, with no robotaxi or Optimus milestone met. Expense is already running: $802m in the first nine months of 2026, $9.74bn unrecognised on the one milestone management judges probable, and $105.82bn-$120.37bn on the rest [S4]. Dilution of 10.7% is designed, not tail, and sits above the current valuation rather than beside it.

### The board can refuse less than it appears

Nine directors sit in three classes, six labelled independent under Nasdaq rules, with Robyn Denholm as chair since November 2018. Ira Ehrenpreis, who chairs both the compensation and the nominating and governance committees, joined SpaceX's board in February 2026; Kimbal Musk is the CEO's brother; JB Straubel, a director, runs Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier. arguments.markdown:
Tesla offers no cash exit at $1.59 trillion. It has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation, and its entire $45.4B of cash and short-term investments would retire 2.85% of the 3.953B shares outstanding. The largest buyout ever completed — Electronic Arts at $55B in August 2026 — is 3.4% of Tesla's market capitalisation, so no financial sponsor can write this cheque, and no automaker can either: GM and Ford together are $118.4B, 7.4% of Tesla. What remains is a sale into a market that trades $14.0B of Tesla a day, or a share exchange into SpaceX, and both leave the return hostage to a re-rating that five years have not delivered. [S3, S130]

### The company returns nothing, and cannot return much

Tesla's 10-K states that it has never declared or paid a cash dividend, does not anticipate doing so, and purchased no equity securities in fiscal 2025. Trailing free cash flow of $3,303M is a 0.2% yield on the capitalisation, and nine-month capital expenditure of $13,014M runs at 2.1x depreciation: the cash is going into factories, cells and training compute, not to holders. Against GM's 12.4% total shareholder yield and Ford's 5.9%, Tesla's is zero. Even a maximal buyback using the whole cash pile would move the share count by less than three points, and it would leave a company spending $17B a year on capital projects with no liquidity buffer. Capital return is a governance choice, and the controlling shareholder has consistently chosen reinvestment. [S6]

### The exit that always works is the tape

The secondary market is the only channel that is always open. Tesla trades 36.96M shares and $14.0B a day over twenty days, so a $500M position is 3.6% of a single day's value and no holder is trapped by liquidity. Short interest of 69.35M shares, 2.19% of the float and 2.2 days to cover, means the marginal seller is not fighting a crowded short either. Passive ownership is a flow that follows the index and the price rather than a bid that supports it; Tesla's exact float-adjusted S&P 500 weight is not disclosed in the sources retrieved, and after the top ten names reached 39.03% of the index on 2026-10-10 the marginal index buyer is a shrinking share of demand. [S15, S114]

### No control buyer exists, at any price

A cash takeover is arithmetically out of reach. The pieces themselves are worth $170B on the sum of the parts — vehicles at 1.0x sales, energy at 3.5x, net cash at book — and a control buyer for those assets alone would pay $200-250B with a premium, which is one-eighth of the current capitalisation and therefore not a route to today's price. Alphabet, at $3,493.5B, is the only US company with the balance sheet to write a $1.6T cheque, and it is the closest competitor in autonomous driving, which makes antitrust the binding constraint rather than price. Musk's 19.8% stake and 207.5M pledged shares mean nothing happens without him, and a hostile approach is legally and financially impossible at this size. [S5, S6]

| Route | Named buyer or venue | Rationale | Timing | Likelihood | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secondary sale | NasdaqGS | $14.0B daily turnover; no lock-up for public holders | Continuous | High | S15 |
| Share exchange with SpaceX | SpaceX (NasdaqGS: SPCX) | Musk-sponsored combination; special committees formed 2026-10-20 | 2027-2028 | Medium | S129, S128 |
| Cash take-private | None identified | $1,594.1B is 29x the largest LBO on record ($55B) | None | Very low | S130 |
| Acquisition by an automaker | GM, Ford | Combined market cap $118.4B, 7.4% of Tesla | None | Very low | S17, S19 |
| Acquisition by a platform company | Alphabet | $3,493.5B market cap, but antitrust in autonomy | None | Very low | S113 |
| Buyback or dividend | Tesla | No programme; no dividend ever declared | None | Very low | S3 |

### The one live route is a share exchange with SpaceX

On 2026-10-21 both boards formed special committees to explore a combination, days after Musk called the idea a "good idea" on the third-quarter earnings call. SpaceX listed on 2026-06-12 at $135 a share and a $1.77T valuation, reached $2.1T on its first day, and the combined group would be worth well over $3 trillion. At those marks Tesla holders would own 43% of the equity — but they would exchange one-share-one-vote stock for a company where super-voting shares give Musk about 84% of the vote, against 20% at Tesla. That is the governance price of the only transformative exit available, and it is being negotiated by two boards that have not historically pushed back: Tesla invested $2B in xAI after its chair expressed scepticism, and it rescued SolarCity in 2016. [S129, S128]

| Transaction | Year | Value | Multiple | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Electronic Arts take-private (PIF, Silver Lake, Affinity) | 2026 | $55.0B | $210 a share cash; largest LBO on record | S130 |
| SpaceX IPO (NasdaqGS: SPCX) | 2026 | $1.77T at pricing; $2.1T on day one | $135 a share; largest IPO on record | S128 |
| Waymo round (Alphabet, Dragoneer, DST, Sequoia) | 2026 | $126B post-money | 2.8x the $45B of October 2024 | S120 |
| Tesla as a holding, 2021-2026 | 2026 | — | +0.1% over five years | S15 |

The precedents frame both ends of the range: what control has cost in this market, and what a Tesla holder has actually earned while waiting for one.

| Exit value per share in five years | Market capitalisation | Five-year IRR from $403.30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| $19 (bear: autonomy nil, vehicles 0.39x, net cash $28B) | $76B | -45.7% a year | S6, S17, S16 |
| $107 (base) | $429B | -23.3% a year | S6, S120 |
| $111 (probability-weighted 25/50/25) | $444B | -22.7% a year | S6, S120 |
| $212 (bull) | $847B | -12.1% a year | S6, S120 |
| $437 (blue sky) | $1,747B | +1.6% a year | S120, S123 |
| $650 (the 10%-a-year hurdle) | $2,600B | +10.0% a year | arithmetic on S15 |
| $408.61 (consensus target, 2026-10-25) | $1,615B | +1.3% over twelve months | S141, S144 |

| Policy test | Effect on the exit | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Foreign ownership and national security | A non-US buyer for Tesla alone, and any foreign bid for a combined Tesla-SpaceX, faces review; SpaceX's launch and defence work makes approval implausible | S128 |
| Tariffs | Third-quarter 2026 energy revenue was held back by tariff-related customer refunds | S6 |
| US electric-vehicle incentives | Regulatory credit revenue fell to $113M in the third quarter of 2026 from $417M a year earlier | S6 |
| Deal approvals | A Tesla shareholder vote (Musk cited a 50% threshold) plus the SpaceX special committee, board and controlling shareholder | S129 |
| Index treatment and lock-up | The combined company's index eligibility and SpaceX lock-up terms are not disclosed | S128 |

### What would make the exit valuable, and what stands in the way

The counter-case deserves weight. A negotiated combination would carry a premium to the undisturbed price, and a holder who sells into it captures that premium without waiting for a re-rating; SpaceX's Starlink cash flows are real, so the merged entity would have earnings that Tesla alone does not; and if the ratio is struck on market values, a Tesla holder participates in that cash flow from day one. The risk is that the ratio, not a cash price, is what gets negotiated, and that a controlled board sets it. The 2025 CEO Performance Award reinforces the point: its change-of-control terms let unearned shares vest on market-capitalisation milestones alone, so the controlling shareholder's incentive in a sale is to maximise the headline value, not the terms minority holders receive. [S5, S132]

For a public-equity holder the practical conclusion is that monetisation is a sale into the secondary market at whatever multiple prevails, with a merger into SpaceX as the only event that could produce a premium, and no dividend, no buyback and no cash bid to fall back on. Confidence is high that no cash exit exists and medium on the merger: the talks are exploratory and no ratio, premium or timetable has been disclosed. What would settle it: the exchange ratio and voting structure the committees propose; whether SpaceX's segment financials are published before a vote; the treatment of unvested award shares in a combination; the lock-up and index terms for the combined entity; and whether any special committee obtains an independent fairness opinion that values Tesla on a sum of the parts rather than on the combined-company narrative.

The 2025 CEO Performance Award is the control instrument: 423,743,904 shares in 12 tranches of 35,311,992, each tied to a market-capitalisation milestone from $2.0 trillion to $8.5 trillion and to 1 of 12 operational milestones (20 million vehicles, 10 million FSD subscriptions, 1 million bots, 1 million robotaxis, Adjusted EBITDA of $50bn to $400bn); none was earned at 2026-10-19 [S5].
