{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## ESG评估 ESG Assessment (esg, revision 3 by Regulatory Analyst, 8,745 characters)
Tesla's policy position has inverted. The 2025-2026 reset removes a high-margin revenue stream worth $2,763m at its 2024 peak and leaves the robotaxi licence fragmented across US states and unapproved in China, while the offsetting upsides — federal AV preemption and tariffs on Chinese rivals — are real but not yet law. Automotive regulatory credit revenue fell from $2,763m in 2024 to $1,993m in 2025 (-28%) and to $113m in Q3 2026 from $417m (-73%); credits carry almost no cost of revenue, so their loss took total automotive gross margin from 18.4% to 17.8% in 2025. The credit-free margin is the right base. [S3, S4]

### The credit pool has already collapsed

The US instrument is unambiguous. Section 30D's $7,500 new clean vehicle credit applied only to vehicles acquired on or before 2025-09-30; the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, enacted 2025-07-04, terminated it and the used-vehicle 25E credit thereafter. The 2026 revision is a repeal, not a tightening: EPA's final rule of 2026-02-18 rescinds the 2009 endangerment finding and repeals the light-, medium- and heavy-duty GHG standards, and the Department of Transportation finalised its CAFE rollback on 2026-10-01. Both remove the compliance demand that priced Tesla's credits; EIA reported on 2026-10-19 that battery-electric sales remained lower after the credit expired. California's ACC II and the Section 177 states preserve a partial market, not the 2024 price level. [S117, S116, S64, S98]

### The robotaxi licence is a state-by-state binary

Autonomy is the part of the equity value policy can switch on or off, and the record is narrower than the narrative. Texas requires a TxDMV authorisation for commercial SAE Level 4/5 operation from 2026-05-28 under SB 2807 — a no-fee, non-expiring registration regime, which is why Austin scaled first. California is the opposite: CPUC's AV permit table lists Waymo, Zoox, Nuro, WeRide and Tensor but not Tesla, and Tesla's California service runs under a non-AV limousine/TCP authority. Federally the binding constraint is enforcement — NHTSA's FSD probes and the October 2026 school-zone review — while the preemption fix, H.R. 7390 SELF DRIVE Act of 2026, advanced only from a House subcommittee on a 12-11 party-line vote on 2026-02-10. Waymo holds a CPUC driverless permit and Zoox a federal exemption; Tesla holds neither. [S118, S119, S80, S125]

### China taxes the base; Europe protects it for now

China policy has become a tax on Tesla's largest manufacturing base. From 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31 the NEV purchase tax is halved rather than exempt — an effective 5%, capped at RMB 15,000 per car — regressive for Tesla's higher-priced trims and landing alongside a 16% fall in Q3 2026 China sales, a cut in the vehicle export rebate and no unsupervised FSD approval. Europe is the exception: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 has imposed a countervailing duty on China-built BEVs since 2024-10-30 for five years, at 7.8% for Tesla Shanghai against 35.3% for SAIC, on top of the 10% common duty — 17.8% versus 45.3% for Chinese brands. That room is time-limited: the EU softened 2025-2027 CO2 compliance to a three-year average and proposed the same for 2030-2032, reducing legacy makers' urgency to buy credits. [S124, S77, S127, S126]

### Governance is the largest ESG item

Governance is the largest ESG item because it changes the share count and the cost of capital. The 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423.7m shares in 12 tranches, approved on 2025-11-06 — 10.7% of the 3.95bn shares outstanding at the low end — with $105.82-120.37bn of unrecognised stock compensation on the milestones not yet probable and $9.74bn on the one deemed probable (20 million vehicles, recognised over 8.9 years). Capital allocation matters as much as pay design: Tesla invested $2.0bn in xAI Holdings in January 2026 and, after SpaceX acquired xAI Holdings on 2026-02-02, converted that right into SpaceX Class A stock in March 2026. Musk holds 19.8% and 207.5m shares are pledged. Six of nine directors are independent under Nasdaq rules; three carry outside ties — Ehrenpreis and Kimbal Musk to SpaceX's board, Straubel to Redwood, a Tesla supplier — and one share carries one vote, but a governance discount is warranted. [S5, S3, S4]

### What is not financially material

Three ESG claims do not survive contact with the financials. Tesla's operational footprint is small against the use-phase emissions its products avoid, and the 2025 10-K discloses no material environmental proceeding; the real exposure is upstream, in battery materials, where it files an annual conflict-minerals report but no supplier-level data. Labour and product safety are tails: the California Civil Rights Department's bench trial began on 2026-09-21 before Judge Peter Borkon, is scheduled to run to 2026-10-30 and had no verdict as of 2026-10-29, while the August 2025 Autopilot verdict was $129m compensatory with Tesla 33% at fault plus $200m punitive, against an immaterial accrual. The strongest counter-evidence runs the other way — the US tariff wall on Chinese-built EVs, the EU's relative tariff advantage, possible federal AV preemption and performance-contingent pay — which is why policy is a discount on the multiple, not an exit signal. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 投资潜力与投资逻辑 Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 5 by Lead Analyst, 8,808 characters)
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $356, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,060 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 769 robotaxi vehicles registered in Texas on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S4]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $42.50 a share, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets, and autonomy at $259B in the base case — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance — which is $65.6 a share on 3,952.6M shares, so $42.50 + $65.6 = $108.1 and the base rounds to $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $52.50 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $465 mid-point lifts expected value to $253, still 37% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

::: scenarios
| Scenario | Probability | Drivers | Outcome | Signposts | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull | 25% | Robotaxi in several metros at 1.0x Waymo's $126B; energy at 6.0x sales; 1.74M FSD subscriptions | $212 a share, -47% from $403.30; -12.1% a year to 2031 | Robotaxi revenue line disclosed; California driverless permit; Texas fleet above 5,000 vehicles | S6, S120 |
| Base | 50% | Autonomy at $259B, the probability-weighted blend of the four branches (35% × $40B, 40% × $126B, 20% × $600B, 5% × $1,500B); core at $42.50; energy at 3.5x sales | $107 a share, -73% | Q4 2026 update with no robotaxi revenue; Texas fleet below 1,000 | S6, S120 |
| Bear | 25% | Autonomy written down; vehicles at GM's 0.39x sales; Terafab commitment; credit-free margin | $19 a share, -95% | Unsupervised FSD slips past 2027; NHTSA recall of the Cybercab; merger vote fails | S6, S120, S137 |
:::

### Key assumptions, ranked

| Rank | Assumption | Confidence | What would disprove it | Impact if wrong | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031: 15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile is what the reverse DCF needs | low | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | Registrations flat near 769 vehicles; no fare disclosure; safety-driver hours rising | S4, S6, S137 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | medium | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | Each 100 bp is $756M, 22% of trailing operating income | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% with revenue growth | medium | Q4 margin below 25% once tariff refunds lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | Q3 revenue fell 16% to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | low | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | Terafab's $16.8B first phase sits outside the 2026 budget | S4, S134 |
| 5 | No value-transferring exchange ratio; award dilution held near 12% | low | Ratio struck below market, or new tranches granted | -$40 to -$80 a share | Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers | S5, S135, S138 |

Assumption 1 sets the price and is the least evidenced: no robotaxi revenue, no fare and no cost per mile are disclosed, so the largest component of value rests on a third-party fleet count. Assumptions 2 and 3 decide whether the core is worth $42.50 or $21.75, and management can still influence both in 2027 — the ex-credit operating margin has been cut to 2.2-2.5%, while energy supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M third-quarter gross profit at a margin 2.5 times Fluence's 13.1%. Assumptions 4 and 5 are about survival and dilution rather than growth: $36.18B of net cash covers eighteen months of zero free cash flow, but not that plus a $16.8B capital call whose Tesla share is undisclosed. [S4, S6]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cisco | cautionary | 2000-2024 | Revenue grew from $12.5B to $57B and trailing net income passed its 1999 level by 2003, yet a buyer at the March 2000 peak of $500B waited until 2021 to break even. A correct thesis does not rescue the entry multiple. | S140 |
| Amazon | cautionary | 1999-2001 | The business compounded into one of the great franchises, but the stock fell more than 90% and took a decade to recover; the option paid only for the holder who could sit through the drawdown. | S143 |
| GM Cruise | cautionary | 2016-2024 | More than $10B of operating losses and less than $500M of revenue before GM shut the robotaxi unit in December 2024 for $1B a year of savings. Automaker capital is no substitute for paid driverless miles. | S142 |
| Waymo | best | 2024-2026 | The valuation went from $45B in October 2024 to $126B in February 2026 on 500,000 paid driverless rides a week — proof the service can scale, and a mark that Tesla's autonomy value exceeds 11-fold. | S120 |
:::

The precedents give one rule: when a real technology shift is already in the price, the entry multiple sets the return, not whether the technology wins; the base rate for a follower in autonomy is a write-off, not a slow fade; and the leader's private mark, $126B, is the only independent price for the option — 9% of what the market pays for Tesla's version. A holder should own Tesla's autonomy at a discount to that mark, not at 11.3 times it, and size the position so the Cruise outcome is survivable. [S140, S142]

### Where the case turns, and what to do now

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. At $403.30 it sits in the third zone, with the ten-year Treasury at 4.99% raising the discount rate on post-2030 cash flows. Do not invest new money now. Wait for one of three milestones: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless deployment permit, or special-committee terms at a premium to market rather than at market. If the mandate requires exposure, hold a residual of 0.25-0.5% of net asset value, sized so a failed vote and a 30% drawdown do not breach the risk budget, and vote against any ratio that transfers value to the controlling shareholder. Pass on the blue-sky branch: it needs global robotaxi and humanoid dominance and pays 8% from here. Diligence questions: revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, the share of rides running without a safety driver, and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Confidence is high that the core is not worth $403.30, medium on the autonomy tree, low on the merger. What would change the call: a second consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-credit operating margin, an FSD licensing contract with a named automaker, or a ratio that values Tesla at a premium to its undisturbed price. arguments.markdown:
At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 Tesla is a $1,594.1B equity in which $42.50 a share, $170B, is the vehicle, energy, services and net-cash business and $356 a share, $1,424B, is autonomy and robotics; on 25/50/25 of $212/$107/$19 the probability-weighted value is $111, so the share is a reduce and new money is an option purchase. A market 50% smaller leaves a $105B core, $26 a share, at 94% autonomy; customer acquisition cost doubled adds $8.1B; revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B of gross profit; a 5.0x peer multiple on free cash flow 30% lower is $130; financing six months late is covered by the September facilities [S6, S15, S120, S4, S115]. None reverses the conclusion. An exchange ratio at a premium does, a board decision rather than an operating one, and the one risk the recommendation must price. The three premises carrying the $1,424B are deteriorating at once: NHTSA's Cybercab self-certification inquiry closes for comment on 2026-10-30, the special committees formed on 2026-10-20 have no terms, and nine-month free cash flow of $1,883M contains $7,332M from stretching payables to 75.3 days.

### The core is not harsh at 1.0x sales; it is generous

The sum of the parts pays $91B for vehicles and services at 1.0x sales, $43B for energy at 3.5x and $36B of net cash at book. At GM's implied 0.39x, vehicles and services are worth $29B and the core is $87B, $21.75 a share, with autonomy at 95% of the price; a control buyer for the pieces tops out at $200-250B, $50-62.50, where autonomy still holds 84%. Energy's multiple has support — a 29.7% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% — but doubling revenue to $25B on 5.0x adds $82B, $20 a share, and FSD's 1.74M subscribers at $1,200 a year add $42B, $10.5, leaving the best honest core near $70 and autonomy at 83%. The $1,424B premium is 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, for 769 Texas-registered vehicles against 3,000. [S6, S131, S120, S15]

### The scenario tree is generous at the base and shallow in the bear

The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% x $40B regional, 40% x $126B at Waymo parity, 20% x $600B at scale, 5% x $1,500B at dominance — and $259B is 1.0x Waymo for 769 vehicles that reported nine crashes in August 2026 and disclose no revenue per mile. On the regional branch alone the base is $52.50 and the probability-weighted value $84, still 79% below the close. The 40% probability I attach to unsupervised customer FSD within 2027 and 40% for a merger within a year sit above the record: EA26002 covers 2.88M vehicles, DP26010 opened on 2026-10-09, and no cross-company vote of this kind has passed. The $35 bear was too shallow: at $19 — autonomy at zero, vehicles at 0.39x, energy at 1.5x, net cash $29B after a Terafab call — the drawdown is 95% and the weighted value falls only from $115 to $111. Above $437 the path I had missed is a 10-15% ratio premium in a $3.60T combination, paying $443-487 without one driverless mile. [S120, S137, S6, S5]

### Cash carries a two-year slip, not a slip plus a revenue fall

Net cash of $36.18B and $30B of facilities signed in September 2026 carry a two-year autonomy slip at zero free cash flow without issuing a share. The combination does not survive a revenue fall: at a 19% gross margin, revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B of gross profit against $19.1B of annual operating expense, taking operating cash flow to zero or minus $2B, and with $20-25B of capital expenditure the annual burn is $20-27B, exhausting cash and facilities before 2029. Reported cash flow already borrows from suppliers: payables and accruals added $7,332M and days payable rose from 62.8 to 75.3, worth $2.9B, so normalised free cash flow is minus $1.0B. Terafab adds a commitment Tesla does not control: a $16.8B first phase joint with SpaceX, Tesla's share undisclosed, outside the ">$20B" 2026 capital budget and described in SpaceX's IPO filing as a "general framework" with no binding commitment — which caps the near-term cash risk and demolishes the strategic-asset defence. Tesla is Baa3 against SpaceX at Baa1, and the September facilities' pricing is undisclosed. [S4, S134, S138, S147]

### The merger is an option, not a floor

arguments.markdown:
At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 Tesla is a $1,594.1B equity in which $42.50 a share, $170B, is the vehicle, energy, services and net-cash business and $356 a share, $1,424B, is autonomy and robotics; on 25/50/25 of $212/$107/$19 the probability-weighted value is $111, so the share is a reduce and new money is an option purchase. A market 50% smaller leaves a $105B core, $26 a share, at 94% autonomy; customer acquisition cost doubled adds $8.1B; revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B; a 5.0x peer multiple on free cash flow 30% lower is $130; financing six months late is covered by the September facilities [S6, S15, S120, S4, S115]. None reverses the conclusion. An exchange ratio at a premium does, a board decision, and the one risk the recommendation must price. The three premises carrying the $1,424B are deteriorating at once: NHTSA's Cybercab self-certification inquiry closes for comment on 2026-10-30, the special committees formed on 2026-10-20 have no terms, and nine-month free cash flow of $1,883M contains $7,332M from stretching payables to 75.3 days.

### The core is not harsh at 1.0x sales; it is generous

The sum of the parts pays $91B for vehicles and services at 1.0x sales, $43B for energy at 3.5x and $36B of net cash at book. At GM's implied 0.39x, vehicles and services are worth $29B and the core is $87B, $21.75 a share, with autonomy at 95% of the price; a control buyer tops out at $200-250B, $50-62.50, where autonomy still holds 84%. Energy's multiple has support — a 29.7% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% — but doubling revenue to $25B on 5.0x adds $82B, $20 a share, and FSD's 1.74M subscribers at $1,200 a year add $42B, $10.5, leaving the best honest core near $70 and autonomy at 83%. The $1,424B premium is 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, for 769 Texas-registered vehicles against 3,000. [S6, S131, S120, S15]

### The scenario tree is generous at the base and shallow in the bear

The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% x $40B regional, 40% x $126B at Waymo parity, 20% x $600B at scale, 5% x $1,500B at dominance — and $259B is 1.0x Waymo for 769 vehicles that reported nine crashes in August 2026 and disclose no revenue per mile. On the regional branch alone the base is $52.50 and the probability-weighted value $84, still 79% below the close. My 40% probability for unsupervised customer FSD in 2027 and 40% for a merger within a year sit above the record: EA26002 covers 2.88M vehicles, DP26010 opened on 2026-10-09. The $35 bear was too shallow: at $19 — autonomy at zero, vehicles at 0.39x, energy at 1.5x, net cash $29B after a Terafab call — the drawdown is 95% and the weighted value falls only from $115 to $111. Above $437 the path I had missed is a 10-15% ratio premium in a $3.60T combination, paying $443-487 without one driverless mile. [S120, S137, S6, S5]

### Cash carries a two-year slip, not a slip plus a revenue fall

Net cash of $36.18B and $30B of facilities signed in September 2026 carry a two-year autonomy slip at zero free cash flow without issuing a share. The combination does not survive a revenue fall: at a 19% gross margin, revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B of gross profit against $19.1B of annual operating expense, taking operating cash flow to zero or minus $2B, and with $20-25B of capital expenditure the annual burn is $20-27B, exhausting cash and facilities before 2029. Reported cash flow already borrows from suppliers: payables and accruals added $7,332M and days payable rose from 62.8 to 75.3, worth $2.9B, so normalised free cash flow is minus $1.0B. Terafab adds a commitment Tesla does not control: a $16.8B first phase joint with SpaceX, Tesla's share undisclosed, outside the ">$20B" 2026 capital budget and described in SpaceX's IPO filing as a "general framework" with no binding commitment — which caps near-term cash risk and weakens the strategic-asset defence. Tesla is Baa3 against SpaceX at Baa1; the facilities' pricing is undisclosed. [S4, S134, S138, S147]

### The merger is an option, not a floor

On 2026-10-20 Musk said both boards had formed special committees, that no terms were agreed and none assured; the Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares, not of those cast, so abstentions count against, and the 2026-10-19 proxy sets the 2026-12-03 annual meeting with no merger proposal. At market the deal is value-neutral: $1,594.1B plus SpaceX's $2.01T is $3.60T, and Tesla holders taking 43-44% own exactly today's price; any premium must be conceded by SpaceX. Either way Tesla holders get 43% of the economics and a shareholder with 84% of the votes. The 2025 award writes the incentive down: on a change of control operational milestones lapse and market-cap milestones vest, 423.7M shares are 10.7% dilution, the first $2.0T milestone sits 25% above today's capitalisation, against a $9.74B probable charge and $105.82-120.37B unrecognised. Musk has pledged 207.5M shares, 5.2% of the count, three of nine directors are SpaceX-linked and the committee uses two. [S5, S135, S138]

### Policy is a $5.60 option; competition is a terminal-value risk

Twenty-five state attorneys general and 12 cities and counties sued on 2026-03-19 in the D.C. Circuit over EPA's 2026-02-12 repeal of the 2009 endangerment finding, consolidated on 2026-05-20; a reversal restores the credit pool, but $1.5B of credits at 15x is $22.5B, $5.6 a share, against Q3 credit revenue of $113M, down 73%, credits at 45.8% of FY2025 operating income. Policy is a small option and the base case gives it nothing. Competition is different in kind: BYD holds 2.4% of the European market at EUR 5,500 less per car, Xiaomi is near break-even in its first production year and Waymo runs 500,000 paid rides a week on 3,000 vehicles. If revenue per mile falls from $0.60 to $0.45, the reverse DCF needs 20.9M robotaxis rather than 15.7M, above global annual capacity — $40-60 a share off the bull branch and nothing off 2027 earnings. The unknown unknown is a regulatory stop before any revenue evidence: a recall that grounds the fleet removes the data the model learns from. [S136, S138, S59, S4]

::: risk-matrix
| Risk | Probability | Impact | Level | Timing | Signpost | Mitigation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unsupervised FSD slips past 2027 | 60% | Bull reverts to base; -$85/share | critical | Q2 2027 target | No date in the Q4 update; monitors still in Austin | Option size only; no adds | S57, S6 |
| NHTSA rejects Cybercab self-certification or EA26002 becomes a recall | 35% | -$45 to -$90/share | critical | Comment window closes 2026-10-30 | Audit finding; service pause; fleet shrinks | Exit on a service suspension | S137, S80 |
| Autonomy re-rated to the $40B regional branch | 55% | Weighted value -$55/share | high | 2027 | No robotaxi revenue line in the Q4 update | Underwrite $52.50 plus regional | S120, S6 |
| Payables reverse, free cash flow negative | 60% | -$10 to -$15/share | medium | Q4 2026 | Days payable below 65 with negative free cash flow | Value on normalised -$1.0B | S4 |
| Capex or a Terafab draw forces debt or equity | 30% | -$15 to -$30/share | high | 2027-2028 | First draw on the $30B facilities | No adds; read the debt note quarterly | S4, S134, S147 |
| Merger at market, or the vote fails | 60% | -$25 to -$50/share | high | Not before mid-2027 | No 8-K naming advisers; no terms | Carry the merger at zero | S135, S5 |
| Exchange ratio transfers value to the controlling holder | 40% | -$40 to -$80/share | high | Announcement day | Control-change terms; committee demands | Vote against; require operating milestones | S5, S138 |
| BYD, Xiaomi or Waymo compress revenue per mile | high | -$40 to -$60/share on the bull branch | high | 2027-2029 | BYD European share above 2.4%; Waymo above 1M rides a week | Re-underwrite price per mile | S138, S59 |
:::

::: diligence
**Open diligence — three items no filing yet settles**

- **Robotaxi revenue, fare and driverless share:** Q4 2026 shareholder update, 2026 Form 10-K Item 7 and the segment note, TxDMV registrations and CPUC's deployment list; it decides whether the $259B base value stands [S6, S4, S119].
- **Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call:** the definitive agreements, Tesla's 2026 Form 10-K commitments note and SpaceX's 2026 Form 20-F related-party note; it decides 2027-2028 equity need [S147, S134].
- **Per-tranche thresholds of the 2025 CEO award:** the award agreement at Annex C to the 2025 proxy (SEC EX-99.2) and the 2025 DEF 14A compensation section; they decide dilution on a change of control [S5, S132].
:::

::: info danger
**A premium exchange ratio is the only route to $403 that needs no robotaxi mile.** At market, $1,594.1B plus SpaceX's $2.01T is $3.60T and Tesla holders' 43-44% is exactly today's price; a 10-15% ratio premium pays $443-487 without a California permit or an unsupervised release. The one event that could turn reduce into hold; size for a failed vote and a 30% fall (sources S135, S5).
:::

arguments.markdown:
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $356, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 769 robotaxi vehicles registered in Texas on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S4]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $42.50 a share, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets, and autonomy at $259B in the base case — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance — which is $65.6 a share on 3,952.6M shares, so $42.50 + $65.6 = $108.1 and the base rounds to $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $52.50 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $465 mid-point lifts expected value to $253, still 37% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

::: scenarios
| Scenario | Probability | Drivers | Outcome | Signposts | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull | 25% | Robotaxi in several metros at 1.0x Waymo's $126B; energy at 6.0x sales; 1.74M FSD subscriptions | $212 a share, -47% from $403.30; -12.1% a year to 2031 | Robotaxi revenue line disclosed; California driverless permit; Texas fleet above 5,000 vehicles | S6, S120 |
| Base | 50% | Autonomy at $259B, the probability-weighted blend of the four branches (35% × $40B, 40% × $126B, 20% × $600B, 5% × $1,500B); core at $42.50; energy at 3.5x sales | $107 a share, -73% | Q4 2026 update with no robotaxi revenue; Texas fleet below 1,000 | S6, S120 |
| Bear | 25% | Autonomy written down; vehicles at GM's 0.39x sales; Terafab commitment; credit-free margin | $19 a share, -95% | Unsupervised FSD slips past 2027; NHTSA recall of the Cybercab; merger vote fails | S6, S120, S137 |
:::

### Key assumptions, ranked

| Rank | Assumption | Confidence | What would disprove it | Impact if wrong | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031: 15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile is what the reverse DCF needs | low | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | Registrations flat near 769 vehicles; no fare disclosure; safety-driver hours rising | S4, S6, S137 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | medium | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | Each 100 bp is $756M, 22% of trailing operating income | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% with revenue growth | medium | Q4 margin below 25% once tariff refunds lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | Q3 revenue fell 16% to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | low | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | Terafab's $16.8B first phase sits outside the 2026 budget | S4, S134 |
| 5 | No value-transferring exchange ratio; award dilution held at 10.7% | low | Ratio struck below market, or new tranches granted | -$40 to -$80 a share | Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers | S5, S135, S138 |

Assumption 1 sets the price and is the least evidenced: no robotaxi revenue, no fare and no cost per mile are disclosed, so the largest component of value rests on a third-party fleet count. Assumptions 2 and 3 decide whether the core is worth $42.50 or $21.75, and management can still influence both in 2027 — the ex-credit operating margin has been cut to 2.2-2.5%, while energy supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M third-quarter gross profit at a margin 2.5 times Fluence's 13.1%. Assumptions 4 and 5 are about survival and dilution rather than growth: $36.18B of net cash covers eighteen months of zero free cash flow, but not that plus a $16.8B capital call whose Tesla share is undisclosed. [S4, S6]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cisco | cautionary | 2000-2024 | Revenue grew from $12.5B to $57B and trailing net income passed its 1999 level by 2003, yet a buyer at the March 2000 peak of $500B waited until 2021 to break even. A correct thesis does not rescue the entry multiple. | S140 |
| Amazon | cautionary | 1999-2001 | The business compounded into one of the great franchises, but the stock fell more than 90% and took a decade to recover; the option paid only for the holder who could sit through the drawdown. | S143 |
| GM Cruise | cautionary | 2016-2024 | More than $10B of operating losses and less than $500M of revenue before GM shut the robotaxi unit in December 2024 for $1B a year of savings. Automaker capital is no substitute for paid driverless miles. | S142 |
| Waymo | best | 2024-2026 | The valuation went from $45B in October 2024 to $126B in February 2026 on 500,000 paid driverless rides a week — proof the service can scale, and a mark that Tesla's autonomy value exceeds 11-fold. | S120 |
:::

The precedents give one rule: when a real technology shift is already in the price, the entry multiple sets the return, not whether the technology wins; the base rate for a follower in autonomy is a write-off, not a slow fade; and the leader's private mark, $126B, is the only independent price for the option — 9% of what the market pays for Tesla's version. A holder should own Tesla's autonomy at a discount to that mark, not at 11.3 times it, and size the position so the Cruise outcome is survivable. [S140, S142]

### Where the case turns, and what to do now

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. At $403.30 it sits in the third zone, with the ten-year Treasury at 4.99% raising the discount rate on post-2030 cash flows. Do not invest new money now. Wait for one of three milestones: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless deployment permit, or special-committee terms at a premium to market rather than at market. If the mandate requires exposure, hold a residual of 0.25-0.5% of net asset value, sized so a failed vote and a 30% drawdown do not breach the risk budget, and vote against any ratio that transfers value to the controlling shareholder. Pass on the blue-sky branch: it needs global robotaxi and humanoid dominance and pays 8% from here. Diligence questions: revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, the share of rides running without a safety driver, and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Confidence is high that the core is not worth $403.30, medium on the autonomy tree, low on the merger. What would change the call: a second consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-credit operating margin, an FSD licensing contract with a named automaker, or a ratio that values Tesla at a premium to its undisturbed price. [S15, S5]

arguments.markdown:
Tesla scores 4.0 out of 10, and the score is not close to the line that would justify new money: at $403.30 the shares price the autonomy option at $1,424B, 89% of the equity, while the business that pays the bills earns a 2.2-2.5% operating margin once regulatory credits are stripped out. The recommendation is Reduce — trim existing exposure to a residual, buy nothing — on a twelve-month horizon, with medium confidence in the direction and high confidence in the arithmetic. The composite is a weighted average of seven dimensions, and two do most of the work: valuation at 2 out of 10 with a 20% weight and governance at 3 out of 10 with a 15% weight. Remove either and the stock still scores below 5. [S15, S4]

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business quality and moat | 15% | 6 | Energy earned a 33.1% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% and vertical integration in cells and packs is real; vehicle share is falling in China and the premium band is contested | S6, S63, S59 |
| Growth durability | 15% | 5 | Energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881B in Q3 2026 and deliveries fell 2%, so growth now depends on a robotaxi fleet of 769 vehicles | S6, S4, S137 |
| Unit economics and margins | 15% | 4 | The ex-credit operating margin is 2.2-2.5% and trailing ROIC is 5.5% against an 11-14% cost of capital | S3, S4 |
| Balance sheet and cash conversion | 15% | 5 | $36.18B of net cash and $30B of undrawn facilities, offset by a 61% fall in nine-month free cash flow and payables at 75.3 days against 62.8 | S4 |
| Governance and capital allocation | 15% | 3 | A 423.7M-share award with $105.82-120.37B of unrecognised compensation, three of nine directors tied to SpaceX, no dividend or buyback | S5, S138 |
| Valuation and margin of safety | 20% | 2 | 443x trailing and 183x 2027E earnings against an 18.5x trailing P/E and 2.4x EV/sales median for the six peers shown in section 8; the margin of safety turns positive only below $111 | S15, S115 |
| Catalysts, regime and positioning | 5% | 3 | A binary merger process is the only re-rating path, against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury and a VIX of 17.20 | S24, S23, S135 |

The weighting is deliberate. A heavy weight on valuation is right because at the current multiple the entry price, not the technology, dominates a five-year return. The governance weight reflects what a standard framework misses: the controlling shareholder's compensation is tied to market-capitalisation milestones, so management is paid for the narrative that supports the multiple rather than for per-share cash flow, and a change of control accelerates the award. Business quality scores 6 rather than 8 because the strongest part of the franchise, energy storage, is a small and shrinking share of revenue in dollars, while vehicles are losing share in the region that sets global prices.

The counter-evidence deserves its own paragraph, because the score could be too harsh in one place: energy earns a 33.1% gross margin at $210M of revenue per GWh, Tesla's $34,436 cost per vehicle is below every Western competitor, and a triple-digit multiple has persisted for two years without mean reversion. If energy revenue doubles and FSD licensing adds a second stream, the core could be worth $70 a share rather than $42.50. That moves the composite by less than half a point, because the core is 11% of the price and the autonomy premium is 11.3 times the leader's mark. The risks run both ways: if the bear branch materialises — autonomy written down, vehicles valued at GM's multiple, the Terafab commitment drawn — value collapses to a small fraction of today's price and Reduce becomes Sell or Avoid at any size. The base case carries $259B of autonomy on a probability-weighted blend of four branches, not the $40B regional fleet alone: at regional-only autonomy the base would be $52.50 and the probability-weighted value $84, and the recommendation would not change. The only branch that lifts the score above 5 is the merger: a negotiated ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price would justify Hold, with the position capped because a failed vote returns the stock to a level set by the operating business. [S6, S63, S120]

Kelly arithmetic at the current price is negative, so the correct unconstrained position is zero. The table sets out the inputs.

| Sizing measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Probability-weighted value | $111 a share on 25/50/25 ($212 / $107 / $19) | S6, S120 |
| Expected return from $403.30 | -72% | S15 |
| Expected value including the merger branch at 40% | $253 a share | S135 |
| Kelly fraction | negative in every branch; constrained to 0 | S6, S120 |
| Residual cap where a mandate requires exposure | 0.5% of net asset value | arithmetic on S6 |
| Fund loss at a 95% bear case on a 0.5% position | -0.48% of net asset value | S6 |

The regime argues for the smaller end of any range: the ten-year Treasury at 4.99%, up 0.93 points in twelve months, raises the discount rate on cash flows arriving after 2030, the S&P 500 is 1.6% below its high with the VIX at the 52nd percentile, and consumer discretionary has lagged the index by 0.3 points over three months. [S24, S23, S22]

### Sensitivity: what moves the value

::: sensitivity
| Rank | Assumption | Base | What would disprove it | Impact on value | Impact level | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031 (15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile implied by the price) | Autonomy at $259B across four weighted branches; 769 registered vehicles; the regional branch alone is $40B, or $52.50 a share | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | high | Registrations flat near 769; no fare disclosure | S4, S6, S137 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | 18.1% in Q3 2026 | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | -$8 a share per 100 bp; -$34 on a 4-point miss | high | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% | 33.1% in Q3 2026, part of it tariff refunds and warranty reimbursements | Q4 margin below 25% once one-offs lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | high | Revenue -16% year over year to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | $13.0B in nine months; above $20B for 2026 | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | medium | Terafab's $16.8B first phase outside the budget | S4, S134 |
| 5 | No value-transferring exchange ratio and dilution of 10.7% from the 2025 award | No terms agreed; a 50%-of-all-shares vote | Ratio struck below market, or new award tranches | -$40 to -$80 a share | high | Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers | S5, S135, S138 |
:::

::: takeaways
1. **Reduce, not Buy:** 89% of the $403.30 price — $1,424B — is an autonomy option valued at 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, while the vehicle and energy business is worth $42.50 a share [S15, S120].
2. **Size to zero:** the probability-weighted value is $111 and the Kelly fraction is negative in every branch, so new money buys nothing and an existing position is capped at 0.5% of net asset value [S6, S120].
3. **Four events would change the call:** a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless permit, an ex-credit operating margin back in double digits, or an exchange ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price [S135, S4].
:::

Five actions would settle the open questions, and each has a date or a document attached. The next results release should be read for a robotaxi revenue line, a fleet count and a fare; a fourth consecutive quarter without one is the clearest signal that the option is not converting. The California DMV and CPUC filings should be checked for a driverless deployment permit, because the current service runs on a limousine authority and no AV permit is listed. The special committees' 8-K should be read for the exchange ratio, the advisers and the treatment of unvested award shares. The annual 10-K should be read for capital expenditure guidance, the Terafab contribution and whether payables reverse. The annual-meeting proxy should be read for the per-tranche thresholds of the CEO award that the text extraction dropped. The conditions for investing are concrete: a share price below the probability-weighted value, or a disclosed robotaxi business whose revenue and cost per mile support the free cash flow the reverse DCF requires. Until one exists, the evidence supports a reduced position and a waiting stance; the score is a statement about the price, not about the engineering.

TSLA closed at $403.30 on 2026-10-29, a $1,594.1B market capitalisation and a $1,558.0B enterprise value, 19% below its 52-week high of $498.83 and 36% above the low of $297.38. The stock is up 14.3% in a month and 30.6% in three, but down 11.3% year to date and 8.4% over twelve months, and the Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-21 — revenue $28.046B, adjusted EPS $0.48 against a $0.45 consensus — have been bought. The regime frames the call: the S&P 500 sits at 7,720.39, up 12.8% year to date and 1.6% below its high, the VIX is 17.20 at the 52nd percentile, and the ten-year Treasury yields 4.99%, up 0.93 points in twelve months, a discount rate that penalises cash flows arriving after 2030. [S15, S141, S22, S23, S24]

### Reduce, at a fraction of the size

Tesla's vehicles, energy and services businesses are worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts; the remaining $356 of the $403.30 price — $1,424B, or 89% of the equity — is an option on robotaxi and robotics that discloses no revenue. Our probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close, on a base that carries $259B of autonomy across four weighted branches rather than the $40B regional fleet alone; even a 40% chance of a premium SpaceX exchange lifts expected value only to $253. The action is to trim rather than to sell short: the option has real value, the balance sheet is not the constraint, and a negotiated exchange ratio could pay $443-487 without any operating delivery. [S6, S15, S120]

Confidence is high on the reported numbers — three years of filings, a third quarter reconciled line by line, and a timestamped market price — medium on the 11-14% cost of capital, and low on anything that requires sizing robotaxi revenue, because no revenue line, fare or cost per mile is disclosed. The 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target and a published range from $128.11 to $600, so the disagreement is about the distribution, not the mean. [S141, S144, S4]

:::

::: briefing

| Three risks | A two-year autonomy slip that takes the stock to the $19 bear case, an ex-credit margin below 15% if US incentives of $6,594 a unit cannot hold price, and 10.7% award dilution plus a failed merger vote that would return the stock below $300 | S4, S5, S135 |

What is Tesla's revenue per robotaxi per week in Austin, and what share of those rides runs without a safety driver?

Without that number the autonomy value cannot be tested against a cost per mile, and every scenario above the bear case rests on a third-party fleet count rather than on unit economics. A disclosed figure that supports the revenue per mile the price implies would move the base case toward the bull case; a quarter of silence after three years of promises would move it toward the bear case.
:::

::: takeaways
1. **The price is the whole debate:** $356 of the $403.30 — 89% — is autonomy and robotics valued at 11.3 times Waymo's $126B, and the core business is worth $42.50 on vehicles at 1.0x sales, energy at 3.5x and net cash at book [S15, S120].
2. **Cash is thinner than it looks:** 61% less free cash flow in nine months, a $7,332M payables stretch and a 5.5% ROIC against an 11-14% cost of capital, with $20B+ of capex still to come [S4].

:::

The follow-up diligence is dated and specific: a robotaxi revenue line, a fleet count and a fare in the next results release; a California driverless deployment permit from the DMV and CPUC filings, where the current service runs on a limousine authority; the exchange ratio, advisers and treatment of unvested awards in the special committees' 8-K; capital expenditure guidance, the Terafab contribution and any payables reversal in the annual 10-K; and the per-tranche thresholds of the CEO award in the proxy for the 2026-12-03 annual meeting. The rating is a statement about the price of an option, not about the quality of the engineering: the vehicle, cell and storage businesses are real, and they are worth about a tenth of what the market pays.

Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. That split constrains the investment case: no plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable for a different reason and on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism and the size: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, 2.8% lower year on year, with incentives at 12% of price, $6,594 per vehicle, and the EV premium over comparable petrol vehicles down to $4,847, or 9.7%. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a run-rate near 0.95 million units a year at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank at a high-single-digit rate in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, and hybrids took 36.6% and plug-in hybrids 10%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September alone, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6% a year earlier. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced in 2026 by the energy-price shock that lifted European electric-car sales close to 30% in the first quarter. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, in line with the market, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved in Tesla's favour for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base whose utilisation depends on demand outside China, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

### Market size: $950 billion of cars, $83 billion of storage

The 2026 market size is $950 billion for electric cars and $82.7 billion for grid storage, measured at Tesla's realised prices because no agency publishes revenue; both are upper-bound proxies, and the battery-electric slice of the three regions where Tesla sells — the actual serviceable market — is not published as a split, so it is bounded rather than measured.

The US row is the firmest because it uses an actual transaction price; the global and EU rows overstate revenue per unit because Tesla prices above the market average. arguments.markdown:
Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. No plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable for a different reason and on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, 2.8% lower year on year, with incentives at 12% of price, $6,594 per vehicle, and the EV premium over comparable petrol vehicles down to 9.7%. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a run-rate near 0.95 million units a year at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank at a high-single-digit rate in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, while hybrids took 36.6% and plug-in hybrids 10%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September alone, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6% a year earlier. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced in 2026 by the energy-price shock that lifted European electric-car sales close to 30% in the first quarter. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, in line with the market, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved in Tesla's favour for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

### Market size: $950 billion of cars, $83 billion of storage

The 2026 market size is $950 billion for electric cars and $82.7 billion for grid storage, measured at Tesla's realised prices because no agency publishes revenue; both are upper-bound proxies, and the battery-electric slice of the three regions where Tesla sells is not published as a split, so the table bounds Tesla's obtainable revenue rather than measuring the serviceable market. Grid storage is the only pool growing faster than Tesla can supply: 353.4 GWh of deployments are expected in 2026, up 28% on 275.3 GWh in 2025, and Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months, 14% of the market, against Megafactory Texas capacity of 50 GWh. The budget owner is a utility or independent power producer on a multi-year contract behind an interconnection queue, so demand is sticky but price-sensitive: energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Autonomous ride-hailing cannot yet be sized from disclosure: Waymo reports about 4,000 vehicles in service and 500,000 paid rides a week, roughly 26 million a year, and even at $100 a ride that is $2.6 billion, 0.3% of the electric-car TAM, while Tesla discloses no fare, booking or paid-ride figure. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at about 1,000, an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S100, S108, S4, S59, S150, S152, S153].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 退出策略分析 Exit Strategy Analysis (exit, revision 5 by Valuation Analyst, 8,450 characters)
Tesla offers no cash exit at $1.59 trillion. It has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation, and its entire $45.4B of cash and short-term investments would retire 2.85% of the 3.953B shares outstanding. The largest buyout ever completed — Electronic Arts at $55B in August 2026 — is 3.4% of Tesla's market capitalisation, so no financial sponsor can write this cheque, and no automaker can either: GM and Ford together are $118.4B, 7.4% of Tesla. What remains is a sale into a market that trades $14.0B of Tesla a day, or a share exchange into SpaceX, and both leave the return hostage to a re-rating that five years have not delivered. [S3, S130]

### The company returns nothing, and cannot return much

Tesla's 10-K states that it has never declared or paid a cash dividend, does not anticipate doing so, and purchased no equity securities in fiscal 2025. Trailing free cash flow of $3,303M is a 0.2% yield on the capitalisation, and nine-month capital expenditure of $13,014M runs at 2.1x depreciation: the cash is going into factories, cells and training compute, not to holders. Against GM's 12.4% total shareholder yield and Ford's 5.9%, Tesla's is zero. Even a maximal buyback using the whole cash pile would move the share count by less than three points, and it would leave a company spending $17B a year on capital projects with no liquidity buffer. Capital return is a governance choice, and the controlling shareholder has consistently chosen reinvestment. [S6]

### The exit that always works is the tape

The secondary market is the only channel that is always open. Tesla trades 36.96M shares and $14.0B a day over twenty days, so a $500M position is 3.6% of a single day's value and no holder is trapped by liquidity. Short interest of 69.35M shares, 2.19% of the float and 2.2 days to cover, means the marginal seller is not fighting a crowded short either. Passive ownership is a flow that follows the index and the price rather than a bid that supports it; Tesla's exact float-adjusted S&P 500 weight is not disclosed in the sources retrieved, and after the top ten names reached 39.03% of the index on 2026-10-10 the marginal index buyer is a shrinking share of demand. [S15, S114]

### No control buyer exists, at any price

A cash takeover is arithmetically out of reach. The pieces themselves are worth $170B on the sum of the parts — vehicles at 1.0x sales, energy at 3.5x, net cash at book — and a control buyer for those assets alone would pay $200-250B with a premium, which is one-eighth of the current capitalisation and therefore not a route to today's price. Alphabet, at $3,493.5B, is the only US company with the balance sheet to write a $1.6T cheque, and it is the closest competitor in autonomous driving, which makes antitrust the binding constraint rather than price. Musk's 19.8% stake and 207.5M pledged shares mean nothing happens without him, and a hostile approach is legally and financially impossible at this size. [S5, S6]

### The one live route is a share exchange with SpaceX

On 2026-10-21 both boards formed special committees to explore a combination, days after Musk called the idea a "good idea" on the third-quarter earnings call. SpaceX listed on 2026-06-12 at $135 a share and a $1.77T valuation, reached $2.1T on its first day, and the combined group would be worth well over $3 trillion. At those marks Tesla holders would own 43% of the equity — but they would exchange one-share-one-vote stock for a company where super-voting shares give Musk about 84% of the vote, against 20% at Tesla. arguments.markdown:
Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. No plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a run-rate near 0.95 million units a year at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank at a high-single-digit rate in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, while hybrids took 36.6%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6%. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced by the 2026 energy-price shock that lifted European electric-car sales close to 30% in Q1. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved Tesla's way for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

### Market size: $950 billion of cars, $83 billion of storage

The 2026 market size is $950 billion for electric cars and $82.7 billion for grid storage, measured at Tesla's realised prices as a proxy because no agency publishes revenue; the battery-electric slice of the three regions where Tesla sells is not published, so the table bounds obtainable revenue rather than measuring the serviceable market. Grid storage is the only pool growing faster than Tesla can supply: 353.4 GWh of deployments are expected in 2026, up 28% on 275.3 GWh in 2025, and Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months, 14% of the market, against 50 GWh of Texas capacity. The budget owner is a utility or independent power producer behind an interconnection queue, so demand is sticky but price-sensitive: energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Ride-hailing cannot yet be sized from disclosure: Waymo reports about 4,000 vehicles in service and 500,000 paid rides a week, roughly 26 million a year; even at $100 a ride that is $2.6 billion, 0.3% of the electric-car TAM, while Tesla discloses no fare, booking or paid-ride figure. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at about 1,000, an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S100, S108, S4, S59, S150, S152, S153].

| Market | Market size (2026E) | Method and basis | Growth | Tesla's obtainable revenue (SOM) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global electric cars (TAM) | $950 billion | 23.0M units × $41,300 realised automotive revenue per unit; a proxy, not a market average | +15% units on 20.0M in 2025 | $72.9 billion: 1.77M units annualised × $41,300 | S100, S6 |
| US battery-electric (TAM) | $52.0 billion | 0.95M run-rate units × $54,754 average transaction price, August 2026 | −46.9% y/y volume in August 2026 | $50.0 billion: Q3 2026 US revenue of $12,495 million annualised | S98, S103, S4 |
| EU battery-electric (TAM) | $101.6 billion | 2.46M units annualised × $41,300 proxy | +40.5% y/y in H1 2026 | Not disclosed by region | S99, S6 |
| Grid battery storage (TAM) | $82.7 billion | 353.4 GWh × $234/kWh realised energy revenue | +28% GWh on 275.3 GWh in 2025 | $11.2 billion: 48 GWh annualised × $234 | S108, S4 |

| Region | Market size (year) | Growth | Tesla's position | Barriers | Key competitors | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| United States | 0.95M BEV a year (2026) | 6% share vs 10%; volume −46.9% in August 2026 | Entered; 51.7% of EV sales; revenue −14.4% in Q3 2026 | Credit repealed 2025-09-30; import tariffs; state ZEV rules | GM, Hyundai-Kia, Toyota, Rivian | S98, S103 |
| China | 9.5M NEV retail (2026E) | −13% in H1 2026; NEV 65.1% of July sales | Entered, local production; 381,088 retail in 9M, −11.9% | MIIT type approval; price competition; export rebate cuts | BYD, Geely, Xiaomi, Li Auto | S101, S102 |
| EU/EFTA | 2.46M BEV (2026E) | +40.5% in H1 2026; 21.7% share | Entered; 153,978 in 9M, +51%; 4.6% of panel new cars | CO2 mandate 2025-2027; tariffs on China-built BEVs | Volkswagen, Stellantis, Hyundai-Kia, BYD | S99, S104 |
| Grid storage | 353.4 GWh (2026E) | +28%; 108 GW added in 2025, +40% | Entered; 36.0 GWh in 9M; Texas at 50 GWh | Cell tariffs under OBBBA; interconnection queues | CATL, BYD, Fluence, Sungrow | S106, S108, S4 |
| Robotaxi | Not disclosed; Waymo 500,000 paid rides a week | From a small base; no audited bookings | Entered: Austin 2026-09-03; 1,051 Texas registrations 2026-10-27 | State AV permits; city rules; NHTSA DP26010 | Waymo, Zoox, Baidu Apollo Go, Pony.ai | S59, S150 |

The counter-case does not overturn the judgement: if US battery-electric share holds for four quarters, the credit will have been worth two-fifths of US demand, and a purpose-built Cybercab could compress cost per paid mile faster than Waymo's retrofit fleet, bringing the robotaxi market forward. Confidence is high on the US and European unit data, medium on China because retail and wholesale definitions diverge, and low on robotaxi because no operator discloses audited paid rides or bookings. Three open diligence questions remain: what did US battery-electric share print in September-October 2026? What share of Giga Shanghai output was exported in Q3 2026? What was Tesla's Megapack realised price per kWh excluding tariff refunds?

::: evidence
**US battery-electric demand stepped down to a new level after the credit expired and has not recovered a year later**

US BEV share of light-duty sales was 6% in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8%; the luxury segment fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. Cox Automotive recorded a $54,754 average transaction price with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle, 88% of the $7,500 credit, yet August volume still fell 46.9% year on year to 78,895 units [S98, S103].
:::

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. No plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a 0.95 million unit annual run-rate at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, while hybrids took 36.6%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6%. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced by the 2026 energy-price shock. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved Tesla's way for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

### Market size: $950 billion of cars, $83 billion of storage

The 2026 market size is $950 billion for electric cars and $82.7 billion for grid storage, measured at Tesla's realised prices as a proxy because no agency publishes revenue; global electric-car units rise from an implied 16.7 million in 2024 to 23.0 million in 2026, a 17.4% compound annual growth rate, and the battery-electric slice of the three regions where Tesla sells is not published, so the table bounds obtainable revenue rather than measuring the serviceable market. Grid storage is the only pool growing faster than Tesla can supply: 353.4 GWh of deployments are expected in 2026, up 28% on 275.3 GWh in 2025, and Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months, 14% of the market, against 50 GWh of Texas capacity. The budget owner is a utility or independent power producer behind an interconnection queue, so demand is sticky but price-sensitive: energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Ride-hailing cannot yet be sized from disclosure: Waymo reports 4,000 vehicles in service and 500,000 paid rides a week, 26 million a year; even at $100 a ride that is $2.6 billion, 0.3% of the electric-car TAM, while Tesla discloses no fare, booking or paid-ride figure. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S100, S108, S4, S59, S150, S152, S153].

What was Tesla's Megapack realised price per kWh excluding tariff refunds?

Cox Automotive recorded a $54,754 average transaction price with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle, 88% of the $7,500 credit, yet August volume still fell 46.9% year on year to 78,895 units [S98, S103].

Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. The proof is in the three numbers together: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5%, so share improves while the absolute business outside Europe shrinks [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% year on year to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were real but small: Toyota 4,964 units (+34.9% month on month), Chevrolet +30.3% and Cadillac +13.1%. Weaker EV programmes retreated after the credit expired and the survivor with the widest line and lowest cost took the share without cutting price. Rivian is the exception that could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in the second quarter of 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only it led 30,317 to 7,498 in every one of those countries, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse for Tesla: its Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Cost of automotive sales was $16,570 million in Q3 2026 for 486,532 deliveries, $34,060 per vehicle, against automotive sales revenue of $41,300 per unit (up from $40,955) and automotive gross margin of 18.5%, up from 17.0%. That is a healthy margin at a premium price point, and it sits 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the cleanest measure of how far Tesla's cost base is from the low end. The margin is protected by mix and software rather than price: FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. A price war in the $25,000-35,000 band would be fought on a cost base Tesla cannot currently match [S4, S6, S101].
