arguments.markdown:
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were small: Toyota 4,964 units (+34.9% month on month), Chevrolet +30.3% and Cadillac +13.1%. Weaker EV programmes retreated after the credit expired and the survivor with the widest line and lowest cost took the share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only it led 30,317 to 7,498 in every one of those countries, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse for Tesla: its Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Cost of automotive sales was $16,570 million for 486,532 deliveries, $34,060 per vehicle, against automotive sales revenue of $41,300 per unit (up from $40,955) and automotive gross margin of 18.5%, up from 17.0%. That is a healthy margin at a premium price point, and it sits 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the measure of the cost gap. The margin is protected by mix and software rather than price: FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. A price war in the $25,000-35,000 band would be fought on a cost base Tesla cannot currently match [S4, S6, S101].

### Storage and autonomy are where the advantage is thinnest

In grid storage the pricing power sits with the cell makers: CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of energy-storage batteries in the first half of 2026, up 81%, for 27.1% of the global ESS battery market, while Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months and its energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Tesla's differentiation is integration and delivery speed, not cell cost. In autonomy the gap is disclosed scale: Waymo reports 4,000 vehicles in service and 500,000 paid rides a week, while Baidu's Apollo Go operates in more than 10 Chinese cities and Tesla publishes no paid-ride count. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S81, S4, S59, S150, S152, S153].

| Robotaxi | Tesla emerges | Waymo: 4,000 vehicles, 500,000 paid rides a week | Baidu Apollo Go: more than 10 cities | Zoox and Pony.ai | Tesla Cybercab | S59, S6 |

The counter-case is that Tesla is converting rather than losing advantage: its US and European share gains came while rivals retreated, automotive gross margin rose year on year, and the Chinese price war ended with more than a dozen automakers raising prices, removing the deflation that hurt it most. That is partly right but does not change the conclusion: the share gains are in shrinking pools and the margin gain is mix-driven, not price-driven. Confidence is high on the US and European share data, medium on the China comparison because retail and wholesale definitions differ, and low on the autonomy comparison because no operator discloses audited paid rides. Two diligence questions follow: Tesla's US EV share in Q4 2026 once Toyota's bZ and Chevrolet's Bolt ramp, and how much of BYD's European volume is plug-in hybrid under the 2027 CO2 review?

plan.decision_question: Is Tesla gaining or losing competitive advantage in vehicles, energy and autonomy, and what does that do to pricing power?
plan.thesis_sentence: Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week.
plan.why_different: This section maps competitors product by product and tests pricing power; the market section sizes the pools and the other sections cover the firm's own technology, financials and valuation.
plan.mechanism: Scale and vertical integration set cost per vehicle; Chinese OEMs' lower cost base and PHEV breadth compress Tesla's price umbrella; in storage the cell makers hold pricing power; in autonomy permits and paid-ride utilisation decide scale.
plan.comparison_set: BYD, Geely, Xiaomi, GM, Hyundai-Kia and Rivian in vehicles; CATL in cells; Waymo, Baidu Apollo Go and Zoox in autonomy; Tesla's own 2025 share and margin.
plan.counter_evidence: Tesla's share gains and margin expansion show conversion rather than loss, the Chinese price war is ending, and a purpose-built Cybercab could beat Waymo on cost per mile.
plan.visual: Competitor table followed by the SWOT quad.
plan.prohibited: huge market; fierce competition; well positioned; clear leader; about/roughly/nearly; vague counts; unsourced share claims

queries: Tesla US EV market share August 2026 Cox Automotive
BYD Europe registrations September 2026 Tesla 45,523
China Model Y vs Geely Xingyuan sales February-July 2026 price
Tesla Q3 2026 automotive gross margin cost per vehicle
CATL global energy storage battery market share H1 2026
Waymo fleet 4,000 vehicles 500,000 paid rides a week
Texas DMV Tesla Robotaxi authorised vehicles Cybercab October 2026
Tesla brand politicisation Tesla Takedown study 2026

rows.benchmark: July 2026 share; pre-credit 2025 share of about 49% in a market twice the size.
rows.confidence: high: Cox Automotive monthly data and EIA volume data agree.
rows.finding: Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market down 46.9% year on year to 78,895 units; Toyota sold 4,964 units (+34.9% month on month), Chevrolet +30.3% and Cadillac +13.1%.
rows.follow_up: What is Tesla's US EV share in Q4 2026 once Toyota's bZ and Chevrolet's Bolt ramp?
rows.implication: US share is defensible inside a smaller pool, but the pool is 46.9% smaller and Rivian's 215,000-unit plant can take share as it ramps.
rows.mechanism: Weaker EV programmes retreated after the credit expired; the survivor with the widest line and lowest cost took share without cutting price, so share gain signals attrition rather than pricing power.
rows.weakens: A single month; Toyota's and Rivian's ramps could reverse the gain; Tesla's own volume fell with the market.

rows.benchmark: BYD's 39,583 total registrations against 7,498 battery-electric units.
rows.confidence: medium: panel definitions and brand attribution vary by country.
rows.finding: In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only led 30,317 to 7,498; Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier.
rows.follow_up: How much of BYD's European volume is plug-in hybrid under the 2027 CO2 review?
rows.implication: Tesla leads the European BEV contest in 2026 but BYD is the five-year threat because it can attack below Model Y and move up.
rows.mechanism: BYD's route is powertrain breadth and price rather than a better battery car; the CO2 mandate rewards both BEVs and, partly, PHEVs, giving BYD two ways to comply.

rows.benchmark: Geely's Xingyuan at just under RMB 100,000, about 38% of the Model Y's RMB 263,500 entry price.
rows.confidence: medium: retail and wholesale definitions differ; model-level prices are list prices.
rows.finding: Tesla's Model Y sold more than 180,000 units in China from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000; Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September.
rows.follow_up: What is Tesla's China gross margin after the export rebate cut?
rows.implication: Tesla cannot compete below the premium band on cost; China is an export base, not a share-expansion market.
rows.mechanism: Chinese OEMs carry a structurally lower cost base and can price a mass-segment car at a third of Model Y while still selling more units than it.

rows.benchmark: Geely's sub-RMB 100,000 bestseller; BYD's in-house LFP cells.
rows.confidence: high: company filing figures.
rows.finding: Cost of automotive sales was $16,570 million for 486,532 deliveries, $34,060 per vehicle, against automotive revenue of $41,300 per unit and an automotive gross margin of 18.5%, up from 17.0%; FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million and services revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million.
rows.follow_up: What happens to the 18.5% margin if Tesla launches a $25,000-30,000 model?
rows.implication: Pricing power is confined to the premium band; a price war below $35,000 would be fought on a cost base Tesla cannot match today.
rows.mechanism: Premium mix, software and services protect the margin; the cost base is 2.3 times the Chinese volume bestseller's retail price, so Tesla cannot follow a price cut down-market.

rows.benchmark: CATL's 27.1% share; Tesla's 36.0 GWh against 125.0 GWh of CATL cells in H1 2026.
rows.confidence: high on CATL and Tesla volumes, medium on the ESS cell share denominators.
rows.finding: CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of energy-storage batteries in the first half of 2026, up 81%, for 27.1% of the global ESS battery market, while Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months and energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 on lower Megapack prices and tariff refunds.
rows.follow_up: What is Tesla's Megapack price per kWh excluding tariff refunds?
rows.implication: Tesla is a scale follower in cells and a price-taker on Megapack pricing; its 33.1% energy gross margin comes from integration, not cell cost.
rows.mechanism: Cell makers with LFP scale set the cost floor; Tesla differentiates on integration, grid-forming software and delivery speed, which supports margin but not price.

rows.benchmark: Waymo's 4,000 vehicles and 500,000 paid rides a week; Baidu Apollo Go in more than 10 Chinese cities.
rows.confidence: medium: fleet counts from a state registry and a tracker; no operator discloses audited paid rides.
rows.finding: Waymo reports 4,000 vehicles in service and 500,000 paid rides a week; Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records), NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, and Tesla publishes no paid-ride count.
rows.follow_up: How many paid rides a week does Tesla run in Austin, and at what fare?
rows.implication: Tesla trails Waymo by roughly four times on vehicles and by an undisclosed margin on rides; autonomy is optionality, not proven advantage.
rows.mechanism: Permits and paid-ride utilisation decide scale; Texas self-certification lets Tesla register cars quickly, but registration is not service and California still lists Tesla only for testing with a driver.
rows.source_type: independent tracker plus primary (NHTSA) and independent (TechCrunch)

rows.benchmark: Tesla's 2026 Europe registrations (+51%) against the politicisation finding.
rows.confidence: medium: one peer-reviewed study, and the European data cut against a strong brand-damage effect.
rows.finding: A 2026 peer-reviewed study of the Tesla Takedown campaign finds brand politicisation shifted partisan consumer preference against Tesla in the United States.
rows.follow_up: What is Tesla's US brand consideration among independent and Republican buyers in 2026?
rows.implication: Brand damage caps the US recovery and raises the cost of defending share, even if European sales are holding.
rows.mechanism: Partisan identity attaches to the product, so a slice of buyers avoids the brand regardless of price or product quality.
rows.weakens: Tesla's European registrations rose 51% in 2026 and US share rose to 51.7%, so the effect may be confined to a segment rather than the whole market.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 市场与行业分析 Market & Industry Analysis (market, revision 6 by Market Analyst, 8,655 characters)
Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. No plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a 0.95 million unit annual run-rate at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, while hybrids took 36.6%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6%. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced by the 2026 energy-price shock. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved Tesla's way for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

### Market size: $950 billion of cars, $83 billion of storage

The 2026 market size is $950 billion for electric cars and $82.7 billion for grid storage, measured at Tesla's realised prices as a proxy because no agency publishes revenue; global electric-car units rise from an implied 16.7 million in 2024 to 23.0 million in 2026, a 17.4% compound annual growth rate, and the battery-electric slice of the three regions where Tesla sells is not published, so the table bounds obtainable revenue rather than measuring the serviceable market. Grid storage is the only pool growing faster than Tesla can supply: 353.4 GWh of deployments are expected in 2026, up 28% on 275.3 GWh in 2025, and Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months, 14% of the market, against 50 GWh of Texas capacity. The budget owner is a utility or independent power producer behind an interconnection queue, so demand is sticky but price-sensitive: energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Ride-hailing cannot yet be sized from disclosure: Waymo reports 4,000 vehicles in service and 500,000 paid rides a week, 26 million a year; even at $100 a ride that is $2.6 billion, 0.3% of the electric-car TAM, while Tesla discloses no fare, booking or paid-ride figure. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S100, S108, S4, S59, S150, S152, S153].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 竞争格局 Competitive Landscape (competition, revision 4 by Market Analyst, 8,850 characters)
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were small: Toyota 4,964 units (+34.9% month on month), Chevrolet +30.3% and Cadillac +13.1%. Weaker EV programmes retreated after the credit expired and the survivor with the widest line and lowest cost took the share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only it led 30,317 to 7,498 in every one of those countries, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse for Tesla: its Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Cost of automotive sales was $16,570 million for 486,532 deliveries, $34,060 per vehicle, against automotive sales revenue of $41,300 per unit (up from $40,955) and automotive gross margin of 18.5%, up from 17.0%. That is a healthy margin at a premium price point, and it sits 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the measure of the cost gap. The margin is protected by mix and software rather than price: FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. A price war in the $25,000-35,000 band would be fought on a cost base Tesla cannot currently match [S4, S6, S101].

### Storage and autonomy are where the advantage is thinnest

In grid storage the pricing power sits with the cell makers: CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of energy-storage batteries in the first half of 2026, up 81%, for 27.1% of the global ESS battery market, while Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months and its energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Tesla's differentiation is integration and delivery speed, not cell cost. In autonomy the gap is disclosed scale: Waymo reports 4,000 vehicles in service and 500,000 paid rides a week, while Baidu's Apollo Go operates in more than 10 Chinese cities and Tesla publishes no paid-ride count. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S81, S4, S59, S150, S152, S153].

| Robotaxi | Tesla emerges | Waymo: 4,000 vehicles, 500,000 paid rides a week | Baidu Apollo Go: more than 10 cities | Zoox and Pony.ai | Tesla Cybercab | S59, S6 |

The counter-case is that Tesla is converting rather than losing advantage: its US and European share gains came while rivals retreated, automotive gross margin rose year on year, and the Chinese price war ended with more than a dozen automakers raising prices, removing the deflation that hurt it most. That is partly right but does not change the conclusion: the share gains are in shrinking pools and the margin gain is mix-driven, not price-driven. Confidence is high on the US and European share data, medium on the China comparison because retail and wholesale definitions differ, and low on the autonomy comparison because no operator discloses audited paid rides. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 技术与产品 Technology & Product (technology_product, revision 6 by Product Analyst, 8,800 characters)
Tesla's technology is proven where it is a manufacturing problem — dry-electrode cells, Megapack integration — and unproven where the valuation sits, judged against two comparison sets: Waymo in autonomy and BYD in manufacturing cost. Compared with Waymo, Tesla has 2.0 million cumulative autonomous miles against 500,000 paid rides a week; compared with BYD, its 486,532 quarterly deliveries trail BYD's 762,478 electric cars. Its paid driverless permit exists in one state. The technology justifies a premium to a capital-intensive manufacturer in energy and process engineering; it does not yet justify the multiple of a software platform [S6, S76, S107].

### How FSD works, and where it stops

FSD (Supervised) is vision-only: eight cameras feed an end-to-end neural network that outputs steering, acceleration and braking, trained on video from 10.2 million delivered vehicles and run on in-house inference silicon. There is no lidar or radar. Two problems stay unsolved. Cameras blinded by rain, fog or low sun are the subject of NHTSA's Engineering Analysis EA26002, opened 2026-03-19 over 13 crashes in 2.88 million vehicles, testing whether the system detects the degradation. The second is the reliability increment that permits removing the supervisor, which is why customer-owned unsupervised driving moved to Q2 2027. Tesla's October 2026 report claims 6,006,200 miles per major collision, a company-computed, non-fault-based figure the regulator has not verified [S58, S80].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |

| FSD miles per major collision | 6,006,200 (North America, October 2026) | Company report, FSD-engaged miles | S58 |
| Cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles | 2.0 million (to 2026-09-30) | Company quarterly update | S6 |
| FSD subscriptions and attach | 1.74 million; more than 75% of North American deliveries | Company KPI, excludes free trials | S6 |
| 4680 cell output and density | More than 1 million cells/week; more than 40 GWh; 272 Wh/kg | Giga Texas line data and teardown estimates | S56 |

### Robotaxi: a real service, on one state's terms

Paid Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03. Tesla publishes no fleet count, so the only dated line is third-party: 769 Teslas registered for autonomous use in Texas on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, after 44 active across seven metros in H1 2026; Tesla claimed 300-plus Cybercabs in Austin on 2026-10-10, and NHTSA's DP26010 (2026-10-09) describes a monitored fleet of 1,000. The count is unconfirmed by Tesla or Texas DMV, which disclose no fares, trips per vehicle, utilisation or insurance cost per mile. Permits remain the constraint: Texas allows self-certified commercial driverless operation, while California lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC for testing with a driver only (2026-10-22) [S73, S74, S82, S107].

| Dimension | Tesla | Benchmark | What it means | Source |

| Weekly paid rides | Not disclosed | Waymo: 500,000 a week on about 3,000 vehicles | At 5 miles a ride, 2.5 million rider-only miles weekly — more than Tesla's cumulative total | S107 |
| Cell performance | 4680: 272 Wh/kg, 10-80% in 35-40 minutes | CATL Qilin 3: full charge in six minutes | Tesla leads on cost, trails on density and charging | S56 |
| BEV volume, Q3 2026 | 486,532 units | BYD 762,478 passenger BEVs, +30.89% year over year | Cost leadership has moved to China | S76 |

### Cells: a cost moat, not a performance one

Giga Texas runs above one million 4680 cells a week at more than 40 GWh of installed capacity, and since January 2026 both electrodes use the dry process in production — a step CATL, Panasonic, LG and Samsung SDI have not taken to commercial scale. The economics are real: electrode cost 50% lower at full scale, 41% less line capex and more than 30% less factory energy. The product is not: energy density trails by 10-15%, charging is slower than Panasonic 2170 packs, yields above 90% sit below the 98% of mature producers, and Tesla still buys CATL LFP and Panasonic or LG 2170 cells for Shanghai and Fremont Model Y. Battery availability, not demand, remained the stated limit on 2026 volume [S56].

### Patents: thin disclosure, deliberately

### Product inventory

| Megapack, Megablock | Commercial | 2019; Megapack 3 in 2025 | $2.881bn segment Q3 2026 | 33.1% | Ramp 50 GWh Texas | S4, S6 |
| Optimus | Early production | 2026-10-21 | None disclosed | None disclosed | 20,000 units a week by end-2027, company claim (2026-10-21), unverified | S57 |

### Energy is the proven technology

Megapack is the one line where Tesla holds a genuine integration advantage and prices it: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026 at a 33.1% gross margin, with 50 GWh of Texas capacity starting. arguments.markdown:
Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. No plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a 0.95 million unit annual run-rate at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, while hybrids took 36.6%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6%. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced by the 2026 energy-price shock. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved Tesla's way for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

### Market size: $950 billion of cars, $83 billion of storage

The 2026 market size is $950 billion for electric cars and $82.7 billion for grid storage, measured at Tesla's realised prices as a proxy because no agency publishes revenue; global electric-car units rise from an implied 16.7 million in 2024 to 23.0 million in 2026, a 17.4% compound annual growth rate, and the battery-electric slice of the three regions where Tesla sells is not published, so the table bounds obtainable revenue rather than measuring the serviceable market. Grid storage is the only pool growing faster than Tesla can supply: 353.4 GWh of deployments are expected in 2026, up 28% on 275.3 GWh in 2025, and Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months, 14% of the market, against 50 GWh of Texas capacity. The budget owner is a utility or independent power producer behind an interconnection queue, so demand is sticky but price-sensitive: energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Ride-hailing cannot yet be sized from disclosure: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, 26 million a year; even at $100 a ride that is $2.6 billion, 0.3% of the electric-car TAM, while Tesla discloses no fare, booking or paid-ride figure. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S100, S108, S4, S59, S150, S152, S153].

The counter-case does not overturn the judgement: if US battery-electric share holds for four quarters, the credit will have been worth two-fifths of US demand, and a purpose-built Cybercab could compress cost per paid mile faster than Waymo's retrofit fleet, bringing the robotaxi market forward. Confidence is high on the US and European unit data, medium on China because retail and wholesale definitions diverge, and low on robotaxi because no operator discloses audited paid rides or bookings. Three open diligence questions remain: what did US battery-electric share print in September-October 2026? What share of Giga Shanghai output was exported in Q3 2026? What was Tesla's Megapack realised price per kWh excluding tariff refunds?

::: evidence
**US battery-electric demand stepped down to a new level after the credit expired and has not recovered a year later**

US BEV share of light-duty sales was 6% in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8%; the luxury segment fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. Cox Automotive recorded a $54,754 average transaction price with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle, 88% of the $7,500 credit, yet August volume still fell 46.9% year on year to 78,895 units [S98, S103].
:::

arguments.markdown:
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were small: Toyota 4,964 units (+34.9% month on month), Chevrolet +30.3% and Cadillac +13.1%. Weaker EV programmes retreated after the credit expired and the survivor with the widest line and lowest cost took the share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only it led 30,317 to 7,498 in every one of those countries, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse for Tesla: its Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Cost of automotive sales was $16,570 million for 486,532 deliveries, $34,060 per vehicle, against automotive sales revenue of $41,300 per unit (up from $40,955) and automotive gross margin of 18.5%, up from 17.0%. That is a healthy margin at a premium price point, and it sits 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the measure of the cost gap. The margin is protected by mix and software rather than price: FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. A price war in the $25,000-35,000 band would be fought on a cost base Tesla cannot currently match [S4, S6, S101].

### Storage and autonomy are where the advantage is thinnest

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 技术与产品 Technology & Product (technology_product, revision 6 by Product Analyst, 8,800 characters)
Tesla's technology is proven where it is a manufacturing problem — dry-electrode cells, Megapack integration — and unproven where the valuation sits, judged against two comparison sets: Waymo in autonomy and BYD in manufacturing cost. Compared with Waymo, Tesla has 2.0 million cumulative autonomous miles against 500,000 paid rides a week; compared with BYD, its 486,532 quarterly deliveries trail BYD's 762,478 electric cars. Its paid driverless permit exists in one state. The technology justifies a premium to a capital-intensive manufacturer in energy and process engineering; it does not yet justify the multiple of a software platform [S6, S76, S107].

### How FSD works, and where it stops

FSD (Supervised) is vision-only: eight cameras feed an end-to-end neural network that outputs steering, acceleration and braking, trained on video from 10.2 million delivered vehicles and run on in-house inference silicon. There is no lidar or radar. Two problems stay unsolved. Cameras blinded by rain, fog or low sun are the subject of NHTSA's Engineering Analysis EA26002, opened 2026-03-19 over 13 crashes in 2.88 million vehicles, testing whether the system detects the degradation. The second is the reliability increment that permits removing the supervisor, which is why customer-owned unsupervised driving moved to Q2 2027. Tesla's October 2026 report claims 6,006,200 miles per major collision, a company-computed, non-fault-based figure the regulator has not verified [S58, S80].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| FSD miles per major collision | 6,006,200 (North America, October 2026) | Company report, FSD-engaged miles | S58 |
| Cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles | 2.0 million (to 2026-09-30) | Company quarterly update | S6 |
| FSD subscriptions and attach | 1.74 million; more than 75% of North American deliveries | Company KPI, excludes free trials | S6 |
| 4680 cell output and density | More than 1 million cells/week; more than 40 GWh; 272 Wh/kg | Giga Texas line data and teardown estimates | S56 |

### Robotaxi: a real service, on one state's terms

Paid Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03. Tesla publishes no fleet count, so the only dated line is third-party: 769 Teslas registered for autonomous use in Texas on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, after 44 active across seven metros in H1 2026; Tesla claimed 300-plus Cybercabs in Austin on 2026-10-10, and NHTSA's DP26010 (2026-10-09) describes a monitored fleet of 1,000. The count is unconfirmed by Tesla or Texas DMV, which disclose no fares, trips per vehicle, utilisation or insurance cost per mile. Permits remain the constraint: Texas allows self-certified commercial driverless operation, while California lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC for testing with a driver only (2026-10-22) [S73, S74, S82, S107].

| Dimension | Tesla | Benchmark | What it means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weekly paid rides | Not disclosed | Waymo: 500,000 a week on about 3,000 vehicles | At 5 miles a ride, 2.5 million rider-only miles weekly — more than Tesla's cumulative total | S107 |
| Cell performance | 4680: 272 Wh/kg, 10-80% in 35-40 minutes | CATL Qilin 3: full charge in six minutes | Tesla leads on cost, trails on density and charging | S56 |
| BEV volume, Q3 2026 | 486,532 units | BYD 762,478 passenger BEVs, +30.89% year over year | Cost leadership has moved to China | S76 |

### Cells: a cost moat, not a performance one

Giga Texas runs above one million 4680 cells a week at more than 40 GWh of installed capacity, and since January 2026 both electrodes use the dry process in production — a step CATL, Panasonic, LG and Samsung SDI have not taken to commercial scale. The economics are real: electrode cost 50% lower at full scale, 41% less line capex and more than 30% less factory energy. The product is not: energy density trails by 10-15%, charging is slower than Panasonic 2170 packs, yields above 90% sit below the 98% of mature producers, and Tesla still buys CATL LFP and Panasonic or LG 2170 cells for Shanghai and Fremont Model Y. Battery availability, not demand, remained the stated limit on 2026 volume [S56].

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fleet data and training set | 7 | 10.2 million vehicles and billions of FSD miles | 3-4 years | S6 |
| Dry-electrode process | 7 | Both electrodes dry above 90% yield; no rival at scale | 3 years | S56 |
| Vertical integration (cells, packs, chips) | 6 | Process know-how and capital; AI6 foundry dependence caps it | 3-5 years | S6, S79 |
| Driverless permits | 4 | Texas self-certification is easy; California and the EU are not | 1-2 years Texas, 3+ California | S73 |
| **Composite** | **6/10** | 3 years for the cell line, 2 for Megapack integration | **3 years of lead time** | S56, S73 |

### Patents: thin disclosure, deliberately

| Four PCT filings, published 2026-04-16 | Optimus Gen 3 forearm, wrist, joint and hand assemblies | WIPO/PCT | Priority 2024-10-10 | — | Published, national phase pending | 22 degrees of freedom per hand | S75 |
| US20260310299A1 | Flexible touch sensors for robotic hands | US | Not disclosed | — | Published 2025-10-08 | Tactile sensing | S75 |
| Maxwell portfolio (acquired 2019, $235m) | Dry electrode manufacturing IP | US | Pre-2019 | Granted, owned | In force | Underpins the 4680 dry process | S56 |

The 10-K rests the case on data, manufacturing cost and vertical integration, not patents; Musk said in April 2026 that the V3 hand would not use the patented Optimus design.

### Product inventory

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model 3/Y | Commercial | 2017-2020 | $20.09bn automotive sales Q3 2026; 478,237 units (98.3%) | 18.5% total automotive | Next-generation platform, no date | S6, S76 |
| Cybercab and Robotaxi | Early commercial | 2026-09-03, Austin | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Unsupervised customer cars Q2 2027 | S6, S57 |
| Megapack, Megablock | Commercial | 2019; Megapack 3 in 2025 | $2.881bn segment Q3 2026 | 33.1% | Ramp 50 GWh Texas | S4, S6 |
| Optimus | Early production | 2026-10-21 | None disclosed | None disclosed | 20,000 units a week by end-2027, company claim (2026-10-21), unverified | S57 |

### Energy is the proven technology

Megapack is the one line where Tesla holds a genuine integration advantage and prices it: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026 at a 33.1% gross margin, with 50 GWh of Texas capacity starting. The weak point is the order book, not the product: the 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified. A contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it; a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. Wood Mackenzie ranks Tesla second among integrators behind Sungrow, and revenue fell 16% to $2.881bn even as volume rose [S4, S6, S72].

::: evidence
**The Optimus output target is an unverified company claim, and the humanoid benchmark sits elsewhere.**

On the Q3 2026 call of 2026-10-21 Tesla set a target of 20,000 Optimus units a week by end-2027 and began early production, but it discloses no unit count, external customer, task list or revenue. A named customer, supplier orders at that volume or an Optimus revenue line would confirm it; another year of demonstration video and no billed unit would contradict it. Figure AI, valued at $39bn in September 2025, completed an 11-month Figure 02 deployment at BMW's Spartanburg plant contributing to more than 30,000 X3 vehicles, the external validation Optimus has not matched [S57, S149].
:::

### What would change the judgement

The strongest counter-case is that FSD is already monetised: attach, subscriptions and deferred revenue rose in Q3 2026. Against it, repeated NHTSA recalls on the 2026 Model Y show launch quality slipping, and the attach rate is North American only while China sales fell with FSD approval pending. Optimus is the thinner half of the autonomy branch: a production line and no external customer.

Diligence questions: what did Austin earn per robotaxi per week, how many Cybercabs ran without a monitor, and what fare, trips per vehicle and insurance cost per mile sit behind that revenue? What is blended pack cost per kWh? Does EA26002 end in a recall, and what would that do to the release date? Until the first two are answered, Tesla owns the best-proven manufacturing technology in the sector and has not proven the one the share price pays for."}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 市场与行业分析 Market & Industry Analysis (market, revision 7 by Market Analyst, 8,694 characters)
Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. No plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a 0.95 million unit annual run-rate at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, while hybrids took 36.6%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6%. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced by the 2026 energy-price shock. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved Tesla's way for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

### Market size: $950 billion of cars, $83 billion of storage

The 2026 market size is $950 billion for electric cars and $82.7 billion for grid storage, measured at Tesla's realised prices as a proxy because no agency publishes revenue; global electric-car units rise from an implied 16.7 million in 2024 to 23.0 million in 2026, a 17.4% compound annual growth rate, and the battery-electric slice of the three regions where Tesla sells is not published, so the table bounds obtainable revenue rather than measuring the serviceable market. Grid storage is the only pool growing faster than Tesla can supply: 353.4 GWh of deployments are expected in 2026, up 28% on 275.3 GWh in 2025, and Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months, 14% of the market, against 50 GWh of Texas capacity. The budget owner is a utility or independent power producer behind an interconnection queue, so demand is sticky but price-sensitive: energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Ride-hailing cannot yet be sized from disclosure: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, 26 million a year; even at $100 a ride that is $2.6 billion, 0.3% of the electric-car TAM, while Tesla discloses no fare, booking or paid-ride figure. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S100, S108, S4, S59, S150, S152, S153].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 竞争格局 Competitive Landscape (competition, revision 5 by Market Analyst, 8,889 characters)
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were small: Toyota 4,964 units (+34.9% month on month), Chevrolet +30.3% and Cadillac +13.1%. Weaker EV programmes retreated after the credit expired and the survivor with the widest line and lowest cost took the share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only it led 30,317 to 7,498 in every one of those countries, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse for Tesla: its Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Cost of automotive sales was $16,570 million for 486,532 deliveries, $34,060 per vehicle, against automotive sales revenue of $41,300 per unit (up from $40,955) and automotive gross margin of 18.5%, up from 17.0%. That is a healthy margin at a premium price point, and it sits 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the measure of the cost gap. The margin is protected by mix and software rather than price: FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. A price war in the $25,000-35,000 band would be fought on a cost base Tesla cannot currently match [S4, S6, S101].

### Storage and autonomy are where the advantage is thinnest

In grid storage the pricing power sits with the cell makers: CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of energy-storage batteries in the first half of 2026, up 81%, for 27.1% of the global ESS battery market, while Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months and its energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Tesla's differentiation is integration and delivery speed, not cell cost. In autonomy the gap is disclosed scale: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, while Baidu's Apollo Go operates in more than 10 Chinese cities and Tesla publishes no paid-ride count. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S81, S4, S59, S150, S152, S153].

The counter-case is that Tesla is converting rather than losing advantage: its US and European share gains came while rivals retreated, automotive gross margin rose year on year, and the Chinese price war ended with more than a dozen automakers raising prices, removing the deflation that hurt it most. That is partly right but does not change the conclusion: the share gains are in shrinking pools and the margin gain is mix-driven, not price-driven. Confidence is high on the US and European share data, medium on the China comparison because retail and wholesale definitions differ, and low on the autonomy comparison because no operator discloses audited paid rides. Two diligence questions follow: Tesla's US EV share in Q4 2026 once Toyota's bZ and Chevrolet's Bolt ramp, and how much of BYD's European volume is plug-in hybrid under the 2027 CO2 review?

### Energy is the proven technology

Megapack is the one line where Tesla holds a genuine integration advantage and prices it: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026 at a 33.1% gross margin, with 50 GWh of Texas capacity starting. The weak point is the order book, not the product: the 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified. A contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it; a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. Figure AI, valued at $39bn in September 2025, completed an 11-month Figure 02 deployment at BMW's Spartanburg plant contributing to more than 30,000 X3 vehicles, the external validation Optimus has not matched [S57, S149].

### What would change the judgement

The strongest counter-case is that FSD is already monetised: attach, subscriptions and deferred revenue rose in Q3 2026. Against it, repeated NHTSA recalls on the 2026 Model Y show launch quality slipping, and the attach rate is North American only while China sales fell with FSD approval pending. Optimus is the thinner half of the autonomy branch: a production line and no external customer.

Diligence questions: what did Austin earn per robotaxi per week, how many Cybercabs ran without a monitor, and what fare, trips per vehicle and insurance cost per mile sit behind that revenue? What is blended pack cost per kWh? Does EA26002 end in a recall, and what would that do to the release date? Until the first two are answered, Tesla owns the best-proven manufacturing technology in the sector and has not proven the one the share price pays for.

arguments.markdown:
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were small (Toyota 4,964 units, +34.9% month on month; Chevrolet +30.3%; Cadillac +13.1%), and weaker EV programmes retreated once the credit expired, letting the widest-line, lowest-cost survivor take share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only led 30,317 to 7,498 across those countries, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse: Tesla's Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Q3 2026 automotive cost of revenue of $16,754 million over 486,532 deliveries is $34,436 per vehicle, against automotive revenue of $20,560 million, or $42,258 per unit: an 18.5% automotive gross margin, up from 17.0%. That margin is healthy at a premium price point and rests on mix, credits and software rather than price: regulatory credits fell to $113 million from $417 million after a $475 million reversal for returned credits, FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. The $34,436 is 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the Geely Xingyuan at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820): the cost gap a $25,000-35,000 price war would expose [S4, S6, S101].

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BYD | Seal, Sealion, Qin, Yuan | BEV plus PHEV, in-house LFP cells | China MIIT; EU countervailing duty | 39,583 European registrations in September 2026 | 2.7% of EU registrations in June 2026 | Two powertrains meet CO2 limits at lower cost; cell integration | Only 7,498 BEVs in the September panel against Tesla's 30,317 | S104, S101 |
| Geely | Xingyuan, Galaxy | BEV and PHEV | China MIIT; EU tariff on China-built units | Nearly 197,500 Xingyuan units February-July 2026 at just under RMB 100,000 | Best-selling model in China | Price point a third of Model Y; mass-segment volume | Thin autonomy and software stack | S101 |
| Xiaomi | SU7, YU7 | BEV, consumer-electronics software | China MIIT | Model Y outsold SU7 and Li Auto's i6 in the February-July 2026 top ten | Not disclosed | Brand pull with Chinese tech buyers; phone-channel distribution | Capacity ramp unproven; China-only | S101 |
| GM | Chevrolet, Cadillac EVs | Ultium BEV | US FMVSS; no federal credit since 2025-09-30 | Chevrolet +30.3% and Cadillac +13.1% in August 2026 | Below Tesla's 51.7% | Dealer network; truck and SUV franchises | Smaller EV volume; margin dilution | S103 |
| Hyundai-Kia | Ioniq, EV6, EV9 | 800V BEV | US FMVSS; EU type approval | Hyundai fourth in US EV sales; Kia +12% month on month | Below Tesla's 51.7% | 800V charging speed; warranty; cost control | Weaker software and charging network | S103 |
| Rivian | Mid-size SUV and pickup | BEV, zonal architecture | US FMVSS; deliveries from Q2 2026 | 215,000 units of Normal capacity; Autonomy+ since April 2026 | Below Tesla's 51.7% | Purpose-built brand; entry price below Model X | Unprofitable at current utilisation; no energy business | S96 |

### Storage and autonomy are where the advantage is thinnest

In grid storage the pricing power sits with the cell makers: CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of energy-storage batteries in the first half of 2026, up 81%, for 27.1% of the global ESS battery market, while Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months and its energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Tesla's differentiation is integration and delivery speed, not cell cost. In autonomy the gap is disclosed scale: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, while Baidu's Apollo Go operates in more than 10 Chinese cities and Tesla publishes no paid-ride count. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y; TxDMV registry via TeslaNorth and Drive Tesla Canada), with no in-service count disclosed; NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S81, S4, S59, S150, S154, S152, S153].

| Robotaxi | Tesla emerges | Waymo: 4,000 vehicles, 500,000 paid rides a week | Baidu Apollo Go: more than 10 cities | Zoox and Pony.ai | Tesla Cybercab | S59, S6 |

The counter-case is that Tesla is converting rather than losing advantage: its US and European share gains came while rivals retreated, automotive gross margin rose year on year, and the Chinese price war ended with more than a dozen automakers raising prices, removing the deflation that hurt it most. Partly right, but the conclusion holds: the share gains are in shrinking pools and the margin gain is mix-driven, not price-driven. Confidence is high on the US and European share data, medium on the China comparison because retail and wholesale definitions differ, and low on the autonomy comparison because no operator discloses audited paid rides. Two diligence questions follow: Tesla's US EV share in Q4 2026 once Toyota's bZ and Chevrolet's Bolt ramp, and how much of BYD's European volume is plug-in hybrid under the 2027 CO2 review?

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 投资潜力与投资逻辑 Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 6 by Lead Analyst, 8,808 characters)
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $356, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 769 robotaxi vehicles registered in Texas on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S4]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $42.50 a share, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets, and autonomy at $259B in the base case — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance — which is $65.6 a share on 3,952.6M shares, so $42.50 + $65.6 = $108.1 and the base rounds to $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $52.50 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $465 mid-point lifts expected value to $253, still 37% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

Assumption 1 sets the price and is the least evidenced: no robotaxi revenue, no fare and no cost per mile are disclosed, so the largest component of value rests on a third-party fleet count. Assumptions 2 and 3 decide whether the core is worth $42.50 or $21.75, and management can still influence both in 2027 — the ex-credit operating margin has been cut to 2.2-2.5%, while energy supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M third-quarter gross profit at a margin 2.5 times Fluence's 13.1%. Assumptions 4 and 5 are about survival and dilution rather than growth: $36.18B of net cash covers eighteen months of zero free cash flow, but not that plus a $16.8B capital call whose Tesla share is undisclosed. [S4, S6]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cisco | cautionary | 2000-2024 | Revenue grew from $12.5B to $57B and trailing net income passed its 1999 level by 2003, yet a buyer at the March 2000 peak of $500B waited until 2021 to break even. A correct thesis does not rescue the entry multiple. | S140 |
| Amazon | cautionary | 1999-2001 | The business compounded into one of the great franchises, but the stock fell more than 90% and took a decade to recover; the option paid only for the holder who could sit through the drawdown. | S143 |
| GM Cruise | cautionary | 2016-2024 | More than $10B of operating losses and less than $500M of revenue before GM shut the robotaxi unit in December 2024 for $1B a year of savings. Automaker capital is no substitute for paid driverless miles. | S142 |
| Waymo | best | 2024-2026 | The valuation went from $45B in October 2024 to $126B in February 2026 on 500,000 paid driverless rides a week — proof the service can scale, and a mark that Tesla's autonomy value exceeds 11-fold. | S120 |

The precedents give one rule: when a real technology shift is already in the price, the entry multiple sets the return, not whether the technology wins; the base rate for a follower in autonomy is a write-off, not a slow fade; and the leader's private mark, $126B, is the only independent price for the option — 9% of what the market pays for Tesla's version. A holder should own Tesla's autonomy at a discount to that mark, not at 11.3 times it, and size the position so the Cruise outcome is survivable. [S140, S142]

### Where the case turns, and what to do now

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. At $403.30 it sits in the third zone, with the ten-year Treasury at 4.99% raising the discount rate on post-2030 cash flows. Do not invest new money now. Wait for one of three milestones: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless deployment permit, or special-committee terms at a premium to market rather than at market. If the mandate requires exposure, hold a residual of 0.25-0.5% of net asset value, sized so a failed vote and a 30% drawdown do not breach the risk budget, and vote against any ratio that transfers value to the controlling shareholder. Pass on the blue-sky branch: it needs global robotaxi and humanoid dominance and pays 8% from here. Diligence questions: revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, the share of rides running without a safety driver, and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Confidence is high that the core is not worth $403.30, medium on the autonomy tree, low on the merger. What would change the call: a second consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-credit operating margin, an FSD licensing contract with a named automaker, or a ratio that values Tesla at a premium to its undisturbed price. arguments.markdown:
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were small (Toyota 4,964 units, +34.9% month on month; Chevrolet +30.3%; Cadillac +13.1%), and weaker EV programmes retreated once the credit expired, letting the widest-line, lowest-cost survivor take share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only led 30,317 to 7,498, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse: Tesla's Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Q3 2026 automotive cost of revenue of $16,754 million over 486,532 deliveries is $34,436 per vehicle, against automotive revenue of $20,560 million, or $42,258 per unit: an 18.5% automotive gross margin, up from 17.0%. That margin is healthy at a premium price point and rests on mix, credits and software rather than price: regulatory credits fell to $113 million from $417 million, FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. The $34,436 is 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the Geely Xingyuan at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820): the cost gap a $25,000-35,000 price war would expose [S4, S6, S101].

### Storage and autonomy are where the advantage is thinnest

In grid storage the pricing power sits with the cell makers: CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of energy-storage batteries in the first half of 2026, up 81%, for 27.1% of the global ESS battery market, while Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months and its energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Tesla's differentiation is integration and delivery speed, not cell cost. In autonomy the gap is disclosed scale: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, while Baidu's Apollo Go operates in more than 10 Chinese cities and Tesla publishes no paid-ride count. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y; TxDMV registry via TeslaNorth and Drive Tesla Canada), with no in-service count disclosed; NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S81, S4, S59, S150, S154, S152, S153].

| Compact and mid-size BEV | Tesla leads | Tesla: 51.7% of US EV sales | BYD: 39,583 European registrations | Geely Xingyuan at under RMB 100,000 | Xiaomi SU7 and YU7 | S103, S104, S101 |
| Grid battery storage | Tesla challenges | CATL: 27.1% of ESS cells | Tesla: 36.0 GWh in 9M 2026 | Fluence and Sungrow | Chinese LFP integrators | S81, S4 |
| Robotaxi | Tesla emerges | Waymo: 4,000 vehicles, 500,000 paid rides a week | Baidu Apollo Go: more than 10 cities | Zoox and Pony.ai | Tesla Cybercab | S59, S6 |

The counter-case is that Tesla is converting rather than losing advantage: its US and European share gains came while rivals retreated, automotive gross margin rose year on year, and the Chinese price war ended with more than a dozen automakers raising prices. Partly right, but the conclusion holds: the share gains are in shrinking pools and the margin gain is mix-driven, not price-driven. Confidence is high on the US and European share data, medium on the China comparison because retail and wholesale definitions differ, and low on the autonomy comparison because no operator discloses audited paid rides. Two diligence questions follow: Tesla's US EV share in Q4 2026 once Toyota's bZ and Chevrolet's Bolt ramp, and how much of BYD's European volume is plug-in hybrid under the 2027 CO2 review?

Its cost per vehicle of $34,436 is 2.3 times that Chinese retail price, CATL holds 27.1% of ESS cells, and Tesla reports no paid-ride figure against Waymo's 500,000 a week [S103, S104, S102, S4, S81, S59]. Tesla scores 4.0 out of 10, and the score is not close to the line that would justify new money: at $403.30 the shares price the autonomy option at $1,424B, 89% of the equity, while the business that pays the bills earns a 2.2-2.5% operating margin once regulatory credits are stripped out. The recommendation is Reduce — trim existing exposure to a residual, buy nothing — on a twelve-month horizon, with medium confidence in the direction and high confidence in the arithmetic. The composite is a weighted average of seven dimensions, and two do most of the work: valuation at 2 out of 10 with a 20% weight and governance at 3 out of 10 with a 15% weight. Remove either and the stock still scores below 5. [S15, S4]

| Governance and capital allocation | 15% | 3 | A 423.7M-share award with $105.82-120.37B of unrecognised compensation, three of nine directors tied to SpaceX, no dividend or buyback | S5, S138 |
