| Catalysts, regime and positioning | 5% | 3 | A binary merger process is the only re-rating path, against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury and a VIX of 17.20 | S24, S23, S135 |

The weighting is deliberate. A heavy weight on valuation is right because at the current multiple the entry price, not the technology, dominates a five-year return. The governance weight reflects what a standard framework misses: the controlling shareholder's compensation is tied to market-capitalisation milestones, so management is paid for the narrative that supports the multiple rather than for per-share cash flow, and a change of control accelerates the award. Business quality scores 6 rather than 8 because the strongest part of the franchise, energy storage, is a small and shrinking share of revenue in dollars, while vehicles are losing share in the region that sets global prices.

The counter-evidence deserves its own paragraph, because the score could be too harsh in one place: energy earns a 33.1% gross margin at $210M of revenue per GWh, Tesla's $34,436 cost per vehicle is below every Western competitor, and a triple-digit multiple has persisted for two years without mean reversion. If energy revenue doubles and FSD licensing adds a second stream, the core could be worth $70 a share rather than $42.50. That moves the composite by less than half a point, because the core is 11% of the price and the autonomy premium is 11.3 times the leader's mark. The risks run both ways: if the bear branch materialises — autonomy written down, vehicles valued at GM's multiple, the Terafab commitment drawn — value collapses to a small fraction of today's price and Reduce becomes Sell or Avoid at any size. The base case carries $259B of autonomy on a probability-weighted blend of four branches, not the $40B regional fleet alone: at regional-only autonomy the base would be $52.50 and the probability-weighted value $84, and the recommendation would not change. The only branch that lifts the score above 5 is the merger: a negotiated ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price would justify Hold, with the position capped because a failed vote returns the stock to a level set by the operating business. [S6, S63, S120]

At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 Tesla is a $1,594.1B equity in which $42.50 a share, $170B, is the vehicle, energy, services and net-cash business and $356 a share, $1,424B, is autonomy and robotics; on 25/50/25 of $212/$107/$19 the probability-weighted value is $111, so the share is a reduce and new money is an option purchase. A market 50% smaller leaves a $105B core, $26 a share, at 94% autonomy; customer acquisition cost doubled adds $8.1B; revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B; a 5.0x peer multiple on free cash flow 30% lower is $130; financing six months late is covered by the September facilities [S6, S15, S120, S4, S115]. None reverses the conclusion. An exchange ratio at a premium does, a board decision, and the one risk the recommendation must price. The three premises carrying the $1,424B are deteriorating at once: NHTSA's Cybercab self-certification inquiry closes for comment on 2026-10-30, the special committees formed on 2026-10-20 have no terms, and nine-month free cash flow of $1,883M contains $7,332M from stretching payables to 75.3 days.

### The core is not harsh at 1.0x sales; it is generous

The sum of the parts pays $91B for vehicles and services at 1.0x sales, $43B for energy at 3.5x and $36B of net cash at book. At GM's implied 0.39x, vehicles and services are worth $29B and the core is $87B, $21.75 a share, with autonomy at 95% of the price; a control buyer tops out at $200-250B, $50-62.50, where autonomy still holds 84%. Energy's 3.5x has support — a 29.7% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% — but doubling revenue to $25B on 5.0x adds $82B, $20 a share, and FSD's 1.74M subscribers at $1,200 a year add $42B, $10.5, leaving the best honest core near $70 and autonomy at 83%. The $1,424B premium is 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, for 769 Texas-registered vehicles against 3,000. [S6, S131, S120, S15]

### The scenario tree is generous at the base and shallow in the bear

The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% x $40B regional, 40% x $126B at Waymo parity, 20% x $600B at scale, 5% x $1,500B at dominance — and $259B is 1.0x Waymo for 769 vehicles that reported nine crashes in August 2026 and disclose no revenue per mile. On the regional branch alone the base is $52.50 and the probability-weighted value $84, still 79% below the close. My 40% probability for unsupervised customer FSD in 2027 and 40% for a merger within a year sit above the record: EA26002 covers 2.88M vehicles, DP26010 opened on 2026-10-09. The $35 bear was too shallow: at $19 — autonomy at zero, vehicles at 0.39x, energy at 1.5x, net cash $29B after a Terafab call — the drawdown is 95% and the weighted value falls only from $115 to $111. Above $437 the path I had missed is a 10-15% ratio premium in a $3.60T combination, paying $443-487 without one driverless mile. [S120, S137, S6, S5]

### Cash carries a two-year slip, not a slip plus a revenue fall

Net cash of $36.18B and $30B of facilities signed in September 2026 carry a two-year autonomy slip at zero free cash flow without issuing a share. The combination does not survive a revenue fall: at a 19% gross margin, revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B of gross profit against $19.1B of annual operating expense, taking operating cash flow to zero or minus $2B, and with $20-25B of capital expenditure the annual burn is $20-27B, exhausting cash and facilities before 2029. Reported cash flow already borrows from suppliers: payables and accruals added $7,332M and days payable rose from 62.8 to 75.3, worth $2.9B, so normalised free cash flow is minus $1.0B. Terafab adds a commitment Tesla does not control: a $16.8B first phase joint with SpaceX, Tesla's share undisclosed, outside the ">$20B" 2026 capital budget and described in SpaceX's IPO filing as a "general framework" with no binding commitment — which caps near-term cash risk and weakens the strategic-asset defence. Tesla is Baa3 against SpaceX at Baa1; the facilities' pricing is undisclosed. [S4, S134, S138, S147]

### The merger is an option, not a floor

On 2026-10-20 Musk said both boards had formed special committees, that no terms were agreed and none assured; the Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares, not of those cast, so abstentions count against, and the 2026-10-19 proxy sets the 2026-12-03 annual meeting with no merger proposal. At market the deal is value-neutral: $1,594.1B plus SpaceX's $2.01T is $3.60T, and Tesla holders taking 43-44% own exactly today's price; any premium must be conceded by SpaceX. Either way Tesla holders get 43% of the economics and a shareholder with 84% of the votes. The 2025 award writes the incentive down: on a change of control operational milestones lapse and market-cap milestones vest, 423.7M shares are 10.7% dilution, the first $2.0T milestone sits 25% above today's capitalisation, against a $9.74B probable charge and $105.82-120.37B unrecognised. Musk has pledged 207.5M shares, 5.2% of the count; three of nine directors are SpaceX-linked and the committee uses two. [S5, S135, S138]

### Policy is a $5.60 option; competition is a terminal-value risk

Twenty-five state attorneys general and 12 cities and counties sued on 2026-03-19 in the D.C. Circuit over EPA's 2026-02-12 repeal of the 2009 endangerment finding, consolidated on 2026-05-20; a reversal restores the credit pool, but $1.5B of credits at 15x is $22.5B, $5.6 a share, against Q3 credit revenue of $113M, down 73%, credits at 45.8% of FY2025 operating income. Policy is a small option and the base case gives it nothing. Competition is different in kind: BYD holds 2.4% of the European market at EUR 5,500 less per car, Xiaomi is near break-even in its first production year and Waymo runs 500,000 paid rides a week on 3,000 vehicles. If revenue per mile falls from $0.60 to $0.45, the reverse DCF needs 20.9M robotaxis rather than 15.7M, above global annual capacity — $40-60 a share off the bull branch and nothing off 2027 earnings. The unknown unknown is a regulatory stop before revenue: a recall that grounds the fleet removes the data the model learns from. [S136, S138, S59, S4]

arguments.markdown:
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were small (Toyota 4,964 units, +34.9% month on month; Chevrolet +30.3%; Cadillac +13.1%), and weaker EV programmes retreated once the credit expired, letting the widest-line, lowest-cost survivor take share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only led 30,317 to 7,498, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse: Tesla's Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Q3 2026 automotive cost of revenue of $16,754 million over 486,532 deliveries is $34,436 per vehicle, against automotive revenue of $20,560 million, or $42,258 per unit: an 18.5% automotive gross margin, up from 17.0%. That margin is healthy at a premium price point and rests on mix, credits and software rather than price: regulatory credits fell to $113 million from $417 million, FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. The $34,436 is 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the Geely Xingyuan at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820): the cost gap a $25,000-35,000 price war would expose [S4, S6, S101].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 发展方向与战略 Development Strategy (strategy, revision 4 by Product Analyst, 8,686 characters)
Tesla's strategy has become a capital-allocation bet rather than an operating one: more than $20bn of 2026 capex and $30bn of new credit facilities are committed to autonomy, robots and semiconductors while nine-month 2026 operating income of $2.06bn implies a return on invested capital near 3%, below any plausible cost of capital. The strategy earns its keep only if unsupervised robotaxi revenue arrives before 2028, and the 12-month test is customer-owned unsupervised driving in mid-2027, not another reveal [S4, S78].

### The plan and the return do not yet match

Tesla guided in the Q3 2026 filing to capital expenditure above $20bn for 2026, after spending $13.01bn in the first nine months against $6.13bn a year earlier, and in September 2026 signed three credit agreements for aggregate commitments of $30bn. Cash and short-term investments were $45.45bn at 2026-09-30 against $9.5bn of debt, so the plan is funded; it is no longer self-funding. Nine-month operating income of $2.06bn on $89.29bn of equity, annualised after tax over roughly $71bn of invested capital, gives a return near 3% — depressed by ramp assets, but low enough that every further billion of capex lowers the return until the new assets sell something [S6]. Research and development rose 69% year over year to $2.76bn in Q3 2026, most of it for autonomy and robotics.

### Pricing and mix are carrying the capex

| Item | Q3 2026 | Q3 2025 | Read | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive gross margin | 18.5% | 17.0% | Cost cuts and mix offset lower prices | S4 |
| Regulatory credit revenue | $113m | $417m | A subsidy that no longer pays for the plan | S4 |
| Energy segment revenue | $2.881bn | $3.415bn | Volume up, price down | S4 |
| Services gross profit | $734m | $366m | FSD subscriptions and repair work | S6 |
| China deliveries | 142,133 | 16% lower year over year | Share loss in the largest market | S77 |
| Total deliveries | 486,532 | 497,099 | Flat volume on an ageing core line-up | S6 |

The read is that Tesla is funding autonomy from a mature car business, a fading credit stream and a fast-growing but deflating storage business; none of the three is a rising price. The Semi is a logical adjacency because it shares cells, motors and Megachargers with the core; Optimus is not an adjacency yet, because it has a production line and no customer.

### Milestones: what has actually shipped

| Milestone | Target date | Status at 2026-10-29 | What it proves | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cybercab in the Austin robotaxi fleet | 2026 | Met: paid rides from 2026-09-03 | Hardware and a Texas permit | S6 |
| Customer-owned unsupervised FSD | Q4 2026, now Q2 2027 | Slipped by about two quarters | Converts the owner fleet into robotaxi supply without capex | S57 |
| Optimus production | 2026 | Met: early production from 2026-10-21 | Manufacturing readiness, not demand | S6 |
| Optimus at 20,000 units a week | End-2027 | Company claim on the 2026-10-21 call, unverified: no unit count, customer or revenue disclosed | Whether a humanoid is a product; a named customer or supplier orders would confirm it, a second year of demonstrations would contradict it | S57 |
| Tesla Semi volume production | 2026 | Met: Nevada high-volume line | Entry into Class 8 trucking | S6 |
| Next-generation affordable platform | Not dated | Not publicly disclosed | The volume and cost reset | S6 |
| 400 MW of training compute | 2026-12-31 | 225 MW installed (Cortex 1 and 2) | Whether the compute constraint eases | S6 |
| Austin Fab equipment commissioning | 2027 | Under construction | Vertical integration into silicon | S6 |
| FSD approval in China | Not dated | Pending; CFO negotiating | Monetising the largest market | S77 |
| Megafactory Texas at 50 GWh | 2026-2027 | Production began Q3 2026 | Energy scale-up | S6 |

### Partners: concentration, not diversification

| Partner | Scope | Signed | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Samsung Electronics | AI6 foundry at Taylor, Texas; $16.5bn through 2033 | 2025-07-28 | AI5 taped out on 2nm in July 2026; AI6 to follow | S79 |
| CATL | LFP cells for Shanghai vehicles and storage | Not disclosed | Active | S56 |
| Panasonic, LG Energy Solution | 2170 cells for Fremont and Shanghai | Not disclosed | Active | S56 |
| xAI, then SpaceX | $2bn xAI investment converted into SpaceX Class A shares after SpaceX acquired xAI | 2026-01; converted 2026-02 | Stake held; a merger is openly discussed | S78 |
| Maxwell Technologies | Dry-electrode intellectual property acquired for $235m | 2019 | Integrated into 4680 production | S56 |

The partner map shows the strategic risk: Tesla's autonomy roadmap runs through a single foundry for AI6, its vehicles still depend on CATL, Panasonic and LG for cells, and its largest related-party exposure is to companies its chief executive also controls.

### Geography: China becomes an export base

Tesla's China sales fell 16% year over year in Q3 2026 to 142,133 units while Giga Shanghai exports reached a record 132,978; retail sales for 2026 to date are down 12% as exports doubled, and Beijing cuts the EV export tax rebate in April 2027. Shanghai, with more than 950,000 units of capacity, is now a cost and export base rather than a growth market, exposed to tariffs in the markets it ships to. Berlin set a production record and the US business carries the FSD attach rate, which is why the company's own numbers look better in North America than in the two regions that decide its cost base [S77, S76, S102].

### Energy is where the strategy is working

The energy plan is coherent and funded: 50 GWh of Megafactory Texas capacity started in Q3 2026 alongside 40 GWh in California and 20 GWh in Shanghai, with 7 GWh of Nevada LFP cell capacity in early ramp and the first Megapacks built from Tesla-made cells. The 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified: a contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it, and a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. A 33.1% segment gross margin and data-centre demand give the capital a return that autonomy does not yet. The tension is that revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881bn even as volume rose, so the plan is adding capacity into falling prices [S6, S72].

### The capital allocation question

In January 2026 Tesla invested $2bn in xAI; the stake became SpaceX Class A shares when SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026, and the Q1 2026 cash flow statement records a $2.002bn purchase of SpaceX equity. Three of nine directors have SpaceX ties, the 2026 proxy is set for a 2026-12-03 meeting, and the 2025 CEO award pays out on a deal price without operational milestones — only one of twelve operational milestones is rated probable, leaving $105.8-120.4bn of unrecognised stock compensation. A shareholder is no longer buying only a car and storage company; a merger scenario makes the position a bet on Musk's wider portfolio, which argues for a smaller size [S78].

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. No plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a 0.95 million unit annual run-rate at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, while hybrids took 36.6%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6%. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced by the 2026 energy-price shock. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved Tesla's way for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

### Market size: $950 billion of cars, $83 billion of storage

The 2026 market size is $950 billion for electric cars and $82.7 billion for grid storage, measured at Tesla's realised prices as a proxy because no agency publishes revenue; global electric-car units rise from an implied 16.7 million in 2024 to 23.0 million in 2026, a 17.4% compound annual growth rate, and the battery-electric slice of the three regions where Tesla sells is not published, so the table bounds obtainable revenue rather than measuring the serviceable market. Grid storage is the only pool growing faster than Tesla can supply: 353.4 GWh of deployments are expected in 2026, up 28% on 275.3 GWh in 2025, and Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months, 14% of the market, against 50 GWh of Texas capacity. The budget owner is a utility or independent power producer behind an interconnection queue, so demand is sticky but price-sensitive: energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Ride-hailing cannot yet be sized from disclosure: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, 26 million a year; even at $100 a ride that is $2.6 billion, 0.3% of the electric-car TAM, while Tesla discloses no fare, booking or paid-ride figure. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y; TxDMV registry via TeslaNorth and Drive Tesla Canada), with no in-service count disclosed; NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S100, S108, S4, S59, S150, S154, S152, S153].

The counter-case does not overturn the judgement: if US battery-electric share holds for four quarters, the credit will have been worth two-fifths of US demand, and a purpose-built Cybercab could compress cost per paid mile faster than Waymo's retrofit fleet, bringing the robotaxi market forward. Tesla's strategy has become a capital-allocation bet rather than an operating one: more than $20bn of 2026 capex and $30bn of new credit facilities are committed to autonomy, robots and semiconductors while nine-month 2026 operating income of $2.06bn implies a return on invested capital near 3%, below any plausible cost of capital. Tesla guided in the Q3 2026 filing to capital expenditure above $20bn for 2026, after spending $13.01bn in the first nine months against $6.13bn a year earlier, and in September 2026 signed three credit agreements for aggregate commitments of $30bn. Cash and short-term investments were $45.45bn at 2026-09-30 against $9.5bn of debt, so the plan is funded; it is no longer self-funding. Nine-month operating income of $2.06bn on $89.29bn of equity, annualised after tax over roughly $71bn of invested capital, gives a return near 3% — depressed by ramp assets, but low enough that every further billion of capex lowers the return until the new assets sell something [S6]. Tesla's China sales fell 16% year over year in Q3 2026 to 142,133 units while Giga Shanghai exports reached a record 132,978; retail sales for 2026 to date are down 12% as exports doubled, and Beijing cuts the EV export tax rebate in April 2027. None reverses the conclusion. An exchange ratio at a premium does, a board decision, and the one risk the recommendation must price. The three premises carrying the $1,424B are deteriorating at once: NHTSA's Cybercab self-certification inquiry closes for comment on 2026-10-30, the special committees formed on 2026-10-20 have no terms, and nine-month free cash flow of $1,883M contains $7,332M from stretching payables to 75.3 days.

### The core is not harsh at 1.0x sales; it is generous

The sum of the parts pays $91B for vehicles and services at 1.0x sales, $43B for energy at 3.5x and $36B of net cash at book. At GM's implied 0.39x, vehicles and services are worth $29B and the core is $87B, $21.75 a share, with autonomy at 95% of the price; a control buyer tops out at $200-250B, $50-62.50, where autonomy still holds 84%. The $1,424B premium is 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, for 769 Texas-registered vehicles against 3,000. [S6, S131, S120, S15]

### The scenario tree is generous at the base and shallow in the bear

The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% x $40B regional, 40% x $126B at Waymo parity, 20% x $600B at scale, 5% x $1,500B at dominance — and $259B is 1.0x Waymo for 769 vehicles that reported nine crashes in August 2026 and disclose no revenue per mile. My 40% probability for unsupervised customer FSD in 2027 and 40% for a merger within a year sit above the record: EA26002 covers 2.88M vehicles, DP26010 opened on 2026-10-09. The $35 bear was too shallow: at $19 — autonomy at zero, vehicles at 0.39x, energy at 1.5x, net cash $29B after a Terafab call — the drawdown is 95% and the weighted value falls only from $115 to $111. Above $437 the path I had missed is a 10-15% ratio premium in a $3.60T combination, paying $443-487 without one driverless mile. [S120, S137, S6, S5]

### Cash carries a two-year slip, not a slip plus a revenue fall

Net cash of $36.18B and $30B of facilities signed in September 2026 carry a two-year autonomy slip at zero free cash flow without issuing a share. The combination does not survive a revenue fall: at a 19% gross margin, revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B of gross profit against $19.1B of annual operating expense, taking operating cash flow to zero or minus $2B, and with $20-25B of capital expenditure the annual burn is $20-27B, exhausting cash and facilities before 2029. Reported cash flow already borrows from suppliers: payables and accruals added $7,332M and days payable rose from 62.8 to 75.3, worth $2.9B, so normalised free cash flow is minus $1.0B. Terafab adds a commitment Tesla does not control: a $16.8B first phase joint with SpaceX, Tesla's share undisclosed, outside the ">$20B" 2026 capital budget and described in SpaceX's IPO filing as a "general framework" with no binding commitment — which caps near-term cash risk and weakens the strategic-asset defence. ### The merger is an option, not a floor

On 2026-10-20 Musk said both boards had formed special committees, that no terms were agreed and none assured; the Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares, not of those cast, so abstentions count against, and the 2026-10-19 proxy sets the 2026-12-03 annual meeting with no merger proposal. Twenty-five state attorneys general and 12 cities and counties sued on 2026-03-19 in the D.C. Circuit over EPA's 2026-02-12 repeal of the 2009 endangerment finding, consolidated on 2026-05-20; a reversal restores the credit pool, but $1.5B of credits at 15x is $22.5B, $5.6 a share, against Q3 credit revenue of $113M, down 73%, credits at 45.8% of FY2025 operating income. Policy is a small option and the base case gives it nothing. Competition is different in kind: BYD holds 2.4% of the European market at EUR 5,500 less per car, Xiaomi is near break-even in its first production year and Waymo runs 500,000 paid rides a week on 3,000 vehicles. arguments.markdown:
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $356, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 1,051 authorised robotaxi vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27, 544 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S150]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $42.50 a share, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets, and autonomy at $259B in the base case — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance — which is $65.6 a share on 3,952.6M shares, so $42.50 + $65.6 = $108.1 and the base rounds to $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $52.50 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $465 mid-point lifts expected value to $253, still 37% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

::: scenarios
| Scenario | Probability | Drivers | Outcome | Signposts | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull | 25% | Robotaxi in several metros at 1.0x Waymo's $126B; energy at 6.0x sales; 1.74M FSD subscriptions | $212 a share, -47% from $403.30; -12.1% a year to 2031 | Robotaxi revenue line disclosed; California driverless permit; Texas authorised fleet above 5,000 vehicles | S6, S120, S150 |
| Base | 50% | Autonomy at $259B, the probability-weighted blend of the four branches (35% × $40B, 40% × $126B, 20% × $600B, 5% × $1,500B); core at $42.50; energy at 3.5x sales | $107 a share, -73% | Q4 2026 update with no robotaxi revenue despite 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles; no fare or cost per mile disclosed | S6, S120, S150 |
| Bear | 25% | Autonomy written down; vehicles at GM's 0.39x sales; Terafab commitment; credit-free margin | $19 a share, -95% | Unsupervised FSD slips past 2027; NHTSA recall of the Cybercab; merger vote fails | S6, S120, S137 |
:::

### Key assumptions, ranked

| Rank | Assumption | Confidence | What would disprove it | Impact if wrong | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031: 15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile is what the reverse DCF needs | low | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | Authorisations flat near 1,051 Texas vehicles; no fare disclosure; safety-driver hours rising | S4, S6, S137, S150 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | medium | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | Each 100 bp is $756M, 22% of trailing operating income | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% with revenue growth | medium | Q4 margin below 25% once tariff refunds lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | Q3 revenue fell 16% to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | low | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | Terafab's $16.8B first phase sits outside the 2026 budget | S4, S134 |
| 5 | No value-transferring exchange ratio; award dilution held at 10.7% | low | Ratio struck below market, or new tranches granted | -$40 to -$80 a share | Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers | S5, S135, S138 |

Assumption 1 sets the price and is the least evidenced: no robotaxi revenue, no fare and no cost per mile are disclosed, so the largest component of value rests on a registry count of authorised vehicles rather than on unit economics. Assumptions 2 and 3 decide whether the core is worth $42.50 or $21.75, and management can still influence both in 2027 — the ex-credit operating margin has been cut to 2.2-2.5%, while energy supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M third-quarter gross profit at a margin 2.5 times Fluence's 13.1%. Assumptions 4 and 5 are about survival and dilution rather than growth: $36.18B of net cash covers eighteen months of zero free cash flow, but not that plus a $16.8B capital call whose Tesla share is undisclosed. [S4, S6]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cisco | cautionary | 2000-2024 | Revenue grew from $12.5B to $57B and trailing net income passed its 1999 level by 2003, yet a buyer at the March 2000 peak of $500B waited until 2021 to break even. A correct thesis does not rescue the entry multiple. | S140 |
| Amazon | cautionary | 1999-2001 | The business compounded into one of the great franchises, but the stock fell more than 90% and took a decade to recover; the option paid only for the holder who could sit through the drawdown. | S143 |
| GM Cruise | cautionary | 2016-2024 | More than $10B of operating losses and less than $500M of revenue before GM shut the robotaxi unit in December 2024 for $1B a year of savings. Automaker capital is no substitute for paid driverless miles. | S142 |
| Waymo | best | 2024-2026 | The valuation went from $45B in October 2024 to $126B in February 2026 on 500,000 paid driverless rides a week — proof the service can scale, and a mark that Tesla's autonomy value exceeds 11-fold. | S120 |
:::

The precedents give one rule: when a real technology shift is already in the price, the entry multiple sets the return, not whether the technology wins; the base rate for a follower in autonomy is a write-off, not a slow fade; and the leader's private mark, $126B, is the only independent price for the option — 9% of what the market pays for Tesla's version. A holder should own Tesla's autonomy at a discount to that mark, not at 11.3 times it, and size the position so the Cruise outcome is survivable. [S140, S142]

### Where the case turns, and what to do now

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. At $403.30 it sits in the third zone, with the ten-year Treasury at 4.99% raising the discount rate on post-2030 cash flows. Do not invest new money now. Wait for one of three milestones: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless deployment permit, or special-committee terms at a premium to market rather than at market. If the mandate requires exposure, hold a residual of 0.25-0.5% of net asset value, sized so a failed vote and a 30% drawdown do not breach the risk budget, and vote against any ratio that transfers value to the controlling shareholder. Pass on the blue-sky branch: it needs global robotaxi and humanoid dominance and pays 8% from here. Diligence questions: revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, the share of rides running without a safety driver, and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Confidence is high that the core is not worth $403.30, medium on the autonomy tree, low on the merger. What would change the call: a second consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-credit operating margin, an FSD licensing contract with a named automaker, or a ratio that values Tesla at a premium to its undisturbed price. [S15, S5]

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's strategy has become a capital-allocation bet rather than an operating one: more than $20bn of 2026 capex and $30bn of new credit facilities are committed to autonomy, robots and semiconductors while nine-month 2026 operating income of $2.06bn implies a return on invested capital near 3%, below any plausible cost of capital. The strategy earns its keep only if unsupervised robotaxi revenue arrives before 2028, and the 12-month test is customer-owned unsupervised driving in mid-2027, not another reveal [S4, S78].

### The plan and the return do not yet match

Tesla guided in the Q3 2026 filing to capital expenditure above $20bn for 2026, after spending $13.01bn in the first nine months against $6.13bn a year earlier, and in September 2026 signed three credit agreements for aggregate commitments of $30bn. Cash and short-term investments were $45.45bn at 2026-09-30 against $9.5bn of debt, so the plan is funded; it is no longer self-funding. Nine-month operating income of $2.06bn on $89.29bn of equity, annualised after tax over roughly $71bn of invested capital, gives a return near 3% — depressed by ramp assets, but low enough that every further billion of capex lowers the return until the new assets sell something [S6]. Research and development rose 69% year over year to $2.76bn in Q3 2026, most of it for autonomy and robotics.

### Pricing and mix are carrying the capex

| Item | Q3 2026 | Q3 2025 | Read | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive gross margin | 18.5% | 17.0% | Cost cuts and mix offset lower prices | S4 |
| Regulatory credit revenue | $113m | $417m | A subsidy that no longer pays for the plan | S4 |
| Energy segment revenue | $2.881bn | $3.415bn | Volume up, price down | S4 |
| Services gross profit | $734m | $366m | FSD subscriptions and repair work | S6 |
| China deliveries | 142,133 | 16% lower year over year | Share loss in the largest market | S77 |
| Total deliveries | 486,532 | 497,099 | Flat volume on an ageing core line-up | S6 |

The read is that Tesla is funding autonomy from a mature car business, a fading credit stream and a fast-growing but deflating storage business; none of the three is a rising price. The Semi is a logical adjacency because it shares cells, motors and Megachargers with the core; Optimus is not an adjacency yet, because it has a production line and no customer.

### Milestones: what has actually shipped

| Milestone | Target date | Status at 2026-10-29 | What it proves | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cybercab in the Austin robotaxi fleet | 2026 | Met: paid rides from 2026-09-03 | Hardware and a Texas permit | S6 |
| Customer-owned unsupervised FSD | Q4 2026, now Q2 2027 | Slipped by about two quarters | Converts the owner fleet into robotaxi supply without capex | S57 |
| Optimus production | 2026 | Met: early production from 2026-10-21 | Manufacturing readiness, not demand | S6 |
| Optimus at 20,000 units a week | End-2027 | Company claim on the 2026-10-21 call, unverified: no unit count, customer or revenue disclosed | Whether a humanoid is a product; a named customer or supplier orders would confirm it, a second year of demonstrations would contradict it | S57 |
| Tesla Semi volume production | 2026 | Met: Nevada high-volume line | Entry into Class 8 trucking | S6 |
| Next-generation affordable platform | Not dated | Not publicly disclosed | The volume and cost reset | S6 |
| 400 MW of training compute | 2026-12-31 | 225 MW installed (Cortex 1 and 2) | Whether the compute constraint eases | S6 |
| Austin Fab equipment commissioning | 2027 | Under construction | Vertical integration into silicon | S6 |
| FSD approval in China | Not dated | Pending; CFO negotiating | Monetising the largest market | S77 |
| Megafactory Texas at 50 GWh | 2026-2027 | Production began Q3 2026 | Energy scale-up | S6 |

### Partners: concentration, not diversification

| Partner | Scope | Signed | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Samsung Electronics | AI6 foundry at Taylor, Texas; $16.5bn through 2033 | 2025-07-28 | AI5 taped out on 2nm in July 2026; AI6 to follow | S79 |
| CATL | LFP cells for Shanghai vehicles and storage | Not disclosed | Active | S56 |
| Panasonic, LG Energy Solution | 2170 cells for Fremont and Shanghai | Not disclosed | Active | S56 |
| xAI, then SpaceX | $2bn xAI investment converted into SpaceX Class A shares after SpaceX acquired xAI | 2026-01; converted 2026-02 | Stake held; a merger is openly discussed | S78 |
| Maxwell Technologies | Dry-electrode intellectual property acquired for $235m | 2019 | Integrated into 4680 production | S56 |

The partner map shows the strategic risk: Tesla's autonomy roadmap runs through a single foundry for AI6, its vehicles still depend on CATL, Panasonic and LG for cells, and its largest related-party exposure is to companies its chief executive also controls.

### Geography: China becomes an export base

Tesla's China sales fell 16% year over year in Q3 2026 to 142,133 units while Giga Shanghai exports reached a record 132,978; retail sales for 2026 to date are down 12% as exports doubled, and Beijing cuts the EV export tax rebate in April 2027. Shanghai, with more than 950,000 units of capacity, is now a cost and export base rather than a growth market, exposed to tariffs in the markets it ships to. Berlin set a production record and the US business carries the FSD attach rate, which is why the company's own numbers look better in North America than in the two regions that decide its cost base [S77, S76, S102].

### Energy is where the strategy is working

The energy plan is coherent and funded: 50 GWh of Megafactory Texas capacity started in Q3 2026 alongside 40 GWh in California and 20 GWh in Shanghai, with 7 GWh of Nevada LFP cell capacity in early ramp and the first Megapacks built from Tesla-made cells. The 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified: a contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it, and a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. A 33.1% segment gross margin and data-centre demand give the capital a return that autonomy does not yet. The tension is that revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881bn even as volume rose, so the plan is adding capacity into falling prices [S6, S72].

### The capital allocation question

In January 2026 Tesla invested $2bn in xAI; the stake became SpaceX Class A shares when SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026, and the Q1 2026 cash flow statement records a $2.002bn purchase of SpaceX equity. Three of nine directors carry outside ties — two to SpaceX (Ehrenpreis and Kimbal Musk), one to Straubel at Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier — and the committee uses two. The 2026 proxy is set for a 2026-12-03 meeting, and the 2025 CEO award pays out on a deal price without operational milestones — only one of twelve operational milestones is rated probable, leaving $105.8-120.4bn of unrecognised stock compensation. A shareholder is no longer buying only a car and storage company; a merger scenario makes the position a bet on Musk's wider portfolio, which argues for a smaller size [S78].

### What must be true in 12 months

Three signposts decide whether the strategy is earning its cost of capital. First, unsupervised driving in customer-owned cars in at least one US state by 2027-06-30, with robotaxi revenue disclosed separately — without it, the capex is a subsidy to a pilot. Second, energy gross margin holding above 25% once tariff refunds lapse and 50 GWh of Texas capacity ramps, which tests whether Megapack has pricing power or is a commodity; the unverified backlog claim needs a contracted figure or 2027 deployments above 36.0 GWh to become evidence. Third, capital discipline: 2027 capex at or below $25bn with positive free cash flow, rather than a further draw on the $30bn facilities. The humanoid plan needs its first named customer or billed unit before a 20,000-a-week target means anything. The counter-case is strong: FSD attach above 75% in North America, 1.74 million subscriptions, a record energy backlog and $45.45bn of cash mean the plan can be funded through a slip, and Q3 2026 free cash flow of $1.53bn shows the core still generates cash [S6, S57].

Diligence questions: what is the 2027 capex number and how much of it is contractually committed? What revenue did robotaxi and FSD each earn in Q3 2026? Will the December 2026 meeting put a SpaceX transaction to a shareholder vote, and on what terms? My confidence is high that the strategy is funded and well-resourced for energy, medium that autonomy revenue arrives before 2028, and low that a humanoid robot contributes to profit before 2029.

rows.mechanism: BYD's route is powertrain breadth and price rather than a better battery car; the CO2 mandate rewards both BEVs and, partly, PHEVs, giving BYD two ways to comply.

rows.weakens: The 39,583 BYD figure includes PHEVs and the panel's country mix flatters Tesla's BEV-only lead; a BYD BEV ramp in 2027 would close it.

rows.mechanism: Chinese OEMs carry a structurally lower cost base and can price a mass-segment car at a third of Model Y while still selling more units than it.
rows.benchmark: Geely's Xingyuan at just under RMB 100,000, 38% of the Model Y's RMB 263,500 entry price.
rows.weakens: Tesla's China margin may still be positive and exports keep Shanghai utilisation high; list prices understate discounting.

Regulatory credits fell to $113 million from $417 million, FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million and services revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million.

arguments.markdown:
Tesla scores 4.0 out of 10, and the score is not close to the line that would justify new money: at $403.30 the shares price the autonomy option at $1,424B, 89% of the equity, while the business that pays the bills earns a 2.2-2.5% operating margin once regulatory credits are stripped out. The recommendation is Reduce — trim existing exposure to a residual, buy nothing — on a twelve-month horizon, with medium confidence in the direction and high confidence in the arithmetic. The composite is a weighted average of seven dimensions, and two do most of the work: valuation at 2 out of 10 with a 20% weight and governance at 3 out of 10 with a 15% weight. Remove either and the stock still scores below 5. [S15, S4]

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business quality and moat | 15% | 6 | Energy earned a 33.1% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% and vertical integration in cells and packs is real; vehicle share is falling in China and the premium band is contested | S6, S63, S59 |
| Growth durability | 15% | 5 | Energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881B in Q3 2026 and deliveries fell 2%, so growth now depends on a robotaxi fleet of 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles | S6, S4, S150 |
| Unit economics and margins | 15% | 4 | The ex-credit operating margin is 2.2-2.5% and trailing ROIC is 5.5% against an 11-14% cost of capital | S3, S4 |
| Balance sheet and cash conversion | 15% | 5 | $36.18B of net cash and $30B of undrawn facilities, offset by a 61% fall in nine-month free cash flow and payables at 75.3 days against 62.8 | S4 |
| Governance and capital allocation | 15% | 3 | A 423.7M-share award with $105.82-120.37B of unrecognised compensation, three of nine directors carrying outside ties of which two are to SpaceX, no dividend or buyback | S5, S138 |
| Valuation and margin of safety | 20% | 2 | 443x trailing and 183x 2027E earnings against an 18.5x trailing P/E and 2.4x EV/sales median for the six peers shown in section 8; the margin of safety turns positive only below $111 | S15, S115 |
| Catalysts, regime and positioning | 5% | 3 | A binary merger process is the only re-rating path, against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury and a VIX of 17.20 | S24, S23, S135 |

The weighting is deliberate. A heavy weight on valuation is right because at the current multiple the entry price, not the technology, dominates a five-year return. The governance weight reflects what a standard framework misses: the controlling shareholder's compensation is tied to market-capitalisation milestones, so management is paid for the narrative that supports the multiple rather than for per-share cash flow, and a change of control accelerates the award. Business quality scores 6 rather than 8 because the strongest part of the franchise, energy storage, is a small and shrinking share of revenue in dollars, while vehicles are losing share in the region that sets global prices.

The counter-evidence deserves its own paragraph, because the score could be too harsh in one place: energy earns a 33.1% gross margin at $210M of revenue per GWh, Tesla's $34,436 cost per vehicle is below every Western competitor, and a triple-digit multiple has persisted for two years without mean reversion. If energy revenue doubles and FSD licensing adds a second stream, the core could be worth $70 a share rather than $42.50. That moves the composite by less than half a point, because the core is 11% of the price and the autonomy premium is 11.3 times the leader's mark. The risks run both ways: if the bear branch materialises — autonomy written down, vehicles valued at GM's multiple, the Terafab commitment drawn — value collapses to a small fraction of today's price and Reduce becomes Sell or Avoid at any size. The base case carries $259B of autonomy on a probability-weighted blend of four branches, not the $40B regional fleet alone: at regional-only autonomy the base would be $52.50 and the probability-weighted value $84, and the recommendation would not change. The only branch that lifts the score above 5 is the merger: a negotiated ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price would justify Hold, with the position capped because a failed vote returns the stock to a level set by the operating business. [S6, S63, S120]

Kelly arithmetic at the current price is negative, so the correct unconstrained position is zero. The table sets out the inputs.

| Sizing measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Probability-weighted value | $111 a share on 25/50/25 ($212 / $107 / $19) | S6, S120 |
| Expected return from $403.30 | -72% | S15 |
| Expected value including the merger branch at 40% | $253 a share | S135 |
| Kelly fraction | negative in every branch; constrained to 0 | S6, S120 |
| Residual cap where a mandate requires exposure | 0.5% of net asset value | arithmetic on S6 |
| Fund loss at a 95% bear case on a 0.5% position | -0.48% of net asset value | S6 |

The regime argues for the smaller end of any range: the ten-year Treasury at 4.99%, up 0.93 points in twelve months, raises the discount rate on cash flows arriving after 2030, the S&P 500 is 1.6% below its high with the VIX at the 52nd percentile, and consumer discretionary has lagged the index by 0.3 points over three months. [S24, S23, S22]

### Sensitivity: what moves the value

::: sensitivity
| Rank | Assumption | Base | What would disprove it | Impact on value | Impact level | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031 (15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile implied by the price) | Autonomy at $259B across four weighted branches; 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles; the regional branch alone is $40B, or $52.50 a share | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | high | Authorisations flat near 1,051; no fare disclosure | S4, S6, S137, S150 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | 18.1% in Q3 2026 | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | -$8 a share per 100 bp; -$34 on a 4-point miss | high | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% | 33.1% in Q3 2026, part of it tariff refunds and warranty reimbursements | Q4 margin below 25% once one-offs lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | high | Revenue -16% year over year to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | $13.0B in nine months; above $20B for 2026 | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | medium | Terafab's $16.8B first phase outside the budget | S4, S134 |
| 5 | No value-transferring exchange ratio and dilution of 10.7% from the 2025 award | No terms agreed; a 50%-of-all-shares vote | Ratio struck below market, or new award tranches | -$40 to -$80 a share | high | Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers | S5, S135, S138 |
:::

::: takeaways
1. **Reduce, not Buy:** 89% of the $403.30 price — $1,424B — is an autonomy option valued at 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, while the vehicle and energy business is worth $42.50 a share [S15, S120].
2. **Size to zero:** the probability-weighted value is $111 and the Kelly fraction is negative in every branch, so new money buys nothing and an existing position is capped at 0.5% of net asset value [S6, S120].
3. **Four events would change the call:** a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless permit, an ex-credit operating margin back in double digits, or an exchange ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price [S135, S4].
:::

Five actions would settle the open questions, and each has a date or a document attached. The next results release should be read for a robotaxi revenue line, a fleet count and a fare; a fourth consecutive quarter without one is the clearest signal that the option is not converting. The California DMV and CPUC filings should be checked for a driverless deployment permit, because the current service runs on a limousine authority and no AV permit is listed. The special committees' 8-K should be read for the exchange ratio, the advisers and the treatment of unvested award shares. The annual 10-K should be read for capital expenditure guidance, the Terafab contribution and whether payables reverse. The annual-meeting proxy should be read for the per-tranche thresholds of the CEO award that the text extraction dropped. The conditions for investing are concrete: a share price below the probability-weighted value, or a disclosed robotaxi business whose revenue and cost per mile support the free cash flow the reverse DCF requires. Until one exists, the evidence supports a reduced position and a waiting stance; the score is a statement about the price, not about the engineering.

arguments.markdown:
TSLA closed at $403.30 on 2026-10-29, a $1,594.1B market capitalisation and a $1,558.0B enterprise value, 19% below its 52-week high of $498.83 and 36% above the low of $297.38. The stock is up 14.3% in a month and 30.6% in three, but down 11.3% year to date and 8.4% over twelve months, and the Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-21 — revenue $28.046B, adjusted EPS $0.48 against a $0.45 consensus — have been bought. The regime frames the call: the S&P 500 sits at 7,720.39, up 12.8% year to date and 1.6% below its high, the VIX is 17.20 at the 52nd percentile, and the ten-year Treasury yields 4.99%, up 0.93 points in twelve months, a discount rate that penalises cash flows arriving after 2030. [S15, S141, S22, S23, S24]

### Reduce, at a fraction of the size

Tesla's vehicles, energy and services businesses are worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts; the remaining $356 of the $403.30 price — $1,424B, or 89% of the equity — is an option on robotaxi and robotics that discloses no revenue. Our probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close, on a base that carries $259B of autonomy across four weighted branches rather than the $40B regional fleet alone; even a 40% chance of a premium SpaceX exchange lifts expected value only to $253. The action is to trim rather than to sell short: the option has real value, the balance sheet is not the constraint, and a negotiated exchange ratio could pay $443-487 without any operating delivery. [S6, S15, S120]

Confidence is high on the reported numbers — three years of filings, a third quarter reconciled line by line, and a timestamped market price — medium on the 11-14% cost of capital, and low on anything that requires sizing robotaxi revenue, because no revenue line, fare or cost per mile is disclosed. The 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target and a published range from $128.11 to $600, so the disagreement is about the distribution, not the mean. [S141, S144, S4]

::: verdict
| Rating | Action | Composite score | Confidence | Horizon | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reduce | Trim to a residual of at most 0.5% of net asset value; no new money | 4.0 / 10 | Medium | 12 months | S15, S6, S120 |
:::

::: briefing
| Card | Text | Source |
|---|---|---|
| What the business earns | Energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026 at $210M of revenue per GWh and services 15.9%; together they supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M quarterly gross profit, while regulatory credits fell to $113M, or 15.7% of operating income, from 45.8% of FY2025 operating income | S6, S4 |
| What is not growing | Energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881B and deliveries fell 2%; the robotaxi fleet authorised in Texas was 1,051 vehicles at 2026-10-27, of which 544 were Cybercabs, with paid rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03 | S6, S150 |
| The quality of the cash | Nine-month free cash flow fell 61% to $1,883M as capital expenditure doubled to $13,014M; operating cash flow of $14,897M was carried by a $7,332M payables stretch, with days payable at 75.3 against 62.8, and net cash stands at $36.18B | S4 |
| What the price pays for | 443x trailing earnings, 241x 2026E and 183x 2027E against an 18.5x trailing P/E and 2.4x EV/sales median for the six peers in section 8, on a core business worth $42.50 a share and an autonomy option worth $356, or 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark | S15, S115, S120 |
| Autonomy evidence | 2.0M cumulative unsupervised miles at 2026-09-30, customer-owned unsupervised FSD slipped to about Q2 2027, California testing is with a driver only, and no robotaxi revenue line exists; Waymo runs about 500,000 paid rides a week | S6, S120 |
| Governance and the merger | A 423.7M-share CEO award (10.7% of the count) carries $105.82-120.37B of unrecognised compensation, three of nine directors carry outside ties of which two are to SpaceX, and special committees formed on 2026-10-20; an exchange at market would give Tesla holders 44% of a $3.60T group with no premium | S5, S135, S138 |
| Policy | The federal purchase credit ended for vehicles acquired after 2025-09-30, the EPA repealed the light-duty GHG standards on 2026-02-18 and DOT rolled back CAFE on 2026-10-01, so the ex-credit operating margin of 2.2-2.5% is the base case | S116, S3, S4 |
| Three positives | A $34,436 cost per vehicle below every Western competitor, dry-electrode 4680 cells at yields above 90%, $36.18B of net cash, and a merger path that could re-rate the shares without an operating delivery | S6, S5 |
| Three risks | A two-year autonomy slip that takes the stock to the $19 bear case, an ex-credit margin below 15% if US incentives of $6,594 a unit cannot hold price, and 10.7% award dilution plus a failed merger vote that would return the stock below $300 | S4, S5, S135 |
:::

::: efficiency
| Measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue, trailing twelve months | $103.6B: automotive $75.0B, energy $12.3B, services $16.3B | S6 |
| Operating income, Q3 2026 | $718M, a 2.6% margin, down 56% year over year | S4 |
| Free cash flow, trailing twelve months | $3,303M, a 0.2% yield on the market capitalisation | S4, S15 |
| Gross margin, Q3 2026 | 19.6% consolidated; 33.1% in energy | S4, S6 |
| Valuation | $1,594.1B market capitalisation; $1,558.0B enterprise value; 443x trailing and 183x 2027E earnings | S15, S115 |
| Returns | Trailing ROIC 5.5% against an estimated 11-14% cost of capital | S4 |
:::

::: one-question
What is Tesla's revenue per robotaxi per week in Austin, and what share of those rides runs without a safety driver?

Without that number the autonomy value cannot be tested against a cost per mile, and every scenario above the bear case rests on a registry count of authorised vehicles rather than on unit economics. A disclosed figure that supports the revenue per mile the price implies would move the base case toward the bull case; a quarter of silence after three years of promises would move it toward the bear case.
:::

::: takeaways
1. **The price is the whole debate:** $356 of the $403.30 — 89% — is autonomy and robotics valued at 11.3 times Waymo's $126B, and the core business is worth $42.50 on vehicles at 1.0x sales, energy at 3.5x and net cash at book [S15, S120].
2. **Cash is thinner than it looks:** 61% less free cash flow in nine months, a $7,332M payables stretch and a 5.5% ROIC against an 11-14% cost of capital, with $20B+ of capex still to come [S4].
3. **One event can change the call:** a premium exchange ratio into SpaceX would pay $443-487 without any robotaxi revenue, but the vote needs 50% of all shares, no terms are agreed, and a failed vote returns the stock below $300 [S135, S5].
:::

The follow-up diligence is dated and specific: a robotaxi revenue line, a fleet count and a fare in the next results release; a California driverless deployment permit from the DMV and CPUC filings, where the current service runs on a limousine authority; the exchange ratio, advisers and treatment of unvested awards in the special committees' 8-K; capital expenditure guidance, the Terafab contribution and any payables reversal in the annual 10-K; and the per-tranche thresholds of the CEO award in the proxy for the 2026-12-03 annual meeting. The rating is a statement about the price of an option, not about the quality of the engineering: the vehicle, cell and storage businesses are real, and they are worth about a tenth of what the market pays.

### Customers, buyers and how growth arrives

Tesla sells direct in two segments: automotive at $69,526m of 2025 revenue and energy at $12,771m [S71]. The vehicle buyer is a household or fleet paying cash or Tesla financing; the energy buyer is a utility or developer signing multi-year procurement, with 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026 against 18.5% for automotive. Growth now comes from storage, software (1.74 million FSD subscriptions) and paying Cybercab rides in Austin since 2026-09-03.

### Ownership is concentrated without a dual class

| Elon Musk | Common, incl. 286,428,773 restricted | 699,580,882 | 19.8% | 19.8% | S5 |

Percentages follow the proxy, whose denominator excludes unearned award shares; free float is capped by those stakes, and a margin call on the pledged block would add supply at the worst moment. With one class and no super-voting stock, control runs through the CEO office, the board seat and stake size rather than a charter provision, unlike Ford's dual-class family control or Alphabet's founder shares.

### Control is priced through a contingent award

The 2025 CEO Performance Award is the control instrument: 423,743,904 shares in 12 tranches of 35,311,992, each tied to a market-capitalisation milestone from $2.0 trillion to $8.5 trillion and to 1 of 12 operational milestones (20 million vehicles, 10 million FSD subscriptions, 1 million bots, 1 million robotaxis, Adjusted EBITDA of $50bn to $400bn); none was earned at 2026-10-19 [S5]. At $2.0 trillion the first tranche implies $506 per share on 3.95 billion shares, and because the operational test falls away in a change of control, a deal at $3.0 trillion would earn three tranches, 105.9 million shares, with no robotaxi or Optimus milestone met. Expense is already running: $802m in the first nine months of 2026, $9.74bn unrecognised on the one milestone management judges probable, and $105.82bn-$120.37bn on the rest [S4]. Dilution of 10.7% is designed, not tail, and sits above the current valuation rather than beside it.

### The board can refuse less than it appears

Nine directors sit in three classes, six labelled independent under Nasdaq rules, with Robyn Denholm as chair since November 2018. Ira Ehrenpreis, who chairs both the compensation and the nominating and governance committees, joined SpaceX's board in February 2026; Kimbal Musk is the CEO's brother; JB Straubel, a director, runs Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier. Related-party flows are small in dollars but pointed: Tesla agreed on 2026-01-16 to invest $2.00bn in xAI, converted into SpaceX Class A stock when SpaceX bought xAI on 2026-02-02 and funded on 2026-03-12, while xAI bought $430.1m of Megapacks and SpaceX bought $143.3m of vehicles in 2025. A board setting a Tesla-SpaceX exchange ratio would do so with three of nine directors carrying outside ties — Ehrenpreis and Kimbal Musk to SpaceX, Straubel to Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier — two of those to SpaceX itself; the proxy's retail auto-voting programme adds standing instructions to vote with the board outside a defined special matter [S78]. The counterweight is narrow: the Special Committee used only Denholm and Wilson-Thompson, and 78.2% of votes cast backed 2025 pay.

### Capital allocation has no return floor

Tesla has never paid a dividend, repurchased no shares in 2025, and holds no authorisation to offset dilution. It ended 2026-09-30 with $45.45bn of cash and short-term investments, generated $14.90bn of operating cash flow in nine months against $13.01bn of capex, guided 2026 capex above $20bn, and signed three credit agreements with $30bn of commitments in September 2026 [S6]. Against Ford and GM, which return cash, Tesla offers neither dividend nor buyback, so cash returned to holders is zero while insiders realise value through equity sales. Litigation moved rather than vanished: the Delaware Supreme Court reinstated the 2018 award on 2025-12-19, the 96,000,000-share interim award was forfeited on 2026-04-21, and a securities class action filed on 2025-08-04 in the Western District of Texas covers purchasers from 2023-04-19 to 2025-06-22 over Autopilot, FSD and Robotaxi statements.

A multi-year holder is paid for four things: a contingent award that accelerates on a deal price rather than operating proof; conflict committees that include SpaceX-affiliated directors; new debt against a thin free-cash-flow buffer; and key-person concentration in a CEO who also runs SpaceX. Three conditions would change this judgement — an independent special committee for any SpaceX transaction, no change-of-control acceleration without operating milestones, and a buyback sized to offset stock compensation. None appears in the 2026 proxy, so the governance discount stays. Confidence is high on structure, medium on how a Texas court would treat a challenge to the award; diligence should ask for the pledge's loan-to-value.

The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% x $40B regional, 40% x $126B at Waymo parity, 20% x $600B at scale, 5% x $1,500B at dominance — and $259B is 1.0x Waymo for 769 vehicles that reported nine crashes in August 2026 and disclose no revenue per mile. arguments.markdown:
At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 Tesla is a $1,594.1B equity in which $42.50 a share, $170B, is the vehicle, energy, services and net-cash business and $356 a share, $1,424B, is autonomy and robotics; on 25/50/25 of $212/$107/$19 the probability-weighted value is $111, so the share is a reduce and new money is an option purchase. A market 50% smaller leaves a $105B core, $26 a share, at 94% autonomy; CAC doubled adds $8.1B; revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B; a 5.0x multiple on free cash flow 30% lower is $130; financing six months late is covered by the September facilities [S6, S15, S120, S4, S115]. None reverses the conclusion; a premium exchange ratio does, the one risk the recommendation must price. The three premises carrying the $1,424B are deteriorating at once: NHTSA's Cybercab self-certification inquiry closes for comment on 2026-10-30, the special committees formed on 2026-10-20 have no terms, and nine-month free cash flow of $1,883M contains $7,332M from stretching payables to 75.3 days.

### The core is not harsh at 1.0x sales; it is generous

The sum of the parts pays $91B for vehicles and services at 1.0x sales, $43B for energy at 3.5x and $36B of net cash at book. At GM's implied 0.39x, vehicles and services are worth $29B and the core is $87B, $21.75 a share, with autonomy at 95% of the price; a control buyer tops out at $200-250B, $50-62.50, where autonomy still holds 84%. Energy's 3.5x has support — a 29.7% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% — but doubling revenue to $25B on 5.0x adds $82B, $20 a share, and FSD's 1.74M subscribers at $1,200 a year add $42B, $10.5, leaving the best honest core near $70, autonomy at 83%. The $1,424B premium is 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, for 1,051 Texas-authorised vehicles against Waymo's 4,000. [S6, S131, S120, S15, S151]

### The scenario tree is generous at the base and shallow in the bear

The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% x $40B regional, 40% x $126B at Waymo parity, 20% x $600B at scale, 5% x $1,500B at dominance — and $259B is 2.1x Waymo's $126B for a fleet that reported nine crashes in August 2026 and discloses no revenue per mile. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03. Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week. On the regional branch alone the base is $52.50, 79% below the close, and the 40% probabilities for 2027 unsupervised FSD and a merger sit above the record: EA26002 covers 2.88M vehicles and DP26010 opened on 2026-10-09. An NHTSA rejection has a 35% probability and a $45-90 a share impact. The $35 bear was too shallow: at $19 — autonomy at zero, vehicles at 0.39x, energy at 1.5x, net cash $29B after a Terafab call — the drawdown is 95% and the weighted value falls only from $115 to $111. Above $437 the path is a 10-15% ratio premium, $443-464. [S120, S137, S6, S5, S150, S151, S152, S153, S59]

### Cash carries a two-year slip, not a slip plus a revenue fall

Net cash of $36.18B and $30B of facilities signed in September 2026 carry a two-year autonomy slip at zero free cash flow without issuing a share. The combination does not survive a revenue fall: at a 19% gross margin, 30% lower revenue removes $6.0B of gross profit against $19.1B of annual operating expense, so with $20-25B of capex the annual burn is $20-27B and cash plus facilities run out before 2029. Reported cash flow already borrows from suppliers: payables and accruals added $7,332M and days payable rose from 62.8 to 75.3, worth $2.9B, so normalised free cash flow is minus $1.0B. Terafab adds a commitment Tesla does not control: a $16.8B first phase with SpaceX, Tesla's share undisclosed, outside the ">$20B" 2026 capital budget and called a "general framework" with no binding commitment in SpaceX's IPO filing — capping near-term cash risk and weakening the strategic-asset defence. Tesla is Baa3, SpaceX Baa1; the facilities' pricing is undisclosed. [S4, S134, S138, S147]

### The merger is an option, not a floor

On 2026-10-20 Musk said both boards had formed special committees, no terms agreed and none assured; the Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares, not of those cast, so abstentions count against, and the 2026-10-19 proxy sets the 2026-12-03 annual meeting with no merger proposal. At market the deal is value-neutral: $1,594.1B plus SpaceX's $2.01T is $3.60T, and Tesla holders taking 43-44% own today's price; any premium must be conceded by SpaceX. Either way Tesla holders get 43% of the economics but 84% of votes sit with one holder. The 2025 award writes the incentive down: on a change of control operational milestones lapse and market-cap milestones vest, 423.7M shares are 10.7% dilution, the first $2.0T milestone sits 25% above today's capitalisation, against a $9.74B probable charge and $105.82-120.37B unrecognised. Musk has pledged 207.5M shares, 5.2% of the count; three of nine directors carry outside ties — two to SpaceX (Ehrenpreis, Kimbal Musk), one to Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier — and the committee uses two. [S5, S135, S138]

### Policy is a $5.60 option; competition is a terminal-value risk

Twenty-five state attorneys general and 12 cities and counties sued on 2026-03-19 in the D.C. Circuit over EPA's 2026-02-12 repeal of the 2009 endangerment finding, consolidated on 2026-05-20; a reversal restores the credit pool, but $1.5B of credits at 15x is $22.5B, $5.6 a share, against Q3 credit revenue of $113M, down 73% and 45.8% of FY2025 operating income. Competition is different in kind: BYD holds 2.4% of the European market at EUR 5,500 less per car, Xiaomi is near break-even in its first production year and Waymo runs 500,000 paid rides a week on 4,000 vehicles. If revenue per mile falls from $0.60 to $0.45, the reverse DCF needs 20.9M robotaxis rather than 15.7M, above global annual capacity — $40-60 a share off the bull branch and nothing off 2027 earnings. The unknown unknown is a recall that grounds the fleet and removes its training data. [S136, S138, S59, S4]

| NHTSA rejects Cybercab self-certification or EA26002 becomes a recall | 35% | -$45 to -$90/share | critical | Closes 2026-10-30 | Audit finding; service pause | Exit on a service suspension | S137, S80 |

### Open diligence: three items no filing yet settles

|---|---|---|---|
| Robotaxi revenue, fare and driverless share | Q4 2026 update; 2026 Form 10-K Item 7 and segment note; TxDMV; CPUC | Decides the $259B base | S6, S4, S119 |
| Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call | Definitive agreements; 2026 Form 10-K commitments note; SpaceX 2026 Form 20-F related-party note | Decides 2027-2028 equity need | S147, S134 |
| Per-tranche thresholds of the 2025 CEO award | Award agreement Annex C, SEC EX-99.2; 2025 DEF 14A compensation | Decides change-of-control dilution | S5, S132 |

::: info danger
**A premium exchange ratio is the only route to $403 that needs no robotaxi mile.** At market, $1,594.1B plus SpaceX's $2.01T is $3.60T and Tesla holders' 43-44% is today's price; a 10-15% ratio premium pays $443-464 with no driverless mile. The one event that could turn reduce into hold; size for a failed vote and a 30% fall (S135, S5).
