Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03. Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week. On the regional branch alone the base is $52.50, 79% below the close, and the 40% probabilities for 2027 unsupervised FSD and a merger sit above the record: EA26002 covers 2.88M vehicles and DP26010 opened on 2026-10-09. An NHTSA rejection has a 35% probability and a $45-90 a share impact. The $35 bear was too shallow: at $19 — autonomy at zero, vehicles at 0.39x, energy at 1.5x, net cash $29B after a Terafab call — the drawdown is 95% and the weighted value falls only from $115 to $111. Above $437 the path is a 10-15% ratio premium, $443-464. [S120, S137, S6, S5, S150, S151, S152, S153, S59]

### Cash carries a two-year slip, not a slip plus a revenue fall

Net cash of $36.18B and $30B of facilities signed in September 2026 carry a two-year autonomy slip at zero free cash flow without issuing a share. The combination does not survive a revenue fall: at a 19% gross margin, 30% lower revenue removes $6.0B of gross profit against $19.1B of annual operating expense, so with $20-25B of capex the annual burn is $20-27B and cash plus facilities run out before 2029. Reported cash flow already borrows from suppliers: payables and accruals added $7,332M and days payable rose from 62.8 to 75.3, worth $2.9B, so normalised free cash flow is minus $1.0B. Terafab adds a commitment Tesla does not control: a $16.8B first phase with SpaceX, Tesla's share undisclosed, outside the ">$20B" 2026 capital budget and called a "general framework" with no binding commitment in SpaceX's IPO filing — capping near-term cash risk and weakening the strategic-asset defence. Tesla is Baa3, SpaceX Baa1; the facilities' pricing is undisclosed. [S4, S134, S138, S147]

### The merger is an option, not a floor

On 2026-10-20 Musk said both boards had formed special committees, no terms agreed and none assured; the Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares, not of those cast, so abstentions count against, and the 2026-10-19 proxy sets the 2026-12-03 annual meeting with no merger proposal. At market the deal is value-neutral: $1,594.1B plus SpaceX's $2.01T is $3.60T, and Tesla holders taking 43-44% own today's price; any premium must be conceded by SpaceX. Either way Tesla holders get 43% of the economics but 84% of votes sit with one holder. The 2025 award writes the incentive down: on a change of control operational milestones lapse and market-cap milestones vest, 423.7M shares are 10.7% dilution, the first $2.0T milestone sits 25% above today's capitalisation, against a $9.74B probable charge and $105.82-120.37B unrecognised. Musk has pledged 207.5M shares, 5.2% of the count; three of nine directors carry outside ties — two to SpaceX (Ehrenpreis, Kimbal Musk), one to Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier — and the committee uses two. [S5, S135, S138]

### Policy is a $5.60 option; competition is a terminal-value risk

Twenty-five state attorneys general and 12 cities and counties sued on 2026-03-19 in the D.C. Circuit over EPA's 2026-02-12 repeal of the 2009 endangerment finding, consolidated on 2026-05-20; a reversal restores the credit pool, but $1.5B of credits at 15x is $22.5B, $5.6 a share, against Q3 credit revenue of $113M, down 73% and 45.8% of FY2025 operating income. Competition is different in kind: BYD holds 2.4% of the European market at EUR 5,500 less per car, Xiaomi is near break-even in its first production year and Waymo runs 500,000 paid rides a week on 4,000 vehicles. If revenue per mile falls from $0.60 to $0.45, the reverse DCF needs 20.9M robotaxis rather than 15.7M, above global annual capacity — $40-60 a share off the bull branch and nothing off 2027 earnings. The unknown unknown is a recall that grounds the fleet and removes its training data. [S136, S138, S59, S4]

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 投资潜力与投资逻辑 Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 7 by Lead Analyst, 8,945 characters)
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $356, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 1,051 authorised robotaxi vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27, 544 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S150]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $42.50 a share, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets, and autonomy at $259B in the base case — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance — which is $65.6 a share on 3,952.6M shares, so $42.50 + $65.6 = $108.1 and the base rounds to $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $52.50 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $465 mid-point lifts expected value to $253, still 37% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. arguments.markdown:
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $356, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 1,051 authorised robotaxi vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27, 544 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S150]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $42.50 a share, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets, and autonomy at $259B in the base case — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance — which is $65.6 a share on 3,952.6M shares, so $42.50 + $65.6 = $108.1 and the base rounds to $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $52.50 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $454 mid-point lifts expected value to $248, still 38% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

arguments.markdown:
Tesla scores 4.0 out of 10, and the score is not close to the line that would justify new money: at $403.30 the shares price the autonomy option at $1,424B, 89% of the equity, while the business that pays the bills earns a 2.2-2.5% operating margin once regulatory credits are stripped out. The recommendation is Reduce — trim existing exposure to a residual, buy nothing — on a twelve-month horizon, with medium confidence in the direction and high confidence in the arithmetic. The composite is a weighted average of seven dimensions, and two do most of the work: valuation at 2 out of 10 with a 20% weight and governance at 3 out of 10 with a 15% weight. Remove either and the stock still scores below 5. [S15, S4]

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business quality and moat | 15% | 6 | Energy earned a 33.1% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% and vertical integration in cells and packs is real; vehicle share is falling in China and the premium band is contested | S6, S63, S59 |
| Growth durability | 15% | 5 | Energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881B in Q3 2026 and deliveries fell 2%, so growth now depends on a robotaxi fleet of 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles | S6, S4, S150 |
| Unit economics and margins | 15% | 4 | The ex-credit operating margin is 2.2-2.5% and trailing ROIC is 5.5% against an 11-14% cost of capital | S3, S4 |
| Balance sheet and cash conversion | 15% | 5 | $36.18B of net cash and $30B of undrawn facilities, offset by a 61% fall in nine-month free cash flow and payables at 75.3 days against 62.8 | S4 |
| Governance and capital allocation | 15% | 3 | A 423.7M-share award with $105.82-120.37B of unrecognised compensation, three of nine directors carrying outside ties of which two are to SpaceX, no dividend or buyback | S5, S138 |
| Valuation and margin of safety | 20% | 2 | 443x trailing and 183x 2027E earnings against an 18.5x trailing P/E and 2.4x EV/sales median for the six peers shown in section 8; the margin of safety turns positive only below $111 | S15, S115 |
| Catalysts, regime and positioning | 5% | 3 | A binary merger process is the only re-rating path, against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury and a VIX of 17.20 | S24, S23, S135 |

The weighting is deliberate. A heavy weight on valuation is right because at the current multiple the entry price, not the technology, dominates a five-year return. The governance weight reflects what a standard framework misses: the controlling shareholder's compensation is tied to market-capitalisation milestones, so management is paid for the narrative that supports the multiple rather than for per-share cash flow, and a change of control accelerates the award. Business quality scores 6 rather than 8 because the strongest part of the franchise, energy storage, is a small and shrinking share of revenue in dollars, while vehicles are losing share in the region that sets global prices.

The counter-evidence deserves its own paragraph, because the score could be too harsh in one place: energy earns a 33.1% gross margin at $210M of revenue per GWh, Tesla's $34,436 cost per vehicle is below every Western competitor, and a triple-digit multiple has persisted for two years without mean reversion. If energy revenue doubles and FSD licensing adds a second stream, the core could be worth $70 a share rather than $42.50. That moves the composite by less than half a point, because the core is 11% of the price and the autonomy premium is 11.3 times the leader's mark. The risks run both ways: if the bear branch materialises — autonomy written down, vehicles valued at GM's multiple, the Terafab commitment drawn — value collapses to a small fraction of today's price and Reduce becomes Sell or Avoid at any size. The base case carries $259B of autonomy on a probability-weighted blend of four branches, not the $40B regional fleet alone: at regional-only autonomy the base would be $52.50 and the probability-weighted value $84, and the recommendation would not change. The only branch that lifts the score above 5 is the merger: a negotiated ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price would justify Hold, with the position capped because a failed vote returns the stock to a level set by the operating business. [S6, S63, S120]

Kelly arithmetic at the current price is negative, so the correct unconstrained position is zero. The table sets out the inputs.

| Sizing measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Probability-weighted value | $111 a share on 25/50/25 ($212 / $107 / $19) | S6, S120 |
| Expected return from $403.30 | -72% | S15 |
| Expected value including the merger branch at 40% | $248 a share | S135 |
| Kelly fraction | negative in every branch; constrained to 0 | S6, S120 |
| Residual cap where a mandate requires exposure | 0.5% of net asset value | arithmetic on S6 |
| Fund loss at a 95% bear case on a 0.5% position | -0.48% of net asset value | S6 |

The regime argues for the smaller end of any range: the ten-year Treasury at 4.99%, up 0.93 points in twelve months, raises the discount rate on cash flows arriving after 2030, the S&P 500 is 1.6% below its high with the VIX at the 52nd percentile, and consumer discretionary has lagged the index by 0.3 points over three months. [S24, S23, S22]

### Sensitivity: what moves the value

::: sensitivity
| Rank | Assumption | Base | What would disprove it | Impact on value | Impact level | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031 (15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile implied by the price) | Autonomy at $259B across four weighted branches; 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles; the regional branch alone is $40B, or $52.50 a share | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | high | Authorisations flat near 1,051; no fare disclosure | S4, S6, S137, S150 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | 18.1% in Q3 2026 | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | -$8 a share per 100 bp; -$34 on a 4-point miss | high | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% | 33.1% in Q3 2026, part of it tariff refunds and warranty reimbursements | Q4 margin below 25% once one-offs lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | high | Revenue -16% year over year to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | $13.0B in nine months; above $20B for 2026 | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | medium | Terafab's $16.8B first phase outside the budget | S4, S134 |
| 5 | No value-transferring exchange ratio and dilution of 10.7% from the 2025 award | No terms agreed; a 50%-of-all-shares vote | Ratio struck below market, or new award tranches | -$40 to -$80 a share | high | Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers | S5, S135, S138 |
:::

::: takeaways
1. **Reduce, not Buy:** 89% of the $403.30 price — $1,424B — is an autonomy option valued at 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, while the vehicle and energy business is worth $42.50 a share [S15, S120].
2. **Size to zero:** the probability-weighted value is $111 and the Kelly fraction is negative in every branch, so new money buys nothing and an existing position is capped at 0.5% of net asset value [S6, S120].
3. **Four events would change the call:** a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless permit, an ex-credit operating margin back in double digits, or an exchange ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price [S135, S4].
:::

Five actions would settle the open questions, and each has a date or a document attached. The next results release should be read for a robotaxi revenue line, a fleet count and a fare; a fourth consecutive quarter without one is the clearest signal that the option is not converting. The California DMV and CPUC filings should be checked for a driverless deployment permit, because the current service runs on a limousine authority and no AV permit is listed. The special committees' 8-K should be read for the exchange ratio, the advisers and the treatment of unvested award shares. The annual 10-K should be read for capital expenditure guidance, the Terafab contribution and whether payables reverse. The annual-meeting proxy should be read for the per-tranche thresholds of the CEO award that the text extraction dropped. The conditions for investing are concrete: a share price below the probability-weighted value, or a disclosed robotaxi business whose revenue and cost per mile support the free cash flow the reverse DCF requires. Until one exists, the evidence supports a reduced position and a waiting stance; the score is a statement about the price, not about the engineering.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 竞争格局 Competitive Landscape (competition, revision 7 by Market Analyst, 8,973 characters)
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were small (Toyota 4,964 units, +34.9% month on month; Chevrolet +30.3%; Cadillac +13.1%), and weaker EV programmes retreated once the credit expired, letting the widest-line, lowest-cost survivor take share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only led 30,317 to 7,498, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse: Tesla's Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Q3 2026 automotive cost of revenue of $16,754 million over 486,532 deliveries is $34,436 per vehicle, against automotive revenue of $20,560 million, or $42,258 per unit: an 18.5% automotive gross margin, up from 17.0%. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 技术与产品 Technology & Product (technology_product, revision 8 by Product Analyst, 8,877 characters)
Tesla's technology is proven where it is a manufacturing problem — dry-electrode cells, Megapack integration — and unproven where the valuation sits, judged against two comparison sets: Waymo in autonomy and BYD in manufacturing cost. Compared with Waymo, Tesla has 2.0 million cumulative autonomous miles against 500,000 paid rides a week on 4,000 vehicles; compared with BYD, its 486,532 quarterly deliveries trail BYD's 762,478 electric cars. Its paid driverless permit exists in one state. The technology justifies a premium to a capital-intensive manufacturer in energy and process engineering; it does not yet justify the multiple of a software platform [S6, S59, S76, S107].

### How FSD works, and where it stops

FSD (Supervised) is vision-only: eight cameras feed an end-to-end neural network that outputs steering, acceleration and braking, trained on video from 10.2 million delivered vehicles and run on in-house inference silicon. There is no lidar or radar. Two problems stay unsolved. Cameras blinded by rain, fog or low sun are the subject of NHTSA's Engineering Analysis EA26002, opened 2026-03-19 over 13 crashes in 2.88 million vehicles, testing whether the system detects the degradation. The second is the reliability increment that permits removing the supervisor, which is why customer-owned unsupervised driving moved to Q2 2027. Tesla's October 2026 report claims 6,006,200 miles per major collision, a company-computed, non-fault-based figure the regulator has not verified [S58, S80].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| FSD miles per major collision | 6,006,200 (North America, October 2026) | Company report, FSD-engaged miles | S58 |
| Cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles | 2.0 million (to 2026-09-30) | Company quarterly update | S6 |
| FSD subscriptions and attach | 1.74 million; more than 75% of North American deliveries | Company KPI, excludes free trials | S6 |
| 4680 cell output and density | More than 1 million cells/week; more than 40 GWh; 272 Wh/kg | Giga Texas line data and teardown estimates | S56 |

### Robotaxi: a real service, on one state's terms

Tesla publishes no fleet count of its own. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03. Registrations record authorisations, not vehicles in service, and Tesla discloses no fares, trips per vehicle, utilisation or insurance cost per mile. Permits remain the constraint: Texas allows self-certified commercial driverless operation, while California lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC for testing with a driver only (2026-10-22) [S73, S118, S150, S151, S152].

| Cell performance | 4680: 272 Wh/kg, 10-80% in 35-40 minutes | CATL Qilin 3: full charge in six minutes | Tesla leads on cost, trails on density and charging | S56 |
| BEV volume, Q3 2026 | 486,532 units | BYD 762,478 passenger BEVs, +30.89% year over year | Cost leadership has moved to China | S76 |

### Cells: a cost moat, not a performance one

Giga Texas runs above one million 4680 cells a week at more than 40 GWh of installed capacity, and since January 2026 both electrodes use the dry process in production — a step CATL, Panasonic, LG and Samsung SDI have not taken to commercial scale. The economics are real: electrode cost 50% lower at full scale, 41% less line capex and more than 30% less factory energy. The product is not: energy density trails by 10-15%, charging is slower than Panasonic 2170 packs, yields above 90% sit below the 98% of mature producers, and Tesla still buys CATL LFP and Panasonic or LG 2170 cells for Shanghai and Fremont Model Y. Battery availability, not demand, remained the stated limit on 2026 volume [S56].

### Energy is the proven technology

Megapack is the one line where Tesla holds a genuine integration advantage and prices it: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026 at a 33.1% gross margin, with 50 GWh of Texas capacity starting. The weak point is the order book, not the product: the 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified. A contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it; a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. {"url":"https://cnevpost.com/2026/10/01/huawei-hima-sept-2026-deliveries/","title":"Huawei HIMA delivers 37,490 vehicles in September, extending year-on-year decline to fourth month","text":"Lei Kang

 •

 Huawei HIMA monthly deliveries

 2024

 2025

 2026

HIMA's September deliveries fell 29.15% year-on-year, with year-to-date growth slowing to 5.27%.
Deliveries declined 10.95% from August, marking the alliance's third consecutive month-on-month decrease.

Huawei-led Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance (HIMA) delivered 37,490 vehicles in September, its fourth consecutive month of year-on-year declines, signaling mounting sales pressure.
September deliveries fell 29.15% from a year earlier and 10.95% from August, according to figures HIMA released on Thursday. The alliance also recorded its third consecutive month-on-month decline.
In the first 9 months of the year, HIMA delivered 367,229 vehicles, up 5.27% from a year earlier. That marked a sharp slowdown from the 11.42% growth recorded in the first 8 months.

HIMA said cumulative deliveries across its lineup had exceeded 1.56 million vehicles.
The September sales decline came during a month of several new product debuts. HIMA last month launched or opened pre-sales for the updated Luxeed R7, Stelato V8, Luxeed RX and updated Aito M8.
The decline also coincided with changes to the partnership between Huawei and Seres (HKEX: 9927) over the Aito brand. Aito was HIMA's first brand and remains among the alliance's biggest sales contributors.
Huawei and Seres announced on September 15 that Aito would explore a new partnership model within HIMA, with Seres taking the lead and Huawei providing support.
The changes cover product definition, product design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations. Aito will remain within HIMA, with customer benefits and ongoing services unaffected.
HIMA's other brands will retain the model in which Huawei leads the entire process. Luxeed, Stelato, Maextro and Shangjie are outside the scope of the changes.
Chinese media outlet Yicai reported on Thursday that the 2 companies had recently begun a new round of talks and were expected to adjust their partnership model again.
The report said the cooperation model over Aito was unlikely to change. Building on that arrangement, the partnership could deepen further, rather than simply shift to a model in which Seres leads and Huawei provides support.
Aito opened pre-sales for the updated M8 SUV on September 30. Its starting pre-sales price is 389,800 yuan ($57,880), 30,000 yuan above the previous version's starting list price.
The updated M8 continues to offer extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) and battery electric vehicle (BEV) variants, with 5-seat and 6-seat configurations.
The BEV version offers a CLTC range of up to 830 kilometers, while the EREV has a combined range of up to 1,435 kilometers.
The M8 is a core model for Aito, but sales have weakened recently. Its cumulative deliveries had exceeded 180,000 vehicles as of August 6, though sales have fallen month-on-month for several consecutive months.

 Aito will remain in HIMA, while Huawei will continue to lead operations across the alliance's 4 other brands.

arguments.title: Huawei HIMA delivers 37,490 vehicles in September, extending year-on-year decline to fourth month
arguments.claims: Huawei-led HIMA delivered 37,490 vehicles in September 2026, down 29.15% year on year and 10.95% month on month, a fourth consecutive year-on-year decline; 367,229 vehicles in January-September 2026, up 5.27%; cumulative 1.56 million. arguments.title: Xpeng September deliveries hit 2026 high despite slight year-on-year decline
arguments.claims: Xpeng delivered 41,256 vehicles in September 2026, down 0.78% year on year and up 5.50% month on month; Q3 2026 deliveries 118,390, a record, up 2.05% year on year; January-September 2026 deliveries 284,367, down 9.20%. arguments.claims_weakened: The claim that Xpeng is a volume threat that is still scaling: 9M 2026 deliveries are down 9.20% year on year despite the record quarter; its September volume is roughly a tenth of BYD's.

{"url":"https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/xpeng-announces-vehicle-delivery-results-for-september-and-third-quarter-2026-302895410.html","title":"XPENG Announces Vehicle Delivery Results for September and Third Quarter 2026","text":", /PRNewswire/ -- XPeng Inc. ("XPENG" or the "Company,"NYSE: XPEV and HKEX: 9868), a leading global Physical AI company, today announced its vehicle delivery results for September and the third quarter of 2026.
In September 2026, XPENG delivered 41,256 vehicles, representing a 5% increase over the prior month. Monthly deliveries of the XPENG L03 exceeded 10,000 units.
For the third quarter of 2026, XPENG delivered a total of 118,390 vehicles, marking a 15% increase over the previous quarter.
On September 17, 2026, XPENG officially launched the G9L, a premium flagship SUV featuring XPENG's latest technologies, in China. The model's global launch will take place in Paris, France, in October.
On September 22, 2026, XPENG began rolling out XOS 6.3.0 in China, powered by the latest version of its VLA 2.0 model.
As of September 30, 2026, XPENG's self-operated charging network in China covered more than 430 cities and comprised over 4,000 stations, including more than 3,510 ultra-fast charging stations, with over 22,200 charging piles in total. On September 15, XPENG opened its first-ever X-Energy megawatt ultra-fast charging station in Hong Kong.
XPENG's electric vehicles delivered from January to September 2026 are expected to reduce life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions by more than 4.14 million tons compared to internal combustion engine vehicles, equivalent to the carbon absorbed by 68.53 million young trees over 10 years.
About XPENG
XPENG is a leading global Physical AI company, dedicated to bringing artificial intelligence into the physical world to reshape future mobility and smart living. Through in-house R&D, XPENG has developed a full-stack Physical AI architecture spanning Turing AI chips, world foundation models, and highly integrated software and hardware applications. This unified technology foundation of XPENG powers an expansive product portfolio of smart EVs, robotaxis, and humanoid robots, advancing the deployment of Physical AI at scale. Headquartered in Guangzhou, China, XPENG is dual-primary listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. With global capabilities across R&D, manufacturing, sales, and services, XPENG drives continuous technological innovation and fosters an open Physical AI ecosystem, making life smarter, safer, and better for users worldwide. For more information, please visit https://www.xpeng.com/.

arguments.markdown:
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in 9M 2026, and Chinese retail down 11.9% to 381,088 in a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. Behind it the gains were small (Toyota 4,964 units, +34.9% month on month; Chevrolet +30.3%; Cadillac +13.1%), and weaker EV programmes retreated after the credit expired, letting the widest-line, lowest-cost survivor take share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: its mid-size SUV has sold since Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only led 30,317 to 7,498, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse: Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai wholesale held only on a 58.3% September export rise. Two closer threats sit in Model Y's band: Xpeng delivered 41,256 in September 2026 (−0.78% year on year) and launched the G9L on 2026-09-17 from RMB 231,800 (~$34,420), while Huawei's HIMA delivered 367,229 in January-September 2026, within 4% of Tesla's 381,088 China retail, with the updated AITO M8 from RMB 389,800 (~$57,880) [S104, S101, S102, S155, S156].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Q3 2026 automotive cost of revenue of $16,754 million over 486,532 deliveries is $34,436 per vehicle, against automotive revenue of $20,560 million, or $42,258 per unit: an 18.5% automotive gross margin, up from 17.0%. The margin is healthy at a premium price point and rests on mix, credits and software, not price: regulatory credits fell to $113 million from $417 million, FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. The $34,436 is 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the Geely Xingyuan at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), the gap a $25,000-35,000 price war would expose [S4, S6, S101].

### Storage and autonomy are where the advantage is thinnest

In grid storage pricing power sits with the cell makers: CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of energy-storage batteries in H1 2026, up 81%, for 27.1% of the global ESS cell market, while Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months and energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack prices and tariff refunds. Tesla differentiates on integration and delivery speed, not cell cost. In autonomy the gap is disclosed scale: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, while Baidu's Apollo Go runs in more than 10 Chinese cities and Tesla publishes no paid-ride count. Confidence is high on US and European share data, medium on China because retail and wholesale definitions differ, low on autonomy because no operator discloses audited paid rides. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 竞争格局 Competitive Landscape (competition, revision 7 by Market Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,973 characters)
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026, and Chinese retail sales down 11.9% to 381,088 against a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. The gains behind it were small (Toyota 4,964 units, +34.9% month on month; Chevrolet +30.3%; Cadillac +13.1%), and weaker EV programmes retreated once the credit expired, letting the widest-line, lowest-cost survivor take share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: deliveries of its new mid-size SUV began in Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only led 30,317 to 7,498, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume in the segments below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse: Tesla's Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai's wholesale held only because exports rose 58.3% in September [S104, S101, S102].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Q3 2026 automotive cost of revenue of $16,754 million over 486,532 deliveries is $34,436 per vehicle, against automotive revenue of $20,560 million, or $42,258 per unit: an 18.5% automotive gross margin, up from 17.0%. That margin is healthy at a premium price point and rests on mix, credits and software rather than price: regulatory credits fell to $113 million from $417 million, FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. The $34,436 is 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the Geely Xingyuan at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820): the cost gap a $25,000-35,000 price war would expose [S4, S6, S101].

### Storage and autonomy are where the advantage is thinnest

In grid storage the pricing power sits with the cell makers: CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of energy-storage batteries in the first half of 2026, up 81%, for 27.1% of the global ESS battery market, while Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months and its energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Tesla's differentiation is integration and delivery speed, not cell cost. In autonomy the gap is disclosed scale: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, while Baidu's Apollo Go operates in more than 10 Chinese cities and Tesla publishes no paid-ride count. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 风险评估 Risk Assessment (risk, revision 5 by Red Team Analyst, 8,973 characters)
At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 Tesla is a $1,594.1B equity in which $42.50 a share, $170B, is the vehicle, energy, services and net-cash business and $356 a share, $1,424B, is autonomy and robotics; on 25/50/25 of $212/$107/$19 the probability-weighted value is $111, so the share is a reduce and new money is an option purchase. A market 50% smaller leaves a $105B core, $26 a share, at 94% autonomy; CAC doubled adds $8.1B; revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B; a 5.0x multiple on free cash flow 30% lower is $130; financing six months late is covered by the September facilities [S6, S15, S120, S4, S115]. None reverses the conclusion; a premium exchange ratio does, the one risk the recommendation must price. The three premises carrying the $1,424B are deteriorating at once: NHTSA's Cybercab self-certification inquiry closes for comment on 2026-10-30, the special committees formed on 2026-10-20 have no terms, and nine-month free cash flow of $1,883M contains $7,332M from stretching payables to 75.3 days.

### The core is not harsh at 1.0x sales; it is generous

The sum of the parts pays $91B for vehicles and services at 1.0x sales, $43B for energy at 3.5x and $36B of net cash at book. At GM's implied 0.39x, vehicles and services are worth $29B and the core is $87B, $21.75 a share, with autonomy at 95% of the price; a control buyer tops out at $200-250B, $50-62.50, where autonomy still holds 84%. Energy's 3.5x has support — a 29.7% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% — but doubling revenue to $25B on 5.0x adds $82B, $20 a share, and FSD's 1.74M subscribers at $1,200 a year add $42B, $10.5, leaving the best honest core near $70, autonomy at 83%. The $1,424B premium is 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, for 1,051 Texas-authorised vehicles against Waymo's 4,000. [S6, S131, S120, S15, S151]

### The scenario tree is generous at the base and shallow in the bear

The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% x $40B regional, 40% x $126B at Waymo parity, 20% x $600B at scale, 5% x $1,500B at dominance — and $259B is 2.1x Waymo's $126B for a fleet that reported nine crashes in August 2026 and discloses no revenue per mile. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03. Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week. On the regional branch alone the base is $52.50, 79% below the close, and the 40% probabilities for 2027 unsupervised FSD and a merger sit above the record: EA26002 covers 2.88M vehicles and DP26010 opened on 2026-10-09. An NHTSA rejection has a 35% probability and a $45-90 a share impact. The $35 bear was too shallow: at $19 — autonomy at zero, vehicles at 0.39x, energy at 1.5x, net cash $29B after a Terafab call — the drawdown is 95% and the weighted value falls only from $115 to $111. Above $437 the path is a 10-15% ratio premium, $443-464. [S120, S137, S6, S5, S150, S151, S152, S153, S59]

### Cash carries a two-year slip, not a slip plus a revenue fall

Net cash of $36.18B and $30B of facilities signed in September 2026 carry a two-year autonomy slip at zero free cash flow without issuing a share. The combination does not survive a revenue fall: at a 19% gross margin, 30% lower revenue removes $6.0B of gross profit against $19.1B of annual operating expense, so with $20-25B of capex the annual burn is $20-27B and cash plus facilities run out before 2029. Reported cash flow already borrows from suppliers: payables and accruals added $7,332M and days payable rose from 62.8 to 75.3, worth $2.9B, so normalised free cash flow is minus $1.0B. Terafab adds a commitment Tesla does not control: a $16.8B first phase with SpaceX, Tesla's share undisclosed, outside the ">$20B" 2026 capital budget and called a "general framework" with no binding commitment in SpaceX's IPO filing — capping near-term cash risk and weakening the strategic-asset defence. Tesla is Baa3, SpaceX Baa1; the facilities' pricing is undisclosed. [S4, S134, S138, S147]

### The merger is an option, not a floor

On 2026-10-20 Musk said both boards had formed special committees, no terms agreed and none assured; the Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares, not of those cast, so abstentions count against, and the 2026-10-19 proxy sets the 2026-12-03 annual meeting with no merger proposal. At market the deal is value-neutral: $1,594.1B plus SpaceX's $2.01T is $3.60T, and Tesla holders taking 43-44% own today's price; any premium must be conceded by SpaceX. Either way Tesla holders get 43% of the economics but 84% of votes sit with one holder. The 2025 award writes the incentive down: on a change of control operational milestones lapse and market-cap milestones vest, 423.7M shares are 10.7% dilution, the first $2.0T milestone sits 25% above today's capitalisation, against a $9.74B probable charge and $105.82-120.37B unrecognised. Musk has pledged 207.5M shares, 5.2% of the count; three of nine directors carry outside ties — two to SpaceX (Ehrenpreis, Kimbal Musk), one to Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier — and the committee uses two. [S5, S135, S138]

### Policy is a $5.60 option; competition is a terminal-value risk

Twenty-five state attorneys general and 12 cities and counties sued on 2026-03-19 in the D.C. Circuit over EPA's 2026-02-12 repeal of the 2009 endangerment finding, consolidated on 2026-05-20; a reversal restores the credit pool, but $1.5B of credits at 15x is $22.5B, $5.6 a share, against Q3 credit revenue of $113M, down 73% and 45.8% of FY2025 operating income. Competition is different in kind: BYD holds 2.4% of the European market at EUR 5,500 less per car, Xiaomi is near break-even in its first production year and Waymo runs 500,000 paid rides a week on 4,000 vehicles. If revenue per mile falls from $0.60 to $0.45, the reverse DCF needs 20.9M robotaxis rather than 15.7M, above global annual capacity — $40-60 a share off the bull branch and nothing off 2027 earnings. The unknown unknown is a recall that grounds the fleet and removes its training data. [S136, S138, S59, S4]

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 投资潜力与投资逻辑 Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 8 by Lead Analyst, 8,945 characters)
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $356, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 1,051 authorised robotaxi vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27, 544 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S150]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $42.50 a share, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets, and autonomy at $259B in the base case — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance — which is $65.6 a share on 3,952.6M shares, so $42.50 + $65.6 = $108.1 and the base rounds to $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $52.50 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $454 mid-point lifts expected value to $248, still 38% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

::: scenarios
| Scenario | Probability | Drivers | Outcome | Signposts | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull | 25% | Robotaxi in several metros at 1.0x Waymo's $126B; energy at 6.0x sales; 1.74M FSD subscriptions | $212 a share, -47% from $403.30; -12.1% a year to 2031 | Robotaxi revenue line disclosed; California driverless permit; Texas authorised fleet above 5,000 vehicles | S6, S120, S150 |
| Base | 50% | Autonomy at $259B, the probability-weighted blend of the four branches (35% × $40B, 40% × $126B, 20% × $600B, 5% × $1,500B); core at $42.50; energy at 3.5x sales | $107 a share, -73% | Q4 2026 update with no robotaxi revenue despite 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles; no fare or cost per mile disclosed | S6, S120, S150 |
| Bear | 25% | Autonomy written down; vehicles at GM's 0.39x sales; Terafab commitment; credit-free margin | $19 a share, -95% | Unsupervised FSD slips past 2027; NHTSA recall of the Cybercab; merger vote fails | S6, S120, S137 |
:::

### Key assumptions, ranked

| Rank | Assumption | Confidence | What would disprove it | Impact if wrong | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031: 15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile is what the reverse DCF needs | low | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | Authorisations flat near 1,051 Texas vehicles; no fare disclosure; safety-driver hours rising | S4, S6, S137, S150 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | medium | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | Each 100 bp is $756M, 22% of trailing operating income | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% with revenue growth | medium | Q4 margin below 25% once tariff refunds lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | Q3 revenue fell 16% to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | low | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | Terafab's $16.8B first phase sits outside the 2026 budget | S4, S134 |
| 5 | No value-transferring exchange ratio; award dilution held at 10.7% | low | Ratio struck below market, or new tranches granted | -$40 to -$80 a share | Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers | S5, S135, S138 |

Assumption 1 sets the price and is the least evidenced: no robotaxi revenue, no fare and no cost per mile are disclosed, so the largest component of value rests on a registry count of authorised vehicles rather than on unit economics. Assumptions 2 and 3 decide whether the core is worth $42.50 or $21.75, and management can still influence both in 2027 — the ex-credit operating margin has been cut to 2.2-2.5%, while energy supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M third-quarter gross profit at a margin 2.5 times Fluence's 13.1%. Assumptions 4 and 5 are about survival and dilution rather than growth: $36.18B of net cash covers eighteen months of zero free cash flow, but not that plus a $16.8B capital call whose Tesla share is undisclosed. [S4, S6]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cisco | cautionary | 2000-2024 | Revenue grew from $12.5B to $57B and trailing net income passed its 1999 level by 2003, yet a buyer at the March 2000 peak of $500B waited until 2021 to break even. A correct thesis does not rescue the entry multiple. | S140 |
| Amazon | cautionary | 1999-2001 | The business compounded into one of the great franchises, but the stock fell more than 90% and took a decade to recover; the option paid only for the holder who could sit through the drawdown. | S143 |
| GM Cruise | cautionary | 2016-2024 | More than $10B of operating losses and less than $500M of revenue before GM shut the robotaxi unit in December 2024 for $1B a year of savings. Automaker capital is no substitute for paid driverless miles. | S142 |
| Waymo | best | 2024-2026 | The valuation went from $45B in October 2024 to $126B in February 2026 on 500,000 paid driverless rides a week — proof the service can scale, and a mark that Tesla's autonomy value exceeds 11-fold. | S120 |
:::

The precedents give one rule: when a real technology shift is already in the price, the entry multiple sets the return, not whether the technology wins; the base rate for a follower in autonomy is a write-off, not a slow fade; and the leader's private mark, $126B, is the only independent price for the option — 9% of what the market pays for Tesla's version. A holder should own Tesla's autonomy at a discount to that mark, not at 11.3 times it, and size the position so the Cruise outcome is survivable. [S140, S142]

### Where the case turns, and what to do now

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. At $403.30 it sits in the third zone, with the ten-year Treasury at 4.99% raising the discount rate on post-2030 cash flows. Do not invest new money now. Wait for one of three milestones: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless deployment permit, or special-committee terms at a premium to market rather than at market. If the mandate requires exposure, hold a residual of 0.25-0.5% of net asset value, sized so a failed vote and a 30% drawdown do not breach the risk budget, and vote against any ratio that transfers value to the controlling shareholder. Pass on the blue-sky branch: it needs global robotaxi and humanoid dominance and pays 8% from here. Diligence questions: revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, the share of rides running without a safety driver, and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Confidence is high that the core is not worth $403.30, medium on the autonomy tree, low on the merger. What would change the call: a second consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-credit operating margin, an FSD licensing contract with a named automaker, or a ratio that values Tesla at a premium to its undisturbed price. [S15, S5]"}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 综合评分与投资建议 Comprehensive Scoring & Recommendation (scoring, revision 10 by Lead Analyst, 8,823 characters)
Tesla scores 4.0 out of 10, and the score is not close to the line that would justify new money: at $403.30 the shares price the autonomy option at $1,424B, 89% of the equity, while the business that pays the bills earns a 2.2-2.5% operating margin once regulatory credits are stripped out. The recommendation is Reduce — trim existing exposure to a residual, buy nothing — on a twelve-month horizon, with medium confidence in the direction and high confidence in the arithmetic. The composite is a weighted average of seven dimensions, and two do most of the work: valuation at 2 out of 10 with a 20% weight and governance at 3 out of 10 with a 15% weight. Remove either and the stock still scores below 5. [S15, S4]

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business quality and moat | 15% | 6 | Energy earned a 33.1% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% and vertical integration in cells and packs is real; vehicle share is falling in China and the premium band is contested | S6, S63, S59 |
| Growth durability | 15% | 5 | Energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881B in Q3 2026 and deliveries fell 2%, so growth now depends on a robotaxi fleet of 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles | S6, S4, S150 |
| Unit economics and margins | 15% | 4 | The ex-credit operating margin is 2.2-2.5% and trailing ROIC is 5.5% against an 11-14% cost of capital | S3, S4 |
| Balance sheet and cash conversion | 15% | 5 | $36.18B of net cash and $30B of undrawn facilities, offset by a 61% fall in nine-month free cash flow and payables at 75.3 days against 62.8 | S4 |
| Governance and capital allocation | 15% | 3 | A 423.7M-share award with $105.82-120.37B of unrecognised compensation, three of nine directors carrying outside ties of which two are to SpaceX, no dividend or buyback | S5, S138 |
| Valuation and margin of safety | 20% | 2 | 443x trailing and 183x 2027E earnings against an 18.5x trailing P/E and 2.4x EV/sales median for the six peers shown in section 8; the margin of safety turns positive only below $111 | S15, S115 |
| Catalysts, regime and positioning | 5% | 3 | A binary merger process is the only re-rating path, against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury and a VIX of 17.20 | S24, S23, S135 |

The weighting is deliberate. A heavy weight on valuation is right because at the current multiple the entry price, not the technology, dominates a five-year return. The governance weight reflects what a standard framework misses: the controlling shareholder's compensation is tied to market-capitalisation milestones, so management is paid for the narrative that supports the multiple rather than for per-share cash flow, and a change of control accelerates the award. Business quality scores 6 rather than 8 because the strongest part of the franchise, energy storage, is a small and shrinking share of revenue in dollars, while vehicles are losing share in the region that sets global prices.

The counter-evidence deserves its own paragraph, because the score could be too harsh in one place: energy earns a 33.1% gross margin at $210M of revenue per GWh, Tesla's $34,436 cost per vehicle is below every Western competitor, and a triple-digit multiple has persisted for two years without mean reversion. If energy revenue doubles and FSD licensing adds a second stream, the core could be worth $70 a share rather than $42.50. That moves the composite by less than half a point, because the core is 11% of the price and the autonomy premium is 11.3 times the leader's mark. The risks run both ways: if the bear branch materialises — autonomy written down, vehicles valued at GM's multiple, the Terafab commitment drawn — value collapses to a small fraction of today's price and Reduce becomes Sell or Avoid at any size. The base case carries $259B of autonomy on a probability-weighted blend of four branches, not the $40B regional fleet alone: at regional-only autonomy the base would be $52.50 and the probability-weighted value $84, and the recommendation would not change. The only branch that lifts the score above 5 is the merger: a negotiated ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price would justify Hold, with the position capped because a failed vote returns the stock to a level set by the operating business. [S6, S63, S120]

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 市场与行业分析 Market & Industry Analysis (market, revision 8 by Market Analyst, 8,817 characters)
Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. No plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a 0.95 million unit annual run-rate at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, while hybrids took 36.6%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6%. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced by the 2026 energy-price shock. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved Tesla's way for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

### Market size: $950 billion of cars, $83 billion of storage

The 2026 market size is $950 billion for electric cars and $82.7 billion for grid storage, measured at Tesla's realised prices as a proxy because no agency publishes revenue; global electric-car units rise from an implied 16.7 million in 2024 to 23.0 million in 2026, a 17.4% compound annual growth rate, and the battery-electric slice of the three regions where Tesla sells is not published, so the table bounds obtainable revenue rather than measuring the serviceable market. Grid storage is the only pool growing faster than Tesla can supply: 353.4 GWh of deployments are expected in 2026, up 28% on 275.3 GWh in 2025, and Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months, 14% of the market, against 50 GWh of Texas capacity. The budget owner is a utility or independent power producer behind an interconnection queue, so demand is sticky but price-sensitive: energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Ride-hailing cannot yet be sized from disclosure: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, 26 million a year; even at $100 a ride that is $2.6 billion, 0.3% of the electric-car TAM, while Tesla discloses no fare, booking or paid-ride figure. Adjusted EBITDA is struck before stock-based compensation, so 104 times is understated as a cash multiple. The operating leverage cuts both ways: each 100 basis points of automotive gross margin excluding credits is worth $756 million, or $0.19 a share, on annualised nine-month automotive revenue of $75,561 million, 22% of trailing operating income, so a two-point margin miss plus a $4 billion capital-expenditure overshoot would take 2027 free cash flow to roughly negative $2 billion, while energy growth of 40% at a 30% margin and an automotive margin of 20% would lift it to about $8 billion. Tesla offers no cash exit at $1.59 trillion. It has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation, and its entire $45.4B of cash and short-term investments would retire 2.85% of the 3.953B shares outstanding. The largest buyout ever completed — Electronic Arts at $55B in August 2026 — is 3.4% of Tesla's market capitalisation, so no financial sponsor can write this cheque, and no automaker can either: GM and Ford together are $118.4B, 7.4% of Tesla. What remains is a sale into a market that trades $14.0B of Tesla a day, or a share exchange into SpaceX, and both leave the return hostage to a re-rating that five years have not delivered. [S3, S130]

### The company returns nothing, and cannot return much

Tesla's 10-K states that it has never declared or paid a cash dividend, does not anticipate doing so, and purchased no equity securities in fiscal 2025. Trailing free cash flow of $3,303M is a 0.2% yield on the capitalisation, and nine-month capital expenditure of $13,014M runs at 2.1x depreciation: the cash is going into factories, cells and training compute, not to holders. Against GM's 12.4% total shareholder yield and Ford's 5.9%, Tesla's is zero. Even a maximal buyback using the whole cash pile would move the share count by less than three points, and it would leave a company spending $17B a year on capital projects with no liquidity buffer. Capital return is a governance choice, and the controlling shareholder has consistently chosen reinvestment. [S6]

### The exit that always works is the tape

The secondary market is the only channel that is always open. Tesla trades 36.96M shares and $14.0B a day over twenty days, so a $500M position is 3.6% of a single day's value and no holder is trapped by liquidity. Short interest of 69.35M shares, 2.19% of the float and 2.2 days to cover, means the marginal seller is not fighting a crowded short either. Passive ownership is a flow that follows the index and the price rather than a bid that supports it; Tesla's exact float-adjusted S&P 500 weight is not disclosed in the sources retrieved, and after the top ten names reached 39.03% of the index on 2026-10-10 the marginal index buyer is a shrinking share of demand. [S15, S114]

### No control buyer exists, at any price

A cash takeover is arithmetically out of reach. The pieces themselves are worth $170B on the sum of the parts — vehicles at 1.0x sales, energy at 3.5x, net cash at book — and a control buyer for those assets alone would pay $200-250B with a premium, which is one-eighth of the current capitalisation and therefore not a route to today's price. Alphabet, at $3,493.5B, is the only US company with the balance sheet to write a $1.6T cheque, and it is the closest competitor in autonomous driving, which makes antitrust the binding constraint rather than price. Musk's 19.8% stake and 207.5M pledged shares mean nothing happens without him, and a hostile approach is legally and financially impossible at this size. [S5, S6]

| Share exchange with SpaceX | SpaceX (NasdaqGS: SPCX) | Musk-sponsored combination; special committees formed 2026-10-20 | 2027-2028 | Medium | S129, S128 |
| Cash take-private | None identified | $1,594.1B is 29x the largest LBO on record ($55B) | None | Very low | S130 |
| Acquisition by an automaker | GM, Ford | Combined market cap $118.4B, 7.4% of Tesla | None | Very low | S17, S19 |
| Acquisition by a platform company | Alphabet | $3,493.5B market cap, but antitrust in autonomy | None | Very low | S113 |
| Buyback or dividend | Tesla | No programme; no dividend ever declared | None | Very low | S3 |

### The one live route is a share exchange with SpaceX

On 2026-10-21 both boards formed special committees to explore a combination, days after Musk called the idea a "good idea" on the third-quarter earnings call. SpaceX listed on 2026-06-12 at $135 a share and a $1.77T valuation, reached $2.1T on its first day, and the combined group would be worth well over $3 trillion. At those marks Tesla holders would own 43% of the equity — but they would exchange one-share-one-vote stock for a company where super-voting shares give Musk about 84% of the vote, against 20% at Tesla. That is the governance price of the only transformative exit available, and it is being negotiated by two boards that have not historically pushed back: Tesla invested $2B in xAI after its chair expressed scepticism, and it rescued SolarCity in 2016. ### What would make the exit valuable, and what stands in the way

The counter-case deserves weight. A negotiated combination would carry a premium to the undisturbed price, and a holder who sells into it captures that premium without waiting for a re-rating; SpaceX's Starlink cash flows are real, so the merged entity would have earnings that Tesla alone does not; and if the ratio is struck on market values, a Tesla holder participates in that cash flow from day one. The risk is that the ratio, not a cash price, is what gets negotiated, and that a controlled board sets it. The 2025 CEO Performance Award reinforces the point: its change-of-control terms let unearned shares vest on market-capitalisation milestones alone, so the controlling shareholder's incentive in a sale is to maximise the headline value, not the terms minority holders receive. [S5, S132]

For a public-equity holder the practical conclusion is that monetisation is a sale into the secondary market at whatever multiple prevails, with a merger into SpaceX as the only event that could produce a premium, and no dividend, no buyback and no cash bid to fall back on. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 投资潜力与投资逻辑 Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 8 by Lead Analyst, 8,945 characters)
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $356, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 1,051 authorised robotaxi vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27, 544 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S150]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $42.50 a share, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets, and autonomy at $259B in the base case — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance — which is $65.6 a share on 3,952.6M shares, so $42.50 + $65.6 = $108.1 and the base rounds to $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $52.50 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $454 mid-point lifts expected value to $248, still 38% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

Assumption 1 sets the price and is the least evidenced: no robotaxi revenue, no fare and no cost per mile are disclosed, so the largest component of value rests on a registry count of authorised vehicles rather than on unit economics. Assumptions 2 and 3 decide whether the core is worth $42.50 or $21.75, and management can still influence both in 2027 — the ex-credit operating margin has been cut to 2.2-2.5%, while energy supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M third-quarter gross profit at a margin 2.5 times Fluence's 13.1%. Assumptions 4 and 5 are about survival and dilution rather than growth: $36.18B of net cash covers eighteen months of zero free cash flow, but not that plus a $16.8B capital call whose Tesla share is undisclosed. [S4, S6]

| GM Cruise | cautionary | 2016-2024 | More than $10B of operating losses and less than $500M of revenue before GM shut the robotaxi unit in December 2024 for $1B a year of savings. Automaker capital is no substitute for paid driverless miles. | S142 |
| Waymo | best | 2024-2026 | The valuation went from $45B in October 2024 to $126B in February 2026 on 500,000 paid driverless rides a week — proof the service can scale, and a mark that Tesla's autonomy value exceeds 11-fold. | S120 |
:::

The precedents give one rule: when a real technology shift is already in the price, the entry multiple sets the return, not whether the technology wins; the base rate for a follower in autonomy is a write-off, not a slow fade; and the leader's private mark, $126B, is the only independent price for the option — 9% of what the market pays for Tesla's version. A holder should own Tesla's autonomy at a discount to that mark, not at 11.3 times it, and size the position so the Cruise outcome is survivable. [S140, S142]

### Where the case turns, and what to do now

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. At $403.30 it sits in the third zone, with the ten-year Treasury at 4.99% raising the discount rate on post-2030 cash flows. Do not invest new money now. Wait for one of three milestones: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless deployment permit, or special-committee terms at a premium to market rather than at market. If the mandate requires exposure, hold a residual of 0.25-0.5% of net asset value, sized so a failed vote and a 30% drawdown do not breach the risk budget, and vote against any ratio that transfers value to the controlling shareholder. Pass on the blue-sky branch: it needs global robotaxi and humanoid dominance and pays 8% from here. Diligence questions: revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, the share of rides running without a safety driver, and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Confidence is high that the core is not worth $403.30, medium on the autonomy tree, low on the merger. What would change the call: a second consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-credit operating margin, an FSD licensing contract with a named automaker, or a ratio that values Tesla at a premium to its undisturbed price.
