{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 综合评分与投资建议 Comprehensive Scoring & Recommendation (scoring, revision 10 by Lead Analyst, 8,823 characters)
Tesla scores 4.0 out of 10, and the score is not close to the line that would justify new money: at $403.30 the shares price the autonomy option at $1,424B, 89% of the equity, while the business that pays the bills earns a 2.2-2.5% operating margin once regulatory credits are stripped out. The recommendation is Reduce — trim existing exposure to a residual, buy nothing — on a twelve-month horizon, with medium confidence in the direction and high confidence in the arithmetic. The composite is a weighted average of seven dimensions, and two do most of the work: valuation at 2 out of 10 with a 20% weight and governance at 3 out of 10 with a 15% weight. Remove either and the stock still scores below 5. [S15, S4]

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business quality and moat | 15% | 6 | Energy earned a 33.1% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% and vertical integration in cells and packs is real; vehicle share is falling in China and the premium band is contested | S6, S63, S59 |
| Growth durability | 15% | 5 | Energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881B in Q3 2026 and deliveries fell 2%, so growth now depends on a robotaxi fleet of 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles | S6, S4, S150 |
| Unit economics and margins | 15% | 4 | The ex-credit operating margin is 2.2-2.5% and trailing ROIC is 5.5% against an 11-14% cost of capital | S3, S4 |
| Balance sheet and cash conversion | 15% | 5 | $36.18B of net cash and $30B of undrawn facilities, offset by a 61% fall in nine-month free cash flow and payables at 75.3 days against 62.8 | S4 |
| Governance and capital allocation | 15% | 3 | A 423.7M-share award with $105.82-120.37B of unrecognised compensation, three of nine directors carrying outside ties of which two are to SpaceX, no dividend or buyback | S5, S138 |
| Valuation and margin of safety | 20% | 2 | 443x trailing and 183x 2027E earnings against an 18.5x trailing P/E and 2.4x EV/sales median for the six peers shown in section 8; the margin of safety turns positive only below $111 | S15, S115 |
| Catalysts, regime and positioning | 5% | 3 | A binary merger process is the only re-rating path, against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury and a VIX of 17.20 | S24, S23, S135 |

The weighting is deliberate. A heavy weight on valuation is right because at the current multiple the entry price, not the technology, dominates a five-year return. The governance weight reflects what a standard framework misses: the controlling shareholder's compensation is tied to market-capitalisation milestones, so management is paid for the narrative that supports the multiple rather than for per-share cash flow, and a change of control accelerates the award. Business quality scores 6 rather than 8 because the strongest part of the franchise, energy storage, is a small and shrinking share of revenue in dollars, while vehicles are losing share in the region that sets global prices.

The counter-evidence deserves its own paragraph, because the score could be too harsh in one place: energy earns a 33.1% gross margin at $210M of revenue per GWh, Tesla's $34,436 cost per vehicle is below every Western competitor, and a triple-digit multiple has persisted for two years without mean reversion. If energy revenue doubles and FSD licensing adds a second stream, the core could be worth $70 a share rather than $42.50. That moves the composite by less than half a point, because the core is 11% of the price and the autonomy premium is 11.3 times the leader's mark. The risks run both ways: if the bear branch materialises — autonomy written down, vehicles valued at GM's multiple, the Terafab commitment drawn — value collapses to a small fraction of today's price and Reduce becomes Sell or Avoid at any size. The base case carries $259B of autonomy on a probability-weighted blend of four branches, not the $40B regional fleet alone: at regional-only autonomy the base would be $52.50 and the probability-weighted value $84, and the recommendation would not change. The only branch that lifts the score above 5 is the merger: a negotiated ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price would justify Hold, with the position capped because a failed vote returns the stock to a level set by the operating business. [S6, S63, S120]

Kelly arithmetic at the current price is negative, so the correct unconstrained position is zero. The table sets out the inputs.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 竞争格局 Competitive Landscape (competition, revision 9 by Market Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,989 characters)
Tesla is gaining share in the markets that are shrinking and holding share in the one that is growing, so its vehicle advantage is compressing into a cost-and-brand moat rather than a technology lead, while in storage it is a scale follower to CATL and BYD and in paid autonomy it reports no ride volume against Waymo's 500,000 a week. Three numbers show it: a 51.7% share of US EV sales in August 2026, European registrations up 51% to 153,978 in 9M 2026, and Chinese retail down 11.9% to 381,088 in a market down 12.5% [S103, S104, S102].

### In the United States, Tesla wins by attrition

Tesla sold 40,816 EVs in August 2026 for 51.7% of US EV sales, up 3.4 points from July, in a market that fell 46.9% to 78,895 units. Behind it the gains were small (Toyota 4,964 units, +34.9% month on month; Chevrolet +30.3%; Cadillac +13.1%), and weaker EV programmes retreated after the credit expired, letting the widest-line, lowest-cost survivor take share without cutting price. Rivian could change the arithmetic: its mid-size SUV has sold since Q2 2026 from a Normal, Illinois plant with 215,000 units of annual capacity [S103, S96].

### Europe is a battery-electric contest; China is a price contest

In an 11-country European panel Tesla registered 45,523 cars in September 2026 against BYD's 39,583, and on battery-electric only led 30,317 to 7,498, while Chinese brands as a group took 14.9% of new cars against 8.0% a year earlier. BYD's route into Europe is powertrain breadth and price, not a better battery car, which makes it the most dangerous competitor over five years: it builds volume below Model Y and can move up. In China the contest is worse: Model Y sold more than 180,000 units from February to July 2026 at RMB 263,500-313,500 while Geely's Xingyuan sold nearly 197,500 at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), and Tesla's domestic retail fell 11.9% while Shanghai wholesale held only on a 58.3% September export rise. Two closer threats sit in Model Y's band: Xpeng delivered 41,256 in September 2026 (−0.78% year on year) and launched the G9L on 2026-09-17 from RMB 231,800 (~$34,420), while Huawei's HIMA delivered 367,229 in January-September 2026, within 4% of Tesla's 381,088 China retail, with the updated AITO M8 from RMB 389,800 (~$57,880) [S104, S101, S102, S155, S156, S157].

### Pricing power is real in the premium band and absent below it

Q3 2026 automotive cost of revenue of $16,754 million over 486,532 deliveries is $34,436 per vehicle, against automotive revenue of $20,560 million, or $42,258 per unit: an 18.5% automotive gross margin, up from 17.0%. The margin is healthy at a premium price point and rests on mix, credits and software, not price: regulatory credits fell to $113 million from $417 million, FSD (Supervised) subscriptions reached 1.74 million, services and other revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million, and energy gross margin reached 33.1%. The $34,436 is 2.3 times the retail price of China's volume bestseller, the Geely Xingyuan at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820), the gap a $25,000-35,000 price war would expose [S4, S6, S101].

### Storage and autonomy are where the advantage is thinnest

In grid storage pricing power sits with the cell makers: CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of energy-storage batteries in H1 2026, up 81%, for 27.1% of the global ESS cell market, while Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months and energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack prices and tariff refunds. Tesla differentiates on integration and delivery speed, not cell cost. In autonomy the gap is disclosed scale: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, while Baidu's Apollo Go runs in more than 10 Chinese cities and Tesla publishes no paid-ride count. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y; TxDMV registry via TeslaNorth and Drive Tesla Canada), with no in-service count disclosed; NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S81, S4, S59, S150, S154, S152, S153].

| Robotaxi | Tesla emerges | Waymo: 4,000 vehicles, 500,000 paid rides a week | Baidu Apollo Go: more than 10 cities | Zoox and Pony.ai | Tesla Cybercab | S59, S6 |

The counter-case is conversion rather than loss: US and European share gains came while rivals retreated, automotive gross margin rose year on year, and the Chinese price war ended with more than a dozen automakers raising prices. Partly right, but the gains sit in shrinking pools and the margin gain is mix-driven, not price-driven. Confidence is high on US and European share data, medium on China because retail and wholesale definitions differ, low on autonomy because no operator discloses audited paid rides. Two questions follow: Tesla's US EV share in Q4 2026 as Toyota's bZ and Chevrolet's Bolt ramp, and how much of BYD's European volume is plug-in hybrid under the 2027 CO2 review?

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 市场与行业分析 Market & Industry Analysis (market, revision 8 by Market Analyst, 8,817 characters)
Tesla's 2026-2028 demand is durable in Europe and grid storage and structurally weaker in the United States and China: the expiry of the US clean-vehicle credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US battery-electric share from 10% to 6% and lowered the underlying US growth rate rather than merely pulling sales forward, while China has become a shrinking unit market in which Tesla holds share instead of gaining it. No plausible US price action recovers the volume the credit used to buy, so growth has to come from regulation in Europe and from data-centre load in storage, each durable on a different timetable [S98, S99, S101].

### The United States lost a level, not a quarter

Battery-electric vehicles were 6% of US light-duty sales in Q3 2026 against 10% in Q3 2025, and 6% in the first nine months against 8% a year earlier; in the luxury segment where Tesla's US mix sits, share fell from 31% to 12% while hybrids rose to 16%. A pull-forward would have produced recovery by Q2 2026; a year after expiry there is none, so the credit was creating demand, not borrowing it. Cox Automotive shows the mechanism: the US new-EV average transaction price was $54,754 in August 2026, with incentives of $6,594 per vehicle. Manufacturers replaced 88% of the $7,500 credit with their own money and volume still fell 46.9% year on year in August to 78,895 units, a 0.95 million unit annual run-rate at 5.7% of new-vehicle sales. Tesla's own figures carry the same signal with a twist: US revenue fell 14.4% year on year in Q3 2026 to $12,495 million while global deliveries slipped only 2% to 486,532, but part of the gap is self-inflicted, because Model S and Model X were retired in mid-2026 and other-model deliveries halved to 8,295 from 15,933, $0.7 billion of the $2.1 billion decline. Strip that out and the US Model 3/Y business still shrank in a market that shrank faster, which is why Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 [S98, S103, S4, S6].

### Europe offsets the US

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of the market against 15.8% a year earlier, while hybrids took 36.6%. Tesla registered 153,978 cars in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% from 102,025, and 45,523 in September, 4.6% of panel new-car sales against 2.6%. The mechanism is a fleet-average CO2 mandate for 2025-2027 that makes battery volume the cheapest compliance route, reinforced by the 2026 energy-price shock. The risk is timing: if the 2026 step is pre-compliance borrowing 2027 volume, 2027 will be flat, and hybrids at 36.6% show the mandate is being met partly without battery cars [S99, S104, S100].

### China is penetration without volume

New energy vehicles reached 65.1% of new passenger cars in China in July 2026 from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales fell 12.5% in January-July and total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, so the share gain is arithmetic on a shrinking denominator. Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9%, and Giga Shanghai's September wholesale rose 5.0% to 95,366 only because exports jumped 58.3% to 30,529. Pricing moved Tesla's way for once: more than 15 Chinese automakers raised prices during 2026 as first-quarter industry margins fell to 3.2%, ending the deflation that had squeezed every participant. China should be underwritten as a low-cost export base, not as a growth market for 2027-2028 [S101, S102, S105].

### Market size: $950 billion of cars, $83 billion of storage

The 2026 market size is $950 billion for electric cars and $82.7 billion for grid storage, measured at Tesla's realised prices as a proxy because no agency publishes revenue; global electric-car units rise from an implied 16.7 million in 2024 to 23.0 million in 2026, a 17.4% compound annual growth rate, and the battery-electric slice of the three regions where Tesla sells is not published, so the table bounds obtainable revenue rather than measuring the serviceable market. Grid storage is the only pool growing faster than Tesla can supply: 353.4 GWh of deployments are expected in 2026, up 28% on 275.3 GWh in 2025, and Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in nine months, 14% of the market, against 50 GWh of Texas capacity. The budget owner is a utility or independent power producer behind an interconnection queue, so demand is sticky but price-sensitive: energy revenue fell 16% year on year in Q3 2026 to $2,881 million on lower Megapack average selling prices and tariff refunds. Ride-hailing cannot yet be sized from disclosure: Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week, 26 million a year; even at $100 a ride that is $2.6 billion, 0.3% of the electric-car TAM, while Tesla discloses no fare, booking or paid-ride figure. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y; TxDMV registry via TeslaNorth and Drive Tesla Canada), with no in-service count disclosed; NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03 [S100, S108, S4, S59, S150, S154, S152, S153].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 技术与产品 Technology & Product (technology_product, revision 8 by Product Analyst, 8,877 characters)
Tesla's technology is proven where it is a manufacturing problem — dry-electrode cells, Megapack integration — and unproven where the valuation sits, judged against two comparison sets: Waymo in autonomy and BYD in manufacturing cost. Compared with Waymo, Tesla has 2.0 million cumulative autonomous miles against 500,000 paid rides a week on 4,000 vehicles; compared with BYD, its 486,532 quarterly deliveries trail BYD's 762,478 electric cars. Its paid driverless permit exists in one state. The technology justifies a premium to a capital-intensive manufacturer in energy and process engineering; it does not yet justify the multiple of a software platform [S6, S59, S76, S107].

### How FSD works, and where it stops

FSD (Supervised) is vision-only: eight cameras feed an end-to-end neural network that outputs steering, acceleration and braking, trained on video from 10.2 million delivered vehicles and run on in-house inference silicon. There is no lidar or radar. Two problems stay unsolved. Cameras blinded by rain, fog or low sun are the subject of NHTSA's Engineering Analysis EA26002, opened 2026-03-19 over 13 crashes in 2.88 million vehicles, testing whether the system detects the degradation. The second is the reliability increment that permits removing the supervisor, which is why customer-owned unsupervised driving moved to Q2 2027. Tesla's October 2026 report claims 6,006,200 miles per major collision, a company-computed, non-fault-based figure the regulator has not verified [S58, S80].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| FSD miles per major collision | 6,006,200 (North America, October 2026) | Company report, FSD-engaged miles | S58 |
| Cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles | 2.0 million (to 2026-09-30) | Company quarterly update | S6 |
| FSD subscriptions and attach | 1.74 million; more than 75% of North American deliveries | Company KPI, excludes free trials | S6 |
| 4680 cell output and density | More than 1 million cells/week; more than 40 GWh; 272 Wh/kg | Giga Texas line data and teardown estimates | S56 |

### Robotaxi: a real service, on one state's terms

Tesla publishes no fleet count of its own. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population it is reviewing at 1,000, its estimate and an exposure ceiling rather than an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03. Registrations record authorisations, not vehicles in service, and Tesla discloses no fares, trips per vehicle, utilisation or insurance cost per mile. Permits remain the constraint: Texas allows self-certified commercial driverless operation, while California lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC for testing with a driver only (2026-10-22) [S73, S118, S150, S151, S152].

| Dimension | Tesla | Benchmark | What it means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weekly paid rides | Not disclosed | Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week | At 5 miles a ride, 2.5 million rider-only miles weekly — more than Tesla's cumulative total | S59, S107 |
| Cell performance | 4680: 272 Wh/kg, 10-80% in 35-40 minutes | CATL Qilin 3: full charge in six minutes | Tesla leads on cost, trails on density and charging | S56 |
| BEV volume, Q3 2026 | 486,532 units | BYD 762,478 passenger BEVs, +30.89% year over year | Cost leadership has moved to China | S76 |

### Cells: a cost moat, not a performance one

Giga Texas runs above one million 4680 cells a week at more than 40 GWh of installed capacity, and since January 2026 both electrodes use the dry process in production — a step CATL, Panasonic, LG and Samsung SDI have not taken to commercial scale. The economics are real: electrode cost 50% lower at full scale, 41% less line capex and more than 30% less factory energy. The product is not: energy density trails by 10-15%, charging is slower than Panasonic 2170 packs, yields above 90% sit below the 98% of mature producers, and Tesla still buys CATL LFP and Panasonic or LG 2170 cells for Shanghai and Fremont Model Y. Battery availability, not demand, remained the stated limit on 2026 volume [S56].

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why it is hard | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fleet data and training set | 7 | 10.2 million vehicles and billions of FSD miles | 3-4 years | S6 |
| Dry-electrode process | 7 | Both electrodes dry above 90% yield; no rival at scale | 3 years | S56 |
| Vertical integration (cells, packs, chips) | 6 | Process know-how and capital; AI6 foundry dependence caps it | 3-5 years | S6, S79 |
| Driverless permits | 4 | Texas self-certification is easy; California and the EU are not | 1-2 years Texas, 3+ California | S73 |
| **Composite** | **6/10** | 3 years for the cell line, 2 for Megapack integration | **3 years of lead time** | S56, S73 |

### Patents: thin disclosure, deliberately

| Four PCT filings, published 2026-04-16 | Optimus Gen 3 forearm, wrist, joint and hand assemblies | WIPO/PCT | Priority 2024-10-10 | — | Published, national phase pending | 22 degrees of freedom per hand | S75 |
| US20260310299A1 | Flexible touch sensors for robotic hands | US | Not disclosed | — | Published 2025-10-08 | Tactile sensing | S75 |
| Maxwell portfolio (acquired 2019, $235m) | Dry electrode manufacturing IP | US | Pre-2019 | Granted, owned | In force | Underpins the 4680 dry process | S56 |

The 10-K rests the case on data, manufacturing cost and vertical integration, not patents; Musk said in April 2026 that the V3 hand would not use the patented Optimus design.

### Product inventory

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model 3/Y | Commercial | 2017-2020 | $20.09bn automotive sales Q3 2026; 478,237 units (98.3%) | 18.5% total automotive | Next-generation platform, no date | S6, S76 |
| Cybercab and Robotaxi | Early commercial | 2026-09-03, Austin | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Unsupervised customer cars Q2 2027 | S6, S57 |
| Megapack, Megablock | Commercial | 2019; Megapack 3 in 2025 | $2.881bn segment Q3 2026 | 33.1% | Ramp 50 GWh Texas | S4, S6 |
| Optimus | Early production | 2026-10-21 | None disclosed | None disclosed | 20,000 units a week by end-2027, company claim (2026-10-21), unverified | S57 |

### Energy is the proven technology

Megapack is the one line where Tesla holds a genuine integration advantage and prices it: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026 at a 33.1% gross margin, with 50 GWh of Texas capacity starting. The weak point is the order book, not the product: the 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified. A contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it; a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. Wood Mackenzie ranks Tesla second among integrators behind Sungrow, and revenue fell 16% to $2.881bn even as volume rose [S4, S6, S72].

::: evidence
**The Optimus output target is an unverified company claim, and the humanoid benchmark sits elsewhere.**

On the Q3 2026 call of 2026-10-21 Tesla set a target of 20,000 Optimus units a week by end-2027 and began early production, but it discloses no unit count, external customer, task list or revenue. A named customer, supplier orders at that volume or an Optimus revenue line would confirm it; another year of demonstration video and no billed unit would contradict it. Figure AI, valued at $39bn in September 2025, completed an 11-month Figure 02 deployment at BMW's Spartanburg plant contributing to more than 30,000 X3 vehicles, the external validation Optimus has not matched [S57, S149].
:::

### What would change the judgement

The strongest counter-case is that FSD is already monetised: attach, subscriptions and deferred revenue rose in Q3 2026. Against it, repeated NHTSA recalls on the 2026 Model Y show launch quality slipping, and the attach rate is North American only while China sales fell with FSD approval pending. Optimus is the thinner half of the autonomy branch: a production line and no external customer.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## ESG评估 ESG Assessment (esg, revision 3 by Regulatory Analyst, 8,745 characters)
Tesla's policy position has inverted. The 2025-2026 reset removes a high-margin revenue stream worth $2,763m at its 2024 peak and leaves the robotaxi licence fragmented across US states and unapproved in China, while the offsetting upsides — federal AV preemption and tariffs on Chinese rivals — are real but not yet law. Automotive regulatory credit revenue fell from $2,763m in 2024 to $1,993m in 2025 (-28%) and to $113m in Q3 2026 from $417m (-73%); credits carry almost no cost of revenue, so their loss took total automotive gross margin from 18.4% to 17.8% in 2025. The credit-free margin is the right base. [S3, S4]

### The credit pool has already collapsed

The US instrument is unambiguous. Section 30D's $7,500 new clean vehicle credit applied only to vehicles acquired on or before 2025-09-30; the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, enacted 2025-07-04, terminated it and the used-vehicle 25E credit thereafter. The 2026 revision is a repeal, not a tightening: EPA's final rule of 2026-02-18 rescinds the 2009 endangerment finding and repeals the light-, medium- and heavy-duty GHG standards, and the Department of Transportation finalised its CAFE rollback on 2026-10-01. Both remove the compliance demand that priced Tesla's credits; EIA reported on 2026-10-19 that battery-electric sales remained lower after the credit expired. California's ACC II and the Section 177 states preserve a partial market, not the 2024 price level. [S117, S116, S64, S98]

### The robotaxi licence is a state-by-state binary

Autonomy is the part of the equity value policy can switch on or off, and the record is narrower than the narrative. Texas requires a TxDMV authorisation for commercial SAE Level 4/5 operation from 2026-05-28 under SB 2807 — a no-fee, non-expiring registration regime, which is why Austin scaled first. California is the opposite: CPUC's AV permit table lists Waymo, Zoox, Nuro, WeRide and Tensor but not Tesla, and Tesla's California service runs under a non-AV limousine/TCP authority. Federally the binding constraint is enforcement — NHTSA's FSD probes and the October 2026 school-zone review — while the preemption fix, H.R. 7390 SELF DRIVE Act of 2026, advanced only from a House subcommittee on a 12-11 party-line vote on 2026-02-10. Waymo holds a CPUC driverless permit and Zoox a federal exemption; Tesla holds neither. [S118, S119, S80, S125]

### China taxes the base; Europe protects it for now

China policy has become a tax on Tesla's largest manufacturing base. From 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31 the NEV purchase tax is halved rather than exempt — an effective 5%, capped at RMB 15,000 per car — regressive for Tesla's higher-priced trims and landing alongside a 16% fall in Q3 2026 China sales, a cut in the vehicle export rebate and no unsupervised FSD approval. Europe is the exception: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 has imposed a countervailing duty on China-built BEVs since 2024-10-30 for five years, at 7.8% for Tesla Shanghai against 35.3% for SAIC, on top of the 10% common duty — 17.8% versus 45.3% for Chinese brands. That room is time-limited: the EU softened 2025-2027 CO2 compliance to a three-year average and proposed the same for 2030-2032, reducing legacy makers' urgency to buy credits. [S124, S77, S127, S126]

### Governance is the largest ESG item

Governance is the largest ESG item because it changes the share count and the cost of capital. The 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423.7m shares in 12 tranches, approved on 2025-11-06 — 10.7% of the 3.95bn shares outstanding at the low end — with $105.82-120.37bn of unrecognised stock compensation on the milestones not yet probable and $9.74bn on the one deemed probable (20 million vehicles, recognised over 8.9 years). Capital allocation matters as much as pay design: Tesla invested $2.0bn in xAI Holdings in January 2026 and, after SpaceX acquired xAI Holdings on 2026-02-02, converted that right into SpaceX Class A stock in March 2026. Musk holds 19.8% and 207.5m shares are pledged. Six of nine directors are independent under Nasdaq rules; three carry outside ties — Ehrenpreis and Kimbal Musk to SpaceX's board, Straubel to Redwood, a Tesla supplier — and one share carries one vote, but a governance discount is warranted. [S5, S3, S4]

### What is not financially material

Three ESG claims do not survive contact with the financials. Tesla's operational footprint is small against the use-phase emissions its products avoid, and the 2025 10-K discloses no material environmental proceeding; the real exposure is upstream, in battery materials, where it files an annual conflict-minerals report but no supplier-level data. Labour and product safety are tails: the California Civil Rights Department's bench trial began on 2026-09-21 before Judge Peter Borkon, is scheduled to run to 2026-10-30 and had no verdict as of 2026-10-29, while the August 2025 Autopilot verdict was $129m compensatory with Tesla 33% at fault plus $200m punitive, against an immaterial accrual. The strongest counter-evidence runs the other way — the US tariff wall on Chinese-built EVs, the EU's relative tariff advantage, possible federal AV preemption and performance-contingent pay — which is why policy is a discount on the multiple, not an exit signal. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 商业模式 Business Model (business_model, revision 7 by Fundamentals Analyst, 8,955 characters)
Tesla still makes most of its gross profit selling cars, but after regulatory credits the car business earns little at the operating line. Credits supplied 45.8% of FY2025 operating income and 15.7% in Q3 2026; incremental profit now comes from a 33.1%-margin energy-storage business and a 15.9%-margin services business while AI spending absorbs 86.9% of gross profit. Nine-month 2026 revenue of $78,669 million split into automotive $57,310 million (including $639 million of credits), energy $8,428 million and services $12,931 million, against an automotive share of 85.1% in FY2023. Q3 2026 gross profit divided $3,806 million automotive (69%), $954 million energy (17%) and $734 million services (13%), versus 91%/6%/3% in FY2023. Cash arrives when a vehicle changes hands, on storage milestones and prepayments ($3.30 billion of customer prepayments in deferred revenue at 2026-09-30, from $2.04 billion), and monthly for Supercharging, insurance and FSD [S3, S4, S6].

| Segment | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M 2026 | Q3 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue excluding credits ($M) | 80,629 | 74,307 | 67,533 | 56,671 | 20,447 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Automotive regulatory credits ($M) | 1,790 | 2,763 | 1,993 | 639 | 113 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Energy generation and storage revenue ($M) | 6,035 | 10,086 | 12,771 | 8,428 | 2,881 | S3, S4 |

| Energy gross margin | 18.9% | 26.2% | 29.8% | 30.2% | 33.1% | S3, S4 |

The credit franchise is ending. Tesla booked $2,763 million of automotive regulatory credits in FY2024, $1,993 million in FY2025 and $639 million in 9M 2026; Q3 2026 alone was $113 million, down 73% from $417 million. Credits carry no cost of revenue, so a credit dollar is nearly a dollar of operating profit: 20.1% of operating income in FY2023, 39.0% in FY2024, 45.8% in FY2025, 31.1% in 9M 2026 and 15.7% in Q3 2026. An implied Q4 2025 figure of $542 million shows the collapse came with the removal of the compliance obligation in 2026, not the lapse of the consumer credit: the Department of Transportation finalised its CAFE rollback on 2026-10-01, ending the requirement that made legacy automakers buy zero-emission credits. Without credits, FY2025's 4.6% operating margin is 2.5% and Q3 2026's 2.6% is 2.2% [S4, S64, S66].

Per vehicle the business improved even as credits disappeared. Q3 2026 automotive revenue per delivery excluding credits was $42,026, up 0.5%, while automotive cost of revenue per delivery (automotive cost of revenue divided by deliveries) fell 2.7% to $34,436, so gross profit per vehicle rose 18.0% to $7,591 (18.1% margin) from $6,433 (15.4%). The gain is cost and mix, not price: management attributes the 270 basis points to a higher Asia-Pacific mix from the low-cost Shanghai plant. Tesla does not disclose customer acquisition cost; SG&A per delivery of $4,142 carries corporate and non-vehicle cost, and the first vehicle's gross profit covers it 1.8 times. A three-year LTV estimate of $8,455 adds three years of services gross profit per vehicle ($288 a year on 10.2 million deliveries), giving LTV:CAC of 2.0:1 and payback inside the delivery quarter. Tesla is the only one of the three with positive per-vehicle gross profit after credits: BYD's automotive gross margin was 20.49% in FY2025, from 22.31%, and Rivian's automotive gross profit was a $(36) million loss in Q2 2026 [S63, S65, S68].

Energy is the highest-margin dollar of growth. Storage revenue per GWh fell 23% to $210 million from $273 million, but gross profit per GWh fell only 19% to $69.6 million because cost per GWh fell 25% to $141 million, lifting segment margin to 33.1% from 31.4%. The mechanism is cell integration: the first Megapacks built with Tesla's own Nevada LFP cells shipped in Q3 2026, Megafactory Texas began production with 50 GWh, and the Megapack backlog is nearly sold out through 2027. Fluence earned 13.1% in FY2025; Tesla's advantage is owning the cell, not pricing. Part of the 33.1% is not repeatable: management attributed it partly to tariff refunds and cell-related warranty reimbursements. Services is the quieter engine: revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million on 2% fewer deliveries and gross margin reached 15.9% from 10.5%. Each extra $1 billion of energy revenue at 30% adds $300 million of gross profit; the same dollar of automotive revenue at 18% adds $180 million. FSD and software grow but remain too small to see in the income statement: active subscriptions rose to 1.74 million from 1.04 million, deferred revenue for FSD, connectivity and software was $4.08 billion against $3.87 billion at 2025-12-31, and obligations beyond one year were $10.73 billion, of which $4.80 billion falls due within twelve months. Management's claim that FSD is attached to more than 75% of North American deliveries is company-reported and cannot be tied to a revenue line, because Tesla does not disclose FSD revenue; the observable is $2,345 of deferred balance per active subscription, a stock rather than a price [S67, S4].

The newest change in money flows is who owns the asset. Selling a car converts inventory into revenue once; a robotaxi fleet keeps the vehicle on Tesla's balance sheet and earns per mile, shifting the model from a hardware sale to a utilisation business paid on miles and uptime rather than deliveries. The Cybercab entered Tesla's own Austin fleet on 2026-09-03, but no fare revenue, fleet size or per-mile economics are disclosed, so the model cannot yet be tested. Until then the investable model remains the one in the tables: cars, storage and services.

Counter-case: gross margin improves while the company gets less profitable. Operating expenses of $4,776 million rose 39% against $5,494 million of gross profit, R&D alone rose 69% to $2,761 million, and depreciation rose 17% to $1,580 million and will accelerate as more than $20 billion of 2026 capital expenditure is commissioned. The warranty reserve rose 26% to $10,138 million on 2% fewer deliveries, with claims incurred up 29% to $1,614 million while the provision per delivery fell to $1,227 from $1,463. Inventory rose 13.7% to $14,092 million, with 11 days of vehicle supply. The vehicle line covers its own costs, so break-even is the cost base: $4,776 million of operating expenses needs $27.0 billion of revenue at a 17.7% blended margin; Q3 2026 delivered $28.0 billion for $718 million of operating profit. Normalise energy to a 30% margin and take credits to zero and the quarter earns $515 million, a 1.8% operating margin. For a position, that argues for sizing on the energy and services annuity, with rising margins and a 2027 backlog, and treating autonomy as an option rather than earnings, because at a 1.8% margin the vehicle franchise cannot carry the cost base alone. Confidence is high on the segment arithmetic and medium on how much of the 2026 cost relief is structural rather than tariff and mix. Four diligence questions remain: what is the North American automotive margin excluding credits? What is the energy margin excluding tariff refunds, and at what price is the 2027 backlog contracted? Will Tesla disclose FSD revenue and robotaxi recognition? When do R&D and capital expenditure stop rising as a share of revenue? [S4, S6]

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 发展方向与战略 Development Strategy (strategy, revision 5 by Product Analyst, 8,818 characters)
Tesla's strategy has become a capital-allocation bet rather than an operating one: more than $20bn of 2026 capex and $30bn of new credit facilities are committed to autonomy, robots and semiconductors while nine-month 2026 operating income of $2.06bn implies a return on invested capital near 3%, below any plausible cost of capital. The strategy earns its keep only if unsupervised robotaxi revenue arrives before 2028, and the 12-month test is customer-owned unsupervised driving in mid-2027, not another reveal [S4, S78].

### The plan and the return do not yet match

Tesla guided in the Q3 2026 filing to capital expenditure above $20bn for 2026, after spending $13.01bn in the first nine months against $6.13bn a year earlier, and in September 2026 signed three credit agreements for aggregate commitments of $30bn. Cash and short-term investments were $45.45bn at 2026-09-30 against $9.5bn of debt, so the plan is funded; it is no longer self-funding. Nine-month operating income of $2.06bn on $89.29bn of equity, annualised after tax over roughly $71bn of invested capital, gives a return near 3% — depressed by ramp assets, but low enough that every further billion of capex lowers the return until the new assets sell something [S6]. Research and development rose 69% year over year to $2.76bn in Q3 2026, most of it for autonomy and robotics.

### Pricing and mix are carrying the capex

| Item | Q3 2026 | Q3 2025 | Read | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive gross margin | 18.5% | 17.0% | Cost cuts and mix offset lower prices | S4 |
| Regulatory credit revenue | $113m | $417m | A subsidy that no longer pays for the plan | S4 |
| Energy segment revenue | $2.881bn | $3.415bn | Volume up, price down | S4 |
| Services gross profit | $734m | $366m | FSD subscriptions and repair work | S6 |
| China deliveries | 142,133 | 16% lower year over year | Share loss in the largest market | S77 |
| Total deliveries | 486,532 | 497,099 | Flat volume on an ageing core line-up | S6 |

The read is that Tesla is funding autonomy from a mature car business, a fading credit stream and a fast-growing but deflating storage business; none of the three is a rising price. The Semi is a logical adjacency because it shares cells, motors and Megachargers with the core; Optimus is not an adjacency yet, because it has a production line and no customer.

### Milestones: what has actually shipped

| Milestone | Target date | Status at 2026-10-29 | What it proves | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cybercab in the Austin robotaxi fleet | 2026 | Met: paid rides from 2026-09-03 | Hardware and a Texas permit | S6 |
| Customer-owned unsupervised FSD | Q4 2026, now Q2 2027 | Slipped by about two quarters | Converts the owner fleet into robotaxi supply without capex | S57 |
| Optimus production | 2026 | Met: early production from 2026-10-21 | Manufacturing readiness, not demand | S6 |
| Optimus at 20,000 units a week | End-2027 | Company claim on the 2026-10-21 call, unverified: no unit count, customer or revenue disclosed | Whether a humanoid is a product; a named customer or supplier orders would confirm it, a second year of demonstrations would contradict it | S57 |
| Tesla Semi volume production | 2026 | Met: Nevada high-volume line | Entry into Class 8 trucking | S6 |
| Next-generation affordable platform | Not dated | Not publicly disclosed | The volume and cost reset | S6 |
| 400 MW of training compute | 2026-12-31 | 225 MW installed (Cortex 1 and 2) | Whether the compute constraint eases | S6 |
| Austin Fab equipment commissioning | 2027 | Under construction | Vertical integration into silicon | S6 |
| FSD approval in China | Not dated | Pending; CFO negotiating | Monetising the largest market | S77 |
| Megafactory Texas at 50 GWh | 2026-2027 | Production began Q3 2026 | Energy scale-up | S6 |

### Partners: concentration, not diversification

| Partner | Scope | Signed | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Samsung Electronics | AI6 foundry at Taylor, Texas; $16.5bn through 2033 | 2025-07-28 | AI5 taped out on 2nm in July 2026; AI6 to follow | S79 |
| CATL | LFP cells for Shanghai vehicles and storage | Not disclosed | Active | S56 |
| Panasonic, LG Energy Solution | 2170 cells for Fremont and Shanghai | Not disclosed | Active | S56 |
| xAI, then SpaceX | $2bn xAI investment converted into SpaceX Class A shares after SpaceX acquired xAI | 2026-01; converted 2026-02 | Stake held; a merger is openly discussed | S78 |
| Maxwell Technologies | Dry-electrode intellectual property acquired for $235m | 2019 | Integrated into 4680 production | S56 |

The partner map shows the strategic risk: Tesla's autonomy roadmap runs through a single foundry for AI6, its vehicles still depend on CATL, Panasonic and LG for cells, and its largest related-party exposure is to companies its chief executive also controls.

### Geography: China becomes an export base

Tesla's China sales fell 16% year over year in Q3 2026 to 142,133 units while Giga Shanghai exports reached a record 132,978; retail sales for 2026 to date are down 12% as exports doubled, and Beijing cuts the EV export tax rebate in April 2027. Shanghai, with more than 950,000 units of capacity, is now a cost and export base rather than a growth market, exposed to tariffs in the markets it ships to. Berlin set a production record and the US business carries the FSD attach rate, which is why the company's own numbers look better in North America than in the two regions that decide its cost base [S77, S76, S102].

### Energy is where the strategy is working

The energy plan is coherent and funded: 50 GWh of Megafactory Texas capacity started in Q3 2026 alongside 40 GWh in California and 20 GWh in Shanghai, with 7 GWh of Nevada LFP cell capacity in early ramp and the first Megapacks built from Tesla-made cells. The 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog, so the claim is unverified: a contracted-backlog figure or 2027 deployments above the 36.0 GWh nine-month run at stable revenue per GWh would confirm it, and a third quarter of falling revenue per GWh would contradict it. A 33.1% segment gross margin and data-centre demand give the capital a return that autonomy does not yet. The tension is that revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881bn even as volume rose, so the plan is adding capacity into falling prices [S6, S72].

### The capital allocation question

In January 2026 Tesla invested $2bn in xAI; the stake became SpaceX Class A shares when SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026, and the Q1 2026 cash flow statement records a $2.002bn purchase of SpaceX equity. Three of nine directors carry outside ties — two to SpaceX (Ehrenpreis and Kimbal Musk), one to Straubel at Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier — and the committee uses two. The 2026 proxy is set for a 2026-12-03 meeting, and the 2025 CEO award pays out on a deal price without operational milestones — only one of twelve operational milestones is rated probable, leaving $105.8-120.4bn of unrecognised stock compensation. A shareholder is no longer buying only a car and storage company; a merger scenario makes the position a bet on Musk's wider portfolio, which argues for a smaller size [S78].

### What must be true in 12 months

Three signposts decide whether the strategy is earning its cost of capital. TSLA closed at $403.30 on 2026-10-29, a $1,594.1B market capitalisation and a $1,558.0B enterprise value, 19% below its 52-week high of $498.83 and 36% above the low of $297.38. The regime frames the call: the S&P 500 sits at 7,720.39, up 12.8% year to date and 1.6% below its high, the VIX is 17.20 at the 52nd percentile, and the ten-year Treasury yields 4.99%, up 0.93 points in twelve months, a discount rate that penalises cash flows arriving after 2030. [S15, S141, S22, S23, S24]

### Reduce, at a fraction of the size

Tesla's vehicles, energy and services businesses are worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts; the remaining $356 of the $403.30 price — $1,424B, or 89% of the equity — is an option on robotaxi and robotics that discloses no revenue. Our probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close, on a base that carries $259B of autonomy across four weighted branches rather than the $40B regional fleet alone; even a 40% chance of a premium SpaceX exchange lifts expected value only to $248. The action is to trim rather than to sell short: the option has real value, the balance sheet is not the constraint, and a negotiated exchange ratio could pay $443-464 without any operating delivery. [S6, S15, S120]

Confidence is high on the reported numbers — three years of filings, a third quarter reconciled line by line, and a timestamped market price — medium on the 11-14% cost of capital, and low on anything that requires sizing robotaxi revenue, because no revenue line, fare or cost per mile is disclosed. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 投资潜力与投资逻辑 Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 8 by Lead Analyst, 8,945 characters)
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $42.50 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $356, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 1,051 authorised robotaxi vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27, 544 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S150]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $42.50 a share, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets, and autonomy at $259B in the base case — 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance — which is $65.6 a share on 3,952.6M shares, so $42.50 + $65.6 = $108.1 and the base rounds to $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $52.50 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $454 mid-point lifts expected value to $248, still 38% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

arguments.markdown:
TSLA closed at $403.30 on 2026-10-29, a $1,594.1B market capitalisation and a $1,558.0B enterprise value, 19% below its 52-week high of $498.83 and 36% above the low of $297.38. The stock is up 14.3% in a month and 30.6% in three, but down 11.3% year to date and 8.4% over twelve months, and the Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-21 — revenue $28.046B, adjusted EPS $0.48 against a $0.45 consensus — have been bought. The regime frames the call: the S&P 500 sits at 7,720.39, up 12.8% year to date and 1.6% below its high, the VIX is 17.20 at the 52nd percentile, and the ten-year Treasury yields 4.99%, up 0.93 points in twelve months, a discount rate that penalises cash flows arriving after 2030. [S15, S141, S22, S23, S24]

### Reduce, at a fraction of the size

Tesla's vehicles, energy and services businesses are worth $43.00 a share on 3,952.6M shares; the remaining $360.30 of the $403.30 price — $1,424B, or 89% of the equity — is an option on robotaxi and robotics that discloses no revenue. Our probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close, on a base that carries $259B of autonomy across four weighted branches rather than the $40B regional fleet alone; even a 40% chance of a premium SpaceX exchange lifts expected value only to $248. The action is to trim rather than to sell short: the option has real value, the balance sheet is not the constraint, and a negotiated exchange ratio could pay $443-464 without any operating delivery. [S6, S15, S120]

Confidence is high on the reported numbers — three years of filings, a third quarter reconciled line by line, and a timestamped market price — medium on the 11-14% cost of capital, and low on anything that requires sizing robotaxi revenue, because no revenue line, fare or cost per mile is disclosed. The 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target and a published range from $128.11 to $600, so the disagreement is about the distribution, not the mean. [S141, S144, S4]

::: verdict
| Rating | Action | Composite score | Confidence | Horizon | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reduce | Trim to a residual of at most 0.5% of net asset value; no new money | 4.0 / 10 | Medium | 12 months | S15, S6, S120 |
:::

::: briefing
| Card | Text | Source |
|---|---|---|
| What the business earns | Energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026 at $210M of revenue per GWh and services 15.9%; together they supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M quarterly gross profit, while regulatory credits fell to $113M, or 15.7% of operating income, from 45.8% of FY2025 operating income | S6, S4 |
| What is not growing | Energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881B and deliveries fell 2%; the robotaxi fleet authorised in Texas was 1,051 vehicles at 2026-10-27, of which 544 were Cybercabs, with paid rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03 | S6, S150 |
| The quality of the cash | Nine-month free cash flow fell 61% to $1,883M as capital expenditure doubled to $13,014M; operating cash flow of $14,897M was carried by a $7,332M payables stretch, with days payable at 75.3 against 62.8, and net cash stands at $36.18B | S4 |
| What the price pays for | 443x trailing earnings, 241x 2026E and 183x 2027E against an 18.5x trailing P/E and 2.4x EV/sales median for the six peers in section 8, on a core business worth $43.00 a share and an autonomy option of $1,424B, or 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark | S15, S115, S120 |
| Autonomy evidence | 2.0M cumulative unsupervised miles at 2026-09-30, customer-owned unsupervised FSD slipped to about Q2 2027, California testing is with a driver only, and no robotaxi revenue line exists; Waymo runs about 500,000 paid rides a week | S6, S120 |
| Governance and the merger | A 423.7M-share CEO award (10.7% of the count) carries $105.82-120.37B of unrecognised compensation, three of nine directors carry outside ties of which two are to SpaceX, and special committees formed on 2026-10-20; an exchange at market would give Tesla holders 44% of a $3.60T group with no premium | S5, S135, S138 |
| Policy | The federal purchase credit ended for vehicles acquired after 2025-09-30, the EPA repealed the light-duty GHG standards on 2026-02-18 and DOT rolled back CAFE on 2026-10-01, so the ex-credit operating margin of 2.2-2.5% is the base case | S116, S3, S4 |
| Four positives | A $34,436 cost per vehicle below every Western competitor, dry-electrode 4680 cells at yields above 90%, $36.18B of net cash, and a merger path that could re-rate the shares without an operating delivery | S6, S5 |
| Three risks | A two-year autonomy slip that takes the stock to the $19 bear case, an ex-credit margin below 15% if US incentives of $6,594 a unit cannot hold price, and 10.7% award dilution plus a failed merger vote that would return the stock below $300 | S4, S5, S135 |
:::

::: efficiency
| Measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue, trailing twelve months | $103.6B: automotive $75.0B, energy $12.3B, services $16.3B | S6 |
| Operating income, Q3 2026 | $718M, a 2.6% margin, down 56% year over year | S4 |
| Free cash flow, trailing twelve months | $3,303M, a 0.2% yield on the market capitalisation | S4, S15 |
| Gross margin, Q3 2026 | 19.6% consolidated; 33.1% in energy | S4, S6 |
| Valuation | $1,594.1B market capitalisation; $1,558.0B enterprise value; 443x trailing and 183x 2027E earnings | S15, S115 |
| Returns | Trailing ROIC 5.5% against an estimated 11-14% cost of capital | S4 |
:::

::: one-question
What is Tesla's revenue per robotaxi per week in Austin, and what share of those rides runs without a safety driver?

Without that number the autonomy value cannot be tested against a cost per mile, and every scenario above the bear case rests on a registry count of authorised vehicles rather than on unit economics. A disclosed figure that supports the revenue per mile the price implies would move the base case toward the bull case; a quarter of silence after three years of promises would move it toward the bear case. The report already contains the test: Waymo's 500,000 paid rides a week across 4,000 vehicles is 125 rides per vehicle a week, about 18 a day, so Tesla's Austin fleet has to beat that utilisation at a fare that supports the $0.60 a mile the reverse DCF needs [S59, S120].
:::

::: takeaways
1. **The price is the whole debate:** $360.30 of the $403.30 — 89% — is autonomy and robotics valued at 11.3 times Waymo's $126B, and the core business is worth $43.00 on vehicles at 1.0x sales, energy at 3.5x, services at 1.0x and net cash at book [S15, S120].
2. **Cash is thinner than it looks:** 61% less free cash flow in nine months, a $7,332M payables stretch and a 5.5% ROIC against an 11-14% cost of capital, with $20B+ of capex still to come [S4].
3. **One event can change the call:** a premium exchange ratio into SpaceX would pay $443-464 without any robotaxi revenue, but the vote needs 50% of all shares, no terms are agreed, and a failed vote returns the stock below $300 [S135, S5].
:::

The follow-up diligence is dated and specific: a robotaxi revenue line, a fleet count and a fare in the next results release; a California driverless deployment permit from the DMV and CPUC filings, where the current service runs on a limousine authority; the exchange ratio, advisers and treatment of unvested awards in the special committees' 8-K; capital expenditure guidance, the Terafab contribution and any payables reversal in the annual 10-K; and the per-tranche thresholds of the CEO award in the proxy for the 2026-12-03 annual meeting. The rating is a statement about the price of an option, not about the quality of the engineering: the vehicle, cell and storage businesses are real, and they are worth about a tenth of what the market pays.

arguments.markdown:
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $43.00 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $360.30, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 1,051 authorised robotaxi vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27, 544 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S150]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $43.00 a share on 3,952.6M shares — $170.0B, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets — and autonomy at $259B in the base case: 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance, which is $65.5 a share on the issued count, and the base case is $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $53 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $454 mid-point lifts expected value to $248, still 38% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

:::

The precedents give one rule: when a real technology shift is already in the price, the entry multiple sets the return, not whether the technology wins; the base rate for a follower in autonomy is a write-off, not a slow fade; and the leader's private mark, $126B, is the only independent price for the option — 9% of what the market pays for Tesla's version. A holder should own Tesla's autonomy at a discount to that mark, not at 11.3 times it, and size the position so the Cruise outcome is survivable. [S140, S142]

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. At $403.30 it sits in the third zone, with the ten-year Treasury at 4.99% raising the discount rate on post-2030 cash flows. Do not invest new money now. Wait for one of three milestones: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless deployment permit, or special-committee terms at a premium to market rather than at market. If the mandate requires exposure, hold a residual of 0.25-0.5% of net asset value, sized so a failed vote and a 30% drawdown do not breach the risk budget, and vote against any ratio that transfers value to the controlling shareholder. Pass on the blue-sky branch: it needs global robotaxi and humanoid dominance and pays 8% from here. Diligence questions: revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, the share of rides running without a safety driver, and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Confidence is high that the core is not worth $403.30, medium on the autonomy tree, low on the merger. What would change the call: a second consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-credit operating margin, an FSD licensing contract with a named automaker, or a ratio that values Tesla at a premium to its undisturbed price. [S15, S5]

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 商业模式 Business Model (business_model, revision 7 by Fundamentals Analyst, 8,955 characters)
Tesla still makes most of its gross profit selling cars, but after regulatory credits the car business earns little at the operating line. Credits supplied 45.8% of FY2025 operating income and 15.7% in Q3 2026; incremental profit now comes from a 33.1%-margin energy-storage business and a 15.9%-margin services business while AI spending absorbs 86.9% of gross profit. Nine-month 2026 revenue of $78,669 million split into automotive $57,310 million (including $639 million of credits), energy $8,428 million and services $12,931 million, against an automotive share of 85.1% in FY2023. Q3 2026 gross profit divided $3,806 million automotive (69%), $954 million energy (17%) and $734 million services (13%), versus 91%/6%/3% in FY2023. Cash arrives when a vehicle changes hands, on storage milestones and prepayments ($3.30 billion of customer prepayments in deferred revenue at 2026-09-30, from $2.04 billion), and monthly for Supercharging, insurance and FSD [S3, S4, S6].

| Segment | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M 2026 | Q3 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue excluding credits ($M) | 80,629 | 74,307 | 67,533 | 56,671 | 20,447 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Automotive regulatory credits ($M) | 1,790 | 2,763 | 1,993 | 639 | 113 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Energy generation and storage revenue ($M) | 6,035 | 10,086 | 12,771 | 8,428 | 2,881 | S3, S4 |
| Services and other revenue ($M) | 8,319 | 10,534 | 12,530 | 12,931 | 4,605 | S3, S4 |
| Automotive gross margin excluding credits | 17.7% | 15.4% | 15.4% | 17.7% | 18.1% | S1, S3, S4, S63 |
| Energy gross margin | 18.9% | 26.2% | 29.8% | 30.2% | 33.1% | S3, S4 |

The credit franchise is ending. Tesla booked $2,763 million of automotive regulatory credits in FY2024, $1,993 million in FY2025 and $639 million in 9M 2026; Q3 2026 alone was $113 million, down 73% from $417 million. Credits carry no cost of revenue, so a credit dollar is nearly a dollar of operating profit: 20.1% of operating income in FY2023, 39.0% in FY2024, 45.8% in FY2025, 31.1% in 9M 2026 and 15.7% in Q3 2026. An implied Q4 2025 figure of $542 million shows the collapse came with the removal of the compliance obligation in 2026, not the lapse of the consumer credit: the Department of Transportation finalised its CAFE rollback on 2026-10-01, ending the requirement that made legacy automakers buy zero-emission credits. Without credits, FY2025's 4.6% operating margin is 2.5% and Q3 2026's 2.6% is 2.2% [S4, S64, S66].

Per vehicle the business improved even as credits disappeared. Q3 2026 automotive revenue per delivery excluding credits was $42,026, up 0.5%, while automotive cost of revenue per delivery (automotive cost of revenue divided by deliveries) fell 2.7% to $34,436, so gross profit per vehicle rose 18.0% to $7,591 (18.1% margin) from $6,433 (15.4%). The gain is cost and mix, not price: management attributes the 270 basis points to a higher Asia-Pacific mix from the low-cost Shanghai plant. Tesla does not disclose customer acquisition cost; SG&A per delivery of $4,142 carries corporate and non-vehicle cost, and the first vehicle's gross profit covers it 1.8 times. A three-year LTV estimate of $8,455 adds three years of services gross profit per vehicle ($288 a year on 10.2 million deliveries), giving LTV:CAC of 2.0:1 and payback inside the delivery quarter. Tesla is the only one of the three with positive per-vehicle gross profit after credits: BYD's automotive gross margin was 20.49% in FY2025, from 22.31%, and Rivian's automotive gross profit was a $(36) million loss in Q2 2026 [S63, S65, S68].

| Automotive revenue per delivery, excluding credits | $41,818 | $42,026 | +0.5% | S4, S6 |
| Automotive cost of revenue per delivery | $35,385 | $34,436 | -2.7% | S4, S6 |
| Automotive gross profit per delivery, excluding credits | $6,433 | $7,591 | +18.0% | S4, S6 |
| Energy gross profit per delivery | $2,158 | $1,961 | -9.1% | S4, S6 |
| Services gross profit per delivery | $736 | $1,508 | +105% | S4, S6 |
| SG&A per delivery (acquisition-cost upper bound) | $3,142 | $4,142 | +31.8% | S4, S6 |

| Product | Pricing metric | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 | Peer benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles, net of credits | realised revenue per delivery | $41,818 | $42,026 | BYD automotive gross margin 20.49%, FY2025 | S4, S65 |
| Megapack and Powerwall | realised revenue per GWh deployed | $273 million | $210 million | Fluence gross margin 13.1%, FY2025 | S3, S67 |

Energy is the highest-margin dollar of growth. Storage revenue per GWh fell 23% to $210 million from $273 million, but gross profit per GWh fell only 19% to $69.6 million because cost per GWh fell 25% to $141 million, lifting segment margin to 33.1% from 31.4%. The mechanism is cell integration: the first Megapacks built with Tesla's own Nevada LFP cells shipped in Q3 2026, Megafactory Texas began production with 50 GWh, and the Megapack backlog is nearly sold out through 2027. Fluence earned 13.1% in FY2025; Tesla's advantage is owning the cell, not pricing. Part of the 33.1% is not repeatable: management attributed it partly to tariff refunds and cell-related warranty reimbursements. Services is the quieter engine: revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million on 2% fewer deliveries and gross margin reached 15.9% from 10.5%. Each extra $1 billion of energy revenue at 30% adds $300 million of gross profit; the same dollar of automotive revenue at 18% adds $180 million. FSD and software grow but remain too small to see in the income statement: active subscriptions rose to 1.74 million from 1.04 million, deferred revenue for FSD, connectivity and software was $4.08 billion against $3.87 billion at 2025-12-31, and obligations beyond one year were $10.73 billion, of which $4.80 billion falls due within twelve months. Management's claim that FSD is attached to more than 75% of North American deliveries is company-reported and cannot be tied to a revenue line, because Tesla does not disclose FSD revenue; the observable is $2,345 of deferred balance per active subscription, a stock rather than a price [S67, S4].

The newest change in money flows is who owns the asset. Selling a car converts inventory into revenue once; a robotaxi fleet keeps the vehicle on Tesla's balance sheet and earns per mile, shifting the model from a hardware sale to a utilisation business paid on miles and uptime rather than deliveries. The Cybercab entered Tesla's own Austin fleet on 2026-09-03, but no fare revenue, fleet size or per-mile economics are disclosed, so the model cannot yet be tested. Until then the investable model remains the one in the tables: cars, storage and services.

Counter-case: gross margin improves while the company gets less profitable. Operating expenses of $4,776 million rose 39% against $5,494 million of gross profit, R&D alone rose 69% to $2,761 million, and depreciation rose 17% to $1,580 million and will accelerate as more than $20 billion of 2026 capital expenditure is commissioned. The warranty reserve rose 26% to $10,138 million on 2% fewer deliveries, with claims incurred up 29% to $1,614 million while the provision per delivery fell to $1,227 from $1,463. Inventory rose 13.7% to $14,092 million, with 11 days of vehicle supply. The vehicle line covers its own costs, so break-even is the cost base: $4,776 million of operating expenses needs $27.0 billion of revenue at a 17.7% blended margin; Q3 2026 delivered $28.0 billion for $718 million of operating profit. Normalise energy to a 30% margin and take credits to zero and the quarter earns $515 million, a 1.8% operating margin. For a position, that argues for sizing on the energy and services annuity, with rising margins and a 2027 backlog, and treating autonomy as an option rather than earnings, because at a 1.8% margin the vehicle franchise cannot carry the cost base alone. Confidence is high on the segment arithmetic and medium on how much of the 2026 cost relief is structural rather than tariff and mix. Four diligence questions remain: what is the North American automotive margin excluding credits? What is the energy margin excluding tariff refunds, and at what price is the 2027 backlog contracted? Will Tesla disclose FSD revenue and robotaxi recognition? When do R&D and capital expenditure stop rising as a share of revenue? [S4, S6]

::: evidence
**Tesla's profit now rests on energy and services gross profit, not on credits or on the car**

Energy storage and services supplied $1,688 million of Q3 2026 gross profit at 33.1% and 15.9% margins, while regulatory credits fell to $113 million, 15.7% of operating income, from 45.8% of FY2025 operating income, and operating expenses absorbed 86.9% of gross profit [S4, S6].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 财务分析 Financial Analysis (financials, revision 9 by Fundamentals Analyst, 8,932 characters)
Tesla's earnings do not justify its premium, and the cash behind them is thinning. At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 the equity is worth $1,594.1 billion on 3,952.6 million shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, or $1,558.0 billion of enterprise value after $36.2 billion of net cash: 15.0 times trailing revenue of $103,570 million, 104 times adjusted EBITDA of $14,995 million, 450 times operating income and 483 times trailing free cash flow of $3,303 million [S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S15]. Revenue went from $81,462 million in FY2022 to $96,773 million, $97,690 million and $94,827 million, while operating income fell from $13,656 million to $8,891 million, $7,076 million and $4,355 million, cutting the operating margin from 16.8% to 2.6% in nine months of 2026. Gross margin held between 17.9% and 19.0% from FY2023, so the compression is operating expense: R&D rose from $3,969 million in FY2023 to $6,411 million in FY2025 and $7,078 million in nine months of 2026. FY2023's $14,997 million net income included a $5,001 million income tax benefit, so the fall to $3,794 million in FY2025 understates the decline in pre-tax earnings.

The third quarter is the clearest read on quality. Revenue of $28,046 million was flat, gross profit rose 8.7% to $5,494 million, and operating expenses of $4,776 million rose 39%, leaving operating income of $718 million, down 56%, and net income of $787 million, down 43%, or $0.22 diluted against $0.39. Non-GAAP net income was $1,697 million, or $0.48 against $0.50; the $910 million gap is chiefly $1,165 million of stock-based compensation, partly offset by the excluded $288 million Bitcoin gain and $142 million SpaceX write-down. Pretax income exceeded operating income by $238 million, 30% of net income, and the effective tax rate fell to 16% from 29% partly on a California deferred-tax asset release in the second quarter. Automotive cost of revenue per vehicle delivered was $34,436, down 2.7% on 486,532 deliveries [S4, S6].

Cash generation now depends on working capital rather than profit because supplier balances and customer prepayments are growing faster than earnings. Operating cash flow rose 36% to $14,897 million while net income fell 19.5% to $2,378 million; payables and accrued liabilities contributed $7,332 million against $2,979 million a year earlier, accounts payable rose to $17,239 million from $13,371 million at 2025-12-31, and days payables outstanding went from 62.8 to 75.3, roughly $2.9 billion of cash on the nine-month cost base. Deferred revenue added $1,746 million, mostly storage prepayments that rose to $3.30 billion. Capital expenditure of $13,014 million consumed 87% of operating cash flow, and quarterly free cash flow was $1,444 million, negative $1,092 million and $1,531 million, against $3,990 million in Q3 2025. Depreciation of $4,290 million rose 17% and will climb faster than revenue as the company's repeated guidance of more than $20 billion of 2026 spending is commissioned [S3, S4, S6].

The balance sheet is not the constraint; the return on the capital being deployed is. At 2026-09-30 Tesla held $45,447 million of cash and short-term investments against $9,267 million of debt, or $36,180 million of net cash, and signed $30 billion of credit commitments in September 2026. Interest income of $1,301 million for nine months covered interest expense of $263 million almost five times. Goodwill of $257 million is 0.2% of assets, so acquired goodwill is not the issue; the pressure is in inventory of $14,092 million, up 13.7% since 2025-12-31 while deliveries fell 2%, and a warranty reserve of $10,138 million, up 26%. Invested capital of $53,109 million earned 5.5% after tax, against 28.3% in FY2023 [S4].

Against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a beta of 1.5 to 2.0, our estimate of the cost of capital is 11% to 14%, so the company destroys economic value at current margins. Capital allocation offers no offset: no dividend, no buyback, capital expenditure guided above $20 billion for 2026, and $1.95 billion of stock paid for an AI hardware company in Q2 2026. Equity compensation is the other claim on shareholders: $3,346 million in nine months is 4.3% of revenue; the 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423.7 million shares, 10.7% of the 3,952.6 million outstanding, with $9.74 billion of unrecognised expense on the one milestone judged probable (20 million vehicles, recognised over 8.9 years) and $105.82-120.37 billion on the remaining tranches; the 2018 award was exercised for 304.0 million options in Q2 2026. The economic reading is that Tesla is converting a cost advantage in vehicles and cells into a capital-intensive compute and robotics business before that business has customers, so the shares trade on optionality rather than earnings [S4, S15, S24].

On trailing figures Tesla's market capitalisation is 495 times net income of $3,218 million and 15.0 times sales, against the peer median of 18.5 times earnings and 2.4 times sales: 27 times the median earnings multiple and 6.3 times the median sales multiple. Adjusted EBITDA is struck before stock-based compensation, so 104 times is understated as a cash multiple. The operating leverage cuts both ways: each 100 basis points of automotive gross margin excluding credits is worth $756 million, or $0.19 a share, on annualised nine-month automotive revenue of $75,561 million, 22% of trailing operating income, so a two-point margin miss plus a $4 billion capital-expenditure overshoot would take 2027 free cash flow to roughly negative $2 billion, while energy growth of 40% at a 30% margin and an automotive margin of 20% would lift it to about $8 billion. That asymmetry makes the shares a bet on autonomy and robotics reaching commercial scale, so position size should be set by tolerance for a de-rating from 104 times EBITDA, not by near-term cash generation. Confidence is high on the statements and the cash bridge, medium on the cost of capital and low on any estimate that requires autonomous revenue to be sized. Three diligence questions remain: how much of the payables increase reverses in Q4 2026? What is the split of the 2026 capital budget between maintenance and AI compute? Does the board intend to offset dilution from the performance award? [S15, S17, S19, S21, S111, S113, S121]

::: info danger
**Operating cash flow is financed by suppliers, not by earnings**
Payables and accrued liabilities supplied most of the increase in nine-month operating cash flow while net income fell, and payment days sit at a multi-year high. With equity compensation at a multi-year high share of revenue and a one-off state tax release in the tax line, both the cash and the profit are weaker than reported, and when supplier terms normalise operating cash flow converges on earnings on low single-digit margins.
