arguments.markdown:
At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 Tesla is a $1,594.1B equity split $43.00 a share, $170B, for the vehicle, energy, services and net-cash business and $360.30 a share, $1,424B, for autonomy and robotics; on 25/50/25 of $212/$107/$19 the probability-weighted value is $111, so the share is a reduce and new money is an option purchase. A market 50% smaller leaves a $105B core, $26 a share, at 94% autonomy; CAC doubled adds $8.1B; revenue 30% lower removes $6.0B; a 5.0x multiple on free cash flow 30% lower is $130; financing six months late is covered by the September facilities [S6, S15, S120, S4, S115]. None reverses the conclusion; a premium exchange ratio does, the risk the recommendation must price. The three premises carrying the $1,424B are deteriorating at once: NHTSA's Cybercab self-certification inquiry closes for comment on 2026-10-30, the special committees formed on 2026-10-20 have no terms, and nine-month free cash flow of $1,883M contains $7,332M from stretching payables to 75.3 days.

### The core is not harsh at 1.0x sales; it is generous

The sum of the parts pays $91B for vehicles and services at 1.0x sales, $43B for energy at 3.5x and $36B of net cash at book. At GM's implied 0.39x, vehicles and services are worth $29B and the core is $87B, $21.75 a share, with autonomy at 95% of the price; a control buyer tops out at $200-250B, $50-62.50, where autonomy still holds 84%. Energy's 3.5x has support — a 29.7% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% — but doubling revenue to $25B on 5.0x adds $82B, $20 a share, and FSD's 1.74M subscribers at $1,200 a year add $42B, $10.5, leaving the best honest core near $70, autonomy at 83%. The $1,424B premium is 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, for 1,051 Texas-authorised vehicles against Waymo's 4,000. [S6, S131, S120, S15, S151]

### The scenario tree is generous at the base and shallow in the bear

The base case's $259B of autonomy is an explicit tree — 35% x $40B regional, 40% x $126B at Waymo parity, 20% x $600B at scale, 5% x $1,500B at dominance — and $259B is 2.1x Waymo's $126B for a fleet with nine reported crashes in August 2026 and no disclosed revenue per mile. Tesla's Texas fleet stood at 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y, Texas DMV records); NHTSA's DP26010 puts the population under review at 1,000, an estimate and exposure ceiling, not an active count; paid Cybercab service has run in Austin since 2026-09-03. Waymo operates 4,000 vehicles (TechCrunch's 2026-09-24 fleet estimate) and reports 500,000 paid rides a week. On the regional branch alone the base is $53, with the tree's $84 weighted value 79% below the close, and the 40% probabilities for 2027 unsupervised FSD and a merger sit above the record: EA26002 covers 2.88M vehicles and DP26010 opened on 2026-10-09. An NHTSA rejection has a 35% probability and a $45-90 a share impact. The $35 bear was too shallow: at $19 — autonomy at zero, vehicles at 0.39x, energy at 1.5x, net cash $29B after a Terafab call — the drawdown is 95% and the weighted value falls only from $115 to $111. Above $437 the path is a 10-15% ratio premium, $443-464. [S120, S137, S6, S5, S150, S151, S152, S153, S59]

### Cash carries a two-year slip, not a slip plus a revenue fall

Net cash of $36.18B and $30B of facilities signed in September 2026 carry a two-year autonomy slip at zero free cash flow without issuing a share. The combination does not survive a revenue fall: at a 19% gross margin, 30% lower revenue removes $6.0B of gross profit against $19.1B of annual operating expense, so with $20-25B of capex the annual burn is $20-27B and cash plus facilities run out before 2029. Reported cash flow already borrows from suppliers: payables and accruals added $7,332M and days payable rose from 62.8 to 75.3, worth $2.9B, so normalised free cash flow is minus $1.0B. Terafab adds a commitment Tesla does not control: a $16.8B first phase with SpaceX, Tesla's share undisclosed, outside the ">$20B" 2026 capital budget and called a "general framework" with no binding commitment in SpaceX's IPO filing — capping near-term cash risk and weakening the strategic-asset defence. Tesla is Baa3, SpaceX Baa1; the facilities' pricing is undisclosed. [S4, S134, S138, S147]

### The merger is an option, not a floor

On 2026-10-20 Musk said both boards had formed special committees, no terms agreed and none assured; the Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares, not of those cast, so abstentions count against, and the 2026-10-19 proxy sets the 2026-12-03 annual meeting with no merger proposal. At market the deal is value-neutral: $1,594.1B plus SpaceX's $2.01T is $3.60T, and Tesla holders taking 43-44% own today's price; any premium must be conceded by SpaceX. Either way Tesla holders get 43% of the economics; 84% of votes sit with one holder. The 2025 award writes the incentive down: on a change of control operational milestones lapse and market-cap milestones vest, 423.7M shares are 10.7% dilution, the first $2.0T milestone sits 25% above today's capitalisation, against a $9.74B probable charge and $105.82-120.37B unrecognised. Musk has pledged 207.5M shares, 5.2% of the count; three of nine directors carry outside ties — two to SpaceX (Ehrenpreis, Kimbal Musk), one to Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier — and the committee uses two. [S5, S135, S138]

### Policy is a $5.60 option; competition is a terminal-value risk

Twenty-five state attorneys general and 12 cities and counties sued on 2026-03-19 in the D.C. Circuit over EPA's 2026-02-12 repeal of the 2009 endangerment finding, consolidated on 2026-05-20; a reversal restores the credit pool, but $1.5B of credits at 15x is $22.5B, $5.6 a share, against Q3 credit revenue of $113M, down 73% and 45.8% of FY2025 operating income. Competition is different in kind: BYD holds 2.4% of the European market at EUR 5,500 less per car, Xiaomi is near break-even in its first production year and Waymo runs 500,000 paid rides a week on 4,000 vehicles. If revenue per mile falls from $0.60 to $0.45, the reverse DCF needs 20.9M robotaxis rather than 15.7M, above global annual capacity — $40-60 a share off the bull branch and nothing off 2027 earnings. The unknown unknown is a recall that grounds the fleet and removes its training data. [S136, S138, S59, S4]

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 投资潜力与投资逻辑 Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 9 by Lead Analyst, 8,958 characters)
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $43.00 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $360.30, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 1,051 authorised robotaxi vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27, 544 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S150]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $43.00 a share on 3,952.6M shares — $170.0B, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets — and autonomy at $259B in the base case: 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance, which is $65.5 a share on the issued count, and the base case is $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $53 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $454 mid-point lifts expected value to $248, still 38% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

::: scenarios
| Scenario | Probability | Drivers | Outcome | Signposts | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Base | 50% | Autonomy at $259B, the probability-weighted blend of the four branches (35% × $40B, 40% × $126B, 20% × $600B, 5% × $1,500B); core at $43.00; energy at 3.5x sales | $107 a share, -73% | Q4 2026 update with no robotaxi revenue despite 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles; no fare or cost per mile disclosed | S6, S120, S150 |
| Bear | 25% | Autonomy written down; vehicles at GM's 0.39x sales; Terafab commitment; credit-free margin | $19 a share, -95% | Unsupervised FSD slips past 2027; NHTSA recall of the Cybercab; merger vote fails | S6, S120, S137 |
:::

### Key assumptions, ranked

| Rank | Assumption | Confidence | What would disprove it | Impact if wrong | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031: 15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile is what the reverse DCF needs | low | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | Authorisations flat near 1,051 Texas vehicles; no fare disclosure; safety-driver hours rising | S4, S6, S137, S150 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | medium | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | Each 100 bp is $756M, 22% of trailing operating income | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% with revenue growth | medium | Q4 margin below 25% once tariff refunds lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | Q3 revenue fell 16% to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | low | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | Terafab's $16.8B first phase sits outside the 2026 budget | S4, S134 |
| 5 | No value-transferring exchange ratio; award dilution held at 10.7% | low | Ratio struck below market, or new tranches granted | -$40 to -$80 a share | Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers | S5, S135, S138 |

Assumption 1 sets the price and is the least evidenced: no robotaxi revenue, no fare and no cost per mile are disclosed, so the largest component of value rests on a registry count of authorised vehicles rather than on unit economics. Assumptions 2 and 3 decide whether the core is worth $43.00 or $21.75, and management can still influence both in 2027 — the ex-credit operating margin has been cut to 2.2-2.5%, while energy and services supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M third-quarter gross profit at a margin 2.5 times Fluence's 13.1%. Assumptions 4 and 5 are about survival and dilution rather than growth: $36.18B of net cash covers eighteen months of zero free cash flow, but not that plus a $16.8B capital call whose Tesla share is undisclosed. [S4, S6]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cisco | cautionary | 2000-2024 | Revenue grew from $12.5B to $57B and trailing net income passed its 1999 level by 2003, yet a buyer at the March 2000 peak of $500B waited until 2021 to break even. A correct thesis does not rescue the entry multiple. | S140 |
| Amazon | cautionary | 1999-2001 | The business compounded into one of the great franchises, but the stock fell more than 90% and took a decade to recover; the option paid only for the holder who could sit through the drawdown. | S143 |
| GM Cruise | cautionary | 2016-2024 | More than $10B of operating losses and less than $500M of revenue before GM shut the robotaxi unit in December 2024 for $1B a year of savings. Automaker capital is no substitute for paid driverless miles. | S142 |
| Waymo | best | 2024-2026 | The valuation went from $45B in October 2024 to $126B in February 2026 on 500,000 paid driverless rides a week — proof the service can scale, and a mark that Tesla's autonomy value exceeds 11-fold. | S120 |
:::

The precedents give one rule: when a real technology shift is already in the price, the entry multiple sets the return, not whether the technology wins; the base rate for a follower in autonomy is a write-off, not a slow fade; and the leader's private mark, $126B, is the only independent price for the option — 9% of what the market pays for Tesla's version. A holder should own Tesla's autonomy at a discount to that mark, not at 11.3 times it, and size the position so the Cruise outcome is survivable. [S140, S142]

### Where the case turns, and what to do now

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. At $403.30 it sits in the third zone, with the ten-year Treasury at 4.99% raising the discount rate on post-2030 cash flows. Do not invest new money now. Wait for one of three milestones: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless deployment permit, or special-committee terms at a premium to market rather than at market. If the mandate requires exposure, hold a residual of 0.25-0.5% of net asset value, sized so a failed vote and a 30% drawdown do not breach the risk budget, and vote against any ratio that transfers value to the controlling shareholder. Pass on the blue-sky branch: it needs global robotaxi and humanoid dominance and pays 8% from here. Diligence questions: revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, the share of rides running without a safety driver, and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Confidence is high that the core is not worth $403.30, medium on the autonomy tree, low on the merger. What would change the call: a second consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-credit operating margin, an FSD licensing contract with a named automaker, or a ratio that values Tesla at a premium to its undisturbed price. [S15, S5]"}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 综合评分与投资建议 Comprehensive Scoring & Recommendation (scoring, revision 12 by Lead Analyst, 8,818 characters)
Tesla scores 4.0 out of 10, and the score is not close to the line that would justify new money: at $403.30 the shares price the autonomy option at $1,424B, 89% of the equity, while the business that pays the bills earns a 2.2-2.5% operating margin once regulatory credits are stripped out. The recommendation is Reduce — trim existing exposure to a residual, buy nothing — on a twelve-month horizon, with medium confidence in the direction and high confidence in the arithmetic. The composite is a weighted average of seven dimensions, and two do most of the work: valuation at 2 with a 20% weight and governance at 3 with a 15% weight; without either the stock still scores below 5. [S15, S4]

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business quality and moat | 15% | 6 | Energy earned a 33.1% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% and vertical integration in cells and packs is real; vehicle share is falling in China and the premium band is contested | S6, S63, S59 |
| Growth durability | 15% | 5 | Energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881B in Q3 2026 and deliveries fell 2%, so growth now depends on a robotaxi fleet of 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles | S6, S4, S150 |
| Unit economics and margins | 15% | 4 | The ex-credit operating margin is 2.2-2.5% and trailing ROIC is 5.5% against an 11-14% cost of capital | S3, S4 |
| Balance sheet and cash conversion | 15% | 5 | $36.18B of net cash and $30B of undrawn facilities, offset by a 61% fall in nine-month free cash flow and payables at 75.3 days against 62.8 | S4 |
| Governance and capital allocation | 15% | 3 | A 423.7M-share award with $105.82-120.37B of unrecognised compensation, three of nine directors carrying outside ties of which two are to SpaceX, no dividend or buyback | S5, S138 |
| Valuation and margin of safety | 20% | 2 | 443x trailing and 183x 2027E earnings against an 18.5x trailing P/E and 2.4x EV/sales median for the six peers shown in section 8; the margin of safety turns positive only below $111 | S15, S115 |
| Catalysts, regime and positioning | 5% | 3 | A binary merger process is the only re-rating path, against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury and a VIX of 17.20 | S24, S23, S135 |

The weighting is deliberate. A heavy weight on valuation is right because at the current multiple the entry price, not the technology, dominates a five-year return. The governance weight reflects what a standard framework misses: the controlling shareholder's compensation is tied to market-capitalisation milestones, so management is paid for the narrative that supports the multiple rather than for per-share cash flow, and a change of control accelerates the award. Business quality scores 6 rather than 8 because the strongest part of the franchise, energy storage, is a small and shrinking share of revenue in dollars, while vehicles are losing share in the region that sets global prices.

The counter-evidence deserves its own paragraph: energy earns a 33.1% gross margin at $210M of revenue per GWh, Tesla's $34,436 cost per vehicle is below every Western competitor, and a triple-digit multiple has persisted for two years without mean reversion. If energy revenue doubles and FSD licensing adds a second stream, the core could be worth $70 a share rather than $43.00. That moves the composite by less than half a point, because the core is 11% of the price and the autonomy premium is 11.3 times the leader's mark. The risks run both ways: if the bear branch materialises — autonomy written down, vehicles valued at GM's multiple, the Terafab commitment drawn — value collapses to a small fraction of today's price and Reduce becomes Sell or Avoid at any size. The base case carries $259B of autonomy on a probability-weighted blend of four branches, not the $40B regional fleet alone: at regional-only autonomy the base would be $53 and the probability-weighted value $84, and the recommendation would not change. The only branch that lifts the score above 5 is the merger: a negotiated ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price would justify Hold, with the position capped because a failed vote returns the stock to a level set by the operating business. [S6, S63, S120]

Kelly arithmetic at the current price is negative, so the correct unconstrained position is zero. The table sets out the inputs.

| Sizing measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Probability-weighted value | $111 a share on 25/50/25 ($212 / $107 / $19) | S6, S120 |
| Expected return from $403.30 | -72% | S15 |
| Expected value including the merger branch at 40% | $248 a share | S135 |
| Kelly fraction | negative in every branch; constrained to 0 | S6, S120 |
| Residual cap where a mandate requires exposure | 0.5% of net asset value | arithmetic on S6 |
| Fund loss at a 95% bear case on a 0.5% position | -0.48% of net asset value | S6 |

The regime argues for the smaller end: the ten-year Treasury at 4.99%, up 0.93 points in twelve months, raises the discount rate on cash flows arriving after 2030; the S&P 500 is 1.6% below its high, the VIX is at the 52nd percentile, and consumer discretionary has lagged the index by 0.3 points over three months. [S24, S23, S22]

### Sensitivity: what moves the value

::: sensitivity
| Rank | Assumption | Base | What would disprove it | Impact on value | Impact level | Early warning | Source |

| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031 (15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile implied by the price) | Autonomy at $259B across four weighted branches; 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles; the regional branch alone is $40B, or $10.1 a share on a $43.00 core | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | high | Authorisations flat near 1,051; no fare disclosure | S4, S6, S137, S150 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | 18.1% in Q3 2026 | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | -$0.19 of operating income a share per 100 bp; -$0.76 on a 4-point miss; -$3.5 and -$14 at the 18.5x peer multiple, -$84 per 100 bp at the 443x the shares carry | high | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% | 33.1% in Q3 2026, part of it tariff refunds and warranty reimbursements | Q4 margin below 25% once one-offs lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | high | Revenue -16% year over year to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | $13.0B in nine months; above $20B for 2026 | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | medium | Terafab's $16.8B first phase outside the budget | S4, S134 |
| 5 | No value-transferring exchange ratio and dilution of 10.7% from the 2025 award | No terms agreed; a 50%-of-all-shares vote | Ratio struck below market, or new award tranches | -$40 to -$80 a share | high | Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers | S5, S135, S138 |
:::

::: takeaways
1. **Reduce, not Buy:** 89% of the $403.30 price — $1,424B — is an autonomy option valued at 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark, while the vehicle and energy business is worth $43.00 a share [S15, S120].
2. **Size to zero:** the probability-weighted value is $111 and the Kelly fraction is negative in every branch, so new money buys nothing and an existing position is capped at 0.5% of net asset value [S6, S120].
3. **Four events would change the call:** a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless permit, an ex-credit operating margin back in double digits, or an exchange ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price [S135, S4].
:::

Five actions would settle the open questions. The next results release should be read for a robotaxi revenue line, a fleet count and a fare; a fourth consecutive quarter without one is the clearest signal that the option is not converting. The California DMV and CPUC filings should be checked for a driverless deployment permit, because the current service runs on a limousine authority and no AV permit is listed. The special committees' 8-K should be read for the exchange ratio, the advisers and the treatment of unvested award shares. The annual 10-K should be read for capital expenditure guidance, the Terafab contribution and whether payables reverse. The annual-meeting proxy should be read for the per-tranche thresholds of the CEO award that the text extraction dropped. The conditions for investing are concrete: a share price below the probability-weighted value, or a disclosed robotaxi business whose revenue and cost per mile support the free cash flow the reverse DCF requires. Until one exists, the evidence supports a reduced position and a waiting stance; the score is a statement about the price, not about the engineering."}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 退出策略分析 Exit Strategy Analysis (exit, revision 5 by Valuation Analyst, 8,450 characters)
Tesla offers no cash exit at $1.59 trillion. It has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation, and its entire $45.4B of cash and short-term investments would retire 2.85% of the 3.953B shares outstanding. The largest buyout ever completed — Electronic Arts at $55B in August 2026 — is 3.4% of Tesla's market capitalisation, so no financial sponsor can write this cheque, and no automaker can either: GM and Ford together are $118.4B, 7.4% of Tesla. What remains is a sale into a market that trades $14.0B of Tesla a day, or a share exchange into SpaceX, and both leave the return hostage to a re-rating that five years have not delivered. arguments.markdown:
Tesla still sells cars for a living, but in 2026 its incremental profit comes from energy storage and services while regulatory credits fade, and the car business alone does not cover its cost base. Nine-month 2026 revenue of $78,669 million split into automotive $57,310 million (including $639 million of credits), energy $8,428 million and services $12,931 million. Q3 2026 gross profit divided $3,806 million automotive (69%), $954 million energy (17%) and $734 million services (13%), versus 91%/6%/3% in FY2023. Cash arrives when a vehicle changes hands, on storage milestones and prepayments ($3.30 billion of customer prepayments in deferred revenue at 2026-09-30, from $2.04 billion), and monthly for Supercharging, insurance and FSD [S3, S4, S6].

| Segment | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M 2026 | Q3 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue excluding credits ($M) | 80,629 | 74,307 | 67,533 | 56,671 | 20,447 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Automotive regulatory credits ($M) | 1,790 | 2,763 | 1,993 | 639 | 113 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Energy generation and storage revenue ($M) | 6,035 | 10,086 | 12,771 | 8,428 | 2,881 | S3, S4 |
| Services and other revenue ($M) | 8,319 | 10,534 | 12,530 | 12,931 | 4,605 | S3, S4 |
| Automotive gross margin excluding credits | 17.7% | 15.4% | 15.4% | 17.7% | 18.1% | S1, S3, S4, S63 |
| Energy gross margin | 18.9% | 26.2% | 29.8% | 30.2% | 33.1% | S3, S4 |

The credit franchise is ending. Tesla booked $2,763 million of automotive regulatory credits in FY2024, $1,993 million in FY2025 and $639 million in 9M 2026; Q3 2026 alone was $113 million, down 73% from $417 million. Credits carry no cost of revenue, so a credit dollar is nearly a dollar of operating profit: 20.1% of operating income in FY2023, 39.0% in FY2024, 45.8% in FY2025, 31.1% in 9M 2026 and 15.7% in Q3 2026. An implied Q4 2025 figure of $542 million shows the collapse came with the removal of the compliance obligation in 2026, not the lapse of the consumer credit: the Department of Transportation finalised its CAFE rollback on 2026-10-01, ending the requirement that made legacy automakers buy zero-emission credits. Without credits, FY2025's 4.6% operating margin is 2.5% and Q3 2026's 2.6% is 2.2% [S4, S64, S66].

Per vehicle the business improved even as credits disappeared. Q3 2026 automotive revenue per delivery excluding credits was $42,026, up 0.5%, while automotive cost of revenue per delivery (total automotive cost of revenue divided by deliveries) fell 2.7% to $34,436, so gross profit per vehicle rose 18.0% to $7,591 (18.1% margin) from $6,433 (15.4%). The gain is cost and mix, not price: management attributes the 270 basis points to a higher Asia-Pacific mix from the low-cost Shanghai plant. Tesla does not disclose customer acquisition cost; SG&A per delivery of $4,142 carries corporate and non-vehicle cost and the first vehicle's gross profit covers it 1.8 times. A three-year LTV of $8,455 — three years of services gross profit at $288 a vehicle on 10.2 million deliveries — gives LTV:CAC of 2.0:1 and payback inside the delivery quarter. BYD's automotive gross margin was 20.49% in FY2025, from 22.31%, and Rivian's automotive gross profit was a $(36) million loss in Q2 2026 [S63, S65, S68].

| Per unit | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 | Change | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deliveries (units) | 497,099 | 486,532 | -2.1% | S6 |
| Automotive revenue per delivery, excluding credits | $41,818 | $42,026 | +0.5% | S4, S6 |
| Automotive cost of revenue per delivery | $35,385 | $34,436 | -2.7% | S4, S6 |
| Automotive gross profit per delivery, excluding credits | $6,433 | $7,591 | +18.0% | S4, S6 |
| Energy gross profit per delivery | $2,158 | $1,961 | -9.1% | S4, S6 |
| Services gross profit per delivery | $736 | $1,508 | +105% | S4, S6 |
| SG&A per delivery (acquisition-cost upper bound) | $3,142 | $4,142 | +31.8% | S4, S6 |
| R&D per delivery | $3,279 | $5,675 | +73.1% | S4, S6 |
| Operating profit per delivery | $3,267 | $1,476 | -54.8% | S4, S6 |

| Product | Pricing metric | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 | Peer benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles, net of credits | realised revenue per delivery | $41,818 | $42,026 | BYD automotive gross margin 20.49%, FY2025 | S4, S65 |
| Megapack and Powerwall | realised revenue per GWh deployed | $273 million | $210 million | Fluence gross margin 13.1%, FY2025 | S3, S67 |

Energy is the highest-margin dollar of growth. Storage revenue per GWh fell 23% to $210 million from $273 million on 13.7 GWh deployed, up from 12.5 GWh, but gross profit per GWh fell only 19% to $69.6 million because cost per GWh fell 25% to $141 million, lifting segment margin to 33.1% from 31.4%. The mechanism is cell integration: the first Megapacks built with Tesla's own Nevada LFP cells shipped in Q3 2026 and Megafactory Texas began production with planned capacity of 50 GWh. On the backlog, management said on the 2026-10-21 earnings call that Tesla is "almost sold out of all Megapacks for 2027", and the same day's release cites a "highest-ever order rate and backlog" — company claims only, unverified, with no volume, contract value or price disclosed, so the energy annuity has to be sized on reported deployments, not on the backlog. Management's claim that FSD is attached to more than 75% of North American deliveries is company-reported and cannot be tied to a revenue line, because Tesla does not disclose FSD revenue [S6, S63, S67, S158].

The newest change in money flows is who owns the asset: a robotaxi fleet keeps the vehicle on Tesla's balance sheet and earns per mile, shifting the model from a hardware sale to a utilisation business paid on miles and uptime rather than deliveries. The warranty reserve rose 26% to $10,138 million on 2% fewer deliveries, with claims incurred up 29% to $1,614 million while the provision per delivery fell to $1,227 from $1,463. Inventory rose 13.7% to $14,092 million, with 11 days of vehicle supply. The vehicle line covers its own costs, so break-even is the cost base: $4,776 million of operating expenses needs $27.0 billion of revenue at a 17.7% blended margin; Q3 2026 delivered $28.0 billion for $718 million of operating profit. When do R&D and capital expenditure stop rising as a share of revenue? [S4, S6]

::: evidence
**Tesla's profit now rests on energy and services gross profit, not on credits or on the car**

Energy storage and services supplied $1,688 million of Q3 2026 gross profit at 33.1% and 15.9% margins, while regulatory credits fell to $113 million, 15.7% of operating income, from 45.8% of FY2025 operating income, and operating expenses absorbed 86.9% of gross profit [S4, S6].

arguments.markdown:
Tesla still sells cars for a living, but in 2026 its incremental profit comes from energy storage and services while regulatory credits fade, and the car business alone does not cover its cost base. Nine-month 2026 revenue of $78,669 million split into automotive $57,310 million (including $639 million of credits), energy $8,428 million and services $12,931 million. Q3 2026 gross profit divided $3,806 million automotive (69%), $954 million energy (17%) and $734 million services (13%). Cash arrives on delivery, on storage milestones and customer prepayments ($3.30 billion of deferred revenue at 2026-09-30, from $2.04 billion), and monthly for Supercharging, insurance and FSD [S3, S4, S6].

| Segment | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M 2026 | Q3 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue excluding credits ($M) | 80,629 | 74,307 | 67,533 | 56,671 | 20,447 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Automotive regulatory credits ($M) | 1,790 | 2,763 | 1,993 | 639 | 113 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Energy generation and storage revenue ($M) | 6,035 | 10,086 | 12,771 | 8,428 | 2,881 | S3, S4 |
| Services and other revenue ($M) | 8,319 | 10,534 | 12,530 | 12,931 | 4,605 | S3, S4 |
| Automotive gross margin excluding credits | 17.7% | 15.4% | 15.4% | 17.7% | 18.1% | S1, S3, S4, S63 |
| Energy gross margin | 18.9% | 26.2% | 29.8% | 30.2% | 33.1% | S3, S4 |

The credit franchise is ending. Tesla booked $2,763 million of automotive regulatory credits in FY2024, $1,993 million in FY2025 and $639 million in 9M 2026; Q3 2026 alone was $113 million, down 73% from $417 million. Credits carry no cost of revenue, so a credit dollar is nearly a dollar of operating profit: 20.1% of operating income in FY2023, 39.0% in FY2024, 45.8% in FY2025, 31.1% in 9M 2026 and 15.7% in Q3 2026. An implied Q4 2025 figure of $542 million shows the collapse came with the 2026 removal of the compliance obligation, not the lapse of the consumer credit: the Department of Transportation finalised its CAFE rollback on 2026-10-01, ending the requirement that made legacy automakers buy zero-emission credits. Without credits, FY2025's 4.6% operating margin is 2.5% and Q3 2026's 2.6% is 2.2% [S4, S64, S66].

Per vehicle the business improved even as credits disappeared. Q3 2026 automotive revenue per delivery excluding credits was $42,026, up 0.5%, while automotive cost of revenue per delivery (total automotive cost of revenue divided by deliveries) fell 2.7% to $34,436, so gross profit per vehicle rose 18.0% to $7,591 (18.1% margin) from $6,433 (15.4%). The gain is cost and mix, not price: management attributes the 270 basis points to a higher Asia-Pacific mix from the low-cost Shanghai plant. Tesla does not disclose customer acquisition cost; SG&A per delivery of $4,142 includes corporate cost and the first vehicle's gross profit covers it 1.8 times. A three-year LTV of $8,455 — three years of services gross profit at $288 a vehicle on 10.2 million deliveries — gives LTV:CAC of 2.0:1 and payback inside the delivery quarter. BYD's automotive gross margin was 20.49% in FY2025, from 22.31%, and Rivian's automotive gross profit was a $(36) million loss in Q2 2026 [S63, S65, S68].

| Per unit | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 | Change | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deliveries (units) | 497,099 | 486,532 | -2.1% | S6 |
| Automotive revenue per delivery, excluding credits | $41,818 | $42,026 | +0.5% | S4, S6 |
| Automotive cost of revenue per delivery | $35,385 | $34,436 | -2.7% | S4, S6 |
| Automotive gross profit per delivery, excluding credits | $6,433 | $7,591 | +18.0% | S4, S6 |
| Energy gross profit per delivery | $2,158 | $1,961 | -9.1% | S4, S6 |
| Services gross profit per delivery | $736 | $1,508 | +105% | S4, S6 |
| SG&A per delivery (acquisition-cost upper bound) | $3,142 | $4,142 | +31.8% | S4, S6 |
| R&D per delivery | $3,279 | $5,675 | +73.1% | S4, S6 |
| Operating profit per delivery | $3,267 | $1,476 | -54.8% | S4, S6 |

| Product | Pricing metric | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 | Peer benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles, net of credits | realised revenue per delivery | $41,818 | $42,026 | BYD automotive gross margin 20.49%, FY2025 | S4, S65 |
| Megapack and Powerwall | realised revenue per GWh deployed | $273 million | $210 million | Fluence gross margin 13.1%, FY2025 | S3, S67 |

Energy is the highest-margin dollar of growth. Storage revenue per GWh fell 23% to $210 million from $273 million on 13.7 GWh deployed, up from 12.5 GWh, but gross profit per GWh fell only 19% to $69.6 million because cost per GWh fell 25% to $141 million, lifting segment margin to 33.1% from 31.4%. The mechanism is cell integration: the first Megapacks built with Tesla's own Nevada LFP cells shipped in Q3 2026 and Megafactory Texas began production with planned capacity of 50 GWh. On the backlog, management said on the 2026-10-21 earnings call that Tesla is "almost sold out of all Megapacks for 2027", and the same day's release cites a "highest-ever order rate and backlog" — company claims only, unverified, with no volume, contract value or price disclosed, so the energy annuity has to be sized on reported deployments, not on the backlog. Fluence earned 13.1%; Tesla's edge is owning the cell, not pricing. Part of the 33.1% is not repeatable: management attributed it partly to tariff refunds and cell-related warranty reimbursements. Services is the quieter engine: revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million on 2% fewer deliveries and gross margin reached 15.9% from 10.5%. FSD and software grow but remain too small to see in the income statement: active subscriptions rose to 1.74 million from 1.04 million — a company operating KPI defined for the 2025 CEO Performance Award, not an audited or GAAP-reported metric — while deferred revenue for FSD, connectivity and software was $4.08 billion against $3.87 billion at 2025-12-31. Management's claim that FSD is attached to more than 75% of North American deliveries is company-reported and cannot be tied to a revenue line, because Tesla does not disclose FSD revenue [S6, S63, S67, S158].

The newest change in money flows is who owns the asset: a robotaxi fleet keeps the vehicle on Tesla's balance sheet and earns per mile rather than per delivery. The Cybercab entered Tesla's own Austin fleet on 2026-09-03, but no fare revenue, fleet size or per-mile economics are disclosed, so the model cannot yet be tested; until then the investable model remains cars, storage and services.

Counter-case: gross margin improves while the company gets less profitable. Operating expenses of $4,776 million rose 39% against $5,494 million of gross profit, R&D alone rose 69% to $2,761 million, and depreciation rose 17% to $1,580 million and will accelerate as more than $20 billion of 2026 capital expenditure is commissioned. The warranty reserve rose 26% to $10,138 million on 2% fewer deliveries, with claims incurred up 29% to $1,614 million while the provision per delivery fell to $1,227 from $1,463. Inventory rose 13.7% to $14,092 million, with 11 days of supply. The vehicle line covers its own costs, so break-even is the cost base: $4,776 million of operating expenses needs $27.0 billion of revenue at a 17.7% blended margin; Q3 2026 delivered $28.0 billion for $718 million of operating profit. Normalise energy to a 30% margin and take credits to zero and the quarter earns $515 million, a 1.8% operating margin. For a position, that argues for sizing the energy and services annuity on reported deployments and contracted revenue, not on the undisclosed 2027 backlog, and treating autonomy as an option rather than earnings, because at a 1.8% margin the vehicle franchise cannot carry the cost base alone. Confidence is high on the segment arithmetic, medium on how much of the cost relief is structural. Four diligence questions remain: what is the North American automotive margin excluding credits? What is the energy margin excluding tariff refunds, and what volumes and prices underpin the claimed 2027 Megapack sell-out? Will Tesla disclose FSD revenue and robotaxi recognition? When do R&D and capital expenditure stop rising as a share of revenue? [S4, S6]

::: evidence
**Tesla's profit now rests on energy and services gross profit, not on credits or on the car**

Energy storage and services supplied $1,688 million of Q3 2026 gross profit at 33.1% and 15.9% margins, while regulatory credits fell to $113 million, 15.7% of operating income, from 45.8% of FY2025 operating income, and operating expenses absorbed 86.9% of gross profit [S4, S6].
:::

Tesla's earnings do not justify its premium, and the cash behind them is thinning. Tesla's earnings do not justify its premium, and the cash behind them is thinning. FY2023's $14,997 million net income included a $5,001 million income tax benefit, so the fall to $3,794 million in FY2025 understates the decline in pre-tax earnings.

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's earnings do not justify its premium, and the cash behind them is thinning. At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 the equity is worth $1,594.1 billion on 3,952.6 million shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, or $1,558.0 billion of enterprise value after $36.2 billion of net cash: on the enterprise value, 15.0 times trailing revenue of $103,570 million, 104 times adjusted EBITDA of $14,995 million and 450 times operating income; on the market capitalisation, 443.2 times trailing diluted EPS of $0.91 (net income $3,218 million on 3,541 million diluted shares) and 483 times trailing free cash flow of $3,303 million [S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S15]. Revenue went from $81,462 million in FY2022 to $96,773 million, $97,690 million and $94,827 million, while operating income fell from $13,656 million to $8,891 million, $7,076 million and $4,355 million, and the operating margin from 16.8% to 2.6% in nine months of 2026. Gross margin held between 17.9% and 19.0% from FY2023, so the compression is operating expense: R&D rose from $3,969 million in FY2023 to $6,411 million in FY2025 and $7,078 million in nine months of 2026. FY2023's $14,997 million net income included a $5,001 million income tax benefit, so the fall to $3,794 million in FY2025 understates the decline in pre-tax earnings.

| Gross profit (margin) | 17,660 (18.2%) | 17,450 (17.9%) | 17,094 (18.0%) | 14,965 (19.0%) | 5,494 (19.6%) | S1, S2, S3, S4 |
| Operating income (margin) | 8,891 (9.2%) | 7,076 (7.2%) | 4,355 (4.6%) | 2,057 (2.6%) | 718 (2.6%) | S1, S2, S3, S4 |
| Net income | 14,997 | 7,091 | 3,794 | 2,378 | 787 | S1, S2, S3, S4 |
| Diluted EPS ($) | 4.30 | 2.04 | 1.08 | 0.67 | 0.22 | S1, S2, S3, S4 |
| Operating cash flow | 13,256 | 14,923 | 14,747 | 14,897 | 6,263 | S1, S2, S3, S4, S6 |
| Capital expenditure | 8,898 | 11,339 | 8,527 | 13,014 | 4,732 | S1, S2, S3, S4, S6 |
| Free cash flow | 4,358 | 3,584 | 6,220 | 1,883 | 1,531 | S1, S2, S3, S4, S6 |
| Stock-based compensation | 1,812 | 1,999 | 2,825 | 3,346 | 1,165 | S1, S2, S3, S6 |
| Net cash | 24,437 | 28,685 | 35,906 | 36,180 | 36,180 | S1, S2, S3, S4 |

Revenue of $28,046 million was flat in Q3 2026, gross profit rose 8.7% to $5,494 million, and operating expenses of $4,776 million rose 39%, leaving operating income of $718 million, down 56%, and net income of $787 million, down 43%, or $0.22 diluted against $0.39. Non-GAAP net income was $1,697 million, or $0.48 against $0.50; the $910 million gap is chiefly $1,165 million of stock-based compensation, partly offset by the excluded $288 million Bitcoin gain and $142 million SpaceX write-down. Pretax income exceeded operating income by $238 million, 30% of net income, and the effective tax rate fell to 16% from 29% partly on a state deferred-tax release. Automotive cost of revenue per vehicle delivered was $34,436, down 2.7% on 486,532 deliveries [S4, S6].

Cash generation now depends on working capital: supplier balances and customer prepayments are growing faster than earnings. Operating cash flow rose 36% to $14,897 million while net income fell 19.5% to $2,378 million; payables and accrued liabilities contributed $7,332 million against $2,979 million a year earlier, accounts payable rose to $17,239 million from $13,371 million at 2025-12-31, and days payables outstanding went from 62.8 to 75.3. Deferred revenue added $1,746 million, mostly storage prepayments that rose to $3.30 billion. Capital expenditure of $13,014 million consumed 87% of operating cash flow, and quarterly free cash flow was $1,444 million, negative $1,092 million and $1,531 million, against $3,990 million in Q3 2025. Depreciation of $4,290 million rose 17% and will climb faster than revenue as more than $20 billion of 2026 spending is commissioned [S3, S4, S6].

| Capital expenditure / depreciation | 2.67x | 2.75x | 1.70x | 2.72x | S1, S2, S3, S4 |

The balance sheet is not the constraint; the return on the capital being deployed is. At 2026-09-30 Tesla held $45,447 million of cash and short-term investments against $9,267 million of debt, or $36,180 million of net cash, and signed $30 billion of credit commitments in September 2026. Goodwill is 0.2% of assets; the pressure is in inventory of $14,092 million, up 13.7% since 2025-12-31 while deliveries fell 2%, and a warranty reserve of $10,138 million, up 26%. Invested capital of $53,109 million earned 5.5% after tax on a trailing basis (TTM net operating profit after tax over average invested capital for the four quarters to 2026-09-30), against 28.3% in FY2023; the roughly 3% return on 2026 invested capital that includes the full capital programme is a forward-looking figure on a larger asset base, not a competing measurement of the same period [S4].

Against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a beta of 1.5 to 2.0, our estimate of the cost of capital is 11% to 14%, so the company destroys economic value at current margins. Capital allocation offers no offset: no dividend or buyback, capex guided above $20 billion for 2026, and $1.95 billion of stock paid for an AI hardware company in Q2 2026. Equity compensation is the other claim on shareholders: $3,346 million in nine months is 4.3% of revenue; the 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423.7 million shares, 10.7% of the 3,952.6 million outstanding, with $9.74 billion of unrecognised expense on the one milestone judged probable (20 million vehicles, recognised over 8.9 years) and $105.82-120.37 billion on the remaining tranches. The economic reading is that Tesla is converting a vehicle and cell cost advantage into a capital-intensive compute and robotics business before that business has customers, so the shares trade on optionality rather than earnings [S4, S15, S24].

| Comparable | Trailing P/E | EV/sales | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| GM | 18.8x | n/m | S17 |
| Ford | n/m | n/m | S19 |
| Rivian | n/m | 2.4x | S21 |
| Lucid | n/m | 2.4x | S111 |
| Alphabet | 14.2x | 7.5x | S113 |
| BYD | 18.5x | n/m | S121 |
| Median of the six | 18.5x | 2.4x | S17, S19, S21, S111, S113, S121 |

Tesla trades at 443.2 times trailing diluted EPS of $0.91, 24 times the peer median of 18.5 times earnings, and at 15.0 times sales on the $1,558.0 billion enterprise value, 6.3 times the median 2.4 times sales; market capitalisation over the same $3,218 million of net income is 495 times. Adjusted EBITDA is struck before stock-based compensation, so 104 times is understated as a cash multiple. Each 100 basis points of automotive gross margin excluding credits is worth $756 million, or $0.19 a share, on annualised nine-month automotive revenue of $75,561 million — 22% of trailing operating income — so a two-point margin miss plus a $4 billion capex overshoot would take 2027 free cash flow to roughly negative $2 billion, while energy growth of 40% at a 30% margin and a 20% automotive margin would lift it to about $8 billion. That asymmetry makes the shares a bet on autonomy and robotics, so position size should be set by tolerance for a de-rating from 104 times EBITDA, not by near-term cash generation. Confidence is high on the statements and the cash bridge, medium on the cost of capital and low on any estimate that requires autonomous revenue to be sized. Three diligence questions remain: how much of the payables increase reverses in Q4 2026? What is the split of the 2026 capital budget between maintenance and AI compute? Does the board intend to offset dilution from the performance award? [S15, S17, S19, S21, S111, S113, S121]

::: info danger
**Operating cash flow is financed by suppliers, not by earnings**
Payables and accrued liabilities supplied most of the increase in nine-month operating cash flow while net income fell, and payment days sit at a multi-year high. With equity compensation at a multi-year high share of revenue and a one-off state tax release in the tax line, both the cash and the profit are weaker than reported, and when supplier terms normalise operating cash flow converges on earnings on low single-digit margins.
:::

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's earnings do not justify its premium, and the cash behind them is thinning. At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 the equity is worth $1,594.1 billion on 3,952.6 million shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, or $1,558.0 billion of enterprise value after $36.2 billion of net cash: on the enterprise value, 15.0 times trailing revenue of $103,570 million, 104 times adjusted EBITDA of $14,995 million and 450 times operating income; on the market capitalisation, 443.2 times trailing diluted EPS of $0.91 (net income $3,218 million on 3,541 million diluted shares) and 483 times trailing free cash flow of $3,303 million [S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S15]. Revenue went from $81,462 million in FY2022 to $96,773 million, $97,690 million and $94,827 million, while operating income fell from $13,656 million to $8,891 million, $7,076 million and $4,355 million, and the operating margin from 16.8% to 2.6% in nine months of 2026. Gross margin held between 17.9% and 19.0% from FY2023, so the compression is operating expense: R&D rose from $3,969 million in FY2023 to $6,411 million in FY2025 and $7,078 million in nine months of 2026. FY2023's $14,997 million net income included a $5,001 million income tax benefit, so the fall to $3,794 million in FY2025 understates the decline in pre-tax earnings.

The balance sheet is not the constraint; the return on the capital being deployed is. At 2026-09-30 Tesla held $45,447 million of cash and short-term investments against $9,267 million of debt, or $36,180 million of net cash, and signed $30 billion of credit commitments in September 2026. Goodwill is 0.2% of assets; the pressure is in inventory of $14,092 million, up 13.7% since 2025-12-31 while deliveries fell 2%, and a warranty reserve of $10,138 million, up 26%. Invested capital of $53,109 million earned 5.5% after tax on a trailing basis (TTM net operating profit after tax over average invested capital for the four quarters to 2026-09-30), against 28.3% in FY2023; the roughly 3% return on 2026 invested capital that includes the full capital programme is a forward-looking figure on a larger asset base, not a competing measurement of the same period [S4].

Against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a beta of 1.5 to 2.0, our estimate of the cost of capital is 11% to 14%, so the company destroys economic value at current margins. Capital allocation offers no offset: no dividend or buyback, capex guided above $20 billion for 2026, and $1.95 billion of stock paid for an AI hardware company in Q2 2026. Equity compensation is the other claim on shareholders: $3,346 million in nine months is 4.3% of revenue; the 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423.7 million shares, 10.7% of the 3,952.6 million outstanding, with $9.74 billion of unrecognised expense on the one milestone judged probable (20 million vehicles, recognised over 8.9 years) and $105.82-120.37 billion on the remaining tranches. The economic reading is that Tesla is converting a vehicle and cell cost advantage into a capital-intensive compute and robotics business before that business has customers, so the shares trade on optionality rather than earnings [S4, S15, S24].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 投资潜力与投资逻辑 Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 9 by Lead Analyst, 8,958 characters)
Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $43.00 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $360.30, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 1,051 authorised robotaxi vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27, 544 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S150]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $43.00 a share on 3,952.6M shares — $170.0B, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets — and autonomy at $259B in the base case: 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance, which is $65.5 a share on the issued count, and the base case is $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $53 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $454 mid-point lifts expected value to $248, still 38% below the price. That arithmetic is why the call is Reduce and not Sell — the option has value, just not $1,424B of it. [S120, S6]

| Base | 50% | Autonomy at $259B, the probability-weighted blend of the four branches (35% × $40B, 40% × $126B, 20% × $600B, 5% × $1,500B); core at $43.00; energy at 3.5x sales | $107 a share, -73% | Q4 2026 update with no robotaxi revenue despite 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles; no fare or cost per mile disclosed | S6, S120, S150 |
| Bear | 25% | Autonomy written down; vehicles at GM's 0.39x sales; Terafab commitment; credit-free margin | $19 a share, -95% | Unsupervised FSD slips past 2027; NHTSA recall of the Cybercab; merger vote fails | S6, S120, S137 |
:::

### Key assumptions, ranked

| Rank | Assumption | Confidence | What would disprove it | Impact if wrong | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031: 15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile is what the reverse DCF needs | low | A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line | -$290 a share against the close | Authorisations flat near 1,051 Texas vehicles; no fare disclosure; safety-driver hours rising | S4, S6, S137, S150 |
| 2 | Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds 18-19% | medium | Q4 2026 ex-credit margin below 15% | Each 100 bp is $756M, 22% of trailing operating income | US incentives of $6,594 a unit; China price cuts | S4, S103 |
| 3 | Energy gross margin stays at or above 30% with revenue growth | medium | Q4 margin below 25% once tariff refunds lapse | -$35 to -$50 a share | Q3 revenue fell 16% to $2.881B | S6, S63 |
| 4 | Capital expenditure at or below $25B in 2027 with no equity issuance | low | Guidance above $25B, or a first draw on the $30B facilities | -$15 to -$30 a share | Terafab's $16.8B first phase sits outside the 2026 budget | S4, S134 |

Assumption 1 sets the price and is the least evidenced: no robotaxi revenue, no fare and no cost per mile are disclosed, so the largest component of value rests on a registry count of authorised vehicles rather than on unit economics. Assumptions 2 and 3 decide whether the core is worth $43.00 or $21.75, and management can still influence both in 2027 — the ex-credit operating margin has been cut to 2.2-2.5%, while energy and services supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M third-quarter gross profit at a margin 2.5 times Fluence's 13.1%. Assumptions 4 and 5 are about survival and dilution rather than growth: $36.18B of net cash covers eighteen months of zero free cash flow, but not that plus a $16.8B capital call whose Tesla share is undisclosed. [S4, S6]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cisco | cautionary | 2000-2024 | Revenue grew from $12.5B to $57B and trailing net income passed its 1999 level by 2003, yet a buyer at the March 2000 peak of $500B waited until 2021 to break even. A correct thesis does not rescue the entry multiple. | S140 |
| Amazon | cautionary | 1999-2001 | The business compounded into one of the great franchises, but the stock fell more than 90% and took a decade to recover; the option paid only for the holder who could sit through the drawdown. | S143 |
| GM Cruise | cautionary | 2016-2024 | More than $10B of operating losses and less than $500M of revenue before GM shut the robotaxi unit in December 2024 for $1B a year of savings. Automaker capital is no substitute for paid driverless miles. | S142 |
| Waymo | best | 2024-2026 | The valuation went from $45B in October 2024 to $126B in February 2026 on 500,000 paid driverless rides a week — proof the service can scale, and a mark that Tesla's autonomy value exceeds 11-fold. | S120 |
:::

The precedents give one rule: when a real technology shift is already in the price, the entry multiple sets the return, not whether the technology wins; the base rate for a follower in autonomy is a write-off, not a slow fade; and the leader's private mark, $126B, is the only independent price for the option — 9% of what the market pays for Tesla's version. A holder should own Tesla's autonomy at a discount to that mark, not at 11.3 times it, and size the position so the Cruise outcome is survivable. [S140, S142]

### Where the case turns, and what to do now

Below $111 the probability-weighted value supports ownership; between $111 and $250 the buyer is paying for the merger option; above $250 the stock is a binary bet on a committee. At $403.30 it sits in the third zone, with the ten-year Treasury at 4.99% raising the discount rate on post-2030 cash flows. Do not invest new money now. Wait for one of three milestones: a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with revenue and cost per mile, a California driverless deployment permit, or special-committee terms at a premium to market rather than at market. If the mandate requires exposure, hold a residual of 0.25-0.5% of net asset value, sized so a failed vote and a 30% drawdown do not breach the risk budget, and vote against any ratio that transfers value to the controlling shareholder. Pass on the blue-sky branch: it needs global robotaxi and humanoid dominance and pays 8% from here. Diligence questions: revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, the share of rides running without a safety driver, and Tesla's share of the Terafab capital call. Confidence is high that the core is not worth $403.30, medium on the autonomy tree, low on the merger. What would change the call: a second consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-credit operating margin, an FSD licensing contract with a named automaker, or a ratio that values Tesla at a premium to its undisturbed price. [S15, S5]"}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 商业模式 Business Model (business_model, revision 9 by Fundamentals Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,538 characters)
Tesla still sells cars for a living, but in 2026 its incremental profit comes from energy storage and services while regulatory credits fade, and the car business alone does not cover its cost base. Nine-month 2026 revenue of $78,669 million split into automotive $57,310 million (including $639 million of credits), energy $8,428 million and services $12,931 million. Q3 2026 gross profit divided $3,806 million automotive (69%), $954 million energy (17%) and $734 million services (13%). Cash arrives on delivery, on storage milestones and customer prepayments ($3.30 billion of deferred revenue at 2026-09-30, from $2.04 billion), and monthly for Supercharging, insurance and FSD [S3, S4, S6].

| Segment | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M 2026 | Q3 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue excluding credits ($M) | 80,629 | 74,307 | 67,533 | 56,671 | 20,447 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Automotive regulatory credits ($M) | 1,790 | 2,763 | 1,993 | 639 | 113 | S1, S3, S4 |
| Energy generation and storage revenue ($M) | 6,035 | 10,086 | 12,771 | 8,428 | 2,881 | S3, S4 |
| Services and other revenue ($M) | 8,319 | 10,534 | 12,530 | 12,931 | 4,605 | S3, S4 |
| Automotive gross margin excluding credits | 17.7% | 15.4% | 15.4% | 17.7% | 18.1% | S1, S3, S4, S63 |
| Energy gross margin | 18.9% | 26.2% | 29.8% | 30.2% | 33.1% | S3, S4 |

The credit franchise is ending. Tesla booked $2,763 million of automotive regulatory credits in FY2024, $1,993 million in FY2025 and $639 million in 9M 2026; Q3 2026 alone was $113 million, down 73% from $417 million. Credits carry no cost of revenue, so a credit dollar is nearly a dollar of operating profit: 20.1% of operating income in FY2023, 39.0% in FY2024, 45.8% in FY2025, 31.1% in 9M 2026 and 15.7% in Q3 2026. An implied Q4 2025 figure of $542 million shows the collapse came with the 2026 removal of the compliance obligation, not the lapse of the consumer credit: the Department of Transportation finalised its CAFE rollback on 2026-10-01, ending the requirement that made legacy automakers buy zero-emission credits. Without credits, FY2025's 4.6% operating margin is 2.5% and Q3 2026's 2.6% is 2.2% [S4, S64, S66].

Per vehicle the business improved even as credits disappeared. Q3 2026 automotive revenue per delivery excluding credits was $42,026, up 0.5%, while automotive cost of revenue per delivery (total automotive cost of revenue divided by deliveries) fell 2.7% to $34,436, so gross profit per vehicle rose 18.0% to $7,591 (18.1% margin) from $6,433 (15.4%). The gain is cost and mix, not price: management attributes the 270 basis points to a higher Asia-Pacific mix from the low-cost Shanghai plant. Tesla does not disclose customer acquisition cost; SG&A per delivery of $4,142 includes corporate cost and the first vehicle's gross profit covers it 1.8 times. A three-year LTV of $8,455 — three years of services gross profit at $288 a vehicle on 10.2 million deliveries — gives LTV:CAC of 2.0:1 and payback inside the delivery quarter. BYD's automotive gross margin was 20.49% in FY2025, from 22.31%, and Rivian's automotive gross profit was a $(36) million loss in Q2 2026 [S63, S65, S68].

| Per unit | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 | Change | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deliveries (units) | 497,099 | 486,532 | -2.1% | S6 |
| Automotive revenue per delivery, excluding credits | $41,818 | $42,026 | +0.5% | S4, S6 |
| Automotive cost of revenue per delivery | $35,385 | $34,436 | -2.7% | S4, S6 |
| Automotive gross profit per delivery, excluding credits | $6,433 | $7,591 | +18.0% | S4, S6 |
| Energy gross profit per delivery | $2,158 | $1,961 | -9.1% | S4, S6 |
| Services gross profit per delivery | $736 | $1,508 | +105% | S4, S6 |
| SG&A per delivery (acquisition-cost upper bound) | $3,142 | $4,142 | +31.8% | S4, S6 |
| R&D per delivery | $3,279 | $5,675 | +73.1% | S4, S6 |
| Operating profit per delivery | $3,267 | $1,476 | -54.8% | S4, S6 |

| Product | Pricing metric | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 | Peer benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles, net of credits | realised revenue per delivery | $41,818 | $42,026 | BYD automotive gross margin 20.49%, FY2025 | S4, S65 |
| Megapack and Powerwall | realised revenue per GWh deployed | $273 million | $210 million | Fluence gross margin 13.1%, FY2025 | S3, S67 |

Energy is the highest-margin dollar of growth. Storage revenue per GWh fell 23% to $210 million from $273 million on 13.7 GWh deployed, up from 12.5 GWh, but gross profit per GWh fell only 19% to $69.6 million because cost per GWh fell 25% to $141 million, lifting segment margin to 33.1% from 31.4%. The mechanism is cell integration: the first Megapacks built with Tesla's own Nevada LFP cells shipped in Q3 2026 and Megafactory Texas began production with planned capacity of 50 GWh. On the backlog, management said on the 2026-10-21 earnings call that Tesla is "almost sold out of all Megapacks for 2027", and the same day's release cites a "highest-ever order rate and backlog" — company claims only, unverified, with no volume, contract value or price disclosed, so the energy annuity has to be sized on reported deployments, not on the backlog. Fluence earned 13.1%; Tesla's edge is owning the cell, not pricing. Part of the 33.1% is not repeatable: management attributed it partly to tariff refunds and cell-related warranty reimbursements. Services is the quieter engine: revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million on 2% fewer deliveries and gross margin reached 15.9% from 10.5%. FSD and software grow but remain too small to see in the income statement: active subscriptions rose to 1.74 million from 1.04 million — a company operating KPI defined for the 2025 CEO Performance Award, not an audited or GAAP-reported metric — while deferred revenue for FSD, connectivity and software was $4.08 billion against $3.87 billion at 2025-12-31. Management's claim that FSD is attached to more than 75% of North American deliveries is company-reported and cannot be tied to a revenue line, because Tesla does not disclose FSD revenue [S6, S63, S67, S158].

The newest change in money flows is who owns the asset: a robotaxi fleet keeps the vehicle on Tesla's balance sheet and earns per mile rather than per delivery. The Cybercab entered Tesla's own Austin fleet on 2026-09-03, but no fare revenue, fleet size or per-mile economics are disclosed, so the model cannot yet be tested; until then the investable model remains cars, storage and services.

Counter-case: gross margin improves while the company gets less profitable. Operating expenses of $4,776 million rose 39% against $5,494 million of gross profit, R&D alone rose 69% to $2,761 million, and depreciation rose 17% to $1,580 million and will accelerate as more than $20 billion of 2026 capital expenditure is commissioned. The warranty reserve rose 26% to $10,138 million on 2% fewer deliveries, with claims incurred up 29% to $1,614 million while the provision per delivery fell to $1,227 from $1,463. Inventory rose 13.7% to $14,092 million, with 11 days of supply. The vehicle line covers its own costs, so break-even is the cost base: $4,776 million of operating expenses needs $27.0 billion of revenue at a 17.7% blended margin; Q3 2026 delivered $28.0 billion for $718 million of operating profit. Normalise energy to a 30% margin and take credits to zero and the quarter earns $515 million, a 1.8% operating margin. For a position, that argues for sizing the energy and services annuity on reported deployments and contracted revenue, not on the undisclosed 2027 backlog, and treating autonomy as an option rather than earnings, because at a 1.8% margin the vehicle franchise cannot carry the cost base alone. Confidence is high on the segment arithmetic, medium on how much of the cost relief is structural. Four diligence questions remain: what is the North American automotive margin excluding credits? What is the energy margin excluding tariff refunds, and what volumes and prices underpin the claimed 2027 Megapack sell-out? Will Tesla disclose FSD revenue and robotaxi recognition? When do R&D and capital expenditure stop rising as a share of revenue? [S4, S6]

::: evidence
**Tesla's profit now rests on energy and services gross profit, not on credits or on the car**

Energy storage and services supplied $1,688 million of Q3 2026 gross profit at 33.1% and 15.9% margins, while regulatory credits fell to $113 million, 15.7% of operating income, from 45.8% of FY2025 operating income, and operating expenses absorbed 86.9% of gross profit [S4, S6].
:::"}],"isError":false}

Tesla's earnings do not justify its premium, and the cash behind them is thinning. At $403.30 on 2026-10-29 the equity is worth $1,594.1 billion on 3,952.6 million shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, or $1,558.0 billion of enterprise value after $36.2 billion of net cash: on the enterprise value, 15.0 times trailing revenue of $103,570 million, 104 times adjusted EBITDA of $14,995 million and 450 times operating income; on the market capitalisation, 443.2 times trailing diluted EPS of $0.91 (net income $3,218 million on 3,541 million diluted shares) and 483 times trailing free cash flow of $3,303 million [S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S15]. Revenue went from $81,462 million in FY2022 to $96,773 million, $97,690 million and $94,827 million, while operating income fell from $13,656 million to $8,891 million, $7,076 million and $4,355 million, and the operating margin from 16.8% to 2.6% in nine months of 2026. Gross margin held between 17.9% and 19.0% from FY2023, so the compression is operating expense: R&D rose from $3,969 million in FY2023 to $6,411 million in FY2025 and $7,078 million in nine months of 2026. FY2023's $14,997 million net income included a $5,001 million income tax benefit, so the fall to $3,794 million in FY2025 understates the decline in pre-tax earnings.

Revenue of $28,046 million was flat in Q3 2026, gross profit rose 8.7% to $5,494 million, and operating expenses of $4,776 million rose 39%, leaving operating income of $718 million, down 56%, and net income of $787 million, down 43%, or $0.22 diluted against $0.39. Non-GAAP net income was $1,697 million, or $0.48 against $0.50; the $910 million gap is chiefly $1,165 million of stock-based compensation, partly offset by the excluded $288 million Bitcoin gain and $142 million SpaceX write-down. Pretax income exceeded operating income by $238 million, 30% of net income, and the effective tax rate fell to 16% from 29% partly on a state deferred-tax release. Automotive cost of revenue per vehicle delivered was $34,436, down 2.7% on 486,532 deliveries [S4, S6].

Cash generation now depends on working capital: supplier balances and customer prepayments are growing faster than earnings. Operating cash flow rose 36% to $14,897 million while net income fell 19.5% to $2,378 million; payables and accrued liabilities contributed $7,332 million against $2,979 million a year earlier, accounts payable rose to $17,239 million from $13,371 million at 2025-12-31, and days payables outstanding went from 62.8 to 75.3. Deferred revenue added $1,746 million, mostly storage prepayments that rose to $3.30 billion. Capital expenditure of $13,014 million consumed 87% of operating cash flow, and quarterly free cash flow was $1,444 million, negative $1,092 million and $1,531 million, against $3,990 million in Q3 2025. Depreciation of $4,290 million rose 17% and will climb faster than revenue as more than $20 billion of 2026 spending is commissioned [S3, S4, S6].

The balance sheet is not the constraint; the return on the capital being deployed is. At 2026-09-30 Tesla held $45,447 million of cash and short-term investments against $9,267 million of debt, or $36,180 million of net cash, and signed $30 billion of credit commitments in September 2026. Goodwill is 0.2% of assets; the pressure is in inventory of $14,092 million, up 13.7% since 2025-12-31 while deliveries fell 2%, and a warranty reserve of $10,138 million, up 26%. Invested capital of $53,109 million earned 5.5% after tax on a trailing basis (TTM net operating profit after tax over average invested capital for the four quarters to 2026-09-30), against 28.3% in FY2023; the roughly 3% return on 2026 invested capital that includes the full capital programme is a forward-looking figure on a larger asset base, not a competing measurement of the same period [S4].

Against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a beta of 1.5 to 2.0, our estimate of the cost of capital is 11% to 14%, so the company destroys economic value at current margins. Capital allocation offers no offset: no dividend or buyback, capex guided above $20 billion for 2026, and $1.95 billion of stock paid for an AI hardware company in Q2 2026. Equity compensation is the other claim on shareholders: $3,346 million in nine months is 4.3% of revenue; the 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423.7 million shares, 10.7% of the 3,952.6 million outstanding, with $9.74 billion of unrecognised expense on the one milestone judged probable (20 million vehicles, recognised over 8.9 years) and $105.82-120.37 billion on the remaining tranches. The economic reading is that Tesla is converting a vehicle and cell cost advantage into a capital-intensive compute and robotics business before that business has customers, so the shares trade on optionality rather than earnings [S4, S15, S24].

Tesla trades at 443.2 times trailing diluted EPS of $0.91, 24 times the peer median of 18.5 times earnings, and at 15.0 times sales, 6.3 times the median 2.4 times sales; market capitalisation over the same $3,218 million of net income is 495 times. Adjusted EBITDA is struck before stock-based compensation, so 104 times is understated as a cash multiple. Each 100 basis points of automotive gross margin excluding credits is worth $756 million, or $0.19 a share, on $75,561 million of nine-month automotive revenue, so a two-point margin miss plus a $4 billion capex overshoot would take 2027 free cash flow to roughly negative $2 billion, while energy growth of 40% at a 30% margin and a 20% automotive margin would lift it to about $8 billion. The contrast shows the strategic problem: the market is paying for autonomy and robotics because the vehicle and storage businesses cannot support the multiple on these returns, so position size should be set by tolerance for a de-rating from 104 times EBITDA, not by near-term cash generation. Confidence is high on the statements and the cash bridge, medium on the cost of capital and low on any estimate that requires autonomous revenue to be sized. Three diligence questions remain: how much of the payables increase reverses in Q4 2026? What is the split of the 2026 capital budget between maintenance and AI compute? Does the board intend to offset dilution from the performance award? [S15, S17, S19, S21, S111, S113, S121]

At $403.30 (NasdaqGS, 2026-10-29 20:00 UTC) Tesla's equity is worth $1,594.1B and its enterprise value $1,558.0B. On a sum of the parts, 89% of that price — $1,424B, or $360.30 a share — buys autonomy and robotics, while the automotive, energy and services businesses plus $36.2B of net cash are worth $43.00 a share at peer multiples. That residual is 11.3 times the $126B at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026, and Waymo is the only operator running a scaled driverless service. My probability-weighted value is $111 a share, 72.5% below the close; the disagreement is not about cars, since my $43.00 for the core sits within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47, but about whether 2.0M cumulative unsupervised miles, a robotaxi service confined to one city and zero disclosed Optimus revenue can carry $1.4 trillion. [S15, S120, S6]

Tesla is two assets inside one ticker: a business worth $43.00 a share on a sum of the parts — vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at peer multiples — and an option worth $360.30, or 89% of the $403.30 close, on a robotaxi and humanoid franchise that discloses no revenue. Three tests separate cleanly. The need is real: grid storage is Tesla's fastest-growing equipment market and energy earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026. The capability is partly defensible: 2.5M vehicles of installed capacity, dry-electrode 4680 cells in production on both electrodes since January 2026, and a $34,436 cost per vehicle. The economics do not scale on any evidence available at 2026-10-29: 1,051 authorised robotaxi vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27, 544 of them Cybercabs, paid driverless rides confined to Austin since 2026-09-03, no disclosed fare, and a reverse DCF that needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow. The outcome at this price is unattractive unless an event rather than operating delivery reprices the option. [S6, S15, S150]

The sell side is almost at the price: the 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target, 1.3% above the close, and the published range runs from $128.11 to $600 — a 4.7x spread that makes consensus an average of incompatible models. We put the core at $43.00 a share on 3,952.6M shares — $170.0B, within $5 of Morgan Stanley's $47 for the same assets — and autonomy at $259B in the base case: 35% × $40B regional, 40% × $126B licensing, 20% × $600B multi-metro, 5% × $1,500B dominance, which is $65.5 a share on the issued count, and the base case is $107. That $259B is 2.1 times the $126B post-money at which Waymo raised $16B in February 2026. [S141, S144, S120]

### Every branch but one sits below the price

The tree puts 25% on a bull case that still loses 47%, because the price sits above it. In the bull case ($212) robotaxi reaches several metros at 1.0x Waymo and energy trades at 6.0x sales, a 12.1% annual loss to 2031. In the base case ($107) the core is valued at peer multiples and autonomy at that $259B blend, a 73% loss; regional-only autonomy, the 35% branch, is $10.1 a share, so a base built on it would be $53 and would average $84 with the same bull and bear outcomes — a $27 difference that does not change the call. In the bear case ($19) autonomy is written down, vehicles trade at GM's implied 0.39x sales and the undisclosed Terafab commitment takes cash, a 95% loss. The weights sum to 100%; the probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close. The merger sits outside the tree: adding it as a separate binary at 40% probability and a $454 mid-point lifts expected value to $248, still 38% below the price.
