The weighting is deliberate. A heavy weight on valuation is right because at the current multiple the entry price, not the technology, dominates a five-year return. The governance weight reflects what a standard framework misses: the controlling shareholder's compensation is tied to market-capitalisation milestones, so management is paid for the narrative that supports the multiple rather than for per-share cash flow, and a change of control accelerates the award. Business quality scores 6 rather than 8 because the strongest part of the franchise, energy storage, is a small and shrinking share of revenue in dollars, while vehicles are losing share in the region that sets global prices.

The counter-evidence deserves its own paragraph: energy earns a 33.1% gross margin at $210M of revenue per GWh, Tesla's $34,436 cost per vehicle is below every Western competitor, and a triple-digit multiple has persisted for two years without mean reversion. If energy revenue doubles and FSD licensing adds a second stream, the core could be worth $70 a share rather than $43.00. That moves the composite by less than half a point, because the core is 11% of the price and the autonomy premium is 11.3 times the leader's mark. The risks run both ways: if the bear branch materialises — autonomy written down, vehicles valued at GM's multiple, the Terafab commitment drawn — value collapses to a small fraction of today's price and Reduce becomes Sell or Avoid at any size. The base case carries $259B of autonomy on a probability-weighted blend of four branches, not the $40B regional fleet alone: at regional-only autonomy the base would be $53 and the probability-weighted value $84, and the recommendation would not change. The only branch that lifts the score above 5 is the merger: a negotiated ratio at a premium to the undisturbed price would justify Hold, with the position capped because a failed vote returns the stock to a level set by the operating business. Tesla offers no cash exit at $1.59 trillion. It has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation, and its entire $45.4B of cash and short-term investments would retire 2.85% of the 3.953B shares outstanding. What remains is a sale into a market that trades $14.0B of Tesla a day, or a share exchange into SpaceX, and both leave the return hostage to a re-rating that five years have not delivered. [S3, S130]

### The company returns nothing, and cannot return much

Tesla's 10-K states that it has never declared or paid a cash dividend, does not anticipate doing so, and purchased no equity securities in fiscal 2025. Trailing free cash flow of $3,303M is a 0.2% yield on the capitalisation, and nine-month capital expenditure of $13,014M runs at 2.1x depreciation: the cash is going into factories, cells and training compute, not to holders. Against GM's 12.4% total shareholder yield and Ford's 5.9%, Tesla's is zero. Even a maximal buyback using the whole cash pile would move the share count by less than three points, and it would leave a company spending $17B a year on capital projects with no liquidity buffer. Capital return is a governance choice, and the controlling shareholder has consistently chosen reinvestment. [S6]

### The exit that always works is the tape

The secondary market is the only channel that is always open. Tesla trades 36.96M shares and $14.0B a day over twenty days, so a $500M position is 3.6% of a single day's value and no holder is trapped by liquidity. Short interest of 69.35M shares, 2.19% of the float and 2.2 days to cover, means the marginal seller is not fighting a crowded short either. A cash takeover is arithmetically out of reach. The pieces themselves are worth $170B on the sum of the parts — vehicles at 1.0x sales, energy at 3.5x, net cash at book — and a control buyer for those assets alone would pay $200-250B with a premium, which is one-eighth of the current capitalisation and therefore not a route to today's price. 2. **Cash and balance sheet** — $20B+ of 2026 capex and $30B of September facilities against deteriorating free cash flow; a dilution event is plausible before autonomy revenue.

sources.title: Tesorb: Tesla 4680 Battery — Production and Reality
sources.claims: 4680 is Tesla's cheapest cell per kWh since end-2024; both electrodes dry-process in production confirmed on Q4 2025 call (2026-01-28) by VP Bonne Eggleston; Giga Texas >1 million cells/week, ~40 GWh installed capacity; Cybercell 272 Wh/kg vs 244 Wh/kg Gen 1; yields >90% vs >98% at CATL/Panasonic; energy density 10-15% below competitors; 10-80% charge in 35-40 minutes; lithium refinery in Robstown, Texas operational January 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that 4680 is a performance leader; claims that Tesla cell cost leadership translates into vehicle cost leadership at the pack level.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Tesla starts Optimus robot production in California as profit falls 43% (2026-10-21)
sources.claims: Tesla began Optimus production at Fremont (Q3 2026 shareholder letter, 2026-10-21); Musk called it early production, ramp 'bumpy', claimed 20,000 units/week by end-2027; unsupervised FSD for customer cars pushed to ~Q2 2027 (Elluswamy) vs Musk's April 2026 Q4 2026 target; Q3 2026 revenue $28.04bn, net income $787m (-43%), 486,532 deliveries, energy revenue -16% YoY, services gross profit $734m.
sources.claims_weakened: Optimus as a commercial product in 2026; the credibility of Tesla autonomy timelines.

sources.title: Tesla North: FSD (Supervised) safety report — 6,006,200 miles per major collision (2026-10-27)
sources.claims: Tesla's FSD (Supervised) Vehicle Safety Report (October 2026) states one major collision per 6,006,200 miles in North America with FSD engaged, versus a US average of 660,164 miles — about 9x; prior February 2026 report was ~5.3 million miles.
sources.claims_weakened: Independent verification of FSD safety: the comparison is company-computed, non-fault-based and excludes reporting-bias controls.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Waymo is scaling fast — here's what the fleet data shows (2026-09-24)
sources.claims: Waymo operates ~4,000 robotaxis in 15 US cities, averages 500,000 paid rides/week; 1,102 Waymo AVs registered in Texas as of 2026-09-24; ~80% of fleet in California and Texas; Ojai (Zeekr RT) minivans ~one third of Texas fleet; MoffettNathanson expects 5,100 Ojai imports in 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Any claim that Tesla's robotaxi network is scale-comparable to Waymo in 2026.

sources.title: Tesla Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (Motley Fool)
sources.claims: Automotive gross margin 18.1% excluding regulatory credits (from 16.3% in Q2 2026) on higher Asia-Pacific delivery mix; energy storage gross margin 33.1% helped by tariff refunds and cell-related warranty cost reimbursements; FSD attach rate above 75% of North American new deliveries, +20pp sequentially; Megapack backlog nearly sold out through 2027; capex about $20B for 2026; $30B of new financing facilities; $288M Bitcoin mark-to-market gain and $142M SpaceX equity mark-down in the quarter; regulatory credit revenue $113M vs $417M.
sources.claims_weakened: Suggests part of the Q3 2026 energy margin and automotive margin improvement is one-off (tariff refunds, warranty reimbursements, regional mix) rather than a durable cost step-down; the auto margin figure is management's non-GAAP presentation.

sources.title: Sidley: DOT finalizes rollback of CAFE standards for passenger cars and light trucks (2026-10-01)
sources.claims: The US Department of Transportation finalized a rollback of CAFE standards in late September/October 2026, removing a main compliance driver that had forced legacy automakers to buy zero-emission credits from Tesla and others.
sources.claims_weakened: Undermines any assumption that automotive regulatory credit revenue recovers toward its 2024 peak of $2.76B; supports treating credit revenue as a declining, policy-contingent line.

sources.title: ChinaBizInsider: BYD 2025 profit drops as revenue tops RMB 804 billion
sources.claims: BYD FY2025 gross margin 17.74% (from 19.44% in 2024), automotive business gross margin 20.49% (from 22.31%), net margin 4.1%, net earnings down 18.97% on revenue above RMB 804B.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows Tesla's ex-credit automotive margin (18.1% in Q3 2026) is now close to BYD's auto margin and that China price competition compressed even the lowest-cost producer's margin.

sources.title: Carbon Credits: Tesla Q3 2026 carbon credit revenue falls 73%, profits sink 43%
sources.claims: Tesla's credit revenue peaked at $2.76B in 2024 and fell 28% to about $2.0B in 2025; the quarterly decline continued into 2026 with Q3 2026 credit revenue down 73% year over year.
sources.claims_weakened: Confirms the credit line is in structural decline rather than a one-quarter dip; media framing of a 'profit collapse' may overstate the operating effect given cost cuts and mix.

sources.title: Fluence Energy FY2025 financial results
sources.claims: Fluence FY2025 (ended 2025-09-30) revenue $2.26B and GAAP gross margin about 13.1% (13.7% in Q4), versus 12.6% in FY2024.
sources.claims_weakened: Tesla's 30-33% energy storage gross margin is roughly two and a half times the pure-play systems integrator benchmark, which points to vertical integration into LFP cells rather than pricing power alone.

sources.title: Rivian second quarter 2026 financial results
sources.claims: Rivian Q2 2026 revenue $1.658B (+27%), total gross profit $179M (about 11% margin), automotive gross loss $(36)M against $(335)M a year earlier, with the improvement attributed to volume, higher regulatory credit revenue and an IEEPA tariff refund receivable.
sources.claims_weakened: A pure-EV peer of Tesla's size still loses money at the automotive gross-profit line after credits, so Tesla's positive per-vehicle gross profit is a genuine cost advantage, though both are flattered by tariff refunds in 2026.

sources.title: General Motors Q4 and FY2025 earnings press release (SEC exhibit)
sources.claims: GM FY2025 net income attributable to stockholders $2.7B and EBIT-adjusted $12.7B; Q4 2025 net loss $3.3B with EBIT-adjusted $2.8B; 2026 North America EBIT-adjusted margin guided back to 8-10%.
sources.claims_weakened: Legacy OEM margins in 2025-2026 were hit by charges and tariff costs, so Tesla's 18% gross margin still exceeds GM's implied EBIT margin, though GM returns capital through dividends and a $6B buyback while Tesla returns none.

sources.title: Ford Q4 2025 earnings press release with 2026 guidance
sources.claims: Ford guides full-year 2026 company adjusted EBIT of $8.0-10.0 billion, adjusted free cash flow of $5.0-6.0 billion and capital expenditures of $9.5-10.5 billion, including about $1.5 billion to ramp Ford Energy.
sources.claims_weakened: Tesla's 2026 capital expenditure above $20 billion is roughly double Ford's for a fraction of the unit volume, which is the core of the free-cash-flow dilution case.

sources.title: pv magazine USA: Tesla and Fluence rank in top ten global battery integrators (2026-07-14)
sources.claims: Wood Mackenzie's first global BESS integrator ranking (published 2026-07) places Sungrow first, Tesla second, CATL third, BYD fourth, Fluence seventh; global utility-scale battery installations topped 100 GW in 2025; buyers weight bankability and execution over hardware price.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that Megapack is the global storage leader by volume; Tesla's energy moat rests on integration and software rather than scale.

sources.title: California DMV Autonomous Vehicle Permit Holders (updated 2026-10-22)
sources.claims: As of 2026-10-21, California DMV lists TESLA ROBOTAXI LLC among holders of an Autonomous Vehicle Testing Permit (with a driver) only; Tesla does not appear on the driverless-testing list (updated 2026-10-22) or the deployment list (Waymo, Nuro, Mercedes-Benz).
sources.claims_weakened: Any claim that Tesla operates paid driverless service in California; Tesla's robotaxi revenue is Texas-only in 2026.

sources.title: TeslaNorth: Tesla scales Austin Cybercab fleet to 300+ (2026-10-10)
sources.claims: Tesla's Robotaxi account claimed 300+ Cybercabs serving Austin on 2026-10-10, an 8x increase in 30 days; Texas registration records showed authorized Cybercab VINs rising from 169 to 319; paid Cybercab rides began early September 2026; Model Y robotaxis operate in Dallas; company has not disclosed how many are unsupervised or how many carry safety monitors.
sources.claims_weakened: Company claims of robotaxi scale: registry vehicles, serving vehicles and unsupervised vehicles are different counts.

sources.title: Basenor: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 hand patents revealed — 25 actuators, 22 DoF (2026-04-20)
sources.claims: Tesla published four international patents on 2026-04-16 (priority date 2024-10-10) covering Optimus Gen 3 forearm, wrist, joint and hand: 22 degrees of freedom per hand vs 11 in Gen 2, 25 linear actuators in the forearm, tendon-driven fingers, lead inventor Konstantinos Laskaris; projected cost of goods ~$20,000 per unit at scale; Musk said in April 2026 that V3 would not use this hand design because 'the original design ultimately didn't work'. Also US application US20260310299A1 on flexible touch sensors for robotic hands published 2025-10-08.
sources.claims_weakened: Treating published patents as evidence of the shipped Optimus design; patents lag the programme by design cycles.

sources.title: CnEVPost: Tesla beats Q3 delivery expectations but falls further behind BYD in BEV sales (2026-10-02)
sources.claims: Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3 2026 (-2.13% YoY; 1,324,681 in 9M 2026, +8.77%); BYD sold 762,478 passenger BEVs in Q3 2026 (+30.89%), a lead of 275,946 units (56.72%); BYD 9M 2026 passenger BEVs 1,629,957; BYD outsold Tesla for the full year 2025 (2,256,714 vs 1,636,129); Model 3/Y were 98.30% of Q3 2026 deliveries; Tesla energy storage deployed 13.7 GWh in Q3 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that Tesla retains BEV volume leadership; claims of a widening technology-driven volume advantage.

sources.title: Tesla Newswire: FSD China approval, Q3 2026 China sales -16%, Shanghai exports record
sources.claims: Tesla's China sales fell 16% YoY in Q3 2026 to 142,133 units while Giga Shanghai exports reached a record 132,978; CFO Vaibhav Taneja said on the 2026-10-21 call that Tesla is working 'very diligently' with Chinese regulators on broader FSD approval.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that China remains a growth market for Tesla; the FSD revenue model depends on approvals outside North America.

sources.title: Electrek: Tesla proxy shows a board getting ready for a SpaceX merger (2026-10-19)
sources.claims: Tesla's 2026 proxy (filed 2026-10-19) shows three of nine directors with SpaceX ties (Ira Ehrenpreis joined SpaceX's board in February 2026; Kimbal Musk), a retail auto-voting programme, and a 2025 CEO pay figure of $158.36bn of which only 1 of 12 operational milestones is rated probable (20 million cumulative deliveries), leaving $105.8-120.4bn of unrecognised stock compensation; Musk exercised all 303,960,630 2018 options on 2026-06-16 at ~$405/share (~$116bn); Tesla's $2bn xAI investment converted to SpaceX Class A shares after SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026; FY2025 net income fell 46% to $3.86bn on revenue of $94.8bn; annual meeting set for 2026-12-03.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that Tesla's capital allocation is independent of Musk's other companies; claims that the CEO award aligns pay with robotaxi/Optimus delivery rather than with a deal price.

sources.title: DatacenterDynamics: Samsung signs $16.5bn deal to manufacture Tesla AI6 chips at Taylor, Texas (2025-07-28)
sources.claims: Samsung Electronics signed an eight-year, $16.5bn contract (announced 2025-07-28) to manufacture Tesla's AI6 chip at its Taylor, Texas fab, running through 2033; AI5 completed process-adaptation tape-out on Samsung's 2nm line in Taylor in early July 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that Tesla owns its AI silicon end to end; fab dependence on a single foundry is a supply risk.

sources.title: CNBC: Tesla faces intensifying NHTSA probe of FSD in reduced visibility (2026-03-19)
sources.claims: NHTSA opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 into Tesla's FSD Beta and FSD (Supervised) degradation-detection system in reduced roadway visibility (reported 2026-03-19); the probe covers about 2.88 million vehicles and followed 13 crashes in low-visibility conditions.
sources.claims_weakened: Any claim that FSD (Supervised) is validated outside clear-weather operation; raises the regulatory risk of the vision-only approach.

sources.title: CnEVPost: Global ESS battery market share in H1 2026 — CATL 27.1% (2026-08-04)
sources.claims: Global ESS battery shipments rose 71% YoY to 461.3 GWh in H1 2026; CATL shipped 125.0 GWh of ESS batteries (27.1% share), up 81% YoY; China's share of shipments fell to 43.9% from 50.5%.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that Tesla's Megapack cell costs can undercut Chinese cell supply without tariffs; Chinese cell scale keeps falling in cost.

sources.title: TeslaNorth: NHTSA opens school-zone review of Tesla robotaxis, DP26010 (2026-10-12)
sources.claims: NHTSA opened defect petition review DP26010 on 2026-10-09 into claims that Tesla robotaxis exceed posted limits in active school zones; the agency puts the affected fleet at about 1,000 vehicles.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that the robotaxi fleet is small enough to be immaterial to safety regulators; the monitored fleet is around 1,000 vehicles, larger than the 300+ Austin Cybercab figure the company promotes.

sources.title: Zacks: TSLA Q3 2026 earnings call highlights autonomy and expansion plans
sources.claims: Tesla's Q3 2026 earnings call (2026-10-21) centred on FSD adoption, robotaxi expansion, Optimus commercialisation and a roughly $20bn capital spending plan for 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that Tesla is still guiding to more than $25bn of 2026 capex.

sources.title: Newzino: Tesla's 2026 Executive Exodus — Who's Left? (updated 2026-10-20)
sources.claims: Timeline of 17 senior Tesla departures April 2024-October 2026: Drew Baglino and Rohan Patel (April 2024), Rebecca Tinucci (April 2024, with ~500 Supercharger staff), Omead Afshar (fired 2025-06-26), Troy Jones (dismissed July 2025), Raj Jegannathan (Feb 2026), Sendil Palani VP Finance after 17 years (2026-03-10), Thomas Dmytryk robotaxi infrastructure (2026-03-09), Victor Nechita Cybercab program manager (Feb 2026), Michael So Cybercab NPI (April 2026), Mark Lupkey and Jose del Corral (2026-03-30), Jody Kerns to Rivian and Mike Snyder VP Energy & Charging (both 2026-10-15, Snyder succeeded by AJ Booth). sources.title: Not a Tesla App: profile of Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla VP of AI

Electronics and Communication Engineering, College of Engineering, Guindy (Anna University, Chennai); M.S., Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute; prior employers WABCO Vehicle Control Systems and Volkswagen Electronics Research Lab; led the Tesla Vision radar removal and the FSD V12 end-to-end architecture; now leads FSD, Robotaxi software and Optimus.
sources.claims_weakened: Company filings do not disclose his education or patent record; details rest on media profile rather than primary record.

sources.title: Motley Fool: Who Owns Ford? Largest Shareholders (Class B 2% of shares, 40% of votes)
sources.claims: Ford's Class B shares carry 16 votes each and give the Ford family about 40% of total voting power while representing roughly 2% of shares outstanding, fixed by the charter; benchmark for a family-controlled US automaker against Tesla's single-class, one-share-one-vote structure.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows that Tesla's governance defect is control by a CEO award rather than a dual-class charter; a comparison source aggregating Ford's proxy, not Ford's filing itself.

sources.title: ICCT: Global electric vehicle market monitor for light-duty vehicles in key markets, H1 2026
sources.claims: Over 9.4 million electric light-duty vehicles were sold globally in H1 2026, almost one quarter of all light-duty vehicles sold; country-level detail (Philippines H1 2026: 30,715 light-duty EVs, 15% of new LDVs, BEV 8%, PHEV 7%, HEV 8%; BYD 68% of Philippine EV sales, Tesla 11%, VinFast 9%).
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens a US/China-centric view of demand: growth is migrating to emerging markets where Chinese brands hold the majority share (BYD 68% in the Philippines), so Tesla's addressable volume is thinner than global totals imply.

sources.title: EIA Today in Energy: Hybrid sales rise while battery electric sales remain lower after tax credit expiration (2026-10-19)
sources.claims: US BEV share of new light-duty vehicle sales 6% in Q3 2026 vs 10% in Q3 2025; 6% in first nine months of 2026 vs 8% a year earlier; BEV share of luxury light-duty sales 12% in Q3 2026 vs 31% in Q3 2025; hybrid share 16% in Q3 2026, plug-in hybrid 0.7% vs 1.8%; 23% of US light-duty sales electrified in Q3 2026 vs 24% in Q3 2025; record 12% BEV share in September 2025 before the credits expired; US new-vehicle average transaction price passed $50,000 (Kelley Blue Book). Data source Omdia.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that US BEV demand is durable without subsidies: the BEV share halved within four quarters of the 2025-09-30 credit expiry, and the luxury segment (Tesla's core US positioning) fell from 31% to 12%. Also weakens the idea that hybrids ceded share to BEVs.

sources.title: ACEA: New car registrations +5.3% in August 2026 year-to-date; battery-electric 21.7% market share
sources.claims: EU battery-electric registrations 1,641,333 in January-August 2026, 21.7% of new EU car registrations vs 15.8% a year earlier; hybrid-electric 36.6% share (2,759,718 units); plug-in hybrid 10% (758,082 units); petrol share 21.7% from 28%, diesel 7.3% from 9.4%; BEV growth led by France +74.2%, Germany +53.1%, Denmark +40.9%; total EU registrations +5.3% year to date.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any claim that European BEV demand depends on purchase subsidies: EU BEV share rose 5.9 points year on year to 21.7% in 2026 as several national subsidy schemes narrowed, pointing to CO2-mandate and price-driven demand. Also shows hybrids, not BEVs, remain the largest electrified category in the EU.

sources.title: IEA press release: Close to 30% of cars sold this year are set to be electric (Global EV Outlook 2026)
sources.claims: Global electric car sales expected to reach 23 million in 2026, close to 30% of all cars sold worldwide; 2025 sales grew 20% to more than 20 million (a quarter of new cars); Q1 2026 global sales fell 8% year on year after policy changes in China and the United States, while Europe rose close to 30%, Asia-Pacific excluding China 80% and Latin America 75%; Chinese automakers supplied 60% of electric cars sold worldwide in 2025 and China made about three-quarters of the ~22 million electric cars produced; China accounts for over 80% of battery cell production; global EV fleet projected up to 510 million by 2035 from nearly 80 million today.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens both the 'EV growth has stalled' and the 'EV growth is unstoppable' narratives: the 2026 total still grows while the two largest markets shrink, so the growth is regionally re-weighted rather than broad. Forecasts are model-based estimates for 2026, not outturn data.

sources.title: CNBC: EVs dominate China's car market - five takeaways from the latest auto sales data (CPCA, 2026-08-12)
sources.claims: China Passenger Car Association data as reported 2026-08-12: new energy vehicles were 65.1% of new passenger cars sold in July 2026, up from 54% a year earlier, but NEV sales for January-July 2026 fell 12.5% and total passenger car sales fell 20.3%; Geely Xingyuan the best-selling model February-July 2026 with nearly 197,500 units at just under RMB 100,000 (~$14,820); Tesla Model Y second with more than 180,000 units at RMB 263,500-313,500; BYD passenger car sales fell more than 10% in H1 2026; Volkswagen Lavida the only foreign model in the top ten.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that China's EV transition is still growing volume: penetration rose to 65.1% only because total passenger-car sales fell 20.3%, while NEV units fell 12.5%. Also weakens Tesla's China pricing-power case: its Model Y sells at RMB 263,500-313,500 against a RMB ~100,000 best-seller.

sources.title: Electrek: Tesla's China business is flipping - sales down 12%, exports double (CPCA data)
sources.claims: Tesla China retail sales from CPCA data: 381,088 vehicles sold to Chinese buyers in January-September 2026, down 11.9% year on year; September 2026 retail 64,837 units, down 9.35% year on year but up 29.55% month on month; Giga Shanghai wholesale 95,366 in September 2026 (+5.0% year on year, highest month of 2026); Shanghai exports 30,529 in September (+58.29% year on year); August 2026 retail 50,047 (-12.43% y/y).
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that Tesla's China business is collapsing outright: domestic retail fell 11.9% in nine months, roughly in line with the 12.5% fall in China NEV retail, while Shanghai exports rose, so the plant's utilisation is being held by exports rather than Chinese demand.

sources.title: Cox Automotive EV Market Monitor - August 2026
sources.claims: US new EV sales 78,895 units in August 2026, up 2.5% month on month but down 46.9% year on year; EVs 5.7% of new-vehicle sales; Tesla 40,816 units in August 2026, down 3.8% month on month, share of US EV sales 51.7%, down 3.4 points from July; Toyota 4,964 units (+34.9% m/m), Chevrolet +30.3%, Cadillac +13.1%, Kia +12%; new EV average transaction price $54,754, down 2.8% year on year; EV incentives averaging 12% of ATP (~$6,594 per vehicle), down 19.9% year on year; EV price premium over ICE+ vehicles $4,847 (9.7%); new EV days supply 78.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that Tesla is losing US share: Tesla's share of US EV sales rose to 51.7% in August 2026 while total US EV volume fell 46.9% year on year, so Tesla is gaining share of a shrinking pool. It also weakens the claim that the subsidy removal cut effective prices: OEM incentives of ~$6,594 (12% of ATP) replaced much of the $7,500 credit.

sources.title: European EV Registrations by Brand and Model (September 2026) - evstats.org
sources.claims: European registrations by brand through September 2026: Tesla 153,978 units in an 11-country panel in January-September 2026, up 51% year on year from 102,025; Tesla 45,523 vs BYD 39,583 in that panel in September 2026 (Tesla 22,921 vs BYD 21,008 in September 2025); Tesla 58,527 registrations across 16 countries in September 2026, +81% in the 14 countries with year-earlier data (53,479 vs 29,612); Tesla Model Y the best-selling BEV in September 2026 with 17,413 units in 9 countries vs 8,227 a year earlier; Chinese brands 14.9% of new cars in September 2026 vs 8.0% a year earlier (18.2% including Chinese-owned Volvo, Polestar, smart, Lotus); BEV share 27.9% in the panel in September 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the 'Tesla is in structural retreat in Europe' thesis: Tesla's European registrations rose 51% in January-September 2026 and 81% in September, ahead of the EU BEV market's 40.5% H1 growth. It is a country-panel aggregation, not the full ACEA market, so levels are lower than ACEA totals and September is quarter-end loaded.

sources.title: China Biz Insider: China EV price war ends amid margin collapse
sources.claims: China's EV price war reversed in 2026: more than 15 automakers raised prices during 2026 as Q1 2026 industry margins fell to 3.2% and lithium costs rose 160% to about $27,777 per tonne, squeezing profit margins.
sources.claims_weakened: Contradicts the common assumption that Chinese EV prices keep falling: if 15+ automakers raised prices in 2026, Tesla's relative price position in China improved. Single trade outlet with unverified industry-margin figures; the direction is corroborated by Tesla's own automotive gross margin rising 150 bp year on year in Q3 2026.

sources.title: IEA Global Energy Review 2026: Technology - battery storage
sources.claims: Global battery storage deployment was 108 GW of new capacity in 2025, 40% more than in 2024, with installed capacity eleven times the 2021 level; LFP chemistry around 90% of deployments; battery storage the fastest-growing power technology.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that storage demand growth is slowing: 40% growth in GW terms in 2025 with capacity 11x 2021. It also implies the market is measured in GW, not the GWh Tesla reports, so Tesla's 36.0 GWh must be converted at a project duration before any share figure is credible.

sources.title: Robotaxi Expansion Tracker 2026 (third-party aggregation of operator disclosures and NHTSA filings)
sources.claims: Robotaxi fleet and ride data for 2026: Waymo operating roughly 3,000 robotaxis and about 500,000 paid rides per week (announced 2026-03-27, double April 2025) across 10 US cities with about 4 million rider-only miles per week, targeting 1 million rides per week by December 2026; Tesla's robotaxi service launched in Austin in mid-2025 and had expanded to seven metros with 44 active vehicles in H1 2026; Baidu Apollo Go operational in more than 10 Chinese cities; Zoox charging fares in Las Vegas; Pony.ai operating in China.
sources.claims_weakened: Third-party aggregation, not an operator filing: vehicle counts and ride figures are partly estimated and the Tesla fleet number conflicts with separate community trackers (8 vehicles giving rides in Austin in one week) and with Texas registration counts (546 in late September 2026). Directionally consistent across trackers, but not audit-grade.

sources.title: Energy Industry Review: Battery storage capacity - record growth and trends in 2026 (citing InfoLink Consulting)
sources.claims: Global energy storage system deployments totalled 275.3 GWh in 2025, up 61.3% year on year (InfoLink Consulting); the world is expected to add 353.4 GWh in 2026, driven by AI data-centre demand.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakened by definitional inconsistency across trackers (GWh of cells, systems or deployments) and by the fact that Tesla's own GWh disclosure is deployment, not shipments; used only to bound the 2026 system market at roughly 350 GWh.

sources.title: Political Behavior: Tesla Takedown - Brand Politicization and Partisan Consumerism (2026)
sources.claims: Peer-reviewed evidence that Tesla's brand became politicised: views of Tesla soured among Republicans when the Musk-Trump alliance dissolved into open personal attacks, while Democrats' assessments ceased their year-long decline, consistent with partisan consumerism shifting ratings in both directions rather than a one-way brand collapse.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the simple 'brand damaged for good' thesis: the damage moved with political events and partly reversed for Republican-leaning buyers after the alliance ended, which is consistent with Tesla's US share of EV sales rising to 51.7% in August 2026. Survey attitudes, not sales.

sources.title: Business Quant: Tesla (TSLA) analyst estimates, revenue and EPS consensus
sources.claims: Tesla consensus sell-side estimates by quarter: Q4 2026 revenue $29.77B (range $27.06-32.47B), Q1-Q4 2027 revenue $28.08B/$29.67B/$32.78B/$33.39B; Q4 2026 EPS $0.45, 2027 quarterly EPS $0.41/$0.53/$0.58/$0.68; Q3 2026 actual revenue $28.05B and EPS $0.48. Implies FY2026 revenue ~$108.5B, EPS ~$1.67; FY2027 revenue ~$123.9B, EPS ~$2.20.
sources.claims_weakened: Any view that consensus already models a sharp 2027 robotaxi/Optimus revenue step-up; the 2027 revenue consensus of ~$124B is only 20% above trailing revenue.

sources.title: Federal Register / EPA final rule, 91 FR 7686 (2026-02-18): rescission of the 2009 endangerment finding and repeal of light-, medium- and heavy-duty GHG standards
sources.claims: EPA final rule published 2026-02-18 rescinds the 2009 findings of contribution and endangerment and repeals all GHG emission standards for light-duty, medium-duty and heavy-duty vehicles and engines, on the reading that CAA section 202(a)(1) does not authorise the standards.
sources.claims_weakened: The existence of a federal CO2 compliance market that generates tradeable credits for Tesla after model year 2026.

sources.title: IRS — Clean vehicle tax credits (section 30D available only for vehicles acquired on or before 2025-09-30)
sources.claims: The section 30D new clean vehicle credit is available only for vehicles acquired on or before 2025-09-30; no federal purchase credit applied to vehicles acquired after that date.
sources.claims_weakened: Any assumption that a federal EV purchase incentive still supports US Tesla demand in 2026-2028.

sources.title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles — Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program (Senate Bill 2807, 89R)
sources.claims: SB 2807 (89R) effective 2025-09-01 created a TxDMV authorization for commercial operation of SAE Level 4/5 automated vehicles; final rules effective 2026-02-27; authorization enforceable from 2026-05-28; no fee; authorizations do not expire unless revoked; operators must certify a recording device, minimal-risk condition and emergency-responder interaction plan.
sources.claims_weakened: The view that Texas operation is unregulated; also the view that a Texas authorisation is a high barrier (it is a registration-style regime with no fee).

sources.title: California Public Utilities Commission — Autonomous Vehicle Program permits issued
sources.claims: CPUC AV permit table lists drivered/driverless pilot and deployment permits for Nuro, Tensor, Waymo, WeRide and Zoox; Tesla does not appear as a CPUC AV permit holder as of 2026-10-29, so Tesla has no CPUC autonomous passenger-service authority in California.
sources.claims_weakened: Any claim that Tesla's California 'robotaxi' service is a permitted driverless commercial AV service; it supports the reading that it runs under a non-AV TCP/limousine authority.

sources.title: Waymo: raising a $16 billion investment round at a $126 billion valuation
sources.claims: Waymo raised a $16B round in February 2026 at a $126B post-money valuation, led by Dragoneer, DST Global and Sequoia with Alphabet as majority investor; the largest investment ever in an autonomous vehicle company, more than double the $45B valuation of its October 2024 round.
sources.claims_weakened: Any autonomy valuation for Tesla far above $126B that is not supported by a comparable operating fleet; sets a marked, funded benchmark for a scaled robotaxi leader.

sources.title: Stock Analysis: BYD Company (HKG:1211) statistics and valuation ratios
sources.claims: BYD Company (HKG:1211) trailing P/E 18.48x and forward P/E 12.10x; PEG 1.77.
sources.claims_weakened: A peer set in which Chinese EV leaders trade at anything close to Tesla's multiple; BYD, the largest EV producer by volume, trades at a single-digit forward multiple.

sources.title: FINVIZ: TSLA analyst price targets, October 2026
sources.claims: Wall Street consensus for TSLA as of October 2026: 40 analysts, Buy recommendation; average 12-month target $417.94 (+3.39% to the then price of $404.22), high $600 (+48%), low $66 (-84%).
sources.claims_weakened: The claim that the sell side sees meaningful upside from $403; the average target is within 4% of the price and the target dispersion (±90%) is close to a factor of nine.

sources.title: TMGM market insight: Morgan Stanley watches Robotaxi, Optimus and the core EV business (secondary report of the Morgan Stanley note)
sources.claims: Morgan Stanley's sum-of-the-parts framework assigns about $47 per share to Tesla's core electric-vehicle business, with Robotaxi, network services and Optimus together accounting for about $330 per share.
sources.claims_weakened: Any reading that the street values Tesla mainly on its car business; also shows that a mainstream bull SOTP puts roughly 88% of value on unproven autonomy and robotics.

sources.title: China State Taxation Administration — announcement on 2026-2027 new energy vehicle purchase tax (half rate, RMB 15,000 cap)
sources.claims: State Taxation Administration policy database: for vehicles purchased 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31 new energy vehicles pay half purchase tax (5% effective), with the reduction capped at RMB 15,000 per passenger car; models must meet new technical requirements (including energy-consumption limits) and be listed in the reduced-tax catalogue from 2026-01-01.
sources.claims_weakened: The assumption that China's 2026 NEV demand still enjoys full purchase-tax exemption; the cap makes the subsidy regressive for higher-priced models such as Tesla's.

sources.title: US House Energy and Commerce Committee — subcommittee markup of H.R. 7390 SELF DRIVE Act of 2026 (12-11)
sources.claims: House Energy and Commerce subcommittee markup forwarded H.R. 7390, the SELF DRIVE Act of 2026, to the full committee by a 12-11 roll-call vote; the bill would create a unified national framework for ADS-equipped vehicles and preempt the patchwork of state technical rules; the same markup forwarded H.R. 7389, the Motor Vehicle Modernization Act of 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: The claim that federal AV preemption is law or near-certain; the party-line 12-11 vote shows it is contested and, as of 2026-10-29, not enacted.

sources.title: European Commission — CO2 emission performance standards for cars and vans (2025-2027 three-year averaging; 2030-2032 proposal)
sources.claims: EU light-duty CO2 standards: the Commission proposed in April 2025, and the EU adopted, a 2025-2027 compliance derogation assessed on a three-year average rather than annually; in 2026 the Commission proposed a similar 2030-2032 derogation, easing the near-term pressure on legacy manufacturers to buy credits or cut EV prices.
sources.claims_weakened: The expectation that EU CO2 enforcement forces a 2025-2027 scramble for Tesla regulatory credits or accelerates legacy-OEM EV supply.

sources.title: EUR-Lex — Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 imposing a definitive countervailing duty on imports of new battery electric vehicles originating in China
sources.claims: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 imposes a definitive countervailing duty on battery electric vehicles originating in China for five years from 2024-10-30, with company-specific rates: 7.8% for Tesla (Shanghai) against 35.3% for SAIC and rates in between for other exporters, on top of the 10% common customs duty.
sources.claims_weakened: The view that EU tariffs treat all China-built BEVs alike; Tesla's Shanghai-built cars carry the lowest countervailing rate, a relative advantage over Chinese-brand rivals.

sources.title: SpaceX: announcement of pricing of initial public offering (2026-06-11)
sources.claims: SpaceX priced its IPO of 555,555,555 Class A shares at $135.00 per share on 2026-06-11, listing on Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX from 2026-06-12; the offering raised about $75B at a $1.77T valuation, the largest IPO on record, and the stock reached a market capitalisation of about $2.1T on its first trading day; the offering closed on 2026-06-15 including the full overallotment.
sources.claims_weakened: Any view that a Tesla-SpaceX combination would be a cash exit for Tesla holders; it is a share exchange into a larger, Musk-controlled entity.

sources.title: Semafor: SpaceX and Tesla mega-merger under discussion (2026-10-21)
sources.claims: Special committees of SpaceX and Tesla directors formed in October 2026 to consider a merger of the two companies; Musk said he would recuse himself; SpaceX's June 2026 IPO paved the way; super-voting shares give Musk roughly 84% of the vote at SpaceX versus about 20% at Tesla where every share has equal voting weight; Tesla invested $2B in xAI after its chair expressed scepticism; precedent of Tesla bailing out SolarCity in 2016.
sources.claims_weakened: The assumption that Tesla minority holders would negotiate any combination on equal terms; a share-for-share merger would move them into a controlled company.

sources.title: DealRoom: largest leveraged buyouts in history (EA $55B, closed 2026-08-04)
sources.claims: The largest leveraged buyout on record is the $55B take-private of Electronic Arts, closed 2026-08-04 by a consortium led by Saudi PIF, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners ($210 per share, ~$52.5B equity, $20B of committed debt); it overtook the $45B TXU buyout of 2007.
sources.claims_weakened: The feasibility of any take-private of Tesla at $1.59T: it would be roughly 29x the largest LBO ever completed.

sources.title: Multiples.vc: Fluence Energy public comps and valuation multiples, October 2026
sources.claims: Fluence Energy as of October 2026: market cap $1.2B, revenue $2.6B, 0.5x revenue multiple, EBITDA multiple negative (loss-making).
sources.claims_weakened: Any large EV/sales multiple for Tesla's energy segment; listed pure-play storage integrators trade at or below 1x revenue when they do not earn positive EBITDA.

sources.title: Musk Milestones tracker: 2025 CEO Performance Award tranches and market-capitalisation targets
sources.claims: Elon Musk's 2025 compensation plan consists of 12 tranches of about 35 million shares each, unlocking on market capitalisation milestones together with operational milestones; the top market-capitalisation target is $8.5 trillion.
sources.claims_weakened: Any assumption that dilution ends with the 423.7M restricted shares already issued; the award is designed to add shares at market caps up to 5.3x today's.

sources.title: The New York Times: SpaceX and Tesla explore merger to create a de facto Elon Inc. (2026-10-21)
sources.claims: SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a merger that would consolidate Musk's holdings in rockets, cars and artificial intelligence into a company worth well over $3 trillion, announced 2026-10-21.
sources.claims_weakened: Any exit analysis that treats Tesla as a standalone asset with a standalone valuation.

sources.title: USA TODAY: Musk's SpaceX, Tesla to build $16.8B Terafab chip factory in Texas (2026-08-07)
sources.claims: SpaceX announced on 2026-08-06 that Terafab, a vertically integrated chip plant of more than 100 million square feet in Grimes County, Texas, will be built jointly by SpaceX and Tesla, with an initial phase of about $16.8 billion of capital investment from the two companies and potential later phases. Chips are for Optimus robots, Cybercabs and SpaceX space-based data centres. At least 3,000 jobs are promised and Texas granted $30 million from the Enterprise Fund to SpaceX.
sources.claims_weakened: Undercuts the scenario assumption that 2027 capital expenditure stays at or below $25 billion and that free cash flow is positive without a draw on the September 2026 facilities: Tesla's share of a $16.8 billion joint commitment is not disclosed and sits outside the $20 billion 2026 capital budget. It also adds a related-party capital allocation channel with the controlling shareholder's other company ahead of any exchange ratio.

sources.title: 247 Wall St: Tesla and SpaceX just formed special committees to weigh a merger (2026-10-21)
sources.claims: On the SpaceX Q3 call of 2026-10-20 Musk said both companies formed special committees of independent directors and that he is conflicted and has no role; that no terms have been agreed and there is no guarantee of a deal. He said a Tesla vote would need 50% of all shares outstanding, not of votes cast, which makes every non-vote a no. Tesla's 2026-10-19 proxy sets the annual meeting for 2026-12-03 with three company proposals and no merger vote, so any deal goes to a later meeting. Tesla closed $373.71 on 2026-10-20 and was worth $1.48 trillion; SpaceX closed $147.79 and was worth $2.01 trillion, so Tesla holders would own less than half of a combined group. No exchange ratio has been disclosed. Ira Ehrenpreis joined SpaceX's board after 2026-02-02.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that a negotiated SpaceX combination would carry a premium to the undisturbed Tesla price: no ratio exists, the vote needs 50% of all shares, and SpaceX is the larger side. It also confirms the roughly 3.95 billion share count implied by a $1.48 trillion value at $373.71, which contradicts the 3,541 million share count used for the $1,428 billion capitalisation in the financial section.

sources.title: State Energy & Environmental Impact Center: twenty-five AGs filed suit challenging EPA's endangerment finding repeal
sources.claims: On 2026-03-19 Massachusetts, California, New York and Connecticut led 25 state attorneys general, 12 cities and counties and the Governor of Pennsylvania in a petition in the US Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit challenging EPA's rescission of the 2009 endangerment finding, which EPA finalised on 2026-02-12. The petitions were consolidated by 2026-05-20 and the petitioners moved to complete the administrative record, arguing the response-to-comments document may have been altered after the rescission was declared final.

sources.title: Tesla News Wire: NHTSA data — Tesla robotaxis reported 9 crashes in August 2026, including the first Cybercab crash
sources.claims: NHTSA's Standing General Order automated-driving crash data posted 2026-10-15 records nine Tesla robotaxi crashes in August 2026 (five Dallas, three Austin, one Tampa), all property damage with no injuries, and 36 Tesla ADS crash reports since 2025-06-16, 35 of them Model Y robotaxis. The first Cybercab report was a 5 mph entry into a water-filled pothole with a safety monitor aboard and no passengers. Two August crashes occurred with a remote support operator in control and seven of the nine list a pre-crash speed of 3 mph or less. Texas records listed 769 Tesla robotaxi vehicles at 2026-10-14, including 349 Cybercabs. NHTSA is auditing Tesla's self-certification of the steering-wheel-free Cybercab with a response due 2026-10-30 and is weighing a school-zone speeding petition. Tesla publishes no robotaxi mileage, so the reports are not normalised by miles or fleet size.

sources.title: Investing.com: Tesla's Baa3 rating affirmed by Moody's, outlook stable; Elon Musk calls rating 'ridiculously low' as SpaceX tops it
sources.claims: Moody's affirmed Tesla's Baa3 long-term issuer rating with a stable outlook, citing technology strengths against deteriorating credit metrics, and SpaceX received a first-time Baa1 long-term issuer rating with a stable outlook, placing the merged-counterparty above Tesla in Moody's ranking. Also reported: BYD and Tesla ended H1 2026 with the same 2.4% share of the EU, EFTA and UK car market, BYD up from 1.0% in H1 2025, and BYD undercuts Tesla by about EUR 5,500 per vehicle in Europe.
sources.claims_weakened: The rating gap weakens the assumption that a Tesla holder receives a premium in an all-stock SpaceX combination: the faster-growing, better-rated asset is the larger side of the trade. The European share parity weakens the claim that Tesla's premium is durable against Chinese competition.

sources.title: Cisco stock still isn't back to its 2000 high: Chart of the Week (Yahoo Finance)
sources.claims: Cisco was the most valuable company in the world in March 2000 at about $500B; the stock fell over 70% by April 2000 and almost 90% by October 2000; annual revenue later grew from about $12.5B to about $57B and trailing net income passed its 1999 level by 2003, yet the share price did not surpass its 2000 closing high on an adjusted basis until 2021.
sources.claims_weakened: The claim that a correct technology thesis and rapid revenue growth protect an investor who pays a peak-cycle multiple.

sources.title: Tesla consensus rating and average price target, 2026-10-25 (MarketBeat)
sources.claims: Consensus rating Hold from 48 covering firms (3 sell, 20 hold, 24 buy, 1 strong buy); average 12-month price objective $408.61; Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $0.48 against a $0.45 consensus on revenue of about $28B, flat year over year, with automotive revenue -3% and energy revenue -16%; named targets include Morgan Stanley $410 equal-weight, RBC $480, Jefferies $400, Mizuho $460, Canaccord $442.
sources.claims_weakened: The idea that sell-side consensus is uniformly bullish, or that the average target implies meaningful upside from $403.30.

sources.title: GM to retreat from robotaxis, stop funding Cruise (AP News)
sources.claims: General Motors ended funding for its Cruise robotaxi unit after acquiring a controlling stake for $581M in 2016; Cruise accumulated more than $10B of operating losses while generating less than $500M of revenue; GM folded the operations in house and expected to save about $1B a year.
sources.claims_weakened: The assumption that an automotive incumbent with capital and engineering depth can convert a decade of autonomous-driving spending into a commercial robotaxi business.

sources.title: At one point Amazon stock was down 90% but investors still got rich (CNBC)
sources.claims: Amazon's stock fell more than 90% from its 1999 peak in the dot-com bust, yet long-term holders who stayed were ultimately rewarded as the business compounded.
sources.claims_weakened: Neither direction cleanly: it shows an option-value thesis can be right and still produce a ~94% drawdown, so the entry price and the holder's tolerance determine the return.

sources.title: Tesla (TSLA) Stock Forecast and Analyst Price Targets (Stock Analysis, S&P Global data)
sources.claims: 44 analysts polled by S&P Global put Tesla at a consensus Buy with an average price target of $410.68, a low target of $128.11 (-68%) and a high of $600 (+49%), showing extreme dispersion around the mean.
sources.claims_weakened: The usefulness of a single consensus target as a valuation anchor when the published range spans a 4.7x difference.

sources.title: State Court Order Clears Path for Tesla Race Discrimination Case to Go to Trial
sources.claims: California Civil Rights Department sued Tesla in February 2022; Alameda County Superior Court denied Tesla's motion to throw out the case in May 2026 and the case was then set for trial; CRD alleges systemic anti-Black harassment, pay discrimination ($1,533 monthly pay gap, June 2018-June 2024) and retaliation at Fremont.
sources.claims_weakened: Any suggestion that the CRD case was dismissed or settled before trial.

sources.title: Black Tesla employees accuse company of fostering racial discrimination in major trial (The Guardian)
sources.claims: CRD v. Tesla trial began with opening statements on 2026-09-21 in Alameda County Superior Court before Judge Peter Borkon as a bench trial; the state seeks damages and injunctive relief; trial expected to run through end-October 2026; Tesla denies wrongdoing; no verdict at the time of publication.
sources.claims_weakened: The earlier 2026-07-20 trial date, which slipped to September 2026.

sources.title: Electrek: Tesla, SpaceX confirm 'Terafab' chip fab site — $16.8B first phase (2026-08-06)
sources.claims: Terafab's first phase is about $16.8bn funded by Tesla and SpaceX jointly, with a 100m sq ft site in Grimes County, Texas; the headline figure fell from $25bn in March 2026; SpaceX's IPO filing described Terafab as a 'general framework' with no binding commitments, no finalised IP split and no obligation for either side to keep participating; Tesla separately committed $16.5bn to Samsung for AI6 chips.
sources.claims_weakened: The assumption that Terafab is a firm $16.8bn capital commitment that Tesla must fund: the S-1 language makes the commitment non-binding and Tesla's share undisclosed, so the cash call is optional until definitive agreements are filed.

sources.title: Axis Intelligence: Figure AI statistics 2026 — valuation, robots, funding and production data
sources.claims: Figure AI reached a $39bn post-money valuation in September 2025; its Figure 02 robot completed an 11-month production deployment at BMW's Spartanburg plant, contributing to more than 30,000 X3 vehicles with more than 1,250 operating hours; BotQ is its manufacturing line.
sources.claims_weakened: The deployment metrics are company-reported and not audited; the valuation is a private funding mark, not a revenue multiple; it shows Optimus has a benchmarked rival with named external customers, which weakens any claim that Tesla leads humanoids.

sources.title: TeslaNorth: Cybercab surpasses Model Y as Tesla's Texas robotaxi fleet hits 1,051 (2026-10-27)
sources.claims: Texas DMV records for Tesla Robotaxi, LLC showed 1,051 authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27, all model year 2026: 544 Cybercab and 507 Model Y; the Cybercab count first exceeded the Model Y count that day.
sources.claims_weakened: Authorisation is not active service: the registry does not show how many vehicles carry passengers, run without a monitor, or earn revenue, and Tesla discloses none of those figures.

sources.title: Texas AV Tracker: Tesla Robotaxi live TxDMV registration counts (retrieved 2026-10-29)

Corroborates TeslaNorth's 1,051 figure independently and dates it.

Updated AITO M8 opened pre-sales on 2026-09-30 from RMB 389,800 ($57,880), 30,000 yuan above the previous version, in EREV and BEV form.
