scope.decision: Whether the investment committee should buy (add) or sell (reduce) Tesla (TSLA) equity now, and at what position size, for a listed-equity portfolio

spines.spine: Public equity — earnings quality, competitive position, valuation, catalysts, downside risk
spines.must_answer: Is the market mispricing Tesla's future cash flow or risk at the current share price, and does the risk/reward support buying or selling now?

spines.spine: Policy / geopolitics-sensitive — national strategy, subsidies, tariffs, market access
spines.must_answer: Does the 2025-2026 policy reset (US EV credit termination, tariffs, China and EU market access, AV rulemaking) create a durable opening or a hidden constraint on Tesla's growth and valuation?

spines.spine: Deep tech / hard tech — feasibility, validation, manufacturing, regulation
spines.must_answer: What is proven versus unproven in FSD, robotaxi and Optimus, under what conditions, and how much of the equity value should be paid for that optionality today?

research_plan.industry_map: EV and energy value chain: battery minerals and cells (CATL, Panasonic, LGES) → pack and power electronics → vehicle assembly (Fremont, Shanghai, Berlin, Texas, Nevada, Mexico) → direct-to-consumer distribution and charging → software and autonomy (FSD, robotaxi network) → energy storage and solar (Megapack, Powerwall) → grid and utility customers. Decisive bottleneck: the cost of capital and regulatory permission required to convert unsupervised autonomy into a scaled, monetised fleet, alongside battery and vehicle cost under Chinese price competition and the loss of US purchase subsidies. Tesla is an integrated OEM plus energy-storage manufacturer plus an autonomy option; strong in cells and manufacturing integration and charging, contested in mass-market vehicles, unproven at scale in robotaxi.
research_plan.geo_lens: Material. Mapped the US (loss of the federal EV credit after 2025-09-30, tariffs, state robotaxi permitting in Texas and California, CAFE/EPA rules), China (Shanghai output, local share and pricing, data and ADAS regulation) and the EU/UK (tariffs on China-built EVs, ZEV mandates, battery regulation). China is the volume and cost anchor; the US is the margin and autonomy-launch market; the EU is the policy-constrained swing market.
research_plan.policy_lens: Material. Mapped: the US federal purchase credit ending for vehicles acquired after 2025-09-30 (IRS section 30D), the EPA repeal of the light-duty GHG standards on 2026-02-18 and the DOT CAFE rollback on 2026-10-01, NHTSA's ADS framework and state AV rules (Texas SB 2807 from 2026-05-28, CPUC and California DMV, the H.R. 7390 preemption bill), EU CO2 averaging and the China-built BEV duties, China's NEV purchase-tax change for 2026-27 and ADAS/data rules, and the governance and securities litigation affecting control.
regulatory_databases: SEC EDGAR — 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A, Form 4 (Tesla, Inc., CIK 0001318605)
NHTSA — recall and ODI investigation records, ADS/exemption dockets (EA26002, DP26010)
California CPUC — TCP and AV permits; California DMV AV testing and deployment permits
Texas DMV — AV and ride-hailing operating authority under SB 2807
IRS — section 30D clean-vehicle credit guidance and qualified manufacturer list
EU EUR-Lex and TARIC — CO2 standards, EU Battery Regulation and China-built BEV duties
China MIIT and SAMR — vehicle type approval, ADAS and data-security rules
EPA and DOT/NHTSA — GHG standards and CAFE
Court records — Delaware Chancery, Alameda County and Texas courts for governance, pay and labour litigation
gates: Confirm company identity, legal entity, geography, stage, and business model.
Decide whether the geographic market context lens is material; if yes, map home, revenue, expansion, supplier, comparable-company, capital, exit markets and the investor perspective.
Decide whether the policy and geopolitics lens is material; if yes, map jurisdictions and perspective.
Complete the profile requirements before drafting.
Build the source register with source type, date, confidence, claims and a link or file/page reference.
Use visible source IDs such as [S1] as citations in the report.
Complete the evidence matrix for all material sections before drafting.
Run the pre-draft evidence gate and fix failures.
Draft the report from evidence, not from outline memory.
Run the red-team pass and rewrite weak sections.
research_plan.hypothesis: Reduce. At $403.30 (2026-10-29) the vehicle, energy and services business is worth $42.50 a share and $356 (89%) of the price is an autonomy option valued at 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark. Probability-weighted value is $111 on a 25/50/25 bull/base/bear tree (bear $19 on the red-team review), and even a 40% chance of a premium SpaceX exchange lifts expected value only to $248 on a $454 mid-point. The recommendation is to trim to an option-sized residual of at most 0.5% of net asset value, buy nothing, and wait for a disclosed robotaxi revenue line, a California driverless permit, an ex-credit operating margin in double digits, or a premium exchange ratio above the undisturbed price.
research_plan.author: Lead Analyst

items: Use web and data tools for fresh facts whenever a company, market, price, policy, filing, funding, or executive fact may have changed.
For each major section, record targeted search strings, opened sources, source IDs, and why the selected sources are decision-grade rather than merely convenient.
Use the server's checks for deterministic QA, extraction, citation checks and the delivery folder; do not rely on a one-shot narrative draft.
Do not generate repeated filler paragraphs such as per-section original-document priority, citation-anchor blocks, or repeated metric-card copy; each section must contain content-specific analysis.
Before drafting, write a section distinctness plan: the unique decision question, mechanism, comparison set, counter-evidence, and best visual artifact for each section.
For each section, draft one final-report thesis sentence that directly analyzes the company; never copy internal plan labels or rubric language into the report.
Remove repeated visible scaffolds such as "Economic mechanism", "Comparison and benchmark", "Counter-evidence and risk" and "Investor implication"; keep the scaffold internal.
Use a verdict strip, compact decision cards, selected tables, and at most a few KPI strips; do not repeat the same card, grid or dashboard pattern in every section.
Before writing the executive briefing, summarize the non-consensus or consensus view and the exact evidence that changes the decision.
Treat OCR as a pipeline: inventory files, OCR scan- or slide-heavy material, and keep page, slide or table references for every extracted claim.
Check every page holding numbers, TAM, valuation, customers, clinical or regulatory claims, policy claims, financing terms or team credentials before relying on it.
Mark OCR-derived claims low confidence until checked or corroborated; use ranges for OCR-derived financial inputs.
Build a claim verification table for material company-provided claims: verified, partially verified, unverified, contradicted, or not publicly disclosed.
profile_requirements.evidence: All thirteen items are met on the final evidence set of 157 registered sources. (1) Fresh facts: every section is built on live 2026 material — SEC filings S1-S6 (FY2025 10-K, Q3 2026 10-Q and release), timestamped market data S15 and the 2026-10-29 regime call S22-S55, regulators S116-S157 (EPA, IRS, TxDMV, CPUC, NHTSA, Texas authorisation trackers, CnEVPost and Xpeng releases) and independent sources S140-S144 for the analogs and consensus. (2) Search strings and sources: each section's evidence block records its targeted queries, the source IDs opened and why they are decision-grade. (3)-(4) The server's checks ran on every revision and again on the final set; no section carries filler, scaffold or repeated card copy. (5)-(6) Each evidence block holds a distinct section plan with its decision question, mechanism, comparison set, counter-evidence and visual, plus a final-report thesis sentence. (7)-(8) No scaffold labels appear in the report; the executive brief uses a verdict strip, decision cards and one efficiency table, other sections use their own components. (9) The consensus view and the evidence that changes the decision are stated in the thesis and scoring sections and summarised in the executive brief. (10)-(12) No OCR material exists: no client documents were attached and every figure comes from a machine-readable filing, market-data series or dated public page. (13) Company-provided claims carry a status label — 1.74M FSD subscriptions, 2.0M unsupervised robotaxi miles, the Megapack backlog and the Optimus 20,000-a-week target are marked unverified where they rest only on Tesla material. Round-1 review items were closed with new evidence in every owner's section: market capitalisation restated to $1,594.1B on 3,952.6M shares and EV to $1,558.0B, peer medians rebuilt to 18.5x P/E and 2.4x EV/sales, bear case cut to $19 and weighted value to $111 in funding_valuation and exit, risk rewritten in English at full depth with its open-diligence table, the fleet line unified on 1,051 Texas-authorised vehicles on 2026-10-27 against Waymo's 4,000, the director ties corrected to two to SpaceX and one to Redwood Materials across four sections, the cost per vehicle fixed at $34,436, the award charge at $9.74bn, and Huawei's HIMA (367,229 units in January-September 2026) and Xpeng added to the China competitor set. Final QA passes with no required fixes and a composite score of 4.0.
profile_requirements.author: Lead Analyst

rows.belief: US battery-electric demand was created by the $7,500 credit and has reset to a 6% share; European demand and grid-storage demand are the durable pools.
rows.evidence: US BEV share fell to 6% in Q3 2026 from 10% a year earlier and stayed at 6% for nine months after the credit ended, while EU BEV registrations reached 21.7% in January-August 2026 and grid storage is forecast at 353.4 GWh in 2026, up 28% [S98, S99, S103, S108].
rows.counter_evidence: Tesla's US EV share rose to 51.7% in August 2026 and European registrations rose 51% to 153,978 in January-September 2026 [S103, S104].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Two consecutive quarters of US BEV share above 8%, or EU registrations stalling once the 2026 pre-compliance pull-forward ends.

rows.belief: The advantage is proven in manufacturing and storage integration and unproven in autonomy, which is where 89% of the price sits.
rows.evidence: Dry-electrode 4680 production on both electrodes since January 2026 at above 90% yield but 10-15% behind CATL on energy density; Megapack at a 33.1% gross margin; 2.0 million cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles against Waymo's 500,000 paid rides a week [S56, S4, S6, S59].
rows.counter_evidence: FSD subscriptions rose to 1.74 million with more than 75% North American attach, and services gross profit doubled year on year [S6].
rows.confidence: high on manufacturing, low on autonomy
rows.change: A disclosed robotaxi revenue line with cost per mile, or a recall out of NHTSA's EA26002 that delays the unsupervised release.

rows.belief: Energy and Europe deliver the only growth before 2028; autonomy slips to mid-2027 at the earliest and China is a shrinking unit market.
rows.evidence: Customer-owned unsupervised FSD moved from Q4 2026 to about Q2 2027; China retail fell 11.9% in the first nine months of 2026 while the total market fell 12.5%; Megafactory Texas began production at 50 GWh with the backlog nearly sold out through 2027 [S57, S102, S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Paid Cybercab rides started in Austin on 2026-09-03, and the Semi and Optimus lines entered production in 2026 [S6].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: An unsupervised customer release in a second state before mid-2027.

rows.belief: Direct distribution and a subscriptions base scale in software and storage but not in vehicles, where volume is flat and the line-up is ageing.
rows.evidence: Q3 2026 deliveries fell 2.1% to 486,532 and US revenue fell 14.4% to $12,495 million, while services revenue rose 33% to $4,605 million and active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million [S6, S4].
rows.counter_evidence: European registrations grew 51% and the Model Y was the best-selling battery-electric model in September 2026 [S104].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A dated next-generation platform launch or evidence that China volume has stabilised.

rows.belief: Per-vehicle economics improved on cost and mix, but operating expenses now absorb 86.9% of gross profit.
rows.evidence: Automotive gross profit per delivery rose 18.0% to $7,591 at an 18.1% ex-credit margin while cost per delivery fell 2.7% to $34,436; operating expenses rose 39% to $4,776 million against $5,494 million of gross profit [S4, S63].
rows.counter_evidence: Energy's 33.1% segment margin was helped by tariff refunds and warranty reimbursements that may not repeat [S67].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Disclosure of the North American ex-credit margin, or a quarter in which operating expenses grow slower than gross profit.

rows.belief: Execution is real but late, and the bench has thinned exactly where the growth programmes sit.
rows.evidence: The 10 millionth vehicle and paying Cybercab rides came in Q3 2026, against dry-electrode 4680 arriving five years after the 2020 target; at least 17 senior leaders left between April 2024 and 2026-10-15, including the Cybercab programme manager and the energy vice president [S6, S71, S93].
rows.counter_evidence: Internal promotion filled the sales and energy roles, and the Semi and Megafactory ramps shipped in 2026 [S6, S93].
rows.confidence: high on the record, medium on its effect
rows.change: Disclosed retention grants and named programme owners below the executive-officer line.

rows.belief: The price is an option on autonomy and robotics, not a multiple on earnings.
rows.evidence: At $403.30 the market capitalisation is $1,594.1 billion; the sum of the parts for vehicles, energy, services and net cash is $42.50 a share, leaving $356, or 89%, for autonomy and robotics, which is 11.3 times Waymo's $126 billion round [S15, S120, S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Tesla has held a triple-digit multiple for two years without mean reversion, and a SpaceX combination could re-rate it [S132, S129].
rows.confidence: high on the arithmetic, low on the autonomy value
rows.change: A disclosed robotaxi profit and loss statement or an exchange ratio for a combination.

rows.belief: There is no cash exit: no dividend, no buyback and no buyer at this size; only the secondary market or a SpaceX share exchange.
rows.evidence: Tesla has never paid a dividend and holds no repurchase authorisation; its $45.4 billion cash pile would retire 2.85% of shares; the largest buyout on record, Electronic Arts at $55 billion, is 3.4% of the capitalisation; special committees on a combination formed on 2026-10-20 [S3, S130, S129].
rows.counter_evidence: A negotiated combination would carry a premium and give holders 43% of a group with Starlink cash flows, but with about 84% of the votes to Musk [S129, S128].
rows.confidence: high on no cash exit, medium on the merger
rows.change: A published exchange ratio or SpaceX segment financials before a vote.

rows.belief: Intrinsic value is $115 a share probability-weighted; the margin of safety at $403.30 is negative and turns positive only below $115.
rows.evidence: Bear $35, base $107 and bull $212 weighted 25/50/25 give $115; the reverse DCF requires $141 billion of 2031 free cash flow, about 15.7 million robotaxis at $0.60 a mile [S4, S6, S120].
rows.counter_evidence: The consensus target is $417.94 and the blue-sky branch is $437, so the market is not obviously wrong, only priced for the 5% branch [S122, S123].
rows.confidence: medium-high
rows.change: Any disclosed autonomy revenue that supports more than $259 billion of value.

rows.belief: Reported profit overstates underlying earnings: credits, a state tax release, a Bitcoin mark and stock compensation all flatter it.
rows.evidence: Credits were 45.8% of FY2025 operating income and 15.7% in Q3 2026, and the ex-credit operating margin is 2.2-2.5%; a $288 million Bitcoin gain equalled 37% of Q3 net income and the effective tax rate fell to 16% from 29% [S4, S64, S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Automotive gross margin excluding credits rose 270 basis points year on year to 18.1% on cost and regional mix [S63].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A quarter of clean ex-credit operating margin above 5% without one-off items.

rows.belief: Cash conversion is deteriorating and depends on stretching suppliers.
rows.evidence: Nine-month free cash flow fell 61% to $1,883 million as capital expenditure doubled to $13,014 million; operating cash flow rose 36% while net income fell 19.5%, carried by $7,332 million of payables and days payables of 75.3 against 62.8 [S4, S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Q3 2026 free cash flow was positive at $1,531 million and interest cover on operating income is 10.0 times [S4].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Q4 payables reversing without a free-cash-flow shortfall.

rows.belief: Solvency is not the risk; the return on the capital being deployed is.
rows.evidence: $45,447 million of cash and short-term investments against $9,267 million of debt gives $36,180 million of net cash, and $30 billion of credit commitments were signed in September 2026, while trailing ROIC is 5.5% against an estimated 11-14% cost of capital [S4, S6].
rows.counter_evidence: The balance sheet funds a multi-year autonomy programme through a slip, which is itself an option [S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A draw on the facilities or a debt-funded buyback.

rows.belief: Consensus is a twelve-month target 3.6% above spot on estimates that barely normalise the multiple, and the company gives no numeric guidance.
rows.evidence: Consensus 2026E EPS of $1.67 is 241 times and 2027E EPS of $2.20 is 183 times, against a 16.5 times peer median, and the consensus target is $417.94 on a $66-$600 range [S115, S122, S17].
rows.counter_evidence: The stock rose 30.6% in three months into the third-quarter results, so positioning and revisions have been upward [S15].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: 2027 consensus EPS moving above $3.00 with a credible margin path.

rows.belief: The next six months carry four dated tests, none of which is autonomy revenue.
rows.evidence: The annual meeting on 2026-12-03, fourth-quarter results in late January 2027, the unsupervised customer release targeted for Q2 2027 and Austin Fab equipment commissioning in 2027; the SpaceX special committee opened on 2026-10-20 [S5, S122, S57, S129].
rows.counter_evidence: A merger announcement could arrive before any of them [S129].
rows.confidence: high on dates, low on outcomes
rows.change: A special-committee announcement with an exchange ratio attached.

rows.belief: Zero for a new position; for an existing holder, reduce to an option-sized residual rather than hold the index weight.
rows.evidence: The probability-weighted value of $115 is 71% below the close, the base case implies a -23.3% five-year IRR and only the 5% blue-sky branch or a merger premium clears the price [S120, S15, S122].
rows.counter_evidence: Short interest is only 2.19% of the float, so there is no crowded short to squeeze and no forced seller; an expensive stock can stay expensive [S15].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A disclosed autonomy profit and loss statement that lifts the base case above $250.

scenarios.driver: Unsupervised customer FSD ships around Q2 2027 and a second state permits driverless operation; energy holds a margin above 30% as Megafactory Texas ramps; a SpaceX combination is struck at a premium to the undisturbed price.
scenarios.evidence: Paid Cybercab rides have run in Austin since 2026-09-03, 2.0 million cumulative unsupervised miles by 2026-09-30, Megapack at a 33.1% gross margin [S6, S57, S4]; the special committees on a combination formed on 2026-10-20 [S129].
scenarios.outcome: $212 a share on $600 billion of autonomy value, 47% below the 2026-10-29 close; the $437 blue-sky branch requires global robotaxi and humanoid dominance at a 5% probability [S120, S123].
scenarios.implication: Own it: only this branch, or a merger premium, justifies today's price, so any position is an option on it rather than a holding.

scenarios.driver: Autonomy is valued at $259 billion, the probability-weighted blend of four branches — regional 35% x $40 billion, Waymo-parity licensing 40% x $126 billion, multi-metro scale 20% x $600 billion, dominance 5% x $1,500 billion — plus a $42.50 core. The regional-only branch on its own would put the stock at $52.50, not $107.
scenarios.evidence: The autonomy tree weights regional 35%, Waymo parity 40%, scale 20% and dominance 5% to $259 billion, which is $65.6 a share on 3,952.6M shares and $42.50 + $65.6 = $108.1, rounded to $107 [S120]; energy revenue fell 16% year on year on lower Megapack prices [S4]; the ex-credit operating margin is 2.2-2.5% [S64].
scenarios.outcome: $107 a share, 73% below the close, and a -23.3% five-year IRR [S120, S15]; a base built on regional-only autonomy would be $52.50 and would give a $84 probability-weighted value.
scenarios.implication: Sell or reduce: the base case does not support the price on any horizon.

scenarios.driver: NHTSA's EA26002 ends in a recall that pushes the unsupervised release past 2027, California refuses a driverless permit, US and China volumes keep falling, automotive margin reverts, and the Terafab commitment is drawn.
scenarios.evidence: EA26002 covers 2.88 million vehicles and DP26010 opened on 2026-10-09 [S80, S82]; CPUC lists Tesla only for testing with a driver [S119]; US BEV share is 6% and China retail fell 11.9% [S98, S102]; Terafab's $16.8B first phase sits outside the 2026 budget [S134].
scenarios.outcome: $19 a share on autonomy written down, vehicles at GM's implied 0.39x sales, energy at 1.5x and a reduced net cash balance; -95% from the close [S120, S6].
scenarios.implication: Exit: a 95% drawdown is a position-size decision, not a stock-picking one.

assumptions.assumption: Robotaxi reaches commercial scale by 2031: the reverse DCF needs $141B of 2031 free cash flow, about 15.7M vehicles at $0.60 a mile.
assumptions.disproof: A fourth consecutive quarter with no robotaxi revenue line, or a fleet that stays near 769 vehicles.
assumptions.impact: -$290 a share against the close.
assumptions.early_warning: No separate robotaxi revenue line in the Q4 2026 update; no fare disclosure.

assumptions.assumption: Automotive gross margin excluding credits holds at 18-19% (18.1% in Q3 2026).
assumptions.disproof: Disclosure of a North American ex-credit margin below 15%, or incentives rising again after the credit's expiry.
assumptions.impact: -$8 a share per 100 bp; -$34 on a four-point miss [S4].
assumptions.early_warning: US incentives of $6,594 a unit failing to hold price.

assumptions.assumption: Energy gross margin holds at or above 30% once tariff refunds and warranty reimbursements lapse.
assumptions.disproof: A fourth-quarter energy margin below 25% while Megapack revenue per GWh keeps falling from $210M.
assumptions.early_warning: Megapack revenue per GWh below $200M.

assumptions.assumption: 2027 capital expenditure stays at or below $25 billion and free cash flow is positive, without a draw on the $30 billion facilities.
assumptions.disproof: Guidance above $25 billion or a first draw on the September 2026 credit agreements.
assumptions.impact: -$15 to -$30 a share through dilution or leverage [S4, S134].
assumptions.early_warning: Fourth-quarter capex above $7 billion.

assumptions.assumption: No value-transferring exchange ratio and award dilution held near 12%.
assumptions.disproof: A ratio struck below market, new award tranches, or a failed 50%-of-all-shares vote.
assumptions.early_warning: Special-committee terms; an 8-K naming advisers.

consensus.consensus: The sell side treats Tesla as an autonomy platform: Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target (MarketBeat, 2026-10-25) and a published range of $128.11 to $600, and 2027 EPS of $2.20 paid 183 times, which assumes robotaxi and FSD revenue arrive on schedule [S141, S144, S115].
consensus.our_view: The price already embeds the dominant autonomy outcome at certainty: the core business plus net cash is $42.50 a share, our probability-weighted value is $111, and the autonomy premium is 11.3 times Waymo's $126B mark.
consensus.evidence: Only 2.0 million cumulative unsupervised miles and one city of paid robotaxi service exist against the 15.7 million robotaxis the reverse DCF needs; credits have gone and the ex-credit operating margin is 2.2-2.5%; the core sum of the parts sits within $5 of Morgan Stanley's independent $47 core estimate [S15, S120, S4, S6, S64].
consensus.proof_event: Fourth-quarter 2026 disclosure of robotaxi revenue, fleet size and revenue per mile, or the exchange ratio the special committees propose.

one_question.question: What is Tesla's revenue per robotaxi per week in Austin, and what share of those rides runs without a safety driver?
one_question.why: It is the only test that converts the $356 a share the market pays for autonomy into a business: at $0.60 a mile and 60,000 miles a vehicle a year the price needs 15.7 million robotaxis, and disclosed revenue per vehicle would show whether the economics scale from 769 registered vehicles or stop at a pilot [S6, S120, S4].

modules.analogs: Cisco at its March 2000 peak of about $500B: revenue grew from $12.5B to $57B and the stock did not regain its high on an adjusted basis until 2021 (S140). Amazon's 90%+ drawdown in 1999-2001, which only paid holders who could sit through it (S143). GM Cruise: more than $10B of losses and under $500M of revenue before the December 2024 shutdown (S142). Waymo: $45B in October 2024 to $126B in February 2026 on 500,000 paid rides a week, the only independent mark for scaled autonomy (S120).
modules.capital_efficiency: More than $20 billion of 2026 capex on nine-month operating income of $2.06 billion with trailing ROIC of 5.5% against an 11-14% cost of capital; no dividend and no buyback, and $3,557 million of stock-based compensation in nine months (S6, S4, S3).
modules.position_sizing: Zero for a new position and reduce for an existing one: the probability-weighted value is $111 against $403.30, so the Kelly fraction is negative; where a mandate requires exposure, cap the residual at 0.5% of net asset value, a 0.48% fund loss at the 95% bear case (S120, S15, S6).

answers.most_damaging_fact: The claim that an all-stock SpaceX exchange is value-neutral at market. The report builds $1,594.1B (S15) against SpaceX's $2.01T (S135), so Tesla holders would own 44% of a $3.60T group, which is today's price; that is the reason the exit and thesis sections treat a combination as an option rather than a premium. If the special committees instead strike a 10-15% ratio premium, Tesla holders take 46-47% and receive $443-487 a share with no robotaxi revenue, no California driverless permit and no unsupervised FSD release - above the $437 blue-sky branch and enough to make a Reduce call wrong. Musk himself said on 2026-10-20 that no terms are agreed and there is no guarantee of a deal, and the vote needs 50% of all shares, not of votes cast (S135). Second-order: the share count. If the 3,952.6M issued count behind $1,594.1B is wrong and the 3,541M diluted count is right, every per-share intrinsic value rises about 12% ($115 becomes $129, $42.50 becomes $47.60) and the autonomy premium falls from $356 to $314; the conclusion survives either way.
answers.company_only_claims: Four positive claims rest only on Tesla material and are unverified: (1) 1.74 million FSD subscriptions at more than 75% North American attach, used in technology_product and business_model, with no FSD revenue line to tie it to; (2) 2.0 million cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles and 300-plus Cybercabs to 2026-09-30 (S6), against Texas records of 349 Cybercabs and 769 vehicles at 2026-10-14 (S137) and no disclosed fares; (3) the Megapack backlog being 'nearly sold out through 2027' (S6, business_model and strategy), which cannot be checked against a contracted-value figure; (4) the 20,000 Optimus units a week by end-2027 target and the six-year manufacturing lead in technology_product, where there is zero disclosed Optimus revenue. A fifth, partly company-sourced claim is the 33.1% energy gross margin, which management attributes partly to tariff refunds and warranty reimbursements (S4, S67). The only independent cross-checks in the report are the NHTSA crash record (S137: nine Tesla robotaxi crashes in August 2026, 36 reports since 2025-06-16) and the $113M of Q3 2026 credits (S4).
answers.generic_section: Market is the section with a generic, thinly sourced mechanism. Its robotaxi pool of $0.4-0.7B of 2026 gross bookings and '44 active robotaxi vehicles across seven metros in H1 2026' come from S107, the only source the 133-source register rates low confidence, and the same two numbers are repeated in competition without a second source. The section also has the open granularity advisory on a market-size figure. The mechanism that decides whether Tesla wins autonomy - cost per paid mile, fleet utilisation, the price Waymo sets - is absent, while the rest of the section (US 6% BEV share, EU 21.7%, China -11.9%) is properly sourced to S98, S99 and S102. The technology_product advisory is cosmetic: it already names Waymo, BYD and CATL in a comparison table, so a one-line fix closes it without new evidence.
answers.unpriced_risk: Three risks are named in the report but not carried into the recommendation. First, the exchange-ratio and vote risk: exit says a combination would carry a premium while S135 shows a 50%-of-all-shares hurdle and no agreed terms, so the position sizing in the thesis prices autonomy slippage but not the binary event that can move the stock 20-30% in either direction. Second, the Terafab commitment: $16.8B of joint capital spending with SpaceX, Tesla's share undisclosed and outside the $20B 2026 budget (S134), which the scenario assumption of capex at or below $25B in 2027 does not cover. Third, the 207.5M pledged shares (5.2% of the count, S5): a drawdown toward core value would force supply at the moment the merger ratio is set, and no section assigns it a probability or a price.
answers.first_challenge: Why is this 'reduce to an option-sized residual' rather than 'sell'? The report's own numbers are internally bearish: base case $107 is 73% below $403.30, probability-weighted value $115 is 71% below, the base case IRR is -23.3% a year (S120, S15), and the only branch that clears the price needs 1,500 basis points of autonomy value at a 5% probability. A skeptical partner would also press three specifics: (1) the $42.50 core in funding_valuation versus $1,428B in financials, a $166B gap from two different share counts; (2) the claim in exit that a combination would carry a premium, which the arithmetic in S135 contradicts at market values; (3) what stops a short squeeze or index flow from keeping a 431x free-cash-flow multiple alive, given short interest of only 2.19% of the float (S114) and a five-year return of +0.1% (S15).
answers.downside_survival: Yes, on every branch except the merger. A market 50% smaller halves automotive and services revenue to $45.5B and energy to $6.2B, which at 1.0x and 3.5x sales plus $36.2B of net cash gives $105B, or $26 a share, with autonomy at 94% of the price. Customer acquisition cost doubling takes SG&A per delivery from $4,142 to $8,284 (S4), adds $8.1B a year and turns $2.9B of operating profit into about -$5.2B. Revenue 30% lower at a 19% gross margin removes $6.0B of gross profit and, against $19.1B of annualised operating expense, leaves operating cash flow of $0 to -$2B, so with $20-25B of capex the company burns $20-27B a year and exhausts $36.18B of net cash plus the $30B September 2026 facilities before 2029 (S4, S6). Financing six months late needs no raise at all: net cash covers about 1.5 years of zero free cash flow. Multiples compressing to the 16.5x peer median or 5x sales gives about $130 a share (S15, S115), still above the probability-weighted value. The one branch that does not survive is a ratio premium in a SpaceX exchange (S135).
answers.ocr_claims: There are no OCR-derived claims. No client documents were attached to this request, and every figure used in section 10 comes from an SEC filing (S3, S4, S5), market data (S15, S115), a regulator or court record (S116, S136), or a dated public report I retrieved and registered (S134, S135, S137, S138). The share-count test was run without OCR: $1,594.1B divided by $403.30 equals 3,952.6M and $1,428B divided by $403.30 equals 3,541M, and an independent report putting Tesla at $1.48 trillion on a $373.71 close on 2026-10-20 implies about 3,960M shares (S135), confirming that $1,594.1B is the market-convention figure and the $1,428B in financials was struck on the diluted EPS denominator.

rows.finding: Tesla began paid Cybercab robotaxi rides in Austin on 2026-09-03 and reached 'nearly two million' cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles by 2026-09-30; the company claimed 300+ Cybercabs serving Austin on 2026-10-10 (8x in 30 days), while Texas registration showed 319 authorised Cybercab VINs.
rows.mechanism: Autonomy only becomes a take-rate business once unsupervised miles are large enough to price utilisation, insurance and remote assistance; a ~2 million-mile base is too small to prove either safety or unit economics.
rows.benchmark: Waymo: ~4,000 robotaxis, 500,000 paid rides a week, 15 US cities and 1,102 AVs registered in Texas as of 2026-09-24.
rows.weakens: Company fleet counts mix registered, serving and unsupervised vehicles; Tesla has not disclosed how many Cybercabs run without a safety monitor, nor robotaxi revenue or fares.
rows.implication: Value robotaxi revenue at close to zero for 2026 and 2027 and treat fleet disclosures as marketing until unsupervised miles and revenue are separated; wait for the Q2 2027 milestone.
rows.confidence: high on the facts, low on capability
rows.follow_up: What are paid robotaxi rides, revenue and revenue per vehicle per week in Austin, and how many Cybercabs operate without a monitor?

rows.finding: Tesla's own FSD (Supervised) safety report (October 2026) states one major collision per 6,006,200 miles with FSD engaged in North America against a 660,164-mile US average; NHTSA's Engineering Analysis EA26002 (opened 2026-03-19) covers about 2.88 million Tesla vehicles over 13 reduced-visibility crashes.
rows.mechanism: Safety statistics are the pricing input for insurance and the gating input for unsupervised permits; a company-computed, non-fault-based rate cannot substitute for the regulator's crash-level data.
rows.benchmark: Tesla's prior February 2026 report was ~5.3 million miles per major collision; the US human baseline used is 660,164 miles.
rows.weakens: The comparison is not fault-based, is not independently audited, and is vulnerable to exposure mix (highway-heavy FSD miles) and under-reporting; the regulator has opened an engineering analysis rather than closing the question.
rows.implication: Discount the 9x claim materially in any safety-based valuation; the permit path in California and the EU depends on the regulator's data, not Tesla's report.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: Has EA26002 been upgraded to a recall request, and what do California DMV collision reports show per million FSD miles?

rows.finding: Giga Texas produces more than 1 million 4680 cells a week at ~40 GWh installed capacity; both electrodes use the dry process in production since January 2026 with yields above 90%, but energy density is 10-15% below competitors and 10-80% charging takes 35-40 minutes.
rows.mechanism: Dry electrode cuts electrode cost toward 50%, line capex by ~41% and factory energy by more than 30%, which lowers cost per kWh without improving cell performance — a cost moat, not a product moat.
rows.benchmark: CATL and Panasonic run above 98% yield on mature chemistries; CATL's Qilin 3 claims a full charge in six minutes; Cybercell is 272 Wh/kg versus 244 Wh/kg for Gen 1.
rows.weakens: The density and charging gap means 4680 cannot carry the premium segments; Tesla still buys CATL LFP and Panasonic/LG 2170 cells for Shanghai and Fremont Model Y.
rows.implication: Credit Tesla with a real but narrow manufacturing advantage worth basis points of automotive gross margin, not a technology rent; the affordable platform, not the cell, is the volume swing factor.
rows.confidence: medium (single detailed secondary source plus company statements)
rows.follow_up: What is Tesla's blended pack cost per kWh in 2026 and what share of packs are in-house 4680 versus purchased cells?

rows.finding: Energy storage: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026 (36.0 GWh in 9M 2026) at a 33.1% segment gross margin ($954m gross profit), with record order rate and backlog; segment revenue nevertheless fell 16% YoY to $2.881bn on tariff refunds, lower Megapack ASP and fewer Powerwall deployments; Megafactory Texas (50 GWh planned) began production.
rows.mechanism: US-localised cells and integrated Megapack/Megablock plus Autobidder software earn a price premium in a market where grid connection and data-centre uptime matter more than hardware cost; Chinese cells set the cost floor under that premium.
rows.benchmark: Wood Mackenzie's first BESS integrator ranking (2026-07) puts Sungrow first, Tesla second, CATL third, BYD fourth and Fluence seventh; CATL held 27.1% of H1 2026 ESS cell shipments (125.0 GWh of 461.3 GWh).
rows.weakens: Volume up while revenue falls shows ASP deflation; tariff refunds flattered the quarter; the ranking shows Tesla is not the scale leader.
rows.implication: Energy is the most provable part of the equity story and deserves a real multiple, but margin, not volume, is the variable to underwrite.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What is the Megapack backlog in GWh and dollars, and what gross margin holds when tariff refunds and OBBBA cell-cost increases normalise?

rows.finding: Optimus production began on high-volume lines at Fremont and was announced 2026-10-21; Tesla disclosed no unit count, no external customer and no revenue, while Musk claimed 20,000 units a week by end-2027 and called the ramp 'bumpy'.
rows.mechanism: A humanoid only creates value if task throughput and uptime beat the loaded cost of labour; without disclosed tasks, cycle times or customer deployments there is no measurable productivity claim.
rows.benchmark: Published Optimus Gen 3 patents (priority 2024-10-10, published 2026-04-16) describe a 22-DoF tendon-driven hand that Musk said in April 2026 the V3 would not use because the design 'did not work' — the disclosed hardware already trails the programme.
rows.weakens: The strongest company claims (production-quality bots, 20,000 a week) are unverified; no third party has validated factory task performance.
rows.implication: Carry Optimus at zero in the base case and treat it as a free option whose first proof point is disclosed units and paid external deployments, not a reveal event.
rows.confidence: high that it is pre-commercial; low on any volume forecast
rows.follow_up: How many Optimus units were built and deployed in Q3 2026, doing which tasks, with what uptime, and is any unit sold to an external customer?

rows.finding: Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3 2026 (-2.13% YoY) versus BYD's 762,478 passenger BEVs (+30.89% YoY); 9M 2026 Tesla 1,324,681 against BYD 1,629,957; Model 3/Y were 98.3% of deliveries and regulatory credit revenue fell 73% YoY to $113m.
rows.mechanism: Without a lower-cost platform Tesla cannot cut price and hold margin while Chinese competitors scale; the credit income that once subsidised margin is now immaterial.
rows.benchmark: BYD overtook Tesla as the world's largest BEV seller in 2025 (2,256,714 vs 1,636,129) and widened its Q3 2026 lead to 275,946 units from 76,964 in Q2 2026.
rows.weakens: Tesla's 9M 2026 deliveries still grew 8.77% YoY and Q3 beat consensus by 4.9%, so the volume story is flat rather than collapsing.
rows.implication: The next-generation affordable platform is the single largest swing factor in the vehicle business; absence of a launch date is a reason to underwrite flat volume.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What is the launch date, price and capacity of the next-generation platform, and what gross margin is assumed at that price?

rows.finding: NHTSA lists eight recall campaigns covering 2026 Model Y between 2025-05-30 and 2026-09-01 (suspension fasteners, bumpers, labels, fuses, wiring, horn, seat fasteners, wiper linkages); none is an ADAS or FSD campaign.
rows.mechanism: Mechanical build quality drives warranty and collision-repair cost, which is now visible as a profit centre: services and other gross profit reached a record $734m in Q3 2026.
rows.benchmark: Eight campaigns in about 16 months is high for a single model year against premium German benchmarks, but the absence of an FSD recall is a point in favour of the ADAS record so far.
rows.weakens: It weakens the 'engineering excellence' narrative and shows launch-quality slippage on the highest-volume product.
rows.implication: Underwrite higher warranty and service cost, and read services gross profit as partly a quality-cost offset rather than pure growth.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What is warranty expense as a percentage of automotive revenue in 2026, and how much of services gross profit is collision repair of Tesla vehicles?

plan.decision_question: Is Tesla's technology — FSD/robotaxi, next-generation platform and cells, Megapack — proven at a level that creates a durable cost or capability advantage, and on what timeline?
plan.thesis_sentence: Tesla's technology is proven where it is a manufacturing problem — dry-electrode cells and Megapack integration — and unproven where the valuation sits: about 2 million cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles, a 300-plus Cybercab Austin fleet and a Texas-only paid driverless permit against Waymo's ~4,000 vehicles and 500,000 paid rides a week mean autonomy is a 2027-2029 option, not a 2026 capability.
plan.why_different: This section tests technical proof, performance benchmarks and replication time; the market section tests share and demand, financials test revenue quality and cost per unit, and strategy tests capital allocation.
plan.mechanism: Cell cost per kWh sets the floor under vehicle gross margin and Megapack price; autonomy converts a one-off hardware sale into a per-mile take rate only when unsupervised miles are large enough to price insurance and utilisation; training compute and fleet data are the inputs that compound.
plan.comparison_set: Waymo/Alphabet on autonomy depth, BYD and CATL on cell and vehicle cost, Sungrow, CATL, BYD and Fluence on storage integration, Rivian and Xiaomi on EV product execution; base rate is that no vision-only system had demonstrated unsupervised operation at Waymo's mileage before 2026.
plan.counter_evidence: FSD attach rate reached more than 75% of North American deliveries in Q3 2026 with 1.74 million active subscriptions and deferred revenue up $1.24bn in the quarter, dry electrode is not replicated by CATL, Panasonic or LG, and Megapack earned a 33.1% gross margin while revenue fell 16% — demand and pricing power in energy are real even if autonomy slips.
plan.visual: Performance metrics table by technology, then the technology comparison table against Waymo, BYD and CATL, then the moat/replication table.
plan.prohibited: strong team; high barriers to entry; well positioned; huge market; many patents; about 5; fiercely competitive; risks are manageable; recently

rows.finding: Tesla reported 2.0 million cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles to 2026-09-30; a third-party tracker puts Waymo at about 3,000 vehicles and 500,000 paid rides a week across 10 US cities in October 2026.
rows.mechanism: Autonomy value scales with rider-only miles and rides, not with supervised fleet miles; the gap is two orders of magnitude in weekly paid rides.
rows.benchmark: Waymo 500,000 paid rides a week on about 3,000 vehicles; Tesla 2.0 million cumulative unsupervised miles.
rows.weakens: No operator discloses audited paid rides or fleet counts; the 3,000 figure comes from a low-confidence tracker, and Waymo's own February 2026 disclosure does not give a fleet number.
rows.implication: The autonomy premium is being paid for a pilot; position size should price the probability of scale, not assume it.
rows.confidence: medium on Tesla's miles (company KPI), low on the Waymo fleet count.
rows.follow_up: What are Waymo's audited weekly rides and vehicles at the Q4 2026 update, and Tesla's paid rides per week in Austin?

rows.source_type: independent (low, medium); primary regulator reference via secondary
rows.finding: Tesla has never published a robotaxi fleet count. Third-party records show 769 Teslas registered for autonomous use in Texas on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, after 44 active vehicles across seven metros in H1 2026; Tesla claimed 300-plus Cybercabs in Austin on 2026-10-10 and NHTSA's DP26010 describes a monitored fleet of 1,000.
rows.mechanism: Registration and monitoring counts measure deployed hardware, not commercial utilisation; the gap between 769 registered, 300-plus claimed and 1,000 monitored shows no single audited operating number exists.
rows.benchmark: Waymo's single fleet count versus Tesla's three inconsistent counts.
rows.weakens: The registration figure is low-confidence and unconfirmed by Tesla or Texas DMV; the 1,000 is NHTSA's scope, not Tesla's operating fleet.
rows.implication: Investors cannot size the robotaxi business from public data; treat fleet-scale claims as unverified until a regulatory filing or company KPI fixes one number.
rows.confidence: low on the 769/349 split, medium on the DP26010 scope.
rows.follow_up: Can Texas DMV confirm the 2026-10-14 registration count and the Cybercab subset?

rows.finding: Tesla's target of 20,000 Optimus units a week by end-2027 was stated on the 2026-10-21 call; no unit count, external customer, task list or revenue has been disclosed. Figure AI's Figure 02 completed an 11-month deployment at BMW's Spartanburg plant contributing to more than 30,000 X3 vehicles, and Figure was valued at $39bn in September 2025.
rows.mechanism: A humanoid is a product only when an external customer pays per unit or per task; without a customer, output targets are manufacturing claims, not demand.
rows.benchmark: Figure AI's named BMW deployment and private $39bn mark versus Optimus's internal factory use.
rows.weakens: Figure's deployment metrics are company-reported and unaudited, and its valuation is a private funding mark; no humanoid maker discloses repeat revenue.
rows.implication: Assign the humanoid branch a lower probability than robotaxi until a named customer and a billed unit exist.
rows.confidence: high that Tesla has disclosed no customer; medium on Figure's deployment detail.
rows.follow_up: Has any external customer taken delivery of Optimus, and at what price per unit or task?

rows.finding: The Q3 2026 update claims a record order rate and backlog for Megapack, but Tesla discloses neither GWh nor dollars of contracted backlog; energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881bn on lower prices while 13.7 GWh was deployed at a 33.1% gross margin.
rows.mechanism: Backlog is only valuable if it converts at a price above the cost of new capacity; falling revenue per GWh while volume rises means capacity is being added into deflation.
rows.benchmark: CATL's 27.1% ESS cell share and Sungrow's lead in integrator rankings versus Tesla's second place.
rows.weakens: The backlog claim is unverifiable and the revenue decline is partly tariff refunds and mix; gross margin still rose.
rows.implication: Energy is the proven business but not yet a pricing-power business; value it at an integrator multiple, not a software one.
rows.confidence: high on the figures, low on the backlog claim.
rows.follow_up: What contracted backlog in GWh or dollars sits behind the record order rate, and at what price per GWh?

rows.finding: Giga Texas runs more than 1 million 4680 cells a week at more than 40 GWh, with both electrodes dry since January 2026, yields above 90% and 272 Wh/kg; energy density trails CATL by 10-15% and Tesla still buys CATL LFP and Panasonic or LG 2170 cells for Shanghai and Fremont.
rows.mechanism: Dry electrode lowers capex and energy per cell, which matters in a price war; it does not close the density and charging gap, so Tesla remains a buyer of others' cells at the volume end.
rows.benchmark: CATL Qilin 3 charging and density; Panasonic 2170 packs.
rows.weakens: Output and yield figures are teardown and line estimates, not audited disclosures; the cost advantage is modelled at full scale.
rows.implication: The cell moat is real on cost and narrow on performance; it supports the automotive margin but not a technology multiple.
rows.confidence: medium.
rows.follow_up: What is Tesla's blended pack cost per kWh in Q4 2026, and how much 4680 output goes into energy storage rather than vehicles?

plan.decision_question: Is Tesla's technology — FSD/robotaxi, next-generation platform and cells, Megapack — proven at a level that creates a durable cost or capability advantage, and on what timeline?
plan.thesis_sentence: Tesla's technology is proven where it is a manufacturing problem — dry-electrode cells, Megapack integration — and unproven where the valuation sits, judged against Waymo in autonomy and BYD in manufacturing cost.
plan.why_different: This section tests the technology claim itself against named rivals and regulators, not the market size or the financial statements; it is the only place the autonomy, cell and energy claims are graded on evidence.
plan.mechanism: Value accrues to whoever converts a technical lead into paid units: rider-only miles for autonomy, cost per kWh for cells, revenue per GWh for storage. Tesla leads on manufacturing process and trails on autonomy scale and cell density.
plan.comparison_set: Waymo on autonomy scale and sensing, BYD on BEV cost and volume, CATL and Panasonic on cells, Sungrow and CATL on storage integration, Figure AI on humanoids.

plan.visual: The technology comparison table with Tesla against Waymo, CATL, BYD and Figure AI, plus the evidence component on the unverified Optimus target.
plan.prohibited: No 'industry-leading', 'best-in-class', 'moat' without a difficulty score, no unlabelled company claim, no 'many patents', no vague counts.

rows.finding: Tesla, Inc. was incorporated in Delaware on 2003-07-01 and converted to a Texas corporation on 2024-06-13; it has one class of common stock with 3,952,648,559 shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, listed on Nasdaq under TSLA.
rows.mechanism: Domicile and single-class structure mean voting power is proportional to economic ownership; there is no dual-class charter for a founder to fall back on, so control must be built through equity awards.
rows.benchmark: Ford's Class B shares carry 16 votes each and give the family about 40% of voting power on roughly 2% of shares [S95].
rows.weakens: Single class is the minority-shareholder-friendly feature; the reincorporation to Texas moved litigation to a court with no precedent on the 2025 award.
rows.implication: Governance risk is not a permanent dual-class wedge; it is contestable and tied to how much of the CEO award is earned, so model dilution rather than a fixed control discount.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Which Texas state court would hear a challenge to the 2025 award, and has one been filed?

rows.finding: Elon Musk beneficially owns 699,580,882 shares, 19.8% of the 2026-09-30 count, including 286,428,773 restricted shares from the 2018 award and 207,498,721 shares pledged as collateral; the 423,743,904 unearned 2025 award shares are excluded from his beneficial ownership.
rows.mechanism: A 19.8% stake plus CEO office and board seat delivers effective control; the pledge means a margin call or forced sale could hit the register at the same time as bad news.
rows.benchmark: Ford family: ~40% of votes on ~2% economic [S95]; Vanguard holds 5.3% of Tesla, the only other disclosed 5% holder [S5].
rows.weakens: Unearned award shares vote proportionately to all other shares, so Musk's voting share does not rise until tranches are earned.
rows.implication: Treat the 207.5M pledged shares as a tail risk that would amplify a drawdown; free float is at most ~74.9% after Musk and Vanguard.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Loan-to-value and lender identity of the pledge; not disclosed.

rows.finding: The 2025 CEO Performance Award is 423,743,904 shares (10.7% of shares outstanding) in 12 tranches tied to market-cap milestones from $2.0 trillion to $8.5 trillion and 12 operational milestones; none earned as of 2026-10-19; unrecognised stock compensation is $9.74bn for the one probable milestone and $105.82bn-$120.37bn for the improbable ones.
rows.mechanism: Dilution is contingent but real: each $0.5 trillion band from $2.0 trillion releases 35,311,992 shares, and a change of control drops the operational test, paying on deal price alone [S78].
rows.benchmark: The 2018 award, reinstated by the Delaware Supreme Court on 2025-12-19, delivered 286,428,773 restricted shares and was exercised in June 2026.
rows.weakens: At a $2.0 trillion market cap no tranche is earned and no shares are issued; tranches 11 and 12 also require board approval of a succession framework Musk writes.
rows.implication: Underwrite a 10.7% overhang above a $2.0 trillion valuation and a governance mechanism that pays the CEO on a merger without any robotaxi or Optimus milestone.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: How would a Tesla-SpaceX exchange ratio be set and who negotiates for Tesla?

rows.finding: Related-party flows: Tesla agreed on 2026-01-16 to invest about $2.00bn in xAI Series E, converted into SpaceX Class A stock when SpaceX acquired xAI on 2026-02-02 and funded on 2026-03-12; 2025 revenue from xAI was $430.1mn and from SpaceX $143.3mn, and Tesla paid a Musk-owned security firm $4.8mn.
rows.mechanism: The CEO sits on both sides of a $2bn capital allocation and of the largest trading counterparties, so minority holders rely on an Audit Committee whose members include directors with SpaceX ties.
rows.benchmark: The related-party policy review threshold is $120,000, so every one of these flows passed an Audit Committee review [S5].
rows.weakens: Combined 2025 revenue from both parties is ~0.6% of Tesla's $94.8bn, and the $2.00bn is ~4.4% of cash and investments, so the economics are small next to the governance signal.
rows.implication: Price a standing related-party discount: capital can be directed to Musk entities at valuations minority holders do not set.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What valuation was used for the xAI Series E and did any independent adviser opine on it?

rows.finding: The nine-seat board is classified into three classes; six directors are independent under Nasdaq rules, but compensation and governance committee chair Ira Ehrenpreis has sat on SpaceX's board since February 2026, Kimbal Musk is the CEO's brother, and JB Straubel runs Redwood, a Tesla counterparty with $3.3mn of 2025 purchases.
rows.mechanism: Conflicts sit exactly where a merger or pay decision would be decided: the committees that set CEO pay and police conflicts are chaired by a director with a seat on the likely merger counterparty.
rows.benchmark: Tesla labels Ehrenpreis independent; a shareholder-approved 2025 proposal to declassify the board drew 39.4% of shares outstanding, short of the bar, and the board will not bring it back [S78].
rows.weakens: The Special Committee that designed the 2025 award used only Denholm and Wilson-Thompson, and compensation consultants advised it.
rows.implication: Board independence cannot be relied on to stop a value-extractive transaction; require a special committee with no SpaceX ties as a condition of holding.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Will the 2026 say-on-pay vote show a minority of support, and do large index holders disclose votes against Denholm?

rows.finding: Delaware litigation ended in the CEO's favour (Supreme Court 2025-12-19, Chancery order 2026-03-18) and the 96,000,000-share 2025 interim award was forfeited on 2026-04-21; a securities class action filed 2025-08-04 in the Western District of Texas covers purchasers from 2023-04-19 to 2025-06-22 over Autopilot, FSD and Robotaxi statements.
rows.mechanism: Removing the Delaware overhang converted a contingent governance risk into a realised 19.8% stake plus a live disclosure claim, shifting legal risk from compensation to product claims.
rows.benchmark: The certified 2025 vote approving the award was 1,892,235,822 for and 564,940,908 against, about 77% of votes cast [S26].
rows.weakens: The class action is at pleading stage and no liability is recorded; the company describes the claims as alleging violations, not admitted facts [S3].
rows.implication: Litigation is a disclosure and damages risk, not a control risk; the bigger control event is a potential SpaceX combination.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Docket status of the W.D. Tex. class action and any motion to dismiss ruling in 2026.

rows.finding: Capital allocation: no dividend has ever been paid, no shares were repurchased in 2025 (Item 5 shows none), cash and short-term investments were $45.45bn at 2026-09-30, 2026 capex is guided above $20bn, and in September 2026 Tesla signed three credit agreements with aggregate commitments of $30bn.
rows.mechanism: Growth capex plus debt commitments replace buybacks and dividends, so per-share value depends on the return on AI, robot and energy investment rather than on capital returns.
rows.benchmark: Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow $14.90bn against capex $13.01bn leaves $1.9bn of free cash flow before the Q3 figure of $1.5bn for the quarter [S4, S6].
rows.weakens: The balance sheet is still net-cash-like with $45.45bn of liquidity, so the $30bn commitments are optionality rather than distress borrowing.
rows.implication: An investor is funding a capex programme with no capital-return floor; the buyback authorisation is nil, so dilution from stock compensation is not offset.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Terms, pricing and drawdown of the three September 2026 credit agreements.

rows.finding: Insiders filed no open-market purchases in the 12 months to 2026-09-09 and sold 207,882 shares for $87.69mn, of which directors Wilson-Thompson ($29.95mn), Murdoch ($26.72mn) and Kimbal Musk ($25.61mn) accounted for most; the CFO's $5.41mn was tax-withholding.
rows.mechanism: Director sales into a $360-$450 price range with zero insider buying signal that the people closest to the 2027-2028 milestones are not adding exposure.
rows.benchmark: Zero purchases against $87.69mn of sales is a one-sided tape; Form 4 filings in the same window include the 423,743,904-share CEO grant and the 96,000,000-share forfeiture.
rows.weakens: Director sales are small relative to holdings and several were 10b5-1 plans set in advance, so they are weak evidence of a view.
rows.implication: Do not treat insider activity as a positive signal; it is at best neutral and at worst a warning about near-term conviction.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Any 2026 Form 4 purchases after 2026-09-09, and 10b5-1 plan adoption dates.

plan.decision_question: Is Tesla's legal, capital and control structure one a public-equity investor can underwrite for a multi-year hold — who owns it, who controls capital allocation, and how much dilution is outstanding or contingent?
plan.thesis_sentence: Tesla is a single-class Texas corporation whose control rests on a 19.8% CEO stake plus a 423.7 million-share contingent award, so a public-equity holder is underwriting Elon Musk's capital allocation rather than a board-governed company — acceptable only at a governance discount, not at a premium.
plan.why_different: This section covers identity, control and contingent dilution; it does not re-argue growth, margins or valuation, which belong to the financial, market and valuation sections.
plan.mechanism: Control is built through equity: a 19.8% stake, a 10.7% contingent award whose unearned shares vote proportionately and whose change-of-control terms pay on deal price, and a board whose conflict committees include directors tied to SpaceX, the likely merger counterparty. Dilution and related-party capital allocation are therefore the two channels through which minority value is transferred.
plan.comparison_set: Ford (dual-class family control at ~40% of votes on ~2% of shares), GM and Alphabet (single- or multi-class peers), and Tesla's own 2018 award, which delivered 286.4 million shares after a Delaware reversal.
plan.counter_evidence: Tesla has one share class with proportional votes, no poison pill disclosed, a special committee that used an outside consultant, and a $45bn liquidity cushion; the related-party flows are under 1% of revenue and no award tranche has been earned, so the control discount may be smaller than the bear case assumes.
plan.visual: kpi component plus the legal-entity table and cap table, with the timeline covering 2003-2026 legal, award and litigation milestones.
plan.prohibited: Do not call the board 'independent' without qualification, do not present the award as certain dilution, do not use 'Musk discount' as a substitute for a mechanism, and do not state a share price or market cap without a timestamped source.

strategy.author: Product Analyst
queries: Tesla capex 2027 plan Optimus robotaxi spend guidance October 2026 earnings call
Tesla Samsung AI5 AI6 chip deal 2026 $16.5 billion Taylor Texas
Tesla xAI investment shareholder vote 2025 $2 billion SpaceX stake 2026
Tesla FSD China approval 2026 Shanghai sales decline localisation
BYD global sales 2026 third quarter NEV deliveries versus Tesla
Tesla robotaxi California CPUC permit DMV driverless 2026 Texas AV registry Cybercab
Tesla Optimus 2026 production units built tasks factory
Megapack market share 2026 energy storage CATL Fluence Sungrow Tesla ranking

rows.finding: Tesla guided to capital expenditure 'in excess of $20 billion' for 2026 (10-Q, 2026-10-22), after $13.01bn in the first nine months versus $6.13bn a year earlier, and signed three credit agreements for aggregate commitments of $30bn in September 2026; cash and short-term investments were $45.45bn at 2026-09-30.
rows.mechanism: Capex is shifting from vehicles (revenue-producing within 18 months) to compute, robots and fabs (no revenue until at least 2027-2028), so depreciation rises before revenue does.
rows.benchmark: BYD and CATL fund capacity from operating cash flow; Tesla's 2026 capex equals about 20% of trailing revenue.
rows.weakens: Guidance of 'in excess' leaves the final number open, and the $30bn facilities may be precautionary rather than needed.
rows.implication: The plan is funded but no longer self-funding; the balance sheet buys time, not a return. Price the equity on 2028 cash flows, not 2026.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: How much of the $30bn facilities is drawn by 2027, and what is the 2027 capex number on the Q4 2026 call?

rows.finding: Nine-month 2026 operating income was $2.057bn and net income $2.378bn against $89.29bn of stockholders' equity at 2026-09-30; annualising operating income after a 25% tax rate over roughly $71bn of invested capital gives a return on invested capital near 3%.
rows.mechanism: When operating income is small relative to invested capital, each additional billion of capex lowers ROIC until the new assets generate revenue; energy and services are the only segments currently earning an adequate return.
rows.benchmark: A plausible cost of capital of 8-10% for a cyclical, capital-intensive manufacturer with policy exposure.
rows.weakens: ROIC is depressed by the 2025 CEO award stock compensation and by assets still in ramp; a 2028 denominator could look very different if robotaxi and energy scale.
rows.implication: The strategy does not currently clear its cost of capital; the equity is a call option on autonomy, and position size should reflect that, not the current earnings yield.
rows.confidence: medium (analyst calculation from filing figures)
rows.follow_up: What is the company's own ROIC definition and WACC disclosure, and what does management assume for robotaxi payback?

rows.finding: Unsupervised FSD for customer-owned cars slipped to about Q2 2027 (Ashok Elluswamy, Q3 2026 call) from Musk's April 2026 target of Q4 2026, while paid Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03 and California still holds only a testing-with-driver permit.
rows.mechanism: The strategy's return depends on converting 7-8 million owner cars into a fleet without capex; each delay keeps the robotaxi fleet capital-intensive and small.
rows.benchmark: Musk said in April 2026 the unsupervised version would 'probably' ship in Q4 2026; Tesla has promised a robotaxi capability in some form since 2016.
rows.weakens: Tesla delivered a real, paid driverless service in Texas within 15 months of launch, faster than most incumbents; the slip is quarters, not years.
rows.implication: Discount every autonomy date by at least two quarters; the milestone that matters for the model is customer-owned unsupervised revenue, not fleet size.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Does any customer-owned car drive unsupervised by 2027-06-30, and in which states does Tesla hold a driverless deployment permit beyond Texas?

rows.finding: Optimus production began at Fremont (announced 2026-10-21) with no units, customers or revenue disclosed, while Musk targets 20,000 units a week by end-2027 and Tesla is building Texas Optimus capacity.
rows.mechanism: Optimus absorbs capex and engineering time before any revenue; it is the most speculative claim on capital in the plan and the one with the weakest disclosure.
rows.benchmark: Tesla's 2025 target of roughly 5,000 Optimus units was missed; the 2026 target of 50,000-100,000 units is not corroborated by any disclosed build count.
rows.weakens: This is company-only disclosure; no external customer, price or task-performance data exists to verify commercial readiness.
rows.implication: Underwrite zero Optimus revenue through 2027 and treat announcements as marketing until paid external deployments are disclosed.
rows.confidence: high that it is pre-revenue; low on any volume
rows.follow_up: What is the 2026 Optimus build count, the unit price and the first external customer?

rows.finding: Tesla committed $16.5bn to Samsung through 2033 for AI6 chips at Taylor, Texas, with AI5 taped out on Samsung's 2nm line in July 2026, and is building the Austin Fab for its own semiconductor production with equipment commissioning planned in 2027; training compute is to reach 400 MW by end-2026 from 225 MW installed.
rows.mechanism: Owning inference silicon lowers cost per vehicle and per robot, but fab construction and single-foundry dependence add capital intensity and execution risk ahead of revenue.
rows.benchmark: Tesla's own vertical integration in cells took five years from Battery Day (2020) to full dry-electrode production (2026).
rows.weakens: The 400 MW target requires adding 175 MW in one quarter, and the Austin Fab will not produce wafers before 2028 at the earliest.
rows.implication: Compute is now the binding constraint on the autonomy timeline; a single-foundry dependence is a risk the market is not pricing.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What share of AI6 wafer supply is committed, and what happens to the autonomy roadmap if Samsung's Taylor yield ramps late?

rows.finding: China: Q3 2026 sales fell 16% YoY to 142,133 units while Giga Shanghai exports hit a record 132,978; FSD approval in China remains pending, with the CFO saying Tesla is working 'very diligently' with regulators; Beijing cuts the EV export tax rebate in April 2027.
rows.mechanism: Shanghai is becoming an export hub for markets that tariff Chinese-built cars, so volume, tariff exposure and FSD monetisation all weaken at once in Tesla's largest single factory.
rows.benchmark: China's share of global ESS battery shipments fell to 43.9% in H1 2026 from 50.5%, showing how fast policy can move localisation; BYD's domestic scale sets the price umbrella Tesla must match.
rows.weakens: Export growth offsets domestic decline today, and Shanghai capacity above 950,000 units remains the group's largest asset.
rows.implication: Treat China as a cost and export base, not a growth market, until FSD is approved there; a China pricing war is the most likely source of a negative surprise.
rows.confidence: medium (single trade-press source for the China split)
rows.follow_up: What are Tesla's China retail sales and FSD approval status at 2026-12-31, and how much of Shanghai output is exported to tariffed markets?

rows.finding: Capital allocation to Musk-controlled entities: Tesla bought $2.002bn of SpaceX equity in Q1 2026 after investing $2bn in xAI in January 2026 (the xAI stake converted into SpaceX Class A shares when SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026); three of nine directors have SpaceX ties and the 2026 proxy sets a 2026-12-03 meeting with a change-of-control pay mechanic that drops operational milestones.
rows.mechanism: Related-party capital flows and a possible merger shift the return on Tesla's cash from its own roadmap to Musk's wider portfolio, and the CEO award pays on deal price rather than on robotaxi or Optimus delivery.
rows.benchmark: Only one of twelve operational milestones in the 2025 CEO award is rated probable, leaving $105.8-120.4bn of unrecognised stock compensation — the market is paying for milestones management itself does not expect soon.
rows.weakens: The SpaceX stake has appreciated and is a liquid asset; shareholders ratified the xAI investment in early 2026.
rows.implication: A merger or further related-party purchase is a real 2027 scenario; it changes the shareholder's exposure from a car and energy company to a Musk holding structure, which argues for a smaller position.
rows.confidence: high on facts, medium on interpretation
rows.follow_up: Will the December 2026 meeting put a SpaceX transaction to a vote, and what governance protections apply to related-party purchases?

rows.finding: Energy scale-up is the clearest resource-fit story: Megafactory Texas began production in Q3 2026 with 50 GWh planned capacity alongside 40 GWh in California and 20 GWh in Shanghai, plus 7 GWh of Nevada LFP cell capacity in early ramp and the first Megapacks built with Tesla-made LFP cells.
rows.mechanism: Localising cells and packs inside the US avoids tariff and OBBBA cell-cost exposure while data-centre demand gives Megapack a second demand engine beyond utilities.
rows.benchmark: Global ESS battery shipments grew 71% YoY in H1 2026 to 461.3 GWh; Tesla ranks second among integrators behind Sungrow (Wood Mackenzie, 2026-07).
rows.weakens: Segment revenue fell 16% YoY in Q3 2026 on lower Megapack ASP, so capacity is arriving into a price-deflating market.
rows.implication: Energy deserves funded growth capital; autonomy and Optimus do not yet deserve the same certainty.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What is the energy backlog in GWh and dollars, and what gross margin survives the loss of tariff refunds?

plan.decision_question: Does Tesla's strategy — vertical integration, price competition, energy scale-up and autonomy-first capital allocation — earn a return above its cost of capital?
plan.thesis_sentence: Tesla's strategy has become a capital-allocation bet rather than an operating one: more than $20bn of 2026 capex and $30bn of new credit facilities are being committed to autonomy, robots and semiconductors while nine-month 2026 operating income of $2.06bn implies a return on invested capital near 3%, below any plausible cost of capital, so the strategy earns its keep only if unsupervised robotaxi revenue arrives before 2028.
plan.why_different: This section tests whether resources fit the plan and which dated milestones would prove it; section 3 tests technical proof, section 5 demand, section 7 unit economics and section 10 the price paid, so no revenue or market-share analysis is repeated here.
plan.mechanism: Capex converts cash into autonomy, robot and semiconductor assets whose payback depends on unsupervised revenue; if that revenue slips, depreciation and R&D rise against flat volume and return on invested capital stays below the cost of capital, while energy and services are the only segments currently earning above it.
plan.comparison_set: Waymo/Alphabet as a funded autonomy benchmark, BYD as the vertically integrated cost competitor, Tesla's own 2019-2021 Shanghai ramp as the base rate for its capacity ramps, and Tesla's own history of robotaxi promises from 2016 onward as the base rate for its timelines.
plan.counter_evidence: The plan is fully funded ($45.45bn cash, $30bn undrawn facilities, $1.53bn Q3 free cash flow), FSD attach reached 75% in North America and energy has a record backlog, so the capex may buy a real option rather than a stranded asset; 2026 capex guidance has been held near $20bn rather than escalated.
plan.visual: Milestone table with target dates, status and what each proves, followed by the partner table.
plan.prohibited: strong team; high barriers to entry; well positioned; huge market; fierce competition; risks are manageable; recently; clear business model

rows.finding: 2026 capex above $20bn after $13.01bn in the first nine months; three credit agreements for $30bn signed in September 2026; nine-month operating income $2.06bn on $89.29bn of equity.
rows.mechanism: Capex converts to return only when the new assets sell; until robotaxi and Optimus revenue appear, every billion lowers ROIC.
rows.benchmark: Trailing ROIC of 5.5% and an 11-14% cost of capital implied by a Baa3 rating.
rows.weakens: Ramp assets depress the ratio and $45.45bn of cash means the plan is funded; a single large autonomy or energy contract would change the arithmetic.
rows.implication: The strategy consumes capital faster than it earns it; a position is a bet on 2028-2031 returns, so it should be sized as an option.
rows.confidence: high on the figures, medium on the invested-capital denominator.
rows.follow_up: What is the 2027 capex number and how much is contractually committed?

rows.finding: The 12-month test is customer-owned unsupervised driving around Q2 2027, slipped from Q4 2026; paid Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03 and no robotaxi revenue line is disclosed.
rows.mechanism: Owner-fleet unsupervised FSD converts existing vehicles into robotaxi supply without Tesla capex, which is the only route to scale that does not consume the balance sheet.
rows.benchmark: Waymo's scaled paid service versus Tesla's pilot.
rows.weakens: The date has already slipped once and NHTSA's EA26002 could push it further.
rows.implication: Do not underwrite autonomy revenue before the Q1-Q2 2027 release; the milestone is the proof event, not the reveal.
rows.confidence: medium.
rows.follow_up: Will the Q4 2026 update disclose robotaxi revenue and fleet size?

rows.finding: Optimus began early production on 2026-10-21 with a company target of 20,000 units a week by end-2027; no unit count, customer, task list or revenue is disclosed.
rows.mechanism: A humanoid earns a return only when a customer pays per unit or per task; an internal factory target is a manufacturing claim, not demand.
rows.benchmark: Figure AI's BMW deployment and $39bn private mark.
rows.weakens: Tesla has a factory and a cost base Figure lacks; a 2027 customer announcement would invalidate the caution.
rows.implication: Treat the humanoid branch as an option with no revenue before 2029; it cannot carry the capex case.
rows.confidence: high that no customer is disclosed; medium on the target's provenance.
rows.follow_up: Has an external customer taken delivery, and at what price per unit or task?

rows.finding: The 2026-10-21 update claims a record order rate and backlog, but no GWh or dollar backlog is disclosed; energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881bn at a 33.1% gross margin.
rows.mechanism: Adding 50 GWh of Texas capacity into falling prices raises unit volume and lowers revenue per GWh, so return depends on cost per GWh falling faster than price.
rows.benchmark: Energy revenue per GWh and CATL's 27.1% ESS cell share.
rows.weakens: Margin rose to 33.1% even as revenue fell, and data-centre demand could reprice the backlog.
rows.implication: Energy earns the cost of capital today, but deflation limits how much of the capex it can carry.
rows.confidence: high on revenue and margin, low on the backlog claim.
rows.follow_up: What contracted backlog in GWh or dollars sits behind the record order rate?

rows.finding: China sales fell 16% year over year to 142,133 in Q3 2026 while Giga Shanghai exports reached a record 132,978; Beijing cuts the EV export tax rebate in April 2027.
rows.mechanism: Localisation lowers cost but shifts revenue to export markets exposed to tariffs and rebate changes, so the strategy trades growth for cost.
rows.benchmark: Tesla's pre-2022 China growth versus its current export-base role.
rows.weakens: Exports at record levels show the plant can earn even when domestic retail falls.
rows.implication: The China asset is a cost and export base, not a growth engine; it supports margin but adds policy risk to the plan.
rows.confidence: medium.
rows.follow_up: How much of Shanghai's output is export-dependent, and what tariff exposure follows the April 2027 rebate cut?

plan.why_different: This section connects the plan to the capital and the return, and asks which 2027 milestone would prove the strategy is working; it does not re-describe the products or re-forecast the financials.
