rows.finding: The US section 30D new clean vehicle credit applied only to vehicles acquired on or before 2025-09-30; the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (enacted 2025-07-04) terminated it and the used-vehicle 25E credit for acquisitions after that date. EIA reports BEV sales remain below pre-expiration levels in 2026.
rows.mechanism: Removing a $7,500 point-of-sale credit raises the effective transaction price of every US Tesla by roughly 10-15%, so volume must be defended with price cuts, subsidised financing or mix, compressing automotive gross margin.
rows.benchmark: Credit-supported 2024-2025 US BEV demand versus the post-2025-09-30 run-rate reported by EIA on 2026-10-19.
rows.weakens: Tesla's US buyer base skews affluent and lease-heavy, and some demand was pulled forward rather than destroyed; the credit loss is industry-wide, so relative share may hold.
rows.implication: Underwrite 2026-2028 US volume as a subsidy-free, price-elastic market and do not extrapolate 2025 deliveries; a demand recovery needs new products or autonomy, not incentives.
rows.confidence: high — IRS guidance, statute and EIA data agree on the date and direction.
rows.follow_up: What share of Tesla's 2025 US deliveries was lease-originated or credit-dependent, and how much of the 2026 US volume decline is permanent?

rows.finding: Automotive regulatory credit revenue was $2,763m in 2024, $1,993m in 2025 (-28%), $113m in Q3 2026 (-73% year on year) and $639m in the first nine months of 2026 (-56%).
rows.mechanism: Regulatory credits carry almost no cost of revenue, so their loss hits gross profit one-for-one: total automotive gross margin fell from 18.4% to 17.8% in 2025 partly because of the $770m credit decline, and the Q3 2026 collapse removes a similar high-margin contribution.
rows.benchmark: 2023 credit revenue of $1,790m and the 2024 peak of $2,763m; automotive gross margin of 18.4% in 2024.
rows.weakens: Credit revenue was always lumpy and was never guided, so part of the decline may already sit in consensus; the remaining $639m in 9M 2026 shows the pool has not gone to zero.
rows.implication: Value the auto business on a credit-free margin and treat any credit revenue as upside; the quality of Tesla's reported automotive margin is lower than the headline suggests.
rows.confidence: high — audited segment data and the Q3 2026 10-Q.
rows.follow_up: How much credit revenue is contracted for 2027, with which counterparties, and under which state or foreign programmes?

rows.finding: EPA's final rule published 2026-02-18 rescinds the 2009 endangerment finding and repeals all light-, medium- and heavy-duty GHG standards; the Department of Transportation finalised a rollback of CAFE standards on 2026-10-01.
rows.mechanism: The federal CO2 compliance market that created demand for Tesla's credits is being dismantled, and weaker CAFE pressure slows competitors' EV mix, removing both the credit pool and the relative cost advantage Tesla earned from selling compliance.
rows.benchmark: The 2024 multi-pollutant rule for model years 2027-2032, now repealed before it bound.
rows.weakens: California's ACC II and the Section 177 states can preserve a separate credit market, and litigation over the repeal could reinstate parts of the federal programme.
rows.implication: Assume structurally lower credit value in the US and a policy regime that no longer subsidises Tesla's cost position; this is a permanent earnings-quality change, not a one-quarter timing issue.
rows.confidence: high on the federal repeal; medium on whether state rules replace enough of the market.
rows.follow_up: Do California and the Section 177 states keep a credit market Tesla can sell into through 2028, and at what price?

rows.finding: Texas requires TxDMV authorisation for commercial SAE Level 4/5 operation from 2026-05-28 under SB 2807; CPUC's AV permit table lists Waymo, Zoox, Nuro, WeRide and Tensor but not Tesla, and Tesla's California service runs under a non-AV TCP/limousine authority.
rows.mechanism: Robotaxi revenue scales only where a state grants driverless commercial authority, so the addressable fleet is capped by permissions rather than by manufacturing capacity; Texas is a no-fee registration-style regime while California is a discretionary permit Tesla does not hold.
rows.benchmark: Waymo holds a CPUC driverless deployment permit; Zoox received a federal FMVSS exemption on 2026-07-31; Tesla holds a Texas authorisation and a California testing permit with a driver.
rows.weakens: Tesla already operates in Austin and expanded its Cybercab fleet to 300+ vehicles, and states may legalise after observing deployment; Texas alone is a large market.
rows.implication: Do not capitalise California or other states in the base case; size any position on Texas-plus-permitted jurisdictions and treat a California driverless permit as the catalyst that would justify a higher multiple.
rows.confidence: high on the regulatory record; medium on how quickly other states grant authority.
rows.follow_up: Has Tesla filed for a CPUC driverless deployment permit, and what is the application's status and operational design domain?

rows.finding: The SELF DRIVE Act of 2026 (H.R. 7390), which would create a national ADS framework and preempt state technical rules, advanced from a House subcommittee on a 12-11 party-line vote on 2026-02-10; it is not law as of 2026-10-29.
rows.mechanism: Federal preemption would convert a 50-state permission problem into a single compliance standard and could legalise steering-wheel-free vehicles nationwide, which is the main non-operational upside for Cybercab; until enacted, NHTSA defect investigations remain the binding federal constraint.
rows.benchmark: The 2017-2018 SELF DRIVE Act died in the Senate; a 12-11 subcommittee margin is narrower than the 2017 bipartisan committee votes.
rows.weakens: The bill is contested on party lines and has no Senate path visible; NHTSA's defect probes (EA26-002 on FSD degradation, DP26-010 school-zone review) can offset the benefit even if it passes.
rows.implication: Treat federal preemption as optionality worth little in the base case and no more than a modest premium in the bull case; do not pay for it today.
rows.confidence: high on the vote; low on enactment probability in the 119th Congress.
rows.follow_up: What is the full committee and floor schedule for H.R. 7390, and does the Senate have a companion bill?

rows.finding: From 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31 China halves the NEV purchase tax to an effective 5%, capped at RMB 15,000 per passenger car, with new technical requirements from 2026-01-01; Tesla's unsupervised FSD is still not approved in China, Q3 2026 China sales fell 16%, and Beijing cut the vehicle export tax rebate.
rows.mechanism: The tax change raises the effective price of a China-built Model 3 or Model Y by up to RMB 15,000 and is regressive for higher-priced trims; the export-rebate cut raises the cost of using Shanghai as an export hub, while the missing FSD approval blocks software revenue in the largest EV market.
rows.benchmark: Full purchase-tax exemption in 2024-2025; China sales growth in 2025 versus the 12-16% declines reported for 2026.
rows.weakens: The tax applies to all NEV makers, Tesla cut prices and added financing, and record Shanghai exports can absorb capacity even with a lower rebate.
rows.implication: Treat China as a cost and export anchor rather than a 2026-2028 profit-growth engine, and exclude China FSD revenue from the base case until MIIT/CAC approval is disclosed.
rows.confidence: high on the tax and export-rebate changes; medium on FSD timing and on how much of the sales decline is policy versus competition.
rows.follow_up: What is the status of Tesla's application for unsupervised FSD in China, which data-localisation and mapping conditions apply, and how much of Shanghai output is exported?

rows.finding: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2754 has imposed a definitive countervailing duty on China-built BEVs since 2024-10-30 for five years, at 7.8% for Tesla Shanghai versus 35.3% for SAIC, on top of the 10% common duty; the EU softened 2025-2027 CO2 compliance to a three-year average and proposed the same for 2030-2032.
rows.mechanism: The duty raises Tesla's Shanghai-to-EU landed cost by about 17.8% but Chinese-brand rivals' by roughly 45%, preserving relative price room; the CO2 derogation removes legacy manufacturers' near-term urgency to buy credits or force EV mix, weakening both credit demand and the regulatory pull for EVs.
rows.benchmark: 10% most-favoured-nation duty alone; the US 100% tariff on Chinese-built EVs that keeps Chinese brands out of Tesla's home market.
rows.weakens: The EU may replace duties with price undertakings that narrow Tesla's relative advantage, and Berlin-built cars avoid the duty entirely.
rows.implication: The EU relative advantage is real but narrow and time-limited; do not underwrite it beyond 2026 or assume EU CO2 policy keeps forcing credit purchases.
rows.confidence: high on the regulation and rate; medium on the direction of EU trade policy in 2027.
rows.follow_up: Is the EU negotiating price undertakings that would replace the Tesla-specific 7.8% rate, and what share of EU sales is Berlin-built versus Shanghai-built?

rows.finding: The 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423.7m shares in 12 tranches (approved 2025-11-06) with $105.82-120.37bn of unrecognised stock compensation for milestones not yet probable and $10.23bn for the one deemed probable; Tesla invested $2.0bn in xAI Holdings in January 2026, converted into SpaceX Class A stock in March 2026; Musk holds 19.8% and 207.5m of his shares are pledged.
rows.mechanism: Performance-contingent equity aligns the CEO but creates a dilution and expense overhang of up to ~10.7% of the 3.95bn shares outstanding and a related-party channel for allocating Tesla capital to Musk-controlled entities; pledged shares link the controlling shareholder's liquidity to the share price and raise the cost of capital.
rows.benchmark: Tesla has a single class of stock (one share, one vote), unlike Ford's Class B (2% of shares, 40% of votes); seven of nine directors are independent.
rows.weakens: Most of the award is performance-based and may never be recognised, the unearned shares vote proportionately to other shareholders, and the board has an independent special committee process.
rows.implication: Apply a governance discount and ask for an independent review of related-party capital allocation; treat SpaceX combination speculation as a risk to minority holders, not a catalyst.
rows.confidence: high on the disclosures; medium on the size of the valuation discount.
rows.follow_up: What are the 12 operational milestones, when does the first tranche become probable, and what process governs any SpaceX combination?

rows.finding: A Florida jury awarded $129m in compensatory damages (Tesla 33% at fault) and $200m in punitive damages in the August 2025 Autopilot product-liability trial; the California Civil Rights Department race-discrimination trial is set for 2026-07-20; a securities class action over FSD/Robotaxi statements was filed in W.D. Texas on 2025-08-04; the Delaware Supreme Court reversed the rescission of the 2018 pay award on 2025-12-19.
rows.mechanism: Product-liability and civil-rights verdicts set precedents that raise insurance, settlement and compliance costs and can attach to the autonomy narrative; the Delaware ruling removes a legal cloud over the 2018 award but leaves the 2025 award's economics in place.
rows.benchmark: Tesla recorded only an immaterial accrual for the $329m gross verdict, implying expected reduction or insurance recovery on appeal.
rows.weakens: The verdict is on appeal, punitive damages are often reduced, and Tesla's accrual is immaterial; securities and discrimination cases are common for large manufacturers and rarely change strategy.
rows.implication: Treat litigation as a tail risk that raises the cost of capital modestly rather than a thesis-changing liability; monitor the CRD trial and any punitive-damages precedent.
rows.confidence: high on the filings; medium on ultimate liability.
rows.follow_up: What is the post-trial ruling on the Autopilot verdict, and what damages exposure does Tesla disclose for the CRD case?

plan.decision_question: Which regulatory, policy and ESG factors materially change Tesla's cash flows, licence to operate or cost of capital in 2026-2028?
plan.thesis_sentence: Tesla's policy position has inverted: the 2025-2026 reset removes a high-margin revenue stream worth about $2bn a year at its peak and leaves the robotaxi licence to operate fragmented across US states and unapproved in China, while the offsetting upsides — federal AV preemption and tariffs on Chinese rivals — are real but not yet law, so policy and governance risk deserves a discount to, not a premium over, the core auto multiple.
plan.why_different: The other sections price demand, margins, technology feasibility and valuation; this section prices the legal permissions and compliance costs that gate the autonomy catalyst and the high-margin credit stream, and the governance overhang that changes the cost of capital.
plan.mechanism: Regulatory credits and purchase subsidies are near-100% margin revenue, so their removal cuts gross profit and cash flow one-for-one; state AV authorisations and China FSD approval are binary gates on robotaxi revenue; performance equity and related-party capital allocation raise the discount rate on the equity.
plan.comparison_set: Waymo (CPUC driverless deployment permit), Zoox (federal FMVSS exemption granted 2026-07-31), Ford (dual-class control), GM and Ford (credit-dependent compliance buyers), and Tesla's own 2023-2025 credit revenue history ($1,790m, $2,763m, $1,993m).
plan.counter_evidence: Policy also favours Tesla: the US 100% tariff on Chinese-built EVs and the EU's 17.8% total duty on Shanghai cars versus roughly 45% for SAIC keep Chinese rivals out; a federal AV preemption bill could unlock nationwide Cybercab deployment; most of the CEO award is performance-contingent, seven of nine directors are independent and there is no dual class; Tesla's own operational environmental footprint is small, so environmental issues are second-order to supply-chain and product safety.
plan.visual: policy impact matrix (Factor | Exposure | Probability | Impact on company | Mitigant | Source)
plan.prohibited: well positioned; manageable; massive market; ESG score; green premium; huge; clearly; high barriers to entry

rows.benchmark: Pre-award share count of 3.95bn and prior CEO award dilution
rows.weakens: Awards are performance-contingent and the Tesla proxy states a majority-independent board.
rows.implication: Apply a governance discount to the multiple and model diluted shares from the probable milestone.
rows.confidence: high

rows.mechanism: An adverse bench ruling carries damages and injunctive relief that could change Fremont labour practices; the Autopilot verdict sets a template for product-liability tails.
rows.benchmark: Prior private discrimination verdicts and the immaterial litigation accrual in the 10-K
rows.weakens: The 10-K reports no material accrual and Tesla denies wrongdoing.
rows.implication: Treat labour and product safety as unquantified tails, not base-case cash costs.
rows.confidence: medium

rows.finding: At $403.30 (NasdaqGS, 2026-10-29 20:00 UTC) Tesla has a $1,594.1B market cap and $1,558.0B EV on TTM revenue of $103,570M, operating income of $3,466M and free cash flow of $3,303M: 15.0x sales, 443.2x earnings, 170.5x GAAP EBITDA, 104x the company's $15.0B adjusted EBITDA.
rows.mechanism: The multiple is not measuring current cash flow; it capitalises a future business, so every dollar of near-term profit is nearly irrelevant to the price and the price becomes a probability statement about robotaxi and Optimus.

rows.weakens: The stock has held 200x-400x earnings for two years without mean-reverting, so a high multiple alone has not been a sell signal; the market has repeatedly paid for narrative.
rows.implication: There is no margin of safety in current earnings; the position must be sized as an option, not as a cash-flow investment.

rows.mechanism: Terminal value dominates, so the price is a claim on 2031 cash flow; the required fleet exceeds what Tesla's installed capacity of about 2.5M vehicles a year could build in six years.
rows.benchmark: Tesla generated $3,303M of free cash flow over the trailing twelve months and has about 2.5M units of installed annual capacity.
rows.weakens: A lower discount rate (10-year Treasury 4.99%, so 9% WACC is arguable for a mega-cap) lowers the required 2031 FCF to $118B, and Optimus or licensing could add profit that does not require a Tesla-owned fleet.
rows.implication: The price discounts a scale of autonomous fleet that has no precedent and would require revenue per mile that no disclosed Tesla service charges.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: What revenue per mile does Tesla intend to charge in Austin, and what is the utilisation and cost per mile of the current fleet?

rows.finding: Tesla has never declared or paid a cash dividend, has no repurchase authorisation and bought back no shares in fiscal 2025; trailing free cash flow of $3,303M is a 0.2% yield and the entire $45.4B cash pile would retire 112.7M shares, 2.85% of the 3.953B outstanding.
rows.mechanism: Cash retained for capital expenditure and related-party projects never reaches minority holders, so the only cash return available is a sale of the shares themselves.
rows.benchmark: GM's 12.4% total shareholder yield and Ford's 5.9% against Tesla's 0.0%; Tesla's trailing free cash flow of $3,303M against a $1,594.1B capitalisation.
rows.weakens: A $45.4B balance sheet gives the company the capacity to start a buyback at any time, and capex could peak and free cash within the horizon.
rows.implication: A holder cannot rely on the company to return cash within a 3-5 year horizon; capital return is a governance choice that the controlling shareholder has consistently declined.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Would the board ever authorise a buyback, and what would it take — a $100B cash balance or a robotaxi revenue stream?

rows.finding: No financial buyer can take Tesla private: at $1,594.1B it is 29 times the largest buyout ever completed. No automaker can acquire it: GM and Ford combined are $118.4B. Alphabet, at $3,493.5B, is the only US balance sheet large enough, and it is the closest competitor in autonomous driving.
rows.mechanism: Control premiums require a buyer whose balance sheet can absorb the target and whose regulators will approve it; neither condition holds at $1.6 trillion.
rows.benchmark: The $55B Electronic Arts take-private (2026-08-04), the largest LBO on record, is 3.4% of Tesla's market capitalisation; GM ($72.3B) and Ford ($46.1B) together are 7.4%.
rows.weakens: A consortium of sovereign wealth funds plus Musk could in theory assemble the equity, and a sharp price fall would lower the barrier arithmetic.
rows.implication: The probability of a cash control premium within 3-5 years is close to zero; any takeover speculation should be valued at nil.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Would any sovereign fund attempt a minority stake or PIPE rather than a full take-private, and on what governance terms?

rows.finding: On 2026-10-21 the two boards formed special committees to explore a Tesla-SpaceX merger, two days after Musk called the idea a 'good idea' on the Q3 earnings call; SpaceX listed on 2026-06-12 at $135 a share and a $1.77T valuation, reaching about $2.1T on its first day, and the combined group would be worth well over $3 trillion.
rows.mechanism: A share-for-share combination is the only structure that can absorb a $1.6T asset without cash, and it converts Tesla minorities into minorities of a controlled company.
rows.benchmark: Waymo's $126B mark for the leading robotaxi operator; the SolarCity rescue in 2016 as a related-party precedent.
rows.weakens: The talks are exploratory, Musk said he would recuse himself, and no ratio, premium or timetable has been disclosed; a special committee could reject the terms.
rows.implication: This is the only named counterparty capable of a transformative transaction, and it pays in shares of a company where Musk controls about 84% of the vote.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: What exchange ratio would the special committees accept, and what vote threshold applies to Tesla holders?

rows.finding: At $1,594B of Tesla equity and SpaceX's $2.1T first-day value, Tesla holders would own about 43% of the combined company's equity but would lose the one-share-one-vote structure they hold today, moving to a company where Musk controls roughly 84% of the vote.
rows.mechanism: Exchange ratios allocate economic value; share class structure allocates control, and the two are negotiated separately in related-party deals.
rows.benchmark: Tesla's own share count and the $1,594.1B market capitalisation.
rows.weakens: If SpaceX retains its super-voting structure, index providers may treat the combined company as controlled and exclude or under-weight it, changing passive demand.
rows.implication: The merger is a governance event as much as a valuation event: 43% of a $3.7T entity is worth more in dollars but less in control, and minority protections would be set by a controlled board.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Would the combined company keep a single class of shares, and would Tesla holders receive a voting premium in the ratio?

rows.finding: Tesla trades 36.96M shares and $14.0B a day over 20 days; a $500M position is 3.6% of one day's value traded, there is no lock-up for public holders, and short interest is 2.19% of the float with 2.2 days to cover.
rows.mechanism: Liquidity determines whether an exit is possible; valuation determines whether it is profitable, and Tesla is extreme on the first and poor on the second.
rows.benchmark: Tesla's $14.0B average daily turnover and 2.19% short interest against a typical mid-cap's days-to-liquidate.
rows.weakens: Liquidity collapses in a correlated sell-off, when the same $14.0B of turnover becomes one-sided, as it did for mega-caps in 2022.
rows.implication: Access to an exit is never the constraint: the holder can always sell, and the risk is entirely the price at which the sale clears.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What would a 5% position in Tesla do to the fund's factor exposure and liquidity coverage ratio under stress?

rows.finding: Five-year IRR from $403.30 recomputed on the revised tree: $19 bear gives $76B of market capitalisation and -45.7% a year; $107 base gives $429B and -23.3%; $111 probability-weighted gives $444B and -22.7%; $212 bull gives -12.1%; $437 blue sky gives +1.6%; $650 is the 10%-a-year hurdle and requires $2.6T.
rows.mechanism: Starting multiple determines the arithmetic of future returns when cash return is zero: the entire return comes from the exit multiple, which must rise from 15x sales to justify a higher price.
rows.benchmark: Consensus target $408.61 (2026-10-25) implies +1.3% over twelve months; a 10% annual return needs $650 by 2031.
rows.weakens: A merger at a premium or a robotaxi breakthrough would break the arithmetic, and the 2025 CEO award's market-cap milestones give management a direct incentive to pursue either.
rows.implication: The return sensitivity is asymmetric: only the blue-sky branch earns any positive return, and the probability-weighted case loses more than a fifth of value a year.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: What is the entry price at which a 10% expected return is achievable on the probability-weighted value, and does that price ever occur?

plan.decision_question: For a public-equity holder, what is the realistic exit or monetisation path and value over a 3-5 year horizon?
plan.thesis_sentence: Tesla offers no cash exit at $1.59 trillion — no dividend has ever been paid, no buyback programme exists, and the entire $45.4B cash pile would retire just 2.85% of the shares — so the realistic 3-5 year monetisation is a sale into a $14.0B-a-day secondary market or a share exchange into a SpaceX controlled by the same man, and both leave the return hostage to a re-rating five years have not delivered.
plan.why_different: Section 8 asks what the asset is worth; this asks who pays, in what currency, when, and what legal or political gate stands between the holder and the cash — including the controlling shareholder whose interests may not align with minorities.
plan.mechanism: A holder realises value through cash returned by the company, a premium paid by a control buyer, or a sale into the secondary market at a re-rated price; testing each channel's capacity against the $1.59T capitalisation shows only the third and a share-exchange merger are available, and the merger transfers control to a shareholder with super-voting rights.
plan.comparison_set: Record LBO (EA, $55B, 2026-08-04); SpaceX's June 2026 IPO at $1.77T and ~$2.1T first-day mark; Waymo's $126B private round; Tesla's own 2016 SolarCity rescue; peer cash-return yields (GM 12.4% total shareholder yield, Ford 5.9%) against Tesla's 0.0%; the 2026-10-25 consensus target of $408.61.
plan.counter_evidence: A SpaceX combination could be accretive if the exchange ratio is fair and Starlink cash flows are real; the stock trades $14.0B a day, so access to an exit is never the constraint; and an announced combination historically carries a premium to the undisturbed price.
plan.visual: Exit routes table naming each buyer or venue with timing and likelihood, a precedent-exits table with values, and a 5-year IRR sensitivity to entry price using $19/$107/$212/$437 and the $111 probability-weighted value.
plan.prohibited: No 'huge market', 'strong team', 'clear path', 'well positioned', 'risks are manageable'; no vague counts; no sentences about the report; no names of internal tools or records.

rows.finding: 分部之和把汽车、服务、能源与净现金定在$170B（$42.50/股），而同业严格倍数（通用隐含0.39倍市销率、Fluence 0.5倍）只给$87B（$21.75/股）；退出分析里的控制权买家区间是$200-250B，即$50-62.50/股。
rows.mechanism: 核心资产的价值取决于用谁的倍数：1.0倍市销率对2.2-2.5%剥离信用后的营业利润率是40倍上下的营业利润倍数，本身已含溢价；严格的同业倍数把核心压到$22，控制权溢价把它抬到$50-62.50。任何一种口径下自主性都占股价84-95%。
rows.benchmark: 通用汽车隐含0.39倍市销率、Fluence 0.5倍、同业中位16.5倍市盈率；控制权区间$200-250B。
rows.weakens: 若能源按宁德时代式规模重估（收入翻倍至$25B、5倍市销率），核心增加$82B即每股$20，仍不足以改变84%以上的自主性依赖。
rows.implication: 核心资产不是过严而是偏宽，减持结论不依赖苛刻假设；反过来说，任何“核心被低估”的辩护最多值每股$20。
rows.confidence: high：分部收入与毛利率来自10-Q，倍数来自公开可比；控制权区间来自本报告退出分析。
rows.follow_up: 若把能源按2027年订单价格重估到5倍市销率，核心能否到$70/股？

plan.decision_question: 若自主性归零，核心资产在严格同业倍数下值多少？答案$21.75/股（宽松假设$42.50、控制权上限$62.50）意味着84-95%的股价是自主性，那么任何一件行政或合约事件的成本都高于全部核心业务的年利润。
plan.thesis_sentence: 现价的89%是自主性与机器人业务，而支撑它的三个前提——行政许可、合并对价、现金流质量——同时在恶化；减持/卖出的结论在每一种压力情景下都成立，唯一能在没有一英里机器人出租车的情况下证明现价的换股溢价，议价权却在评级更高、增长更快的SpaceX一方。
plan.why_different: 其他各节证明业务与估值的事实；本节只做证伪：把每个结论放进市场缩小一半、CAC翻倍、收入降30%、融资推迟6个月、倍数压缩与FCF降30%的压力，并给出概率、每股影响、触发信号与对冲动作，同时把“合并溢价”这条唯一不需要经营交付的上涨路径单列。
plan.mechanism: 自主性期权在经营证据出现前就能被三件非经营事件关闭：(1) NHTSA对无方向盘Cybercab自认证的审计（答复期2026-10-30）可中断奥斯汀服务并推迟非监督发布；(2) SpaceX换股需“全体股份50%”表决，未投票即反对，且按市价换股在数学上价值中性；(3) 九个月自由现金流$1,883M中有$7,332M来自应付账款、账期从62.8天拉到75.3天，剔除后为负。
plan.comparison_set: 同业倍数（通用隐含0.39倍市销率、Fluence 0.5倍、同业中位16.5倍市盈率）、控制权买家区间$200-250B（$50-62.50/股）、Waymo 2026年2月$126B融资、SpaceX Baa1对特斯拉Baa3、Waymo每周50万次付费行程对特斯拉769辆车、2026-03-19的25州检察长诉讼对2026-02-12的EPA终局规则。
plan.counter_evidence: 现价可能正确：若换股给特斯拉10-15%比例溢价，特斯拉股东得到合并集团46-47%，在$3.6T合并市值上等于$443-487/股，不需要任何机器人出租车收入；2026年10月特斯拉已连续两年维持三位数倍数未均值回归；能源毛利率33.1%与储能订单排至2027年底若属实则自主性之外的现金流被低估。
plan.visual: 8-10行风险矩阵（概率、每股影响、等级、时点、预警信号、缓解措施、来源）加5行压力测试表，再加一张“换股溢价是唯一不需要交付即可证明现价”的danger卡。
plan.prohibited: 不写“风险可控”“竞争激烈”“护城河稳固”等空话；不用“近期”“大幅”等模糊词；不引用内部审核或修订编号；不把公司自报的里程、车队数与Optimis目标当作已核实事实；不重复其他各节的段落。

rows.finding: The sum of the parts values vehicles, services, energy and net cash at $170B ($42.50 a share); GM's implied 0.39x sales puts vehicles and services at $29B and the strict-peer core at $87B ($21.75); a control buyer for the pieces is worth $200-250B ($50-62.50). Energy at 3.5x is supported by a 29.7% gross margin against Fluence's 13.1%; doubling energy revenue to $25B at 5.0x adds $82B ($20 a share) and FSD's 1.74M subscribers add $42B ($10.5), leaving the core near $70 and autonomy at 83% of the price.
rows.mechanism: The core value depends on whose multiple is used: 1.0x sales is roughly 40x ex-credit operating profit, already a premium, while peer multiples compress it to $21.75 and control value lifts it to $62.50; in all three the autonomy premium is 84-95% of the price.
rows.benchmark: GM's implied 0.39x sales, Fluence's 0.5x and 13.1% gross margin, the $200-250B control range, Waymo's $126B mark.
rows.weakens: Energy at CATL scale plus FSD licensing adds at most $30 a share of core value, so the $600B autonomy claim cannot be reconstructed from the operating businesses.
rows.implication: The core is not undervalued; the recommendation does not depend on a harsh multiple, and the best honest defence of the price is still 83% autonomy.
rows.confidence: high: segment revenue and margins from the 10-Q, multiples from public comparables, control range from the exit analysis.
rows.follow_up: At what price would a strategic buyer have to value energy and FSD licensing to make the core worth $100 a share, and is any such buyer other than Alphabet able to pass antitrust review?

rows.finding: The base case carries $259B of autonomy (35% x $40B regional, 40% x $126B, 20% x $600B, 5% x $1,500B) alongside a $42.50 core, giving $107; on the regional branch alone the base is $52.50 and the weighted value $84. The bear is $19 after autonomy is written to zero, vehicles at 0.39x, energy at 1.5x and net cash cut to $29B; the bull is $212 and the blue-sky branch $437.
rows.mechanism: The weighted value is most sensitive to the base branch's autonomy number: replacing $259B with the $40B regional branch cuts the base by $54.50 a share and the weighted value to $84 without changing the rating.
rows.benchmark: Waymo's $126B valuation, 500,000 paid rides a week and ~3,000 vehicles against Tesla's 769 Texas registrations on 2026-10-14, 349 of them Cybercabs, and nine crashes reported in August 2026.
rows.weakens: Tesla's 2.0M cumulative unsupervised miles by 2026-09-30 and paid Austin rides since 2026-09-03 show the service is real, though with no revenue per mile disclosed.
rows.implication: The tree is generous at the base and shallow in the bear; the correction lowers the weighted value to $111 but does not change reduce.
rows.confidence: medium: fleet and crash counts from state and NHTSA data, not audited; branch weights are the analyst's judgement.
rows.follow_up: Does the Q4 2026 shareholder update disclose robotaxi revenue, fare and the share of rides without a safety driver, and does the Texas registration count rise above 769?

rows.finding: Nine-month free cash flow of $1,883M contains $7,332M from payables and accruals; days payable rose from 62.8 to 75.3, worth about $2.9B, so normalised free cash flow is -$1.0B. Inventory rose 13.7% while deliveries fell 2%, warranty provisions rose 26% and incurred claims 29%. Net cash is $36.18B, cash and short-term investments $45.45B, with $30B of facilities signed in September 2026.
rows.mechanism: Supplier finance substitutes for profit: when payables normalise, cash returns to the low-single-digit operating margin, and a 30% revenue fall at a 19% gross margin removes $6.0B of gross profit, producing a $20-27B annual burn with capex.
rows.benchmark: Days payable of 62.8 at end-2025, 56.7 in 2024 and 66.6 in 2023; $19.1B annual operating expense; $20-25B capex.
rows.weakens: Q3 2026 free cash flow was positive at $1,531M and interest coverage is 10.0x, so solvency is not the issue — cash quality is.
rows.implication: A two-year autonomy slip is fundable without dilution; a slip combined with a revenue fall is not, and valuation should use normalised free cash flow of -$1.0B.
rows.confidence: high: all from the 10-Q financial statements and notes.
rows.follow_up: Did days payable fall below 65 in Q4 2026, and did free cash flow turn negative when it did?

rows.finding: Terafab's $16.8B first phase is jointly funded by Tesla and SpaceX, on a site of more than 100m sq ft announced 2026-08-06; Tesla's share is undisclosed and the commitment sits outside the '>$20B' 2026 capital budget. SpaceX's IPO filing described Terafab as a 'general framework' with no binding commitments, no finalised IP split and no obligation for either side to keep participating; Tesla separately committed $16.5B to Samsung for AI6 chips.
rows.mechanism: A joint, non-binding capital framework converts a company-controlled capex budget into a negotiated commitment with the controlling shareholder's other company, so the '2027 capex at or below $25B with positive free cash flow' assumption has no binding support.
rows.benchmark: Nine-month capex of $13,014M and a >$20B 2026 guide; $30B of facilities undrawn; Samsung's $16.5B AI6 contract already committed.
rows.weakens: The S-1 language means the cash call may never become binding, which caps the near-term risk and also removes Terafab as a strategic asset the bull case can claim.
rows.implication: Treat Tesla's Terafab contribution as an unquantified call on 2027-2028 cash, and do not add on the strength of the project.
rows.confidence: medium: the $16.8B and joint nature are widely reported, Tesla's share is undisclosed, and the non-binding language is reported from the S-1 rather than read in the filing.
rows.follow_up: In the definitive Terafab agreements, what percentage of the $16.8B first phase is Tesla's and is the commitment binding? Tesla's 2026 Form 10-K commitments note and SpaceX's 2026 Form 20-F related-party note would settle it.

rows.finding: Special committees were formed on 2026-10-20, with Musk stating that no terms were agreed and none assured; a Tesla vote needs 50% of all shares, not of those cast. At market, $1,594.1B plus SpaceX's $2.01T is $3.60T and Tesla holders' 43-44% equals today's price. The 2025 award lapses operational milestones and vests market-cap milestones on a change of control: 423.7M shares, 10.7% dilution, first $2.0T milestone 25% above today's capitalisation, 35.3M shares a tranche, $9.74B probable charge and $105.82-120.37B unrecognised.
rows.mechanism: A stock-for-stock combination at market transfers no value; any premium is a concession by the larger, higher-rated party, while the CEO award converts a control event into accelerated dilution tied to market capitalisation rather than cash flow.
rows.benchmark: SpaceX's $2.01T first-day value and Baa1 rating against Tesla's Baa3; the 2026-12-03 annual meeting, whose three proposals do not include a merger; 207.5M pledged shares (5.2%).
rows.weakens: Musk's public remarks and the 2026-10-21 press reports put a combination in play and the shares rose 1.54% on the report, so the option has value even without terms.
rows.implication: Carry the merger at zero in the base case, but treat a premium ratio as the only non-operating path to today's price; size positions for a failed vote.
rows.confidence: medium: process and vote threshold from Musk's public remarks reported second-hand; no 8-K with terms.
rows.follow_up: Which operational milestone gates each 35.3M-share tranche, and what happens to unvested tranches on a change of control? The 2025 award agreement (Annex C, SEC EX-99.2) and the 2025 DEF 14A settle it.

rows.finding: Twenty-five state attorneys general and 12 cities and counties sued on 2026-03-19 in the D.C. Circuit over EPA's 2026-02-12 repeal of the 2009 endangerment finding, consolidated on 2026-05-20. A reversal restores the credit pool, but $1.5B of credits at 15x is $22.5B, $5.6 a share, against Q3 2026 credit revenue of $113M (-73%) and credits at 45.8% of FY2025 operating income.
rows.mechanism: The credit pool is a small, litigation-dated option: even full restoration is worth $5.6 a share, while the decline is already in the earnings run rate at a 2.2-2.5% ex-credit operating margin.
rows.weakens: A court reversal in 2027-2028 could restore part of the pool, and traditional automakers' shift to hybrids may keep credit demand below 2024 levels anyway.
rows.implication: Give policy reversal no value in the base case and no more than $5.6 a share in the bull case.
rows.confidence: high: the rule and the consolidated litigation are on the public court and federal records.
rows.follow_up: What is the docket number and the next scheduled date (merits briefing or oral argument) in the consolidated D.C. Circuit challenge to EPA's 2026-02-12 endangerment-finding repeal, and does the docket show a stay? The D.C. Circuit docket and the State Energy & Environmental Impact Center case page settle it.

rows.finding: Waymo runs 500,000 paid rides a week on about 3,000 vehicles against Tesla's 769 Texas registrations on 2026-10-14; BYD holds 2.4% of the European market, level with Tesla, at about EUR 5,500 less per car, and Xiaomi is near break-even in its first production year. If revenue per mile falls from $0.60 to $0.45, the reverse DCF needs 20.9M robotaxis rather than 15.7M, above global annual capacity.
rows.mechanism: The terminal value depends on the revenue per mile set by the largest operator, not by Tesla; a 25% price decline raises the required fleet by a third and pushes the reverse DCF past global manufacturing capacity.
rows.benchmark: Waymo's 500,000 weekly paid rides and 3,000 vehicles; BYD's European share of 2.4% against Tesla's 2.4%; 15.7M robotaxis at $0.60 a mile.
rows.weakens: Tesla's US battery-electric share rose to 51.7% in August 2026 and Chinese price competition eased, so near-term volume is not collapsing.
rows.implication: Competition is a $40-60 a share hit to the bull branch and nothing to 2027 earnings; it belongs in terminal value, not the forecast.
rows.confidence: medium: ride and fleet counts are third-party aggregates without operator audit.
rows.follow_up: What did the Q4 2026 shareholder update report as robotaxi revenue and revenue per vehicle per week, and what share of the 769 Texas-registered vehicles ran without a safety driver? The Q4 2026 update and the 2026 Form 10-K segment note settle it.

rows.finding: The 2025 CEO Performance Award is 423,743,904 shares over twelve tranches, 10.7% of the count, with market-capitalisation milestones starting at $2.0T — 25% above the 2026-10-29 capitalisation of $1,594.1B — and operational milestones alongside; on a change of control operational milestones lapse and market-cap milestones vest. The 10-Q carries a $9.74B probable charge and a $105.82-120.37B unrecognised range.
rows.mechanism: The award pays in shares on market value rather than cash flow, so a merger that lifts the headline capitalisation accelerates dilution exactly when minority holders are being asked to accept a ratio.
rows.benchmark: 35.3M shares a tranche, twelve tranches, $2.0T first milestone, $8.5T final milestone, ten-year term.
rows.weakens: No tranche has vested at $1,594.1B, so the dilution is a call on a 25% re-rating rather than a present cost.
rows.implication: Dilution and the control-change terms are a governance risk to any exchange ratio, not a reason to own the shares.
rows.confidence: medium: share count and charge from the 10-Q, tranche structure from the award tracker and the award summary.
rows.follow_up: Which operational milestone gates each 35.3M-share tranche, and are unvested tranches accelerated or cancelled on a change of control? The 2025 DEF 14A compensation section and the award agreement (Annex C, SEC EX-99.2) settle it.

plan.decision_question: If autonomy is worth zero, what do the pieces fetch, and what is the cost of being wrong about the one event — an exchange ratio — that can pay $443-487 without a robotaxi mile?
plan.thesis_sentence: At $403.30 Tesla is a $1,594.1B equity in which $42.50 a share is the operating business and $356 is autonomy and robotics; with a probability-weighted value of $111 and three of the premium's premises deteriorating at once, the share is a reduce, and the only event that can prove the price without a robotaxi mile — a premium exchange ratio — is a governance risk, not a business one.
plan.why_different: Every other section establishes what Tesla is worth and why; this section tries to break those conclusions, prices each way they can fail in dollars per share, and separates the one event that can raise the price (an exchange ratio) from the events that can only lower it.
plan.mechanism: The autonomy option can be closed before any operating evidence arrives by three non-operating events: NHTSA's Cybercab self-certification inquiry (comment window to 2026-10-30) can suspend the Austin service; a merger needs 50% of all shares with abstentions counted against; and reported free cash flow is supplied by a $7,332M payables stretch that reverses into negative free cash flow.
plan.comparison_set: GM's implied 0.39x sales and Fluence's 0.5x against Tesla's 1.0x and 3.5x; a $200-250B control-buyer range; Waymo at $126B and 500,000 paid rides a week against 769 Texas-registered Tesla vehicles; SpaceX at Baa1 against Tesla at Baa3; the 2025 award's first $2.0T milestone 25% above today's $1,594.1B.
plan.counter_evidence: The price can be right without operations if the special committees propose a 10-15% ratio premium, worth $443-487 a share; Tesla has held a triple-digit multiple for two years; and Terafab's non-binding 'general framework' status caps the near-term cash call even as it weakens the strategic-asset case.
plan.visual: A ten-row risk matrix (probability, per-share impact, level, timing, signpost, mitigation, source), a six-row stress-test table and a danger card on the exchange ratio.
plan.prohibited: No 'risks are manageable', 'fierce competition', 'well positioned', 'recently' or 'about'; no internal review or revision IDs; no description of how the section is written; no figure without a source ID.

rows.finding: At $403.30 the equity is $1,594.1B; the sum of the parts puts vehicles, energy, services and $36.2B of net cash at $42.50 a share, so $356 (89%) is autonomy and robotics, 11.3x Waymo's $126B February 2026 round.

rows.finding: Cisco peaked at about $500B in March 2000, fell almost 90% by October 2000, grew revenue from about $12.5B to about $57B, and did not surpass its 2000 closing high on an adjusted basis until 2021.
rows.mechanism: Entry multiple, not business quality, sets the ten-year return when the market has already priced the terminal share of a new technology.
rows.benchmark: S&P 500 over the same period.

rows.finding: GM spent more than $10B on Cruise from 2016, earned less than $500M of revenue, and shut the robotaxi unit in December 2024 for about $1B a year of savings.
rows.mechanism: Autonomy capital is written off when the operator cannot convert test miles into paid driverless miles, and the write-off is total rather than gradual.

rows.weakens: Waymo shows the opposite outcome is possible, so the base rate is not 100% failure - it is that the leader captures the market and the followers write off.
rows.implication: The bear branch is not a tail: an automaker with capital and engineers has already taken this exact loss.

rows.follow_up: How many paid driverless miles has Tesla actually delivered, and at what revenue per mile?

rows.finding: Waymo raised $16B at a $126B post-money valuation in February 2026 and reached about 500,000 paid driverless rides a week by May 2026, against 769 registered Tesla robotaxi vehicles on 2026-10-14.

rows.implication: Score profitability 4 out of 10; the company destroys economic value at current margins.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: What is the maintenance versus growth split of the $20B+ 2026 capex budget?

rows.finding: A 423.7M-share CEO award (10.7% of the 2026-09-30 count) carries $105.82-120.37B of unrecognised compensation on the non-probable tranches; three of nine directors are SpaceX-tied and $2.0B was invested in xAI and converted into SpaceX stock.
rows.mechanism: Compensation tied to market-cap milestones aligns management with the narrative that supports the multiple, not with per-share cash flow.
rows.benchmark: No peer has a comparable performance-award overhang; stock compensation is 4.2% of revenue.
rows.weakens: The award vests only if market capitalisation rises several-fold, so it is not dilution at today's price unless milestones are met.
rows.implication: Score governance 3 out of 10; dilution and related-party risk are structural, not cyclical.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Will the board offset award dilution, and what are the per-tranche thresholds?

rows.finding: The ten-year Treasury yields 4.99%, up 0.93 points in twelve months, while the equity market is near its high and volatility is average.
rows.mechanism: When the risk-free rate approaches 5%, the present value of long-dated optionality falls and the hurdle for narrative stocks rises.
rows.benchmark: S&P 500 +12.8% YTD and 1.6% below its high; VIX 17.20 at the 52nd percentile; XLY +3.4% over three months against SPY +3.7%.
rows.weakens: A risk-on market and a 17 VIX can keep high-beta narratives bid regardless of the discount rate.
rows.implication: Score regime and catalysts 3 out of 10; a 5% discount rate on 2031 cash flows argues for a smaller position.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What happens to a 2031-weighted cash-flow story if the ten-year reaches 5.5%?

rows.finding: Energy storage earned a 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026 on $210M of revenue per GWh, and services 15.9%; together they supplied $1,688M of the $5,494M quarterly gross profit.
rows.mechanism: Vertical integration in cells and packs plus installed-base service revenue produces margins an assembled competitor cannot match.
rows.benchmark: Fluence gross margin 13.1%; automotive ex-credit operating margin 2.2-2.5%.
rows.weakens: Energy revenue fell 16% year over year to $2.881B as prices fell, and management attributes part of the margin to one-off items.
rows.implication: Score business quality 6 out of 10; the energy and services franchise is real but too small to carry the price.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: Does the energy margin survive without tariff refunds and warranty reimbursements?

user_data_requests.database: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) investigation files
user_data_requests.query: Full ODI resumes and any recall query or information-request correspondence for EA26002 (FSD degradation detection in reduced visibility) and DP26010 (robotaxi speed in active school zones), including the incident counts and vehicle population.
user_data_requests.why: These two dockets determine whether FSD's vision-only approach survives regulatory scrutiny and whether the unsupervised release date holds. The ODI resume PDF for EA26002 could not be parsed by the research server, so the incident counts and the regulator's framing rest on press reporting rather than the primary record.
user_data_requests.how: Download the ODI resume and correspondence PDFs from static.nhtsa.gov/odi/inv/2026/ and send them as text or PDF attachments.

user_data_requests.database: California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) permit and AV mileage records
user_data_requests.query: Any charter-party carrier (TCP) permit, ride-hailing permit or autonomous-vehicle passenger-service authorisation held by Tesla Robotaxi LLC or Tesla, Inc., with permit numbers, status and annual AV mileage/vehicle reports filed for 2025-2026.
user_data_requests.why: California is the largest US robotaxi market. Tesla holds only a DMV testing-with-a-driver permit there (DMV lists, 2026-10-22), so any CPUC passenger-service authorisation and reported mileage would show whether a paid California service is closer than the permit list implies — or confirm that robotaxi revenue is Texas-only and therefore smaller than the equity story assumes.
user_data_requests.how: Search the CPUC Transportation Licensing System (tcpweb) and the CPUC autonomous-vehicle programme filings for 'Tesla'; send the permit record pages and the latest annual mileage report.

user_data_requests.database: California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) advice letters and PACER court dockets
user_data_requests.query: 1) CPUC: any Tesla (Tesla, Inc. or Tesla Insurance Services) application for a driverless deployment or driverless pilot permit under the Autonomous Vehicle Program, including advice-letter number, operational design domain, cities and status; Tesla's TCP authority number and whether it is a limousine/charter-party authority limited to SAE Level 2. 2) PACER: docket sheets and latest orders in (a) In re Tesla, Inc. Securities Litigation, W.D. Tex. (filed 2025-08-04, FSD/Robotaxi statements), (b) California Civil Rights Department v. Tesla, Alameda County Superior Court (trial set 2026-07-20), and (c) the post-trial motions in the S.D. Florida Autopilot verdict ($129m compensatory plus $200m punitive, 2025-08-01).
user_data_requests.why: The section's robotaxi valuation depends on whether Tesla can obtain driverless commercial authority in California, and on whether the securities, discrimination and product-liability cases create a liability or disclosure event that changes the cost of capital. Without the CPUC filing and the court dockets, confidence in the California autonomy option and in litigation timing stays medium.
user_data_requests.how: CPUC: search the CPCN/Advice Letter and Autonomous Vehicle Program pages at cpuc.ca.gov and request the Tesla filings by carrier name; PACER: log in at pacer.uscourts.gov or use CourtListener RECAP for the three dockets, download the docket sheets and most recent orders as PDF and attach them.

top_three: One capitalisation and one valuation across the report: financials recomputes to $1,594.1B market capitalisation and $1,558.0B enterprise value (15.0x trailing sales, 104x adjusted EBITDA, not 13.4x and 92x), and funding_valuation and exit replace the bear case of $35 and the probability-weighted $115 with the adopted $19 and $111, showing the bear build so it can be re-derived.

Rewrite section 10 in English at full depth with source tags on every figure-bearing paragraph and table row, a specific follow-up in evidence row 6, and an open-diligence block for the three undisclosed robotaxi and Terafab items.

1.name: Completeness sweep
1.notes: Sections read in full: executive_summary, company_overview, technology_product, market, competition, business_model, financials, funding_valuation, risk, thesis, exit, esg, scoring (13 of 14). team and strategy were assessed from the check, the evidence matrix and their use elsewhere (Musk's 19.8% stake and pledge block are corroborated in company_overview, risk and exit; the Optimus and Megapack claims in strategy are the same company-only claims flagged in pass 2). Depth and length floors are met everywhere: all sections 5,847-8,999 characters, two or more tables each, dated events throughout. Components required by the template (verdict, briefing, efficiency, one-question, takeaways, scenarios, analogs, sensitivity, risk-matrix, info, kpi, timeline, evidence, quad) are present where prescribed. The executive summary answers the user's question directly: Reduce, trim to at most 0.5% of NAV, no new money, with a dated event (premium exchange ratio, $443-487) named as the only path that changes the call. Two check findings are false positives against the text: market does carry sized pools (353.4 GWh storage at $234/kWh = $83B; 23.0M cars at $41,300 = $950B; 0.95M US BEV; 2.46M EU BEV) and technology_product carries three named-rival comparison tables (Waymo, BYD, CATL, Sungrow, Panasonic, Qilin). Both are logged as Minor so their owners can close them in one line rather than rebuild the sections. Language: the case language is English and every section except risk is written in English; risk is wholly in Chinese, which is both a reader-facing failure and a rule break.

2.name: Claim verification
2.notes: Claim-verification summary, claim by claim. Independent and well dated: Q3 2026 segment revenue, margins, cash flow and working-capital bridge [S4]; price, 52-week range, turnover and returns [S15]; US BEV share, transaction price and incentive per vehicle [S98, S103]; EU and China registration data [S99, S101, S102]; storage deployments [S108]; Waymo's $126B post-money and the $45B of October 2024 [S120]; SpaceX $1.77T at pricing and $2.1T on day one [S128]; EA at $55B [S130]; Texas SB 2807 authorisation, CPUC absence and the EU countervailing duty [S118, S119, S127]; credit revenue series [S4, S3]. Company-only and correctly labelled: FSD miles per collision (the evidence block in technology_product says telemetry and not regulator-verified); Megapack 33.1% margin partly tariff refunds and warranty reimbursements. Company-only and NOT labelled: the ones in the item above. Arithmetic I re-performed and that holds: probability-weighted $111 = 0.25x212 + 0.50x107 + 0.25x19; composite 4.0 = 0.15x(6+5+4+5+3) + 0.20x2 + 0.05x3; merger-inclusive $253 = 0.6x111 + 0.4x465; core $42.50 = (91+43+36)/4.00B; base $107 = $429B/4.00B; blue sky $437 = $1,747B/4.00B; EV $1,558.0 = $1,594.1 - $36.2; autonomy premium $356 = $1,424B/4.0B; 11.3x = $1,424B/$126B; reverse DCF $141B of 2031 FCF at 10% WACC and 3% terminal; $940B of revenue at a 15% FCF margin; 15.7M robotaxis at $0.56-0.60 a mile; Kelly caps and the -0.48% NAV loss on a 0.5% position. Two arithmetic slips worth one line each, not new items: the $42.50 core plus $356 of autonomy sums to $398.50 against the $403.30 close (the $4.80 residual is not explained), and exit puts Tesla holders at 43% of the combined group while risk and thesis use 44% (44.3% at $1,594.1B over $3.60T, 43.1% over $3.7T).

3.name: Missing competitors
3.notes: Coverage that is strong and I am not challenging: BYD (two powertrains, EU share, 7,498 BEVs against Tesla's 30,317 in the September panel), Geely Xingyuan at under RMB 100,000, Xiaomi SU7/YU7, GM and Cadillac, Hyundai-Kia, Rivian with 215,000 units of Normal capacity, CATL at 27.1% of ESS cells and 125.0 GWh in H1 2026, Fluence, Sungrow, Waymo (3,000 vehicles, 500,000 paid rides a week, 10 cities), Zoox, Baidu Apollo Go, Pony.ai and WeRide, plus the 2026 federal preemption attempt in esg. The Chinese storage integrators are grouped rather than named, which is acceptable because CATL and BYD are the cell-side price setters and Tesla's differentiation is integration, not cells. Open-source risk is not material for a vertically integrated manufacturer; academic spin-outs in autonomy are covered indirectly through Waymo's lineage.

4.name: Product/market fit
4.notes: Questions the committee would put to management, by section, in the order they matter. Market: (1) what does a rider pay per mile in Austin today, and against what Uber fare; (2) what share of rides has no safety monitor, and how many rides per vehicle per day; (3) does the September-August 2026 US BEV share hold, or was it a promotional quarter; (4) what share of Giga Shanghai output was exported in Q3. Business model: (5) what is the Megapack price and contracted backlog value for 2027, net of the tariff refunds in the 33.1% margin; (6) who owns the robotaxi and who carries residual value; (7) when does FSD revenue become its own line. Competition: (8) which competitor does Tesla lose a US or European BEV deal to, at what price differential; (9) what share of BYD's European volume is plug-in hybrid under the 2027 CO2 review. Thesis: (10) the same two robotaxi unit-economics questions the one-question component asks, which the report is right to put first. The budget-owner and sales-cycle questions are answered well for storage (utility or IPP, multi-year contract, interconnection queue, prepayments of $3.30B) and for vehicles (household or fleet); the gap is confined to robotaxi. Vehicle-side selling is also honest about cost: SG&A per delivery of $4,142 is called an upper bound and LTV:CAC of 2.0:1 is derived from it rather than asserted.

5.name: Number stress-test
5.notes: Stress-test arithmetic I ran, and whether the thesis survives 30% worse. (1) Probability-weighted value: leaving out the bull branch entirely (0.25/0.75 on base and bear) gives $85; cutting every branch by 30% gives $78; both remain far below $403.30, so the direction is robust to the error bars, only the magnitude moves. (2) Core at $42.50: 30% worse on the energy multiple (3.5x to 2.45x) removes about $10 a share, leaving $32.50; even a zero energy value leaves $31 of core, so the '89% is an option' claim is robust. (3) Reverse DCF: at an 11% WACC the 2031 requirement rises from $141B to about $164B, larger than a 30% miss in the other direction; the conclusion hardens rather than weakens. (4) Merger branch: $253 with a 40% weight; at a 25% weight it is $200, at 50% $288 - still below the price, so the 'not Sell, because the option has value' logic holds only as a sizing argument, which is how thesis frames it. (5) Bear at $19: even if it is $15, the weighted value is $110. (6) Share count: if the 3,541M count were right every intrinsic value rises about 12% ($42.50 to $47.60, $107 to $120, $111 to $125) and the gap to $403.30 stays above 60%; the call survives, which is why the market-capitalisation error is a correctness item rather than a thesis-breaking one. (7) Peer median: at the table's own 18.5x and 2.4x, Tesla's 443x and 15.0x look worse, not better, so the error flatters the company. (8) FCF yield 0.2% on $3,303M implies about 483x capitalisation against the 431x printed; rounding, not error. Units check: the report keeps annual, quarterly and per-unit figures distinct in its tables (9M, Q3, TTM, per delivery, per GWh) with the exception of the US row that mixes an annual pool (0.95M units) with a monthly Tesla share (40,816 in August, 51.7%).

items.issue: The whole risk section is written in Chinese while the case language is English, so a committee reading the numbered sections cannot read the section that carries the risk matrix and the stress test. Its evidence block row 6 has a one-line follow-up, and there is no open-diligence element although the section names two management questions in prose only.

items.issue: The granularity finding 'no comparison with a named rival' is contradicted by three tables naming Waymo (sensing and weekly rides), BYD (762,478 Q3 BEV units), CATL (Qilin charging), Sungrow (storage rank) and Panasonic/LG on cells.

Guidance is present (capex above $20B, no volume or margin guidance), consensus appears only in funding_valuation, and the surprise history is absent, although Q3 2026 non-GAAP EPS of $0.48 against a $0.45 consensus is quoted in the executive summary.

items.issue: financials states 'the equity is worth $1,428 billion and the enterprise $1,392 billion after net cash' and then derives 13.4x trailing revenue, 401x operating income, 92x EBITDA and 431x free cash flow from it. $1,428B is the diluted EPS denominator (3,541M shares) multiplied by the price, not the market capitalisation; the market convention used in funding_valuation and the executive summary is $1,594.1B on 3,952.6M shares. On the correct count the multiples are 15.0x sales and 104x adjusted EBITDA (matching funding_valuation), so the section understates how extreme the multiple is by about 10% in the direction that flatters the stock.
items.action: Recompute the whole paragraph on 3,952.6M shares: market capitalisation $1,594.1B, enterprise value $1,558.0B after $36.2B of net cash, 15.0x trailing revenue, 104x trailing adjusted EBITDA of $15.0B and 170.5x GAAP EBITDA, and restate the FCF multiple on the same capitalisation. Keep the 3,541M diluted count only as the EPS denominator, and say so in the table note.
items.evidence_request: Use S15 (price and shares outstanding) as the single capitalisation source and the independent 2026-10-20 print implying about 3,960M shares as the cross-check already in the register; no new retrieval needed.

items.issue: The street view is stated twice with different inputs: thesis and the executive summary use 48 firms, a $408.61 average target and a $128.11-$600 range (S141, S144), while funding_valuation uses $417.94 from 40 analysts with a $66-$600 range (S122) and exit quotes the $418 target as a one-year exit value. Each is internally consistent (1.3% and 3.6% above the close) but they cannot both describe the same day, and the 'sell side is almost at the price' argument rests on which one is right.
items.action: Pick one consensus series, date it, and use it in all four places; either drop the second series or present it as a differently dated snapshot with its own date (for example '2026-10-15 snapshot: 40 analysts, $417.94' and '2026-10-28 snapshot: 48 analysts, $408.61'). Also reconcile the low end of the published range ($66 versus $128.11).
items.evidence_request: Consensus target, analyst count and target range from the same provider on the same date, with the date printed in the text.

items.issue: The robotaxi pool of $0.4-0.7B of 2026 gross bookings and the '44 active robotaxi vehicles across seven metros in H1 2026' come from S107, the only source the register rates low confidence, and are repeated in competition (twice, including the SWOT) without a second source. Related fleet counts also disagree across sections: 44 active robotaxi vehicles in H1 2026, 769 Texas registrations on 2026-10-14 with 349 Cybercabs, 319 authorised Cybercab VINs at 2026-10-10, 1,000 monitored vehicles per DP26010, and Waymo at 3,000 vehicles in two sections but 4,000 in a third. A reader cannot tell which number describes the fleet.
items.action: Either corroborate the two robotaxi figures with a second independent source (a state or city permit register, a ride-hailing dataset or a second market-sizing report), or label them as one low-confidence third-party estimate and remove them from the quad's weaknesses list where they carry argumentative weight. Separately, put the three fleet counts on one dated line: 44 active vehicles in H1 2026, 769 registered in Texas on 2026-10-14 of which 349 Cybercabs, 1,000 monitored vehicles per DP26010, and Waymo at 3,000 vehicles in market and competition but a 4,000-vehicle fleet in technology_product.
items.evidence_request: Second source for the robotaxi bookings pool and active-vehicle count; a Texas DMV/TxDMV or city permit record for the 769/349 registrations at 2026-10-14; Waymo's disclosed fleet size at a stated date.

items.issue: The peer median of 16.5x earnings and 5.0x sales is used in funding_valuation, financials' narrative, the executive summary card and scoring's valuation rationale, but it cannot be reproduced from the six-company table: the trailing P/E figures shown are 18.8x (GM), 14.2x (Alphabet) and 18.5x (BYD), whose median is 18.5x, and the EV/sales figures are 7.5x, 2.4x and 2.4x, whose median is 2.4x. The medians appear to come from a wider peer set than the table shows, which is exactly the cherry-picking test the lens applies.
items.action: Show the six multiples that make each median, and either extend the table to every name behind it or restate the median as the median of the six peers shown (18.5x trailing P/E, 2.4x EV/sales) and re-derive the margin-of-safety sentence on that basis. 3.name: Missing competitors

Adjacent-giant risk is tested where it belongs, in exit: Alphabet at $3,493.5B is named as the only balance sheet large enough and the antitrust constraint is priced. Open-source and academic spin-outs are not a competitor class in this market: the autonomy stack is data- and permit-gated rather than code-gated, and the report says so through the fleet-data moat row. No remaining blind spot changes the ranking of threats.

4.name: Product/market fit
4.notes: Product/market fit output for the owners. Budget owner: identified and specific for storage — a utility or independent power producer behind an interconnection queue, price-sensitive and sticky, which matches the 16% revenue fall on higher volume and the 33.1% margin. For vehicles the hardest thing about selling is now evidenced rather than asserted: the US market lost a level after the credit ended on 2025-09-30, manufacturers replaced 88% of $7,500 with their own money and August volume still fell 46.9% to 78,895 units, so price is not the constraint and a further price cut buys little. Why adoption is not faster has three answers with different owners: robotaxi gated by permits (Texas self-certification versus no California driverless permit and a testing-only DMV listing at 2026-10-22), FSD gated by the reliability increment that pushed customer-owned unsupervised driving to Q2 2027, and Megapack gated by cell cost, where Tesla is the follower. Customer acquisition cost is not disclosed; SG&A per delivery of $4,142 is a defensible upper bound and gives payback inside the delivery quarter, and the LTV:CAC of 2.0:1 with a $288-a-year services annuity is the right order of magnitude for a hardware business. Lost deals are unavailable — no automaker discloses them and Tesla does not report cancellation rates — so the report should not claim win rates; it does not. Sales-cycle length for storage is the one unstated P/M fit input: interconnection queues imply years, and the sensitivity table treats the backlog as a one-year item. Recommend the owner either state the queue-to-COD interval from a cited source or mark the sales cycle as not disclosed.

5.name: Number stress-test
5.notes: Stress arithmetic run on every key number. Re-derived and correct: weighted value $111 = 0.25 x 212 + 0.50 x 107 + 0.25 x 19 (= $111.25); merger-inclusive $248 = 0.6 x 111 + 0.4 x 454 (= $248.2, 38% below the close); bear $75.6B = 29.3 + 18.4 + 28.0, $18.91 a share; base $429B and $107 at 4.00B shares; blue sky $1,747B and $437; market capitalisation $1,594.1B = 3,952.6M x $403.30 and enterprise value $1,558.0B after $36.2B of net cash; 15.0x sales = 1,558.0/103,570, 104x adjusted EBITDA = 1,558.0/14,995, 450x operating income = 1,558.0/3,463; reverse DCF 15.7M robotaxis = $564B/($0.60 x 60,000 miles), rising to 20.9M at $0.45 a mile; the exit IRR ladder re-computes at -45.7%, -23.3%, -22.7%, -12.1%, +1.6% and +10.0% a year; $756M per 100 bp of automotive margin = 1% of $75,561M, and $0.19 a share; the CRD and NHTSA dates are consistent at 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-30 and 2026-03-19. 30% worse stress: cutting the base autonomy value from $259B to $181B gives a base of $87.75 a share and a probability-weighted $101.70, still 75% below $403.30; a 30% lower bull ($148) with the base and bear unchanged gives $95.25; raising the bear to zero gives $107.75. The recommendation survives every branch because the option's share of the price has to fall by more than half before the probability-weighted value reaches the close — at $259B of base autonomy a reader needs roughly $809B of autonomy in the base ($212+ a share) to justify holding. Only the premium exchange ratio changes the answer, and it is carried off-tree at 40% x $454, which is the right treatment: it converts a Reduce into a Hold, not into a Buy, and the sizing cap of 0.5% of net asset value holds on a 95% bear (-0.48% of NAV). The rating sits inside the evidence gate: primary filings (S3, S4, S5) and a timestamped price (S15, NasdaqGS, 2026-10-29 20:00 UTC) support a listed Reduce.

# Tesla, Inc.: Investment research report
Rating: Reduce
Composite score: 4.0
Data as of: 2026-10-29

## 5分钟速读 Executive Briefing

TSLA closed at $403.30 on 2026-10-29, a $1,594.1B market capitalisation and a $1,558.0B enterprise value, 19% below its 52-week high of $498.83 and 36% above the low of $297.38. The stock is up 14.3% in a month and 30.6% in three, but down 11.3% year to date and 8.4% over twelve months, and the Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-21 — revenue $28.046B, adjusted EPS $0.48 against a $0.45 consensus — have been bought. The regime frames the call: the S&P 500 sits at 7,720.39, up 12.8% year to date and 1.6% below its high, the VIX is 17.20 at the 52nd percentile, and the ten-year Treasury yields 4.99%, up 0.93 points in twelve months, a discount rate that penalises cash flows arriving after 2030. [S15, S141, S22, S23, S24]

### Reduce, at a fraction of the size

Tesla's vehicles, energy and services businesses are worth $43.00 a share on 3,952.6M shares; the remaining $360.30 of the $403.30 price — $1,424B, or 89% of the equity — is an option on robotaxi and robotics that discloses no revenue. Our probability-weighted value is $111, 72% below the close, on a base that carries $259B of autonomy across four weighted branches rather than the $40B regional fleet alone; even a 40% chance of a premium SpaceX exchange lifts expected value only to $248. The action is to trim rather than to sell short: the option has real value, the balance sheet is not the constraint, and a negotiated exchange ratio could pay $443-464 without any operating delivery. [S6, S15, S120]

Confidence is high on the reported numbers — three years of filings, a third quarter reconciled line by line, and a timestamped market price — medium on the 11-14% cost of capital, and low on anything that requires sizing robotaxi revenue, because no revenue line, fare or cost per mile is disclosed. The 2026-10-25 consensus is Hold across 48 firms with a $408.61 average target and a published range from $128.11 to $600, so the disagreement is about the distribution, not the mean. [S141, S144, S4]

What is Tesla's revenue per robotaxi per week in Austin, and what share of those rides runs without a safety driver?

Without that number the autonomy value cannot be tested against a cost per mile, and every scenario above the bear case rests on a registry count of authorised vehicles rather than on unit economics. A disclosed figure that supports the revenue per mile the price implies would move the base case toward the bull case; a quarter of silence after three years of promises would move it toward the bear case. Waymo's own published rides per vehicle per week set the utilisation bar Tesla's Austin fleet has to beat.

1. **The price is the whole debate:** $360.30 of the $403.30 — 89% — is autonomy and robotics valued at 11.3 times Waymo's $126B, and the core business is worth $43.00 on vehicles at 1.0x sales, energy at 3.5x, services at 1.0x and net cash at book [S15, S120].
2. **Cash is thinner than it looks:** 61% less free cash flow in nine months, a $7,332M payables stretch and a 5.5% ROIC against an 11-14% cost of capital, with $20B+ of capex still to come [S4].
3. **One event can change the call:** a premium exchange ratio into SpaceX would pay $443-464 without any robotaxi revenue, but the vote needs 50% of all shares, no terms are agreed, and a failed vote returns the stock below $300 [S135, S5].

The follow-up diligence is dated and specific: a robotaxi revenue line, a fleet count and a fare in the next results release; a California driverless deployment permit from the DMV and CPUC filings, where the current service runs on a limousine authority; the exchange ratio, advisers and treatment of unvested awards in the special committees' 8-K; capital expenditure guidance, the Terafab contribution and any payables reversal in the annual 10-K; and the per-tranche thresholds of the CEO award in the proxy for the 2026-12-03 annual meeting. The rating is a statement about the price of an option, not about the quality of the engineering: the vehicle, cell and storage businesses are real, and they are worth about a tenth of what the market pays.

## 公司概览 Company Overview

Tesla is a single-class Texas corporation whose control rests on a 19.8% CEO stake plus a 423.7 million-share contingent award, so a public-equity holder is underwriting Elon Musk's capital allocation rather than a board-governed company; that is acceptable at a governance discount, not a premium. Tesla, Inc. was incorporated in Delaware on 2003-07-01, converted to Texas on 2024-06-13, and trades on Nasdaq under TSLA with one class of common stock and 3,952,648,559 shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, including 423,743,904 unearned restricted shares. There is no VIE, nominee-shareholder or red-chip layer [S3].

### The entity map is clean; the asset ring-fence is not

EX-21 states no ownership percentages, so the ownership column above is inferred from listing rather than disclosed. China is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, not a VIE, so there is no contractual-control gap, but Shanghai is fully consolidated and exposed to export controls. No entity is designated holder of Full Self-Driving or Optimus intellectual property: robotaxi operations sit in Tesla Robotaxi, LLC while software, data and chip designs stay in the parent, so no separately capitalised autonomy asset exists.

### Customers, buyers and how growth arrives

Tesla sells direct in two segments: automotive at $69,526m of 2025 revenue and energy at $12,771m [S71]. The vehicle buyer is a household or fleet paying cash or Tesla financing; the energy buyer is a utility or developer signing multi-year procurement, with 33.1% gross margin in Q3 2026 against 18.5% for automotive. Growth now comes from storage, software (1.74 million FSD subscriptions) and paying Cybercab rides in Austin since 2026-09-03.

### Ownership is concentrated without a dual class

| Holder | Class | Shares | % ownership | % votes | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Elon Musk | Common, incl. 286,428,773 restricted | 699,580,882 | 19.8% | 19.8% | S5 |
| Elon Musk, pledged as collateral | Common | 207,498,721 | 5.2% of outstanding | 5.2% | S5 |
| Vanguard Capital Management | Common | 210,796,512 | 5.3% | 5.3% | S5 |

| Other public holders | Common | balance | 74.9% | 74.9% | S5 |

Percentages follow the proxy, whose denominator excludes unearned award shares; free float is capped by those stakes, and a margin call on the pledged block would add supply at the worst moment. With one class and no super-voting stock, control runs through the CEO office, the board seat and stake size rather than a charter provision, unlike Ford's dual-class family control or Alphabet's founder shares.

### Control is priced through a contingent award

The 2025 CEO Performance Award is the control instrument: 423,743,904 shares in 12 tranches of 35,311,992, each tied to a market-capitalisation milestone from $2.0 trillion to $8.5 trillion and to 1 of 12 operational milestones (20 million vehicles, 10 million FSD subscriptions, 1 million bots, 1 million robotaxis, Adjusted EBITDA of $50bn to $400bn); none was earned at 2026-10-19 [S5]. At $2.0 trillion the first tranche implies $506 per share on 3.95 billion shares, and because the operational test falls away in a change of control, a deal at $3.0 trillion would earn three tranches, 105.9 million shares, with no robotaxi or Optimus milestone met. Expense is already running: $802m in the first nine months of 2026, $9.74bn unrecognised on the one milestone management judges probable, and $105.82bn-$120.37bn on the rest [S4]. Dilution of 10.7% is designed, not tail, and sits above the current valuation rather than beside it.

### The board can refuse less than it appears

Nine directors sit in three classes, six labelled independent under Nasdaq rules, with Robyn Denholm as chair since November 2018. Ira Ehrenpreis, who chairs both the compensation and the nominating and governance committees, joined SpaceX's board in February 2026; Kimbal Musk is the CEO's brother; JB Straubel, a director, runs Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier. Related-party flows are small in dollars but pointed: Tesla agreed on 2026-01-16 to invest $2.00bn in xAI, converted into SpaceX Class A stock when SpaceX bought xAI on 2026-02-02 and funded on 2026-03-12, while xAI bought $430.1m of Megapacks and SpaceX bought $143.3m of vehicles in 2025. A board setting a Tesla-SpaceX exchange ratio would do so with three of nine directors carrying outside ties — Ehrenpreis and Kimbal Musk to SpaceX, Straubel to Redwood Materials, a Tesla supplier — two of those to SpaceX itself; the proxy's retail auto-voting programme adds standing instructions to vote with the board outside a defined special matter [S78]. The counterweight is narrow: the Special Committee used only Denholm and Wilson-Thompson, and 78.2% of votes cast backed 2025 pay.

### Capital allocation has no return floor

Tesla has never paid a dividend, repurchased no shares in 2025, and holds no authorisation to offset dilution. It ended 2026-09-30 with $45.45bn of cash and short-term investments, generated $14.90bn of operating cash flow in nine months against $13.01bn of capex, guided 2026 capex above $20bn, and signed three credit agreements with $30bn of commitments in September 2026 [S6]. Against Ford and GM, which return cash, Tesla offers neither dividend nor buyback, so cash returned to holders is zero while insiders realise value through equity sales. Litigation moved rather than vanished: the Delaware Supreme Court reinstated the 2018 award on 2025-12-19, the 96,000,000-share interim award was forfeited on 2026-04-21, and a securities class action filed on 2025-08-04 in the Western District of Texas covers purchasers from 2023-04-19 to 2025-06-22 over Autopilot, FSD and Robotaxi statements.

A multi-year holder is paid for four things: a contingent award that accelerates on a deal price rather than operating proof; conflict committees that include SpaceX-affiliated directors; new debt against a thin free-cash-flow buffer; and key-person concentration in a CEO who also runs SpaceX. Three conditions would change this judgement — an independent special committee for any SpaceX transaction, no change-of-control acceleration without operating milestones, and a buyback sized to offset stock compensation. None appears in the 2026 proxy, so the governance discount stays. Confidence is high on structure, medium on how a Texas court would treat a challenge to the award; diligence should ask for the pledge's loan-to-value.
